title: bd dolt push fails 403: sync.remote points at upstream, not the fork
description: 'bd dolt push' fails with 'fatal: unable to access https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git/: The requested URL returned error: 403'. Cause: .beads/config.yaml line 64 sets sync.remote to git+https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git -- that is UPSTREAM (noshishiRust), which we have no write access to. This repo is an internal fork; the writable remote is 'fork' = https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git. Consequence: beads state is not being backed up off-machine. Confirmed .beads/issues.jsonl is stale (23 issues, all closed, missing ldui-b08), so recent closures live only in the local Dolt DB and would be lost with the workstation. Not auto-fixed: repointing sync.remote decides where issue data gets published, which is a human call. Fix candidates: (a) bd config set sync.remote git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git then bd dolt push; or (b) rely on the git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl and get auto-flush/export working so closures land in commits.
acceptance_criteria: bd dolt push exits 0, OR .beads/issues.jsonl contains ldui-b08 as closed and is committed to the fork.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED. Not sync.remote in config.yaml -- 'bd dolt push' never reads that key. The real setting is the DOLT remote: 'bd dolt remote list' showed origin -> git+https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git (upstream, unwritable). Repointing sync.remote to the fork changed 'bd config get sync.remote' but the very next push still 403'd against upstream, which is what exposed the mistake. Fix applied: bd dolt remote remove origin; bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git. Verified both the SQL-side view (bd dolt remote list) and the CLI-side view (dolt remote -v in .beads/dolt/ldui) agree, then 'bd dolt push' returned 'Push complete.' (exit 0). sync.remote was also left pointing at the fork -- harmless and directionally right. NOTE: 'bd dolt remote add' warns it only writes the SQL side; check the CLI side too. STILL OPEN and NOT fixed by this: .beads/issues.jsonl is stale (23 issues, all closed, missing ldui-b08), so the git-tracked JSONL export is not keeping up with the Dolt DB. Tracked separately in ldui-2ux.
close_reason: Fixed: the Dolt remote 'origin' pointed at upstream noshishiRust (unwritable). Removed and re-added it as git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git; verified SQL-side and CLI-side views agree; 'bd dolt push' now returns 'Push complete.' (exit 0). The title's blame on sync.remote was wrong -- see notes. Residual stale-JSONL issue split out to ldui-izn.

title: SelectableSummaryGroup: card elevation shadow overrides the selection ring (test-selectable-summary FAIL)
description: FOUND 2026-09-01 by cargo xtask verify-full (31/32): tests/selectable_summary_smoke.rs selection_adds_a_ring_without_reflowing_the_grid fails -- the selected and unselected cards report the IDENTICAL computed box-shadow 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.14) 0px 2px 4px 0px' (the card elevation), i.e. the selection ring is gone. Tailwind v4 ring utilities compose into box-shadow; a component-level elevation rule that also sets box-shadow with higher cascade priority wins the whole property and discards the ring. Introduced by 4c91330 (adopt the declared card elevation); that session's final pass did not include this lane. Fix must keep both: ring (selection, no border-width change) and elevation, e.g. express elevation through --tw-shadow / a ring-compatible layer, or apply the ring as an outline. Re-run cargo xtask test-selectable-summary; 11/11 required.
close_reason: Two-part fix: .ld-card-depth now composes with Tailwind's ring variables in both emitters (tokens.css + runtime preamble), and SelectableSummaryCard's selection ring is an outline (not a box-shadow ring the depth audit counts); keyboard focus is the framework's ld-focus-ring at offset 2. Proof on the corrected tree: selectable_summary_smoke 11/11 (ring test asserts outline geometry, elevation survives selection, focus ring offset) and style_audit_smoke 13/13 (depth ceiling 0 holds), both single-threaded against a release server.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Root cause: .ld-card-depth was emitted as a bare 'box-shadow:' rule (unlayered in the runtime preamble; @layer components in tokens.css). Tailwind v4 ring utilities also write box-shadow (composed from --tw-*-shadow variables), so whichever rule wins the cascade discards the other's layers: the preamble copy beat the layered ring-2 and the selection ring vanished, while the tokens.css copy would have lost the elevation instead. Two-part fix: (1) .ld-card-depth now composes like Tailwind's own shadow utilities (sets --tw-shadow and the five-part box-shadow list with transparent fallbacks), in both emitters, so rings/focus rings coexist with elevation for every card family; (2) SelectableSummaryCard's selection ring is now an outline (outline-2 outline-offset-0 outline-primary) rather than a ring-* box-shadow, because the style audit's DEPTH family counts every opaque box-shadow layer as elevation and the page's ceiling is 0 -- an outline paints outside the border box, never enters layout, survives forced-colors, and is not depth. A distinct focus-visible outline (offset 2, base-content) keeps a focused selected card distinguishable. Browser test probes outline geometry, asserts elevation survives selection, and checks the keyboard focus outline; xtask pin updated.

title: RecordHeader: contain right-edge quick-action tooltip without horizontal spill
description:
## Consumer evidence

The 4iiz Office Account satellite composes a compact `RecordHeader` with one status and three glyph quick actions at the standard 1694x1262 desktop viewport. The final action's `Tooltip` wrapper extends beyond the header action cluster, producing horizontal spill in the header section even though the page root itself has no document overflow.

Measured in the rebuilt Account harness:

- page root: `scrollWidth == clientWidth`
- record-header inner row: 1643px scroll width / 1599px client width
- action cluster: 247px scroll width / 203px client width
- the final tooltip wrapper accounts for approximately 44px of right-side spill

The current `render_action` always wraps every glyph control in `<Tooltip tip=name>`. DaisyUI tooltip pseudo-content is therefore included in scrollable overflow at the right edge. This is framework-owned geometry; consumer-specific clipping or overflow-hidden would conceal help and is not an acceptable fix.

External consumer: `4iiz-Office:op-dlfua.7.55`.

## Required change

Make `RecordHeader` quick-action help edge-safe inside its own composition. The last/rightmost action must not increase the header or document scroll width, while hover/focus help remains visible and the button retains its accessible name. Prefer a typed/action-position-aware placement or bounded tooltip treatment owned by `RecordHeader`, not a consumer CSS escape hatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- A RecordHeader with status plus at least three glyph actions fits a constrained desktop container without increasing the container's `scrollWidth`.
- The rightmost action's help remains visible on hover and keyboard focus and stays inside the viewport/container edge.
- Accessible names and disabled-reason wording are unchanged.
- Earlier actions retain normal help placement; no blanket clipping hides tooltips.
- Add browser coverage at a constrained width that asserts both zero horizontal spill and usable rightmost-action help.
close_reason: Root cause: one-shot mount-time measurement saw the stacked (800px) layout; fix: section ResizeObserver bumps layout_generation tracked by every action's placement effect. Browser test passes at rest/hover/keyboard and across an 800->1694 reflow round-trip; native gate 14/14.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
⚠️ THIS BEAD IS NOT DONE. Code landed in 1a8496a, but its own browser check FAILS on first execution — the fifth time in this session that a compile-only suite failed the moment it actually ran.

    tests/reactivity_smoke.rs:5955
    at rest: {"clusterSpills":true,"sectionSpills":true,"pageSpills":false,
              "tooltipClass":"tooltip tooltip-top","tipOpacity":"0",
              "ariaLabel":"Archive account","dataTip":"Archive account"}
    assertion failed: left Bool(true), right Bool(false)

Lane: reactivity_smoke 68 passed / 1 failed — only this one. Everything else in the session's final pass is green (native gate 14/14, layout 15/15, style 13/13, heatmap 13/13, entity-table 20/20, admin-workbench 17/17, bar-chart 9/9, server-column-tools 3/3).

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SAYS: the tooltip is still `tooltip tooltip-top` at rest, so the flip never applied, and the cluster and section both still spill. The measurement machinery is wired (an Effect gated on `row.get().is_some() && tooltip_ref.get().is_some()`, re-measured on pointerenter/focusin), so the likely causes are (a) the `row` NodeRef is never attached to the element the geometry is measured against, leaving the effect's guard permanently false, or (b) `estimated_tooltip_half_width` under-estimates, so `resolved_tooltip_position` concludes Top fits when it does not. The pure function has unit tests that pass, which points at the inputs rather than the arithmetic.

NEXT STEP: log the four measured inputs (row left/right, trigger left/width, half width) from the live page and compare against what the pure function was unit-tested with. The unit tests use a 400px row; the real section is ~1599px, so a half-width estimate that is fine at 400px can be far too small at 1599px.

Do not close this on the native tests: 3175 of them pass and none of them can see a tooltip's rendered geometry.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (found by instrumenting the wasm and reading the measured inputs back, not by reasoning about them): the placement effect DID run, on connected elements, and the pure function correctly returned Top for the geometry it was handed -- row 24..408 (384px wide), archive trigger at x=193.7, i.e. mid-row with room on both sides. That is the STACKED (below-lg) layout: headless Chrome mounts the page at its 800px default window and the harness applies the 1694x1262 viewport afterwards. The reflow into the row layout moved the trigger flush against the right edge, and nothing re-measured because no reactive input had changed. A one-shot mount-time measurement is stale after ANY reflow (breakpoint stacking, a host sidebar collapsing, fonts loading) -- the consumer's shell can produce the same sequence without a test harness.

FIX: RecordHeader owns a ResizeObserver on its section that bumps a layout_generation signal; every action's placement effect tracks it (plus the existing hover/focus re-measure). Every rearrangement that moves a trigger relative to the section changes the section's inline or block size (stacking changes its height), so the observer is the reflow signal. The browser test now also round-trips the viewport 800px -> 1694px and asserts tooltip-top (mid-row) then tooltip-left (edge-flush), proving re-measurement in both directions. A native source-scan test pins the wiring.

title: FilterSidebar: support a single externally placed controlled toggle
description:
## Problem

`FilterSidebar` always renders its own icon-only toggle in the sidebar header. A consumer with an established page-level Hide/Show control therefore has only two bad choices: duplicate the control or abandon the original heading hierarchy.

Office Conversation Detail (`C:/dev/4iiz-Office/surfaces/conversation-detail/src/conversation_detail.rs`, `op-dlfua.7.54`) proves the gap. Its authenticated legacy workbench has one compact top row: Back / Active Conversations / Hide panel. The rebuilt page correctly uses the opinionated `FilterSidebar`, but must also render the legacy top-row action. At 1694x1262 this produces both a page-level text action and the sidebar's internal chevron for the same controlled `collapsed` signal.

This must not be solved with consumer CSS, DOM queries, or a local sidebar.

## Required design

- Add a typed way to place the sidebar toggle externally while retaining `FilterSidebar` as owner of panel structure, dimensions, collapsed rail, active-filter count, transitions, and state-preserving content.
- Preserve today's internal toggle as the backwards-compatible default.
- External mode must render no phantom/hidden internal toggle or header gap.
- Provide a shared typed toggle/control composition (or an equivalent checked API) so the external control has the same localized label, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, focus treatment, and controlled `collapsed`/`on_toggle` semantics as the built-in control.
- The external toggle remains reachable while collapsed; the sidebar's collapsed rail continues to show active-filter count and vertical title.
- Do not introduce a domain-specific workbench or an untyped arbitrary slot that lets the two control paths drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- Default/internal mode is visually and behaviorally unchanged.
- External mode produces exactly one toggle in the accessibility tree and DOM, located where the consumer composes it.
- Activating the external toggle collapses/expands the same panel, retains focus on that control, preserves typed filter/search state and selected content, and keeps `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` truthful.
- Both left- and right-docked sidebars work in expanded and collapsed states without overflow.
- Browser stories cover pointer and keyboard activation, locale changes, active-count rail, repeated collapse/expand, and no duplicate/phantom toggle.
- Document the exact consumer call shape for Office to replace its duplicated top action plus internal chevron.
close_reason:
Implemented in 06895f7, lane re-pinned in f7a977e. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own), admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, layout 15/15, style 13/13.

FilterSidebarTogglePlacement::{Internal (default), External} plus a public FilterSidebarToggle, both routed through ONE shared button function so the two paths cannot drift.

Under External the internal toggle is OMITTED ENTIRELY rather than hidden. That distinction matters here more than usual: ldui-8hba exists because a panel whose toggle was clipped out of the rail could not be reopened at all, so a hidden-but-present toggle would reintroduce exactly that ambiguity. Exactly the control the consumer placed exists, and if both are supplied the component still emits none of its own.

The external toggle takes the same collapsed/on_toggle/toggle_label/side plus a controls id matching the panel, so aria-expanded and aria-controls are framework-owned rather than hand-rolled by the consumer. ldui-8hba's four-cell check (Left/Right x with/without header_actions) is unregressed.

title: EntityTable: expose typed focus requests for external editor mutations
description:
## Consumer defect

4iiz Office `op-dlfua.7.52` uses one controlled `EntityTable` beside an external note editor. Deleting the selected note is initiated by the editor's Delete button, the central API deletes and re-reads, and the page supplies the stable successor selection. In the exact 1694 x 1262 harness proof, ON-1003 was removed and ON-1002 was correctly selected/loaded, but focus fell to `<body>`.

The current EntityTable focus record only begins with `focusin` inside its own region. That correctly handles mutations initiated by a row action, but it cannot service an external editor action. The consumer has no typed way to request focus for a stable row/action after an accepted same-generation snapshot replacement. A consumer DOM query would recreate the prohibited cross-layer focus implementation that `ldui-ifj.3` moved into EntityTable.

## Required contract

Expose a typed, controlled EntityTable focus-request/handle contract for external workflows. It must carry the dataset/access scope, stable row key, desired target (row or named row action), and request identity/generation so one accepted request is applied once. The component must resolve against its actual filtered, sorted, paged, grouped presentation rather than source order.

## Acceptance criteria

- A same-scope request for a visible stable row focuses that row, or the requested visible/enabled named row action, after the accepted data projection paints.
- If the target is filtered away, paged away, removed, disabled, or otherwise not focusable, use a documented table-region fallback; never guess a positional row from source order.
- Reject stale dataset/access scopes and do not steal focus if the user moved to another meaningful target after the request was issued.
- Work in wide and compact layouts and with controlled grouping/paging.
- Browser proof covers an external Delete button removing the selected row and focusing the accepted successor, deletion of the final visible row, filtered/sorted successors, and a failed/declined mutation that leaves native editor focus unchanged.
- Existing internal row-action recovery and reactive-column behavior remain unchanged.

Consumer: `C:\dev\4iiz-Office`, `op-dlfua.7.52`.
close_reason:
Implemented in bcfb9d3. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); entity-table 20/20, reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own), admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, layout 15/15, style 13/13.

focus_request: Signal<Option<EntityFocusRequest>> plus on_focus_request_resolved, with Row/RowAction targets and Row|RowAction|TableRegion|StaleScope|Declined outcomes, resolved against page_row_keys.

IT HOLDS NO ELEMENT REFERENCE. An external editor deletes the selected row, so the element the caller means is destroyed and recreated — the request re-queries by STABLE KEY on the next animation frame and retries one more frame before the table-region fallback. That is the lesson from ldui-9j16's column-move focus loss and ldui-8d94's collapse focus loss, both of which were the same shape.

'Declined' means focus genuinely MOVED since the request was observed (body or a detached node do not count), so a failed mutation must simply issue no request rather than a declined one — documented, because the distinction decides whether a caller retries.

title: EntityTable: keep fitting controlled row groups intact across pagination
description:
## Observed consumer failure

The 4iiz Office Coordinator Activity page uses `EntityRowGrouping` exactly as introduced by `ldui-iyfa`: 3 coordinator groups, each with 17 Task / Goal / Actual rows. At the opinionated desktop auto page size of 18, EntityTable renders the first coordinator's 17 rows, then the next coordinator heading plus its first row. Page 2 correctly repeats `Avery Johnson (continued)` before the remaining 16 rows, so the existing continuation-heading accessibility behavior works.

Exact evidence: Office `op-dlfua.7.47`, sealed harness release `sha256-3a8100c6d9e1438b6f00514ecc9a3bcb0842cbf07fc6dde78b61592e47416852`, 1694 x 1262 desktop viewport. Page 1 footer says `Activities 1-18 of 51`; DOM rows are Morgan heading + all 17 Morgan activities + Avery heading + Avery's first activity. Page 2 is truthfully `Activities 19-36 of 51` and begins with Avery's continuation heading.

This cannot be repaired correctly in the consumer without overriding opinionated pagination or hand-rolling group tables.

## Required component behavior

Make EntityTable pagination group-aware when controlled row grouping is enabled. Keep a whole group together when that group fits within the configured/automatic page capacity, instead of consuming a small remainder on the previous page. Preserve the existing clearly marked continuation heading when a group itself exceeds page capacity or cannot otherwise remain whole.

Auto page-size calculation and footer range/count copy must remain truthful about data rows (group headings are structural, not extra records). Filtering/sorting must recompute group boundaries before pagination. Keyboard navigation, visible-position metadata, focus recovery, compact rendering, and controlled selection must use the resulting visible grouped order.

Do not require the consumer to choose magic page sizes based on current group cardinality.
acceptance_criteria: At desktop and compact breakpoints, a controlled row group that fits within the current page capacity is not split merely to fill leftover rows; oversized groups retain the existing accessible continuation heading, row counts/ranges remain truthful, and browser coverage exercises auto page size, filtering, sorting, selection, and a group larger than one page.
close_reason:
Implemented in bcfb9d3 (one commit with its three siblings; they rewire the same component body and split hunks would not compile alone). VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); browser lanes green — entity-table 20/20, reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own, unrelated), admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, layout 15/15, style 13/13.

RULE: a group whose full row count fits one page capacity is never split to fill the previous page's remainder — the page ends early and the group starts whole. A group LARGER than a whole page cannot be kept whole by any packing, so it degrades to the previous fill-first behaviour under the existing continuation heading; deferring it would still split it and waste a page. Pinned by a property test that a boundary may fall inside a group only when that group exceeds capacity. New EntityPagePlan is the single source of page boundaries and the footer range is read off it rather than recomputed as page*capacity.

⚠️ Its browser check FAILED on first execution, reporting the pages partitioned 20 rows out of 81 — which reads exactly like a plan that DROPS rows. It was the test: the walk read the pager's visible buttons, which are page_window's 7-button WINDOW, not the full page list. The plan partitioned all 81 throughout. Fixed in d127a28 by walking the next control until disabled (bounded so a never-disabling pager fails rather than hangs) and asserting the last footer range ends at the dataset total — the check that would have caught it immediately instead of yielding a quietly wrong sum.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Consumer proof from 4iiz Office NPS Lessons Learned (`op-dlfua.7.51`), exact 1694 x 1262 browser viewport on 2026-09-01:

- One grouped EntityTable owns 48 rows across 14 office groups plus unlinked feedback, with viewport-fit resolving to 14 rows.
- Page 1 renders Charlotte 4, Dallas 3, Durham 4, Fontana 1, then only 2 of Greensboro's 4 rows.
- Page 2 repeats `Greensboro (continued)` for its remaining 2 rows. Greensboro's complete four-row group fits within the 14-row page capacity; keeping it intact would leave two unused rows on page 1 and place all four on page 2.
- The same fill-first behavior splits Raleigh 3/1 across pages 2/3 and unlinked feedback 2/6 across pages 3/4.
- The existing repeated-heading accessibility context works, so this is not context loss. It is the exact `ldui-5in5` presentation defect: a controlled group that fits is split merely to fill the remaining capacity.

Acceptance proof should preserve caller group order and all row/range truth while moving a fitting group atomically to the next page; only a group larger than the resolved page capacity should require a continued fragment.

title: EntityTable: distinguish provider-empty from filtered-empty copy
description: Office Contribution supplies four ledger rows. Filtering Outcome to a non-match correctly produces zero displayed rows, but EntityTable renders the configured provider-empty message 'No contribution credits are present in this snapshot.' This is false because source rows exist; EntityTableTexts exposes only one no_rows string even though the table knows source and filtered counts.
acceptance_criteria: EntityTableTexts exposes distinct provider-empty and filtered-empty localized copy. EntityTable selects provider-empty only when the authoritative source dataset is empty and filtered-empty when source rows exist but the current projection is empty. The distinction works with controlled source_data, local sorting/filtering/paging, compact and desktop layouts, and preserves current defaults for consumers that do not override either string.
close_reason:
Implemented in bcfb9d3. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); browser lanes green — entity-table 20/20, reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own, unrelated), admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, layout 15/15, style 13/13.

EntityTableTexts::no_matching_rows added beside no_rows, with an EntityEmptyState and a data-entity-empty-state hook. The table already knew both counts; showing the provider-empty sentence when source rows exist but none match was simply false.

A caller who sets only the existing string is unchanged, proven two ways rather than asserted: no_rows keeps its meaning, default and render site for the provider case, and the fixture overrides ONLY no_rows via ..Default::default() — the browser check asserts their sentence still appears when the provider is drained, while a non-matching filter (source=81) shows the framework default.

title: FilterSidebar: make collapsed content inert and hidden from accessibility tree
description: Office Journal uses the opinionated right-side FilterSidebar as a collapsible AI Assistant rail. At desktop width, collapsing correctly reduces the rail to 44px and applies opacity-0/pointer-events-none, but descendants remain rendered, visible to the accessibility tree, and keyboard-focusable (including a textarea and action button). Pointer blocking does not implement a true collapsed state.
acceptance_criteria: When collapsed, FilterSidebar content is removed from sequential focus and the accessibility tree using a framework-owned inert/aria-hidden strategy; the toggle remains operable and exposes aria-expanded=false. Expanding restores the original focusability without remounting caller state. Cover left/right variants and an interactive child in browser tests; preserve the existing width transition and active-count presentation.
close_reason:
Implemented in e78d33a. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own), admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, layout 15/15, style 13/13.

inert plus aria-hidden on the panel's main content when collapsed, following ldui-8hba's finding that pointer-events-none hides neither the tab order nor the accessibility tree — content stays reachable and announced while being invisible, which is worse than either state alone.

The aside's own overflow-hidden is untouched, so the collapse transition still CLIPS the 220px content rather than reflowing it — that clipping is load-bearing for the animation and inert does not affect it. The header h3 and the collapsed rail were left alone deliberately: no focusable descendants, and already aria-hidden.

title: KpiStrip: add typed full-row three-summary layout
description: The 4iiz Office Pending reconciliation has exactly three peer KPI summaries matching legacy production. At a 1696px desktop viewport, KpiStrip AutoEight renders a 1617.6px grid as eight tracks and leaves the three 188.2px cards occupying only the first 596.6px. BalancedSix still leaves half the row empty. Consumer CSS track overrides would move opinionated responsive policy into the page.
design: Add a named KpiStrip layout intent for a three-summary row, with a framework-owned responsive ladder that preserves equal peer geometry and fills the available desktop row with three tracks. Keep AutoEight and BalancedSix behavior unchanged. The new type must own compact/non-compact classes, runtime marker, sizing arithmetic, documentation, and browser geometry proof.
acceptance_criteria: At a 1600px-class desktop container, three items using the new typed layout render as three equal tracks spanning the full strip with normal gaps and colored-edge KpiCard semantics. The responsive ladder remains usable below desktop without consumer CSS. Existing AutoEight and BalancedSix snapshots and geometry remain unchanged. Browser coverage measures the three-card row and confirms no horizontal overflow or joined-stat regression.
close_reason:
Implemented in c1c5d18. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own), layout 15/15, style 13/13.

KpiStripLayout::PeerThree, a third typed profile beside AutoEight and BalancedSix. It DIVERGES from the shared ladder at its first rung rather than inheriting it, because a three-peer row can never fill a fourth track — inheriting would be wrong, not merely suboptimal.

Ladder with the arithmetic, as ldui-k3ip established: base 320px -> 2 cols = 152.0px; @lg 512px -> 3 cols = 160.0px. Both clear the measured floors (114px for a two-line label, 125px for a card also carrying a help control). Its test reproduces the bead's own numbers at 1617.6px: AutoEight spans 596.6px, BalancedSix ~800.8px, PeerThree the full row.

AutoEight and BalancedSix are byte-for-byte unchanged (extended into shared loops only). Both new fixtures carry w-full — the zero-width trap documented on the component, where @container makes an element's inline size independent of its contents so a content-sized parent collapses it to ~2px cards with no error.

title: ServerDataTable: localize column resize accessible names
description: Dashboard Detail exact browser proof in 4iiz Office shows fully reactive Spanish table copy, but every ServerDataTable resize separator remains English, for example Resize Fecha column. The hardcoded source is src/components/data_table/header.rs aria-label format Resize header_label column. EntityTable already owns a resize_column text template; the server table needs equivalent typed reactive text ownership rather than a consumer DOM patch.
design: Add a localized resize-column accessible-name template to the typed ServerDataTable text contract, thread it reactively into the shared header, and replace the hardcoded format call. Preserve stable column identity and keyboard resize behavior across locale changes.
acceptance_criteria: A ServerDataTable using Spanish reactive texts renders Cambiar el ancho de la columna Fecha or caller-provided equivalent on its separator; switching EN to ES and back updates the existing separator accessible names without remounting the table; default English remains Resize Date column; browser coverage proves keyboard resizing, table identity, and geometry remain stable.
close_reason:
Implemented in 1bdc6a4. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own), layout 15/15, style 13/13.

DataTableTexts::resize_column, a template defaulting to 'Resize {column} column' and mirroring EntityTableTexts::resize_column, threaded into the shared DataTableHeader through a new optional texts prop. Replaces a hardcoded format! that no locale could reach.

The name identifies WHICH column it resizes by substituting that column's own caller-localized header text, so a Spanish consumer gets 'Cambiar el ancho de la columna Fecha' rather than a generic 'resize'. That matters for a control a keyboard user operates: 'resize' repeated five times names nothing. Both DataTable and ServerDataTable call sites updated; ldui-j6sh's id/name identities untouched.

title: Checkbox needs a controlled checked-state and change-proposal contract
description:
`components::Checkbox` is visually opinionated but cannot participate in controlled application state. Its public props are only color, size, disabled, class, and node_ref. It exposes no checked signal, no atomic change proposal, no indeterminate state, and no first-class id/name/accessible-label identity. The exact consumer reproduction is `C:\dev\4iiz-Office`, Pending Assignments Bead `op-dlfua.7.37`: the legacy Past due only filter must live in the opinionated FilterBar beside controlled Select/Input components, but LDUI Checkbox cannot receive the accepted filter value or notify the owner. Office is therefore forced to render one raw `<input type="checkbox">` while every surrounding control uses LDUI.

This gap encourages three recurring failures: page-local checkbox styling that drifts from tokens/focus rules, imperative node_ref or DOM-query synchronization that creates two sources of truth, and uncontrolled checked attributes that stop following restored/reset state after mount. Do not solve it by documenting a raw input escape hatch, asking consumers to dispatch DOM events, adding arbitrary event/attribute forwarding as the primary contract, or letting Checkbox own persistence. The component should remain domain-neutral and proposal-first.
design:
Add a source-compatible controlled Checkbox binding. The accepted boolean is a reactive Signal and a user click/Space emits one Callback<bool> proposal; the rendered checked property continues to follow only the accepted signal, so a caller may reject or delay a proposal without visual state drifting. Add an optional reactive indeterminate signal implemented through the DOM property, with coherent `aria-checked="mixed"`, and explicit stable id/name plus accessible-label support following the existing Select/Input conventions. Disabled state suppresses proposals and keeps native semantics.

Existing calls that omit the binding retain their current native uncontrolled behavior and exact classes. Controlled and uncontrolled ownership must be mutually unambiguous; do not maintain a hidden internal mirror. Localization belongs to the caller-provided label/accessible-label signal, while focus, pressed motion, forced-colors treatment, checkbox tokens, and native keyboard behavior remain framework-owned. Document usage inside FilterBar and EntityColumnFilter without adding Office vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: Existing Checkbox calls compile unchanged and retain native uncontrolled behavior. A caller can supply reactive accepted checked and indeterminate state plus one typed on_change proposal callback without node_ref or DOM synchronization. Click and Space propose the next boolean exactly once; rejected proposals restore the accepted DOM property; disabled controls emit nothing. Stable id, name, and reactive accessible-label props follow the library field conventions. Indeterminate state exposes coherent native and aria mixed semantics. Component and browser coverage proves external reset, delayed/rejected proposals, EN to ES accessible-label replacement, disabled behavior, indeterminate transitions, form identity, focus-visible, reduced motion, and forced colors. The Office Pending page can replace its raw past-due checkbox with LDUI Checkbox without consumer CSS or imperative DOM code.
close_reason:
Implemented in 85bf1ad, lane re-pinned in f7a977e. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests) and the browser lanes green. Its 12 browser checks run in the registered reactivity lane (69/69).

CheckboxBinding::controlled(Signal<bool>, Callback<CheckboxChangeProposal>) with .with_indeterminate(...); the proposal carries the resulting checked state and the state it came from. A binding struct rather than loose props, so half-configuration is inexpressible.

THE CHECKBOX-SPECIFIC TRAP: the browser toggles the input natively BEFORE any handler runs, so a component that merely listens diverges from accepted truth on every rejected proposal. The handler re-asserts the accepted checked and indeterminate values onto the element BEFORE proposing, and the render reads only accepted signals with no internal mirror. The browser proof is a DECLINED click on a mixed box, which is the only way to demonstrate the component follows the caller rather than the browser.

indeterminate is set via prop: (no content attribute exists) and re-asserted in the change handler, because the browser clears the flag on click — without that the tri-state silently degrades to a plain checkbox after the first interaction.

id/name follow ldui-j6sh's scheme (that module is private, so it is restated rather than imported, and the module doc says so); a minted id never becomes a name. Uncontrolled callers are unchanged, proven by a browser check asserting a bare <Checkbox/> emits exactly class/data-testid/type. Mixed configuration renders ServerDataTable's fail-closed role="alert" rather than EntityTable's panic — chosen deliberately, because a checkbox is a leaf control rendered many times per list and a wasm panic kills the page.

title: KpiStrip needs a typed balanced-six desktop layout profile
description:
`KpiStrip` owns responsive KPI-card layout, but its only layout contract is currently hard-coded in `src/patterns/kpi_strip.rs::kpi_strip_grid_class`: 2 columns, then 3, then 4, then 8 at the widest container breakpoint. That default is useful for short operational strips, but it cannot reproduce a balanced fixed dashboard set.

The exact consumer reproduction is `C:\dev\4iiz-Office`, Dashboard bead `op-dlfua.7.35`. The established Office Leader Dashboard has twelve KPI cards arranged as two rows of six at a 1600-1694px desktop viewport. Show Rate is a detail on the Shows card, so twelve is intentional. Replacing the local card/grid with the opinionated KpiStrip currently produces eight cards followed by a ragged row of four. That changes the first-viewport scan order and makes the lower row visually read as a secondary group even though all twelve KPIs are peers.

The existing arbitrary `class` escape hatch is not an adequate composition contract. A consumer would have to inject competing `@5xl:grid-cols-*` utilities, depend on Tailwind emission/order, repeat the override on every dashboard, and own breakpoint policy that belongs to KpiStrip. That is the same consumer fork this opinionated layer is intended to eliminate.

Do not special-case Office, infer columns from item count, accept arbitrary CSS strings as the new API, or change the current default. The framework needs one typed layout choice for a balanced six-column desktop strip while retaining its existing container-query behavior and accessibility semantics.
design:
Add a typed KpiStrip layout/profile prop with the existing eight-column behavior as the source-compatible default and a balanced-six profile for dashboard scorecards. Naming should follow repository conventions, for example `KpiStripLayout::{AutoEight, BalancedSix}` or a cohesive `KpiStripColumns` enum; do not expose an unchecked integer or a Tailwind class fragment.

The framework continues to own every breakpoint. The six-column profile should keep the same narrow progression (two columns, then three, then four where appropriate) and cap at six once the strip container is wide enough. `compact` remains an independent padding/gap choice; it must not silently change the number of columns. Card item identity, focus, activation, comparison bars, equal label/value offsets, status edges, and reactive EN/ES replacement remain exactly the same across profiles.

The profile is about balanced peer sets, not one product vocabulary. Document a twelve-item scorecard example and a six-item example. Keep container queries so a strip placed beside a 360px assistant rail responds to its actual available width rather than the browser viewport. Do not add page navigation, card content, or Office-specific labels.
acceptance_criteria:
Existing KpiStrip calls compile unchanged and retain the current 2/3/4/8 container-query grid. A caller can select a typed balanced-six profile without supplying CSS classes; at the documented desktop container width twelve cards render as exactly two rows of six and six cards render as one row of six, with equal track widths and no stretched/ragged peer group. Narrow containers still step down without horizontal overflow.

The layout choice is orthogonal to compact spacing and preserves stable item keys, focus during unrelated reactive updates, card activation, baseline comparison geometry, status edges, forced-colors behavior, and EN to ES to EN replacement. Component and browser coverage exercise 12, 6, 5, and empty item sets at the relevant container widths and include a negative control proving the balanced-six assertion fails under the old hard-coded eight-column class. Public rustdoc shows the typed API. The Office Dashboard can delete its `.dashboard-kpi-grid` CSS and render its established 6x2 scorecard using only KpiStrip props.
close_reason: Implemented in 5f7170c. KpiStripLayout::{AutoEight,BalancedSix} typed profile prop, emitted as data-kpi-strip-layout. BalancedSix ladder is 2/3/4/6 with the six-column rung at @4xl (896px -> 136px cards), derived: @3xl would give 114.7px, which clears ldui-tnyq's 114px two-line floor but not ldui-yhvf's 125px help-bearing floor. Container queries throughout; the ladder is data and the emitted class string is asserted against it. Default AutoEight 2/3/4/8 unchanged, proved by character-for-character comparison against the pre-bead literals plus every existing call site compiling untouched. Non-divisible counts leave a ragged last row whose cards keep their full track width (explicit tracks, never auto-fit). At the consumer's measured 1046px container BalancedSix gives 6 cols of 161px vs AutoEight's 8 of 117px, so the ldui-ztgo baseline bar gains room (101px at the narrowest six-column width vs the 82px already shipping). 14 native geometry tests + 4 browser tests in the registered admin_workbench_smoke suite covering 12/6/5/empty and a narrow-column sweep, with the negative control. Native: lib lane +14, 0 failures; showcase check clean; clippy clean for every touched file. Browser lane is compile-only from this session -- needs cargo xtask test-admin-workbench against a fresh dist.

title: BarChart needs typed signed divergence, accessible categories, and reactive copy
description:
`charts::BarChart` cannot currently express a signed categorical comparison or an application-grade accessible/localized chart. Its public data is positional `Vec<(String, f64)>`; domain calculation takes the maximum and clamps at zero, so negative values produce invalid/negative bar geometry rather than bars extending from a zero baseline. Per-bar colors are a second positional vector. The SVG has no accessible name, description, semantic data table, stable category keys, or keyboard/pointer activation, and its empty branch hard-codes English `No data`.

The exact consumer reproduction is `C:\dev\4iiz-Office`, Dashboard Bead `op-dlfua.7.35`. The owner-visible `Ranked` mode is a decomposition of one selected KPI: Office/worker rows sorted most-dragging-first by `current - trailing_12_week_baseline`, negative bars extend left of zero and nonnegative bars right, formatted current and delta values remain visible, outcomes use caller-supplied favorable/unfavorable status while activity measures stay neutral, and the KPI selector updates the chart reactively. The prior Office module hand-built flex bars because the framework chart cannot represent that grammar.

Do not solve this by telling each consumer to pre-absolute the values, draw two unrelated positive charts, supply parallel key/color/value arrays, add a separate hidden table, or hand-code SVG/flex geometry. Absolute values erase direction and two projections drift.
design:
Add a cohesive categorical data model and reactive data source analogous to LineChart. Each category needs a stable key, localized display label, signed numeric value, optional formatted display value/data label, and typed semantic status or theme-token color. The chart owns a finite signed domain spanning min through max and always includes zero. Add an explicit layout/mode for diverging horizontal bars; negative values extend left from the zero line and positive values extend right, with symmetric geometry when magnitudes match. Zero and non-finite/missing values have deterministic honest presentations.

Add reactive `BarChartTexts` for empty/missing/table headings, `accessible_label`, optional description, and an enabled-by-default semantic data table for categorical data. Optional activation must emit the stable category key, label, finite signed value, source, and modifiers; support pointer and Enter/Space with visible focus and stable-key reconciliation after reorder/replacement. Noninteractive charts remain free of artificial button roles/tab stops.

Preserve the existing simple `(label, value)` API and vertical/horizontal behavior through a compatibility conversion if practical. Existing positional `bar_colors` behavior must not silently change. The richer model must keep data/color/status in one item rather than adding more positionally parallel arrays. Semantic status remains caller-owned: the framework must not infer that positive is always favorable because some measures are limits.

Document a most-dragging-first example with negative, zero, and positive current-minus-baseline values, localized formatted current/delta labels, outcome statuses, and an activity-neutral variant. No Office KPI vocabulary, sorting policy, API call, or navigation belongs in the chart.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy BarChart calls retain their current visual output and mismatch-safe positional color behavior. A typed/reactive categorical BarChart can render finite negative, zero, and positive values against one visible zero baseline in diverging-horizontal mode: equal magnitudes have equal geometry on opposite sides, no width/height is negative, and missing/non-finite values never leak NaN/infinity or become fabricated zero. Stable item data carries key, localized label, signed value, formatted display, and caller-owned semantic status without parallel arrays. The SVG has a reactive accessible name/description and an equivalent semantic table; empty/missing/table copy reacts EN -> ES -> EN without changing keys, values, order, focus, or selection. Optional pointer and Enter/Space activation emits stable identity/source/modifiers and focus survives keyed reorder or moves predictably after removal; noninteractive charts gain no tab stops. Browser/unit/story coverage includes signed symmetry, all-negative/all-positive/all-zero, missing/non-finite, activity-neutral versus outcome status, sorted reorder, compact labels, reduced motion, and forced colors. The Office Dashboard Ranked mode can delete its hand-rolled flex-bar geometry and render the selected-KPI decomposition using only BarChart plus caller-owned sorting/KPI selection.
close_reason:
Implemented in 178c4ac, registered in 3973c49, with a real defect fixed in 80cba0b and three suite defects in da60278. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests) and the browser lanes green. Bar-chart lane 9/9.

THE ROOT DEFECT was the domain, not the rendering: it took the maximum and clamped at zero, so negative values produced invalid geometry. Now min.min(0)/max.max(0) with each bar computed as a span from the zero line, so no dimension can be negative and equal magnitudes are congruent in any domain. All-positive callers get an identical 0..max with coordinates asserted against the original formulae; a collapsed span falls back to 0..1 rather than dividing by zero.

Colour is now part of the typed BarChartItem rather than a second positional vector, so a sort or filter cannot misalign the two — the defect was in the SHAPE of the API. Activation carries a stable category_key and NO index field, so the aliasing bug is unrepresentable. Legacy Vec<(String, f64)> callers compile untouched via a From impl on a typed data-source enum, proven at five layers rather than asserted.

Accessibility follows LineChart's precedent: role="group" not role="img" (which would make focusable children presentational and fail the axe gate), a hidden category/value/status table, one roving tab stop, targets marked role="button" only when a callback is wired.

Paint verified by BREAK-AND-REVERT: injecting an unrouted fill and a raw var() stroke each made svg_paint_routing FAIL, green after revert. That matters because a var() in an SVG presentation attribute degrades silently to black.

⚠️ THE CHART WAS UNREACHABLE BY KEYBOARD, found on the suite's first execution — the same first-run reconcile defect as Heatmap (ldui-8d94), in a component written by a different implementer. Its suite also had three of its own defects that made the component look wrong: a triple-nested oracle path comparing everything against Null, a "legacy charts" selector that swept in the interactive LineChart and Heatmap and reported THEIR 60 tab stops as this component's regression, and an assertion that document.activeElement survives clicking a sort button (it cannot; the roving tab stop is the property that matters).

title: Heatmap needs typed accessible categories, keyboard activation, and reactive copy
description:
`charts::Heatmap` is the framework-owned visual for a matrix, but its current public/DOM contract cannot satisfy an accessible localized application page. The SVG has no `role`, accessible name, description, or equivalent data table. The empty branch hard-codes English `No data`. Visible cell text is painted as SVG text but there is no structured row/column/value name for assistive technology. When `on_cell_click` is supplied, the component adds transparent `<rect>` overlays with a pointer cursor and `on:click` only: no focusability, role, accessible name, Enter/Space activation, or focus recovery. The callback emits `(row_index, col_index)`, so an activation is tied to array position rather than stable row/column identity.

The exact consumer reproduction is `C:\dev\4iiz-Office`, Dashboard Bead `op-dlfua.7.35`. Its Heatmap view is one Office row by twelve KPI columns. Each cell must expose the Office, localized KPI label, current formatted value, and direction versus the 12-week baseline; cells may later drill by stable Office/KPI IDs. The existing standalone page hand-rolled an HTML table because the opinionated Heatmap could not carry those semantics. The owner requires the page to use the opinionated component, so the missing accessibility/i18n behavior belongs here rather than in an Office overlay.

This is also a repeated-mistake guard: do not tell consumers to add a second hidden matrix, patch SVG nodes after render, wrap the chart with an unlabeled role, or attach keyboard listeners outside the component. Two parallel data projections drift, and a pointer-only SVG is not an interactive control.
design:
Bring Heatmap to the categorical accessibility posture already established by LineChart while preserving its current static visual API for simple noninteractive callers.

Introduce stable typed row and column categories (`key` plus localized display `label`) and a cohesive cell value that can carry visible text plus a complete caller-owned localized accessible value/summary. An equivalent reactive `HeatmapDataSource` model is acceptable; do not use parallel positional ID arrays. The rendering may still normalize to row/column indices internally, but public activation must return stable row and column keys, display labels, the cell value, source (pointer/keyboard), and modifier state.

Add reactive framework copy such as `HeatmapTexts { no_data, data_table_caption, row_header, column_header, value_header }`, plus `accessible_label`, optional longer description, and `show_data_table` (default true for categorical data). Follow LineChart's approach: the SVG is named/described, and an equivalent semantic table exposes every populated/missing row-column value without requiring a second consumer projection. Missing cells and no-data state must be distinguishable and localized.

When activation is enabled, render real focusable SVG activation targets with an accessible name assembled from the caller's structured/localized cell summary. Support pointer plus Enter/Space, visible focus, reasonable roving focus for a large grid, Escape/dismissal if a detail card exists, reduced motion, and forced colors. Reconcile focus by stable row/column keys across reactive reorder/replacement. A noninteractive Heatmap must not gain artificial button roles or tab stops.

Retain `HeatScale::{Magnitude,Judgement}`, signed caller-owned business sense, max-cell-height behavior, slanted labels, theme-token colors, and current non-finite folding. Do not infer “higher is better,” translate provider values, introduce Dashboard routes, or add arbitrary HTML cell children.
acceptance_criteria: Existing noninteractive Heatmap callers retain their visual geometry, scale behavior, token colors, non-finite handling, and no artificial tab stops. A categorical/reactive Heatmap can be given stable row/column keys, localized labels, an accessible chart name/description, and per-cell visible plus accessible value text without a second consumer-owned matrix. Its semantic data table exposes row, column, value, and missing-cell meaning and can be disabled only explicitly. Empty and missing copy comes from reactive HeatmapTexts; EN -> ES -> EN changes all framework-owned/chart labels without changing stable keys, intensity, focus, or activated identity. When activation is enabled, every eligible cell works by pointer and Enter/Space, has a visible focus indicator and complete localized accessible name, and emits stable row/column keys plus source/modifiers; focus follows the same key after reorder and moves predictably when a cell disappears. Noninteractive mode remains free of button roles/listeners. Browser/component tests cover one-row-by-twelve-columns, multirow, empty, missing/non-finite, reorder, pointer/keyboard activation, compact overflow, reduced motion, and forced colors. Public rustdoc demonstrates the Office-like one-office/twelve-KPI case. The Office Dashboard can delete its hand-rolled heatmap table and meet the same information/accessibility contract with `Heatmap` only.
close_reason:
Implemented in 3880898, with a real defect found and fixed in 80cba0b. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests), and the browser lanes green — reactivity 69, entity-table 20, layout 15, style 13, heatmap 13, search-picker 15, bar-chart 9, selectable-summary 11, keyed-result-list 11, admin-workbench 17, modal 6, section-heading 8, page-quick-actions 5, server-column-tools 3. Heatmap lane 13/13.

Typed HeatmapMatrix with HeatmapCategory rows/columns and HeatmapValue naming its row and column, so a cell's identity is the PAIR (row_key, column_key) — the two axes move independently and are followed separately. Values naming an unknown key are dropped rather than placed at a guess.

TWO-AXIS KEYBOARD MODEL, stated rather than left implicit: Left/Right moves within the row, Up/Down within the column, Home/End reach the row's first/last column (the row never changes), Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End the grid corners, Escape drops the highlight without moving the tab stop, all clamping rather than wrapping.

THE HIDDEN TABLE IS A MATRIX, not a flat list: th[scope="row"] on row labels, th[scope="col"] on columns, a corner cell naming the row axis, one td per coordinate — so a value is located as "North, SLA met" rather than by counting. The SVG's own label texts go aria-hidden when the table is shown, so the axis is not announced twice.

Judgement is not colour-only (hue plus a solid/dashed sense rule plus the verdict in words). Activation carries both keys and NO index field, asserted by a test on the Debug rendering. Legacy positional callers keep working, proven by a published doctest that compiles the exact old call site including on_cell_click.

⚠️ THE GRID WAS UNREACHABLE BY KEYBOARD, found on the suite's first ever execution. The reconcile effect returns early on its first run, so reduce() never ran at mount, roving_key stayed None, and no cell carried tabindex=0 — the correct fallback existed but was unreachable until the data changed. Fixed by reconciling the axes against themselves at mount. BarChart had the identical defect (ldui-y2ed); two components, two authors, the same effect shape.

Paint routing verified by break-and-revert: an injected unrouted stroke made svg_paint_routing fail 18/1, green after revert.
