title: KpiStrip needs typed baseline comparison and card activation
description:
`KpiStrip` owns the independent stat-card visual grammar, but its typed `KpiItem` can currently express only label, value, description, status, trend, and help. A real dashboard consumer therefore cannot express two established KPI behaviors without abandoning the opinionated component: a numeric current-versus-baseline row and activation of a card into the rows behind that number.

The exact reproduction is `C:\dev\4iiz-Office`, Dashboard Bead `op-dlfua.7.35`, standalone source `surfaces/dashboard/src/dashboard.rs`. The production Dashboard renders twelve KPIs. Each card shows the current formatted value, the trailing 12-week baseline, a bounded comparison bar with the baseline/cap marker, the truthful percentage even when over baseline, localized above/below/no-baseline/settling copy, and a keyboard-accessible launch into Dashboard Detail for the same KPI and Office scope.

Because `KpiItem` has no comparison or activation model, the consumer recreated `fn KpiCard` with low-level `Card`, `Badge`, a raw form button, a custom grid, and `shadow-sm`. That immediately lost the framework's current blue edge/elevation, localized `KpiStripTexts`, sizing, accessible-name grammar, and future changes. This Bead exists to remove that reason to fork; Office will delete its local card once the framework capability is available.

This is not a request for Dashboard-specific strings, HTTP forms, URLs, or routing. It is a reusable typed KPI grammar: actual against a comparison value plus an activation intent keyed by the KPI's stable ID. It must also cover unavailable comparison states without fabricating zero or a percentage of zero.

Do not solve it with arbitrary `Children` per card, caller CSS selectors, parallel unkeyed arrays, raw HTML slots, or a consumer-only wrapper around `Card`. Those approaches move layout/accessibility policy back into every page and repeat the current defect.
design:
Extend the framework-owned KPI item/card composition with two optional typed capabilities while preserving the current simple-strip path.

1. Add a typed comparison value owned by the item (name may follow repository conventions), carrying raw finite `current` and `baseline` values plus localized caller copy needed to describe the baseline and comparison. The framework renders the row with the existing opinionated `CapacityBar` semantics: fill is `current / baseline` clamped for geometry, the cap/baseline remains structurally visible, and adjacent text states the truthful ratio even above 100%. A zero, negative, missing, or non-finite baseline renders no misleading bar; the caller's localized no-baseline/settling description remains visible. Status determines semantic emphasis; the framework must not infer business meaning such as “higher is good” from the numbers.

2. Add one strip/card-level activation callback receiving the stable `KpiItem.id`, plus typed caller-owned localized action labeling on an activatable item. The component owns keyboard/pointer semantics and visible/focus treatment; Office maps the emitted ID to its API/route and selected Office scope. Prefer one clear interactive contract (whole-card activation or one framework-rendered action) and prohibit nested interactive descendants. Nonactivatable cards remain nonfocusable groups exactly as today.

Keep the data cohesive. Extending `KpiItem` is acceptable if first-party call sites are migrated; an equivalent typed entry wrapper is acceptable if it avoids a public source break. Do not introduce a comparison/activation vector whose position must accidentally match `items`. Preserve stable `data-kpi-card` identity, reactive `Signal<Vec<...>>` updates, localized `KpiStripTexts`, compact layout, unavailable semantics, help tooltip/description, status edge, trend, and semantic elevation.

Document an Office-like twelve-card example with current value, “12-week avg · 250”, `112%`, localized “12% above the 12-week average”, and detail activation. Include no-baseline, settling, below-baseline, above-baseline, activity-neutral, and unavailable-value examples. The component remains a composition primitive; it does not fetch, navigate, submit forms, or know Office routes.
acceptance_criteria: Existing simple KpiStrip/KpiCard compositions retain their current DOM meaning, responsive grid, blue status edge, compact behavior, unavailable fallback, trend/help behavior, and localized framework copy. A typed KPI item can additionally render a current-versus-baseline comparison using framework-owned CapacityBar geometry: below, equal, and above-baseline values are bounded visually while the displayed/accessibility text remains truthful above 100%; zero/missing/non-finite baselines never produce NaN, infinity, or a fabricated percentage. Business favorable/unfavorable meaning comes from typed status, not inferred “higher is better” logic. A caller can make selected items keyboard- and pointer-activatable through one callback that receives the stable item ID and uses localized accessible/action copy; nonactivatable items remain nonfocusable groups, no nested interactive content is introduced, and activation works in standalone KpiCard and KpiStrip usage. Reactive data and EN/ES copy replacement preserve focus and item identity. Component/unit/browser/story coverage includes twelve cards, compact wrapping, no-baseline, settling, under/equal/over baseline, activation by Enter/Space and pointer, disabled/nonactivatable behavior, reduced motion, and forced colors. Public rustdoc shows the typed pattern. The Office Dashboard can delete its local KpiCard/grid and reproduce all twelve production KPI cards plus detail launches using only KpiStrip/KpiCard props and an Office-owned callback, without consumer card markup or CSS.
close_reason:
Implemented in 67536f1. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree: 12 lanes, zero failures, admin-workbench 13/13 (the fixture now mixes 4 baseline cards with 4 plain, so that suite's existing equal-height and value-alignment asserts become the mixed-card proof). Native gate 14/14, 2954 tests (+38).

BASELINE: KpiItem.baseline(KpiBaseline) with against/absent/settling constructors and a pure resolve() -> KpiComparison. All five sentences are templates on KpiStripTexts, so nothing is hardcoded English.

THE TRUTHFULNESS PROBLEM, which was the crux. The bar is bounded and the number is not, and they are computed from different sources so they cannot silently converge: fill_percent runs through CapacityBar's clamped percent fn, while ratio_percent comes straight from current/baseline. 780 against a 250 baseline pins the bar and still reads 312%, with data-kpi-baseline-saturated recording that the GEOMETRY ran out rather than the value. track_max is pinned at baseline * 1.25, so the marker sits at exactly 80% of the track on every card and never moves - at the cap the fill stops on the tick, and past it the fill crosses a still-visible tick, so a full bar reads "well past the marker" and never "at the cap".

THREE DEGENERATE STATES, EACH DECLARED rather than emergent: zero, negative, NaN and infinite baselines (and a non-finite current) return BEFORE the divide, presenting as no-baseline but carrying data-kpi-baseline-degraded - so a defect stays distinguishable from a legitimate absence and from a settling window, which is the distinction that would otherwise be lost. Placeholders substitute to the localized unavailable string, never to 0.

ACTIVATION: on_activate: Callback<String> emitting the item id, opt-in, rendered as ONE framework-owned Pressable rather than a whole-card handler. The reasoning is sound and worth keeping: a <button> cannot contain the card's paragraphs, role="group" must not change for existing callers, and a synthetic whole-card handler would nest the help affordance inside a control. Help was already non-interactive, so an activatable card has exactly one focusable descendant.

ON THE ELEVATION QUESTION I FLAGGED: it kept the static ld-card-depth rather than the interactive ld-elevated lift, because the card is not the control - lifting the whole card would promise press-anywhere when only one descendant is pressable. ld-elevated is banned from both shell and body by test, so the two cannot be mixed later by accident.

Non-activatable cards are unchanged and proven so: the gate requires both an action and a callback, pre-bead items have neither, and there is no tabindex anywhere in the card source plus a browser focusable-census showing 1 versus 0.

NOTE the ratchet movement this bead predicted did NOT occur, and not because nothing changed: /components/kpi_strip is not in either audit's page set. Filed as ldui-ddhr - the audits sweep 7 of 40+ demo pages and every opinionated pattern is unmeasured.

title: SectionHeading needs typed trailing status placement without abusing actions
description:
`SectionHeading` currently renders its `status` child inside the same flex row as the heading (`src/patterns/section_heading.rs`, title/status row), while only the `actions` slot is a trailing sibling. That is correct for a compact badge beside a heading but cannot express an established full-width section header whose noninteractive maturity/freshness status is aligned at the far right.

The exact consumer reproduction is Office Scorecard (`4iiz-Office` Bead `op-dlfua.7.34`). At 1600 x 1000, the legacy Commitments and Results produced cards place `Provisional — pending measure review` against the right edge, and Completed Work places its unavailable dash there. Composing these through the current opinionated `SectionHeading` puts the text immediately after the title. Passing the text through `actions` would obtain the geometry but falsify the slot contract; hand-rolling the heading or targeting LDUI descendants in consumer CSS would fork shared hierarchy and responsive behavior.

This is a typed composition gap, not a request for Scorecard-specific markup. Preserve the current inline placement as the default and add an explicit framework-owned trailing-status placement suitable for noninteractive status/freshness copy. Document how it coexists with actual actions and how it wraps at compact widths.
design:
Add a small public placement enum, for example `SectionHeadingStatusPlacement::{Inline, Trailing}`, and a static/typed `status_placement` prop whose default is `Inline` for compatibility.

`Inline` must retain the current title-row DOM and rendering. `Trailing` must render the same status slot as a separately identifiable sibling after the title/description group and before any action controls, aligned to the trailing edge at desktop widths and wrapping onto a readable full row at compact widths. Keep DOM order title/description, status, actions; do not duplicate or clone the child. Emit a stable data attribute for browser/story assertions. Status remains noninteractive presentation; consumers still use `actions` for controls.

Add the new case to the component documentation/story catalog and cover desktop, compact wrapping, status-only, actions-only, and status-plus-actions compositions. Do not add a Scorecard variant, consumer class name, arbitrary CSS-string placement prop, or descendant-selector escape hatch.
acceptance_criteria: The default inline status rendering and public API remain source-compatible. A typed trailing placement aligns noninteractive status at the far edge on a wide heading, wraps without overlap or title compression on a compact heading, and remains distinct from the actions slot. Status plus actions have deterministic DOM order and no duplicate content. Component tests and a rendered browser/story case cover inline, trailing, compact, and trailing-plus-actions. Documentation explains when to use each placement. The Office Scorecard Commitments, Results produced, and Track Record headers can reproduce their established geometry using only `SectionHeading` props and no page-local heading/CSS workaround.
close_reason:
Implemented in dceff84. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (67536f1): 12 lanes, zero failures - reactivity 54, entity-table 16, search-picker 15, selectable-summary 11, keyed-result-list 11, layout 9, admin-workbench 13, style 7, modal-close-proposal 6, section-heading 8, page-quick-actions 5, server-column-tools 3. Native gate 14/14 (2954 tests).

SectionHeadingStatusPlacement::{Inline,Trailing} with a status_placement prop, default Inline. A TYPED PLACEMENT RATHER THAN A BOOL because it names intent instead of mechanism, matches exhaustively, and leaves room for a third placement without an ambiguous second flag - a status_trailing: bool would have to be joined by status_centered: bool later.

The bead's real point was semantic, not geometric: routing non-interactive status text through the actions slot gets the right alignment while misrepresenting text as an action surface. The trailing status is therefore a plain div with no role, tabindex or handler, carrying its own data-section-heading-status attribute and never the actions one, always emitted before actions in source - pinned by two unit tests and a browser check asserting DOM order and single occurrence via compareDocumentPosition.

Existing callers are unchanged and proven so: the Inline arm forwards status untouched with the title-row markup identical, pinned by a test on that source line plus a browser check driving the EXISTING fixture that never passes the new prop, and all five pre-existing browser checks were left unmodified.

Long title plus long status - the case where this layout usually breaks - is covered: the title group is flex-1 so it claims space first, status and actions pack to the trailing edge and wrap rather than squeezing the title, with a dedicated fixture asserting the heading keeps real width at desktop and wraps without overlap when compact.

⚠️ CONCURRENCY INCIDENT, and it was my dispatch error rather than this implementation's. I scoped this bead and ldui-ztgo to src/patterns/ in parallel, and both legitimately needed src/patterns/mod.rs to export their new types, so this commit swept ztgo's in-progress exports and main did not compile between dceff84 and 67536f1. Nothing was lost and 67536f1 repaired it. I had serialised the four EntityTable beads for exactly this reason and failed to apply the same logic to a shared mod.rs: disjoint COMPONENTS are not disjoint FILES.

title: DayScheduler hardcodes English interval grammar in interactive event accessible names
description:
Office's standalone Day Planner uses the opinionated DayScheduler with interactive event blocks. In an exact 1600x1000 browser pass, switching the real shell language from EN to ES translated the page and changed the gutter to 24-hour labels, but every event's accessible name retained the English interval grammar, for example: `Cita: Jordan Lee, 09:00 to 10:00`.

This is framework-owned output, not provider data and not an Office composition error. `src/components/day_scheduler/types.rs::event_aria_label` formats `"{}, {} to {}"`, and `src/components/day_scheduler/component.rs` always calls that helper for interactive blocks. The component already offers caller-owned `hour_label` and `now_label`, but there is no hook for the event accessible-name sentence. Searching the LDUI Beads queue for `DayScheduler localization accessible event interval` found no existing issue.

Consumer evidence:
- Repository: `C:\dev\4iiz-Office`
- Surface: `surfaces/day-planner`
- Exact harness URL: `http://127.0.0.1:4181/day-planner/t/test-tab/?pp-freeze=1`
- Office tracking Bead: `op-dlfua.7.33`
- Reproduction: load the harness; choose ES in the standard titlebar; inspect an interactive scheduler event in the accessibility tree. Page-owned visible copy is Spanish, while the event name still contains `to`.

Do not solve this by making Office patch rendered DOM, by putting localized prose into stable event IDs, or by replacing DayScheduler with page-local markup. The opinionated component must expose the localization seam.
design:
Add a typed, optional caller-owned accessible-name formatter to DayScheduler, analogous to its existing `hour_label` formatter. A suitable API is `event_accessible_label: Option<Callback<SchedulerEvent, String>>` (the exact public name may follow repository conventions). For interactive events, call this formatter when supplied; otherwise retain the current `event_aria_label` English default byte-for-byte.

The callback must execute inside the reactive `aria-label` closure so a caller can read its language signal and update the existing event nodes after EN/ES changes. It must receive the structured SchedulerEvent, not a preformatted or concatenated string, so consumers can express locale-specific grammar and word order such as Spanish `"{title}, de {start} a {end}"`. Keep `minute_label` and stable event identity separate from translated prose.

Preserve all existing focus, activation, selection, keyboard move/resize, lane-layout, and display-only behavior. Add public rustdoc that distinguishes the visual `event_content` hook from the accessible-name formatter and shows a localized reactive example. This is a component localization seam, not an Office-specific translation table.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Existing DayScheduler call sites compile without changes and interactive event accessible names retain the exact current English default, including the existing `Standup, 09:00 to 09:15` unit expectation.
2. A caller can supply a typed event accessible-name formatter that receives SchedulerEvent and returns the complete localized name; the component uses that value directly for `aria-label` on interactive event blocks.
3. The formatter may read a reactive locale signal. A browser/component test proves EN -> ES -> EN updates the same rendered event's accessible name without rebuilding the scheduler, changing event identity, losing selection, or losing keyboard focus.
4. Spanish proof contains locale-appropriate interval grammar (for example `de 09:00 a 09:15`) and no framework-generated English ` to ` token.
5. Display-only schedulers remain free of artificial button roles, tab stops, and event aria-labels exactly as today.
6. Keyboard activation, selection, Arrow move, Shift+Arrow resize, overlap layout, custom event content, hour-label formatting, and the now marker remain covered and unchanged.
7. Public rustdoc documents the default and localized callback contract. No consumer-specific strings, DOM post-processing, or page-local scheduler replacement is introduced.
close_reason:
Implemented in a8d6d6d, with the lane re-pinned in fe228b5. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (67536f1): 12 lanes, zero failures - reactivity 54, entity-table 16, search-picker 15, selectable-summary 11, keyed-result-list 11, layout 9, admin-workbench 13, style 7, modal-close-proposal 6, section-heading 8, page-quick-actions 5, server-column-tools 3. Native gate 14/14 (2954 tests).

DayScheduler gains event_accessible_label: Option<Callback<SchedulerEvent, String>>, mirroring the existing hour_label seam.

A CALLBACK RATHER THAN A FORMAT STRING, deliberately: it receives the whole event, so it can reorder and inflect. A format string is localizable but cannot express that Spanish inserts "de"/"a" rather than merely swapping tokens, and the same is true of Japanese and Arabic word order. The cost is pushed onto callers who opt in, which is the right trade for a sentence only they can write correctly.

The default is unchanged and proven so, not asserted: a pure resolve_event_accessible_label falls through to the original event_aria_label when no formatter is supplied, pinned by the pre-existing "Standup, 09:00 to 09:15" test still passing plus a new default test.

THE FAILURE MODE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN THE BUG: an override returning empty or whitespace would leave the event with NO accessible name at all - a screen-reader user gets nothing, where before they at least got English. It falls back to the default instead, covered by two tests.

The non-interactive path is deliberately untouched: aria-label is only emitted when interactive, so a display-only scheduler gains no accessible-name logic. Browser proof asserts EN->ES->EN by same-DOM-node identity with selection preserved, in the registered reactivity lane; its count pin moved 53 -> 54, which the implementer reported rather than working around.

title: Add typed confirmable search-picker dialog for mutation workflows
description:
## Consumer failure that exposed the gap

The Office Client Success page assigns a standing order to one coordinator from a directory of 60+ workers. The established interaction is deliberately two-step: open a searchable coordinator dialog, select a worker, then activate an explicit Assign button. Selecting a result must not itself perform the write.

`SearchPickerDialog<T>` currently treats result activation as the terminal caller action and exposes only a Cancel footer. It has no controlled selected key, selected-result summary, pending state, confirmation callback, confirmation label, or confirmation button. A consumer that needs review-before-mutation must therefore recompose Modal, Input, KeyedResultList, focus management, selected-item retention, and footer actions locally.

This is a shared opinionated-pattern gap, not a request for an Office-specific assignment component. The same interaction applies to reassign, restore, link-record, choose-owner, and other mutations where searching/selecting is reversible but confirming has a side effect.

Office reference: `C:/dev/4iiz-Office/surfaces/client-success/src/client_success.rs`, tracked by `op-dlfua.7.32`. The legacy behavior is in `crates/office-perf-web/src/screens/client_success.rs` around the standing-order Assign modal.

## Required outcome

Provide a typed opinionated dialog for search -> select -> explicitly confirm. Keep the existing immediate-activation `SearchPickerDialog` behavior intact for navigation/open use cases; do not silently change its activation semantics.
design:
Prefer a separate pattern such as `ConfirmableSearchPickerDialog<T>` (name is flexible) rather than adding mutually confusing semantics to `SearchPickerDialog<T>`.

The pattern should own Modal, labelled search Field/Input, typed `KeyedResultList`, loading/error/empty presentation, selected-item summary, focus lifecycle, and footer layout. The caller should provide controlled open/query/status/items/selected-key/pending state plus callbacks for query change, selection change, confirm, close, and retry.

Required invariants:

- Result activation changes the selected key only. It never invokes the mutation callback.
- Confirm resolves the selected key against the current typed item list, or a separately retained typed selected item, before invoking the callback. Stale or missing keys fail closed.
- A selected worker remains visibly named if a later query filters that row out.
- Confirm is disabled when there is no valid selection or while pending.
- Search results use stable business keys and preserve keyboard navigation/replacement safety from `KeyedResultList`.
- Opening focuses search; Escape/Cancel close without confirmation; closing returns focus to the invoking control through the modal lifecycle.
- A stable caller-supplied contract/control ID derives distinct heading, description, search, result-list, selected-summary, cancel, and confirm IDs/names.
- All pattern-owned copy is supplied by a complete reactive text struct: search label/placeholder, empty/loading/error/retry, selected label, cancel, confirm, and pending confirmation.
- The component exposes no business-specific terms such as coordinator, assignment, matter, or client.

If the API instead accepts an optional footer slot on `SearchPickerDialog`, it must still make the two activation models explicit at the type/API level so a consumer cannot accidentally turn result activation into a write.
acceptance_criteria:
- A showcase/browser case demonstrates at least three keyed results, search filtering, keyboard navigation, selection, explicit confirmation, cancellation, and pending state.
- Pointer or Enter activation of a result updates only the selected presentation; a separate side-effect counter remains zero until Confirm is activated.
- Confirm returns the current typed item, fires exactly once, and cannot fire with no selection, a stale key, or while pending.
- Replacing/filtering results preserves the selected summary without reconstructing or mislabelling the payload; confirmation fails closed if the selected identity is no longer valid under the documented policy.
- Escape and Cancel never invoke confirmation and restore focus to the trigger.
- The dialog has an accessible name/description, the search field has a stable label and ID/name, the listbox remains keyboard navigable, and every generated ID is unique across two simultaneous component instances.
- Reactive English/Spanish example copy updates while preserving stable result keys and selected identity.
- Narrow native tests cover pure selection/confirmation resolution, and a real browser test separately proves semantic state, rendered state, callback count, focus recovery, and prohibited side effects.
- Documentation explains when to choose immediate `SearchPickerDialog` versus the confirmable pattern and includes a typed assignment-style example with neutral domain names.
