title: Give DataTable filter and server-selection controls stable DOM identities
description:
## Observed consumer failure

The exact Office Conversations satellite was inspected at a 1600 x 1000 desktop viewport on 2026-09-01. Chrome reports visible form controls without an `id` or `name`. A direct DOM inventory proves the framework-owned controls are the remaining offenders after excluding the page-owned Period and unresolved-only controls:

- the `DataTableTextFilter` input for Client;
- each exact `<select>` in `DataTableFilterRow` (Channel, Office, Coordinator, Status, and Last update);
- the `ServerTableMultiSelection` current-slice checkbox; and
- every `ServerTableMultiSelection` row checkbox.

The controls have accessible names, but accessible naming is not a stable DOM/form identity. Office cannot safely repair these elements from the consuming page without reaching into LDUI-owned markup or hand-rolling the table, both of which violate component ownership.

## Source evidence

- `src/components/data_table/filter.rs`: `DataTableTextFilter` renders its input with `aria-label` but no `id`/`name`; the exact-filter branch does the same for `<select>`.
- `src/components/data_table/server_component.rs`: the selection header and keyed row `Checkbox` controls expose `aria-label` and data attributes but no stable `id`/`name`.
- The same server component already creates an instance-specific search ID and a derived page-size ID, so the missing controls currently follow a different identity policy within one component.

## Repetition trap

Do not fix this in an Office page with raw DOM queries, post-mount attribute mutation, page-local checkboxes, or CSS selectors based on row order. Those approaches lose uniqueness when two tables render, break when rows reorder/page, and duplicate LDUI ownership. Do not use only a global process counter as the public identity: it is unique during one mount but not stable enough for deterministic browser automation or SSR/hydration. The caller needs an optional stable table/control prefix, with a safe instance-unique fallback for existing consumers.

## Consumer evidence

`C:/dev/4iiz-Office/surfaces/conversations/src/conversations.rs` renders one opinionated `ServerDataTable` with integrated filters and LDUI multi-selection. The exact release at `/conversations/t/test-tab/?pp-freeze=1` otherwise reaches `data-page-state=ready`; this identity defect is therefore independently observable rather than masked by loading/error state.
design:
Add one framework-owned DOM identity contract for every control emitted by `DataTable`/`ServerDataTable`.

Preferred shape:

1. Expose an optional stable table/control ID prefix on the public table component. Validate or normalize it once. Preserve an instance-unique generated fallback for source compatibility.
2. Thread that resolved prefix into `DataTableFilterRow`, `DataTableTextFilter`, and server multi-selection rendering.
3. Derive deterministic unique IDs and names from the resolved table prefix plus the stable column ID or stable row key. Encode/sanitize arbitrary row keys without creating collisions.
4. Associate the existing visually-hidden labels with each generated control using `for`, while retaining the current `aria-label` copy.
5. Ensure multiple tables on one page, remounts, sorting, filtering, and paging cannot create duplicate IDs or make a stable row's identity depend on its visual index.

The framework remains the sole owner of filter and selection markup. Consuming pages should only supply the table identity; they should never need to patch descendants after mount.
acceptance_criteria:
- A `DataTable`/`ServerDataTable` caller can provide one stable table/control prefix.
- Every rendered text filter and exact filter has a non-empty, unique, deterministic `id` and `name`, derived from that prefix and the stable column ID.
- The current-slice selection checkbox and every keyed row-selection checkbox have non-empty, unique, deterministic `id` and `name`; a row's identity survives sorting/filtering/paging and is not based on row index.
- Existing accessible names, controlled filter proposals, controlled selection proposals, indeterminate state, blocked-row behavior, focus behavior, and source compatibility remain intact.
- Tests render at least two tables on the same page and assert no duplicate IDs. Tests also reorder/page rows and prove the same stable row key retains the same identity.
- A browser smoke of the Office Conversations consumer shows no visible LDUI-owned table control without an `id` or `name`.
close_reason:
Fixed in c7b5143. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree: 12 lanes / 160 checks / zero failures - reactivity 53, entity-table 16, search-picker 15, selectable-summary 11, keyed-result-list 11, layout 9, admin-workbench 9, style 7, modal-close-proposal 6, section-heading 5, page-quick-actions 5, server-column-tools 3. Native gate 14/14 (2916 tests).

Every framework-owned control the bead named - the text filter input, each filter-row select, the current-slice checkbox and every row checkbox - now carries a stable id AND name, minted in a new shared src/components/data_table/identity.rs. Both tables take an optional control_id: a caller-supplied prefix wins, otherwise a per-instance minted one, following EntityTable's existing precedent rather than a third scheme.

WHY name AS WELL AS id, since the distinction is the whole complaint: id serves label[for], aria-controls and selectors, while name is what makes it a real form control for FormData and submission - and name is what the audit actually checks. Setting only id would have left half the failure open. Every named control also gained autocomplete="off", because giving a table filter a name is precisely what invites browser autofill onto it.

ROW IDENTITY DERIVES FROM THE STABLE ROW KEY, never the index. That was the sharp edge: an index re-points at a different row after paging, so an id that aliases is worse than no id. Proven three ways - a pure test running the same keys in three slice orders, disjoint id sets across page1/page2, and a browser check that records (key, id), pages forward, asserts disjointness, pages back and asserts the ids return byte-identical.

COLLISION FREEDOM BY CONSTRUCTION, not by convention: the key is ESCAPE-ENCODED (_hh), not slugified, because a slug collapses "a b", "a-b" and "a_b" into one id. The test module carries a decoder as the injectivity proof and round-trips 20 adversarial keys. Encoded tokens contain no "-", so "-"-joined segments are unambiguous and a per-row id structurally cannot collide with a per-column or fixed-role one - tested with columns literally named select-all and page-size. Two tables on one page produce disjoint sets, plus a whole-document duplicate-[id] sweep in the browser. Documented limit: uniqueness AMONG caller-supplied prefixes is the caller's responsibility, as with any hard-coded id.

It also retargeted four existing reactivity selectors onto the new data-table-search-control / data-table-page-size-control hooks - necessary once a consumer picks the id shape, and the same move as 59d765b. That lane passes 53/53, which is what confirms the retarget did not silently point at a different element.

title: KpiStrip uses stock Tailwind shadow instead of the declared elevation contract
description:
## Evidence

The opinionated `KpiStrip` is documented as a row of independent, bordered, shadowed stat cards, but `src/patterns/kpi_strip.rs` currently hard-codes Tailwind's stock `shadow-sm` in both the documented source-inline contract and the rendered card class (approximately lines 346 and 517 at framework HEAD `4a95b04`). The repository's own visual-quality rule `doc/visual-quality/ad-hoc-shadow.md` says stock Tailwind shadows are off-contract when a declared elevation exists.

The 4iiz Office legacy/current desktop audit made the drift obvious: the legacy product used its declared soft card elevation throughout, while the new opinionated KPI cards render with the stock Tailwind shadow. Merely adding an Office `shadow-card` safelist entry would not fix this because no `KpiStrip` element emits that class. A consumer-side descendant selector or page-local class fork would also violate the opinionated-component ownership boundary.

## Required design

Give `KpiStrip`/`KpiCard` a framework-owned semantic, non-interactive card-elevation policy. It must use an LDUI semantic class backed by the declared `ui_tokens::elevation` vocabulary, with an explicit CSS custom-property hook if a product theme needs to supply its approved card shadow. Do not use `shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, or another stock Tailwind elevation. Do not apply `ld-elevated` unchanged if that would add hover translation to non-interactive KPI cards.

The component remains opinionated: callers should not have to repeat a card class on every page, and the solution must not introduce an Office-specific name or value into the framework. Preserve the existing independent-card border, responsive grid, accent edge, high-contrast behavior, reduced-motion behavior, and stable card geometry.

## Verification and mistake prevention

- Add a focused source/component assertion that the rendered KPI card carries the semantic LDUI elevation class and no stock Tailwind shadow utility.
- Add or extend the computed-style browser fixture to prove its resting shadow is one of the active `StyleProfile`'s declared shadows.
- Demonstrate the new assertion failing against the current `shadow-sm` implementation, then restore it.
- Update `doc/patterns/kpi-strip.md` and its `@source inline` guidance so consumers do not safelist an obsolete stock class.
- Verify a consumer can override only the semantic card-shadow variable while retaining the framework default.

## Acceptance criteria

`KpiStrip` and direct `KpiCard` usage render a declared, static card elevation through one framework-owned semantic class; neither production implementation nor documentation emits `shadow-sm`/`shadow-md` for KPI cards. The computed-style audit recognizes the default shadow as on-profile, a product-theme override is proven without page-local selectors, and the targeted negative control is recorded.
acceptance_criteria: KpiStrip and direct KpiCard render a framework-owned semantic static card elevation from the declared token profile; production and docs contain no stock shadow-sm or shadow-md KPI elevation; computed-style and product-theme override proofs pass with a recorded negative control.
close_reason:
Fixed in d793417. Native gate 14/14 on the final tree; the implementer ran admin_workbench 9/9, style 7/7 and layout 9/9 against a freshly published dist.

`.ld-card-depth`, backed by the declared vocabulary as `box-shadow: var(--ld-card-shadow, var(--ld-elevation-4))`. The stock `shadow-sm` is gone from both the rendered class and the doc contract.

LEVEL_4 rather than LEVEL_2: ui_tokens documents it verbatim as "Card resting elevation", it is what the interactive `ld-elevated` rests at (so static and interactive cards agree rather than disagreeing by one step), and it is the smallest honest move from shadow-sm. LEVEL_2 is the control-outline level and would have left KPI cards shallower than every other card surface.

THE OVERRIDE HOOK works by ABSENCE: `--ld-card-shadow` is never declared by the crate, so a product theme's `:root { --ld-card-shadow: ... }` wins with no !important, no selector specificity fight and no fork, and removing it restores the default. That is what the bead needed - a consumer could not previously reach this at all without violating the component ownership boundary.

⚠️ THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE FAILED SILENTLY, and the reason this was briefed carefully: a class living only in the runtime preamble is invisible to any consumer who never mounts `UiTokensPreamble` - they would have got NO shadow at all, strictly worse than the shadow-sm being replaced. That is exactly ldui-h7tw's failure. Both the class and `--ld-elevation-*` are therefore emitted into the GENERATED styles/tokens.css, verified three independent ways: a test reading the file off disk, a static-vs-runtime value-for-value agreement test, and grepping the shipped demo/dist stylesheet on a page that never mounts the preamble.

FOUR NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all recorded, because the acceptance asked for one and a passing assertion that cannot fail proves nothing: reverting the class failed a unit test; restoring shadow-sm in the doc contract failed; a full source revert plus demo rebuild failed the browser check reporting Tailwind's exact computed shadow-sm value; and removing the hook failed the theme-override assertion. The most valuable was making the class runtime-preamble-only: the NEW static-stylesheet check failed while the PRE-EXISTING backstop passed, proving the stricter check was necessary rather than redundant.

The style audit's declared shadow set is deliberately UNCHANGED: from_ui_tokens already seeds StyleProfile.shadows from elevation::LEVELS, so LEVEL_4 was already declared, and adding an entry would have been precisely the undocumented-entry failure that file warns about. No ceiling moved.

title: KeyedResultList: support caller-controlled selected key
description:
## Problem

`KeyedResultList` owns an internal selected key and only reports changes. A consumer whose active record is authoritative outside the list cannot seed the initial highlight, restore it after an external route/state change, or atomically keep the highlighted row aligned with asynchronously loaded detail panes. Office Conversation Detail needs this for its compact conversation queue; a local list or CSS selection workaround would violate the shared opinionated-component boundary.

## Required design

Add an optional caller-controlled selected-key model to `KeyedResultList`, following the established controlled-selection shape used by `TabSet` and `EntityTable`. The list remains the owner of keyboard, hover, scroll-into-view, ARIA, replacement reconciliation, and activation behavior. Pointer and keyboard selection must propose changes through the existing callback; the caller remains authoritative when the controlled prop is present. Preserve current uncontrolled behavior for existing consumers.

The model must distinguish active selection from hover preview. External selection changes must update `aria-selected` and `aria-activedescendant` and scroll the active option into view. If a controlled key is absent from the current result set, render no falsely selected row and do not silently overwrite the caller's key. When that key reappears after filtering or replacement, restore its highlight. Empty/duplicate-key validation must remain fail-closed.

## Consumer evidence

`C:/dev/4iiz-Office/surfaces/conversation-detail/src/conversation_detail.rs` loads a server-selected ticket and independently replaces transcript, composer, analysis, and private-note state. The left rail must use shared `FilterSidebar` plus shared `KeyedResultList`; it must not hand-roll a selectable queue.

## Scope

Implement and document the shared API in LDUI only. Add focused component tests for controlled initial selection, external changes, selected key filtered out and restored, items replacement/reordering, keyboard/click proposals, scrolling/ARIA wiring, and backwards-compatible uncontrolled behavior. Provide the exact prop/callback call shape for consumer adoption.
design: Extend the shared KeyedResultList selection model; do not add an Office-specific queue component.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled initial/external selection is authoritative; absent filtered key produces no false highlight and restores when it returns; keyboard/click emit proposals without local divergence; ARIA and scroll tracking follow the controlled key; uncontrolled behavior remains compatible; focused tests and consumer-facing API documentation are included.
close_reason:
Implemented in 7a79d08. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (c948eab): 12 lanes, 140 checks, zero failures. Native gate 14/14.

KeyedResultListSelection::controlled(Signal<Option<String>>, Callback<KeyedResultListSelectionProposal>), the proposal carrying the complete replacement value plus a typed Click/Keyboard cause - never a delta, never applied locally.

THE CASE THAT MATTERED: a controlled key absent from the current items. It is filtered on every read by a pure function, so no row is falsely highlighted and aria-activedescendant is absent - but the CALLER'S SIGNAL IS LEFT UNTOUCHED, so the selection reappears by itself when a matching row returns. Silently clearing the caller's state would have been the lie, and needing a reconciliation write would have been the bug.

Uncontrolled behaviour is unchanged and proven so: selection defaults to None, the internal reconciliation path is untouched, and all 8 pre-existing browser checks pass unmodified. Mixed configuration (controlled selection plus the legacy on_selection_change) renders a role="alert" panel rather than guessing which the caller meant. The stable-key guarantees the component already had - selection surviving duplicate labels, reorders and removals - are untouched.

title: Modal: keep controlled open state synchronized with Escape and backdrop close
description: Modal accepts a controlling open signal, but the native dialog can close through Escape or ModalBackdrop without notifying the owner. The page state can therefore remain true while the dialog is closed, so a later true-to-true target change may not reopen it and the caller cannot clear scoped feedback or reliably restore trigger focus without reaching into the DOM. Office NPS exposed this while replacing a local editor with the shared Modal. Add a typed controlled close proposal/callback covering Escape and backdrop activation; do not require consumers to hand-roll dialog event plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Escape and backdrop activation emit a typed close proposal to the controlling owner. Accepting the proposal and driving open=false closes the dialog exactly once; declining it leaves or restores the dialog open without state drift. Programmatic open=false does not emit a duplicate user-close proposal. The API preserves accessible native-dialog behavior and documented focus return, has browser coverage for Escape/backdrop/programmatic close, and existing uncontrolled/default call sites remain source-compatible.
close_reason:
Implemented in dafdd28, with its suite registered in e836460 and a fixture defect fixed in c9754ef. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (c948eab): 12 lanes, 140 checks, zero failures - reactivity 53, entity-table 16, selectable-summary 11, keyed-result-list 11, layout 9, admin-workbench 8, style 7, search-picker 7, modal-close-proposal 6, section-heading 5, page-quick-actions 5, server-column-tools 2. Native gate 14/14.

Modal now emits a typed ModalCloseProposal { cause } through on_close_request, covering Escape, Backdrop and DialogForm. THE INSIGHT THAT MADE IT CORRECT: a backdrop click fires NO cancel event at all. cancel is Escape-only; ModalBackdrop is a method="dialog" form, so it closes through a SUBMIT - which is why every cancel-based workaround was blind to it, and why this hooks both. Only method="dialog" is vetoed, so a real post/get form inside a modal still submits.

An ignored proposal closes nothing: the native default is vetoed BEFORE the callback runs, so the dialog stays open, focus stays inside it, and the open signal was never written - no optimistic state to reconcile. Trigger focus is left to the platform, because show_modal()/close() already record and restore it; the component's job is only to guarantee every close routes through close().

TWO GAPS FOUND AFTER THE AGENT'S HAND-OFF, both worth recording:

1. The suite was registered in NO xtask lane. It compiled, never ran, and the evidence it existed to produce was structurally unobtainable. Registered in e836460 as test-modal-close-proposal. This was the third such gap in one session.

2. On its first ever execution the suite FAILED: in_content_dialog_form_proposes_its_own_cause read cause "none". The component was right; the demo fixture was wrong, and instructively so. daisyUI's documented close idiom is a raw <button> inside a method="dialog" form, which submits by DEFAULT - but this library's Button defaults to type="button" (ldui-9vs). The identical markup built from Button submits nothing, the dialog never closes, and no proposal is emitted. The failure is completely silent. Fixed with ButtonType::Submit and documented in the fixture, because any consumer copying daisyUI's pattern hits it.

title: Add opinionated selectable summary-card group for diagnostic check selectors
description: Problem: Office Data Quality and similar diagnostic pages need a compact grid of selectable count cards. LDUI currently exposes Pressable, Card, and KpiCard but no typed component that owns single-selection semantics, selected styling, status accent, accessible group labeling, count, description, and keyboard/focus behavior. Consumers are therefore tempted to hand-roll button-as-card markup. Required: add a typed SelectableSummaryCard plus a group model or equivalent opinionated pattern; accept stable id/value, reactive label/count/description, semantic status including clean/warning/error/unavailable, controlled selected value, and on_select callback; render native button semantics with aria-pressed or the appropriate single-selection role; own the compact responsive card geometry, selected border/ring, focus-visible treatment, forced-colors treatment, and localization-ready copy slots. The component must not become a page generator and must not embed domain check names. Acceptance: a consumer can render fourteen compact diagnostic cards with zero and unavailable states, control selection atomically, and use no local card/Pressable styling; keyboard and pointer selection update the controlled value; selected state is visually and semantically exposed; visual-quality source/style/layout/reactivity evidence covers default, selected, clean, warning, error, unavailable, narrow, and forced-colors states. Office reference: op-dlfua.7.48.
close_reason:
Implemented in 4ebdd23, suite registered in c82aea4. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (c948eab): 12 lanes, 140 checks, zero failures. Native gate 14/14. Its own lane, selectable_summary_smoke, passes 11/11 on its first execution.

SelectableSummaryGroup / SelectableSummaryCard with typed items (stable id, reactive label/count/description, semantic status, disabled), controlled selected value and an on_select callback. Typed inputs rather than slots, following ldui-9d0q's reasoning: the defects this pattern exists to prevent live inside slot content where nothing can check them.

ACCESSIBILITY ENCODING, chosen deliberately: role="radiogroup"/radio rather than aria-pressed. Fourteen toggle buttons would mean fourteen tab stops in front of the table and could never state "exactly one selected". The FULL contract is implemented rather than half of it - one roving tab stop (the selected card, else the first selectable), arrows in both axes wrapping and both moving focus AND selecting, Home/End to first/last selectable, native button activation for Space/Enter (not intercepted, which would double-fire), disabled cards skipped everywhere. Half a radiogroup would have been worse than a correct set of toggle buttons.

UNAVAILABLE IS NOT ZERO: count is Option<u64> with two constructors, so a card that could not be measured reads "Not measured" with its own accessible name and data attribute, rather than "0". A card reading 0 when it means "we could not measure this" is a lie a consumer would ship unknowingly.

Matched KpiCard rather than inventing a second card grammar: the same always-laid-out left accent edge defaulting to the house blue with forced-colors:bg-[CanvasText], the same reserved two-line label box, and a container-query grid - with a test that REJECTS viewport breakpoints, which is what stops ldui-tnyq's defect returning through a second card family.

37 new native tests. Its suite was unregistered at hand-off (xtask was outside the agent's scope) and it said so; registered as test-selectable-summary.

title: Add opinionated controlled date filter to EntityTable
description: The Office Awaiting Assignment satellite needs its legacy Arrived on or before cutoff inside the opinionated EntityTable filter row. EntityColumnFilter currently provides controlled text and select filters only, forcing the consumer either to accept a text-only YYYY-MM-DD field or hand-roll a custom date control. Add a framework-owned controlled date filter with the same stable control ID, header/responsive placement, active-state, clear, localization, and proposal-only ownership rules as text and select. This is a shared LDUI feature; Office must not implement a private replacement.
acceptance_criteria: EntityColumnFilter exposes a documented controlled date constructor backed by the shared Input date styling; it renders correctly in header and responsive placements without duplicate IDs; its value is caller-owned and on_change only proposes updates; active filter summary and clear behavior work; localized label support is reactive; tests cover placement, proposal/restore semantics, active state, and clearing; the Office Awaiting page can replace its temporary YYYY-MM-DD text filter without page-local control markup.
close_reason:
Implemented in 4a95b04. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (c948eab): 12 lanes, 140 checks, zero failures. Native gate 14/14.

EntityColumnFilter::date(...) with an EntityDateFilterProposal carrying the complete resulting value plus a typed Edited/Cleared cause and a scope stamp - the same controlled idiom as ldui-nz6d rather than a third convention. The control restores the accepted value after every proposal, so it never diverges optimistically.

IT NEVER COMPARES RENDERED TEXT. EntityDate is a timezone-free civil date and the caller supplies Option<EntityDate> per row through its own accessor, because collapsing a timestamp to a calendar day is the consumer's timezone policy and not something a table component can decide for them. Transport is machine YYYY-MM-DD; parsing is strict (exact length, real calendar day including leap years).

Range ends are INCLUSIVE, stated in the type (EntityDateBound::Inclusive), in the doc table and in a test - not left for a consumer to discover.

THE CASE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN SILENT: an unparseable value. The browser BLANKS an invalid date input, so clearing the filter on bad input would look exactly like "no filter" while actually hiding every row. Instead it becomes an explicit Invalid state that matches nothing, keeps the control ACTIVE so it can be cleared, and exposes aria-invalid plus a localized hint. An inverted range is Impossible and reportable; an unbounded filter matches everything including undated rows, while a half-open one excludes them - each decided rather than emergent.

Composes by ANDing with free-text search and column filters, and under ldui-iyfa's grouping it is an ordinary child-row filter, so an emptied group loses its heading - including when emptied because its rows are undated. The control carries data-entity-filter-kind="date", added to the text and select filters too, because positional queries silently describe a different element when layout changes.

title: ServerDataTable: controlled checkbox multi-selection for a server slice
description:
## Consumer proof

The Office Conversations workspace is a cursor-backed server dataset. Its established workflow selects one or more visible conversation rows, then assigns all selected ticket IDs through one caller-owned mutation. `ServerDataTable` currently exposes only `ServerTableSelection::controlled(Signal<Option<String>>, Callback<Option<String>>)` and deliberately ignores Ctrl/Shift gestures. Replacing it with client-paged `EntityTable` would lie about query ownership; rendering caller checkboxes as ordinary cells would lose header selection, row semantics, focus recovery, and atomic accepted state.

## Required opinionated capability

- Add an opt-in controlled checkbox multi-selection model for `ServerDataTable`, keyed by the existing required `row_key`.
- Accepted truth must be caller-owned (`Signal` of stable keys); user interaction emits a proposal without optimistic divergence.
- Render a leading checkbox column with a select-current-slice header checkbox. Header state is checked only when every selectable displayed key is accepted and indeterminate when some are accepted.
- A new server page/query/dataset must not silently relabel accepted keys. Provide an explicit dataset/scope identity or a documented callback contract so the caller can clear/reconcile selection atomically.
- Disabled/non-selectable rows need a caller-supplied reason exposed to pointer and keyboard users.
- Preserve existing single-selection behavior and source compatibility when the new option is absent. Multi-selection must not alter cursor, sorting, filtering, or presentation preferences.
- Emit stable `aria-selected`, labelled checkbox names, keyboard Space behavior, and deterministic focus recovery after an accepted row disappears.
- Expose the selected-key set/proposal independently from row activation/inspection.

## Acceptance criteria

- A controlled example demonstrates 0/partial/all current-slice selection, parent rejection of a proposal, page replacement, filtered replacement, and selected-row removal.
- Header and row checkbox semantics are correct for mouse and keyboard, including indeterminate state.
- Selection never implies unseen server rows are selected; copy and APIs name the current displayed slice.
- Existing `ServerTableSelection` single-selection callers compile and render unchanged.
- Browser coverage proves focus recovery and no stale key relabelling across a cursor transition.
close_reason:
Implemented in 35fa1b2. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (59d765b): reactivity 52/52, layout 9/9, style 7/7, admin-workbench 8/8, server-column-tools 2/2, entity-table 15/15, each on a freshly published dist for its own target; native gate 14/14.

ServerDataTable gains opt-in controlled checkbox multi-selection keyed by the existing row_key: ServerTableMultiSelection::controlled(Signal<BTreeSet<String>>, Callback<ServerTableSelectionProposal>). Accepted truth stays caller-owned; interaction emits a proposal carrying the COMPLETE replacement set plus a typed cause and a scope stamp, never per-row deltas. Both checkboxes re-assert accepted truth onto the DOM before emitting, so a rejected proposal leaves no optimistic divergence.

THE SEMANTICS THAT MATTER FOR A SERVER TABLE. It only ever holds one page, so the header checkbox means the SELECTABLE ROWS ON THIS PAGE and nothing else: All / Partial / None / NoSelectableRows. Accepted keys outside the page have ZERO effect on it - they never force Partial and never stop a full page reading All. They are surfaced instead in an always-mounted role="status" line ("N selected rows are not on this page") plus a data attribute. That is the honest answer: the alternative would let a header checkbox make a claim about rows the client has never seen, which is the same hazard that shaped ServerTableDisplayedSlice in ldui-9j16.

Off-page keys survive by construction: proposals clone the accepted set and only add or remove the slice's own keys. indeterminate is written as a DOM PROPERTY, not an attribute. Incompatible configuration (selection + multi_selection, or either without row_key) short-circuits to the existing fail-closed role="alert" panel rather than resolving to one model.

I separately verified the risk its own report flagged: the control column is not a Column, and a leading cell that the colgroup does not know about is exactly the desync behind ldui-ibjk. It mints a leading <col> track, so the track count matches the rendered cells.

22 new native tests. NOTE a deliberate divergence from its EntityTable sibling: that one PANICS on incompatible config to match its own file's idiom, where this renders an alert. Recorded on ldui-nz6d.

title: RecordHeader: add opinionated identity, status, and quick-action row
description:
## Problem

Record-detail consumers need a compact, consistent identity header but the opinionated layer only supplies a generic `PageHeader`. Office Account and No-Hire Detail currently rebuild incompatible layouts or omit key affordances. Their established layout needs avatar, primary identity, secondary record metadata/link, status, and glyph quick actions in one responsive row.

This should be a typed composition pattern, not a domain-specific record-page generator.

## Required design

- Add an opinionated `RecordHeader` pattern with slots/typed inputs for:
  - avatar/persona;
  - primary title;
  - one or more compact metadata items (including optional link semantics);
  - primary status badge;
  - optional secondary badges;
  - ordered glyph quick actions with accessible labels and hover-card/tooltips.
- Keep navigation/back and page-level title ownership separate; the pattern is the record identity row below them.
- Support controlled loading, retained-data, and unavailable presentation without replacing the whole record page.
- Quick actions must expose disabled-with-reason, pending, and keyed feedback states; domain callbacks remain consumer-owned.
- Preserve compact one-row desktop presentation and define predictable wrapping on narrower supported widths.
- Allow the status/actions edge to remain right-aligned while long identity text truncates safely.
- Do not own tabs or fetch data; consumers compose the existing controlled Tabs pattern immediately below.

## Acceptance criteria

- Stories cover Account-style metadata and No-Hire-style metadata, with and without avatar, links, badges, and 2–4 icon actions.
- Every glyph-only action has an accessible name, hover/focus help, disabled reason, and visible focus state.
- Long names/matter labels do not overlap status/actions at supported desktop widths.
- Loading/retained/error states keep identity labeling truthful.
- Documentation demonstrates composition with PageHeader above and controlled Tabs below, without duplicating domain state.
close_reason:
Implemented in 57de775. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (59d765b): reactivity 52/52, layout 9/9, style 7/7, admin-workbench 8/8, server-column-tools 2/2, entity-table 15/15, each on a freshly published dist for its own target; native gate 14/14.

RecordHeader is a typed composition pattern, not a record-page generator: avatar/persona, primary title, compact metadata items with optional link semantics, a primary status badge and glyph quick actions in one responsive row.

TYPED INPUTS RATHER THAN SLOTS, deliberately. Every defect this bead names lives INSIDE slot content, where it cannot be checked. Typed builders make them unrepresentable instead: an action cannot exist without a label, a status cannot exist without a visible word, and disabled(reason) takes the reason as its only argument. It also gives the accessible-name construction a pure function to unit-test.

STATUS IS NOT COLOUR-ONLY, across three independent channels: a required always-visible label, a distinct glyph per semantic tone, and colour third and removable, plus an sr-only "Status:" role prefix. There is a test that each glyph actually resolves in the sprite, because an unknown Lucide name degrades silently to blank rather than erroring.

GLYPH-ONLY ACTIONS get their name from one function used verbatim for BOTH aria-label and the tooltip, so the two channels cannot drift, with state qualifiers appended from the Texts struct. Disabled uses aria-disabled rather than native disabled or btn-disabled, either of which would make the reason unreachable.

Its author also widened SectionHeading::text_class to pub(crate) so the two patterns share one type-ramp mapping rather than deriving a second that could drift - outside the file scope I set, disclosed in the report, reviewed and accepted.

35 new native tests; the new demo page has now been through style, layout and the axe-carrying reactivity lane, which was the open item at hand-off.

title: EntityTable: add accessible controlled row groups
description:
## Problem

Opinionated `EntityTable` has no typed row-group/section model. Consumers with repeated child facts must either repeat the group identity in every row or abandon the opinionated table and render many local tables. Office Coordinator Activity demonstrates the gap: 459 activity rows repeat the coordinator name, while the established workflow groups Task / Goal / Actual rows beneath one coordinator heading.

## Required design

- Add optional controlled grouping by stable group key, independent of display label.
- Render an accessible full-width group header/section row with caller-provided label and optional compact metadata/actions.
- Keep one global column header and integrated filter row; do not require a separate table instance per group.
- Define sorting and filtering explicitly: filters apply to child rows, empty groups disappear, group order is stable/caller-controlled, and row sorting occurs within groups unless an explicit group sort is selected.
- Define pagination without lying about counts. Page summaries count data rows; group headers are presentation rows and must not inflate totals. Avoid an orphan group heading as the final visible row.
- Preserve stable row keys, keyboard traversal, row actions, column preferences, export, and compact rendering.
- Allow groups to be collapsed only as an optional controlled feature; the default must expose all filtered rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- A story renders at least three groups with repeated Task / Goal / Actual rows under one global header/filter row.
- Screen-reader structure announces each group and its child rows without repeating the group label as a data cell in every row.
- Filtering removes empty groups; sorting and paging remain deterministic and totals count only actual records.
- Keyboard focus survives group collapse/expansion and filtered row removal.
- CSV export includes the group identity as a column even when the visual table suppresses the repeated cell.
- Documentation shows stable IDs and controlled group state; consumers need no DOM post-processing or local table fork.
close_reason:
Implemented in 9b113f8, with a focus defect found and fixed in 59d765b. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree: entity-table 15/15 (including entity_table_row_groups_are_accessible_and_never_inflate_counts), reactivity 52/52, layout 9/9, style 7/7; native gate 14/14.

EntityRowGrouping::controlled(group_of, groups) with optional order, collapsibility, actions and texts. Key and label are private behind accessors: the KEY alone drives partition, rank, collapse state and the exported identity, while the label reaches only the heading and the export column. Two groups sharing a label stay distinct, and relabelling yields a byte-identical order - both pinned by tests.

ACCESSIBILITY, which is where grouped tables usually break. One <tbody> per section, which already carries role="rowgroup", so the boundary is structural rather than ARIA-invented, opened by a spanning <th id scope="colgroup">. That choice does the real work: HTML's own header-association algorithm then attributes every child cell to its group automatically - no headers attribute, no hidden per-row label, and crucially no repeated data cell, which was the defect being fixed. aria-labelledby on the tbody is a second, independent mechanism. Chosen over one-table-per-group because it preserves exactly one thead and one filter row, which is what the bead exists to protect.

INTERACTION WITH ldui-nz6d, decided rather than left implicit: heading rows carry no row key so they cannot enter EntityTableDisplayedPage, and there is deliberately NO per-group select-all, because a group spans pages and a collapsed one paints nothing - such a control would name keys the table is not painting. Collapsing keeps selected keys accepted and counts them off-page.

COLSPAN comes from one body_colspan signal over the current visible column count plus the selection cell, shared with the empty-state row - the ldui-ibjk lesson, where a cell the colgroup did not know about desynced the grid.

Filters apply to child rows and an emptied group loses its heading; rows sort within groups; paging counts data rows only; orphan headings are unrepresentable; collapse is a filter so every count stays truthful. Sorting, grouping and collapse now resolve into ONE displayed order that body, summary, pager, selection, focus and projection all read.

⚠️ A REAL DEFECT THE BROWSER LANE CAUGHT that 2786 native tests did not: focus was lost on collapse. The heading takes a plain collapsed bool by value, so toggling REPLACES the button rather than mutating it, and the browser dropped focus to <body> - throwing a keyboard user to the top of the document mid-task. Same shape as ldui-9j16's column-move case and fixed the same way in 59d765b: re-query by the stable group key on the next animation frame once the new button exists, keyed by group so focus returns to the SAME toggle rather than somewhere merely plausible. This is exactly why the coverage had to be executed rather than compiled.

27 new native tests (2786 total).

title: EntityTable: make auto-fit page size truthful and controlled
description:
## Problem

`EntityTable` can render an auto-fitted number of rows while its rows-per-page control and pager describe a different page size. The Office Setup comparison showed the control set to 25 while the work-type table rendered five rows and offered four pages; the case-type table rendered seven rows and offered two pages. This gives users two conflicting pagination models and prevents a consumer from explaining or controlling the visible table height.

This is a shared opinionated-component defect, not something each Office satellite should patch with local pagination markup.

## Required design

- Give auto-fit pagination one typed source of truth shared by the rendered body, result summary, rows-per-page control, and pager.
- If auto-fit is active, expose it explicitly (for example `Auto (5)`) and report the effective page size through controlled state/callbacks.
- If a numeric size such as 25 is selected, render up to 25 rows when the dataset has enough rows and available-height policy allows it; do not silently paginate at five while labeling the selection 25.
- Keep the existing bottom-row placement: rows-per-page before `Showing x-y of z`, then the pager.
- Preserve keyboard and screen-reader semantics when the effective size changes after resize.
- Consumers must not need DOM measurement or duplicate pagination state.

## Acceptance criteria

- A browser story with 17 rows cannot show `25` while rendering five rows and advertising four pages.
- Auto-fit and explicit numeric modes each have a single controlled state reflected identically in the body, footer summary, and pager.
- Resizing across at least two desktop heights updates effective auto-fit state atomically without losing the current row unnecessarily.
- Existing sorting, filtering, stable-row-key, and column-preference behavior remains intact.
- Component documentation shows the controlled API and how a satellite persists only explicit user preferences, not a transient measured row count.
close_reason:
Implemented in dfac787. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (59d765b): reactivity 52/52, layout 9/9, style 7/7, admin-workbench 8/8, server-column-tools 2/2, entity-table 15/15, each on a freshly published dist for its own target; native gate 14/14.

The defect was two pagination models disagreeing: the control read 25 while the table rendered five rows and offered four pages. Fixed at the TYPE level rather than the display level. EntityPageSize pairs a mode with the row count actually rendered, keeps its fields private, and is produced only by a total resolution function. Three states are now unrepresentable, the important one being a row count with no mode - the anonymous usize "effective page size" is exactly what let the control label a page it was not describing. There is one Memo<EntityPageSize> and no second page-size signal, so body, summary, control and pager cannot disagree.

Auto-fit is exposed explicitly: the option's VALUE is the stable string "auto" so a resize never moves the selection, while its LABEL carries the fitted count through a new localizable text (Auto (5)). The effective size reaches the caller via on_page_size_resolved and is persisted as page_size_mode alongside page_size in one normalized replacement. Choosing 25 renders 25.

auto_page.rs was neither needed nor touched: the measurement math was already correct and the defect was purely in combining and presenting it. Pinned by a native test deriving all four consumers from one resolution, plus a browser story asserting seventeen rows cannot show twenty-five while rendering five.

title: EntityTable: controlled checkbox multi-selection for bulk page actions
description: The Office Conversations workspace requires the original bulk-assignment grammar while adopting the opinionated EntityTable: a leading checkbox column, per-row controlled selection, and a header checkbox that selects or clears the currently displayed page. EntityTableSelection is explicitly single-select today. Add a typed controlled multi-selection model rather than forcing consumers to hand-render checkbox columns or fall back to low-level tables.
acceptance_criteria: EntityTable accepts a controlled set of stable row keys plus one atomic selection-change callback. When supplied, it renders an accessible leading checkbox column and a header checkbox with checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states. Header selection affects only rows currently displayed after filtering, sorting, and paging; stable selected keys outside the current page are preserved. Row removal and dataset changes cannot alias selection to another key. Single-selection behavior remains backward compatible and configuration rejects combining incompatible selection modes. Add focused keyboard and render coverage.
close_reason:
Implemented in 679e0ce. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (59d765b): reactivity 52/52, layout 9/9, style 7/7, admin-workbench 8/8, server-column-tools 2/2, entity-table 15/15; native gate 14/14.

EntityTableMultiSelection::controlled(Signal<BTreeSet<String>>, Callback<EntityTableSelectionProposal>). One gesture - one row or twenty-five - emits exactly one proposal carrying the COMPLETE key set plus a typed cause and scope stamp, never per-row deltas the caller must reassemble.

The header governs EntityTableDisplayedPage: the keys the table is painting right now, after filtering, sorting and paging - stated in the type rather than in prose. Partial/indeterminate means some but not all of the CURRENTLY DISPLAYED rows; off-page keys can never move it off None nor turn it checked, and their count goes to a role="status" region. Displayed rows are read from the same page_row_keys signal the tbody iterates, itself derived from ldui-5p06's single page-size Memo - not recomputed, which is the bug class 5p06 had just eliminated.

TWO DETAILS THAT USUALLY GET MISSED. indeterminate is set as a DOM property AND re-asserted in on:change, because the browser clears the flag on click - setting it once would silently degrade to a plain checkbox after the first interaction; a test asserts attr:indeterminate appears nowhere. And off-page survival is by CONSTRUCTION rather than by a preservation step: proposals are pure set operations over stable keys and no index exists anywhere, so removal, dataset replacement or sorting can only stop a key being rendered, never re-point it at a different row.

46 new native tests.

⚠️ DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM ITS SERVER SIBLING, recorded so it is a decision rather than an accident: incompatible selection config PANICS here, matching resolve_preference_ownership's existing idiom in the same file, whereas ldui-px06 renders a fail-closed role="alert" panel. Both fail closed, but a panic in CSR wasm kills the app while the alert does not. Consistent within each file, inconsistent between the two tables for the same class of consumer error. Worth unifying on the alert form if it ever bites.

title: KpiStrip: render opinionated colored left accent edge including blue default
description: KpiStrip currently reserves a top accent stripe and deliberately leaves Neutral uncolored. The approved Office stat-card grammar uses independent cards with a colored left edge; ordinary/default cards use the primary blue edge, while semantic states may use their own status color. Make the edge framework-owned so consumers do not hand-style KpiCard containers.
acceptance_criteria: Every default or Neutral KpiCard has a visible primary-blue left accent edge at desktop widths. Info, Success, Warning, and Error cards use the corresponding semantic edge color without changing card geometry. The accent is on the left, not across the top. Mixed-status cards retain aligned content. Forced-colors mode keeps a structural edge. Focused render tests cover Neutral and one semantic state.
close_reason:
Delivered across c750969 (edge + blue default) and 605d85d (forced colors + coverage), VERIFIED IN A BROWSER at 1440.

ACCEPTANCE, item by item:

- Left edge, not a top stripe: the card root is now a flex row with the bar as a self-stretch first child. Measured 3px wide by 132px tall on a 134px card, sitting 1px in from the card's own edge (that 1px is the card border, not padding).
- Every default/Neutral card has a visible primary-blue edge: measured rgb(0, 69, 120) = #004578. Neutral previously returned "" - it now paints the default rather than nothing, which is the substantive half of this bead. An accent that appeared only on exceptional cards would make the EDGE the signal; a universal edge makes the COLOUR the signal, which is what lets one warning card read against seven ordinary ones.
- Semantic states override without changing geometry: info/success/warning cards paint their own colours at identical bar width, asserted directly.
- Mixed-status cards retain aligned content: the bar is laid out unconditionally, so every card's body starts at the same x. This is the horizontal counterpart of ldui-tbaw's finding, where a conditionally-rendered TOP stripe put values in one row at 567 and 570.
- Forced colors keeps a structural edge: forced-colors overrides author background-color with system colours, so a bg-*-only bar disappears outright. It now paints CanvasText. The colour distinction between statuses is deliberately NOT preserved there, because forced-colors exists to replace author colour with the user's palette.
- Focused render tests: kpi_cards_carry_a_left_accent_edge_blue_by_default_ldui_kmpa covers Neutral and one semantic state.

COLOUR SOURCE: the generic ui_tokens::color::STATUS_BLUE_FG, emitted through cargo xtask gen-tokens as --color-status-blue. Deliberately NOT color::table::HEADER - identical #004578 today, but that module exists so the table role can drift independently, and a card accent is not a table role. The token is generated rather than hand-written because styles/tokens.css is generated and the gate's first step fails on drift.

TEST STRENGTH, stated honestly: the check asserts computed geometry and paint rather than class names, so it discriminates the failure modes that matter - a top stripe would report a bar as wide as the card and ~131px of height shortfall against a 4px allowance, and a missing default would fail the explicit rgb(0, 69, 120) assertion. I did not run a separate break-test reverting the implementation; the discrimination is argued from the measured numbers rather than demonstrated by experiment.

EVIDENCE: admin_workbench_smoke 8/8 including the new check, layout_audit_smoke 9/9, style_audit_smoke 7/7, native gate 14/14.

title: EntityTable: place rows-per-page control in the footer before row range
description: The opinionated EntityTable currently hard-codes the Rows per page label/select in the top utility toolbar. Coordinator requires the established desktop table grammar: toolbar actions and column chooser above the table; pagination metadata below the table, ordered Rows per page, Showing start-end of total, then page navigation. Implement this in the shared component rather than consumer markup. Preserve controlled preferences, stable control id/name, viewport-fit behavior, localization, and keyboard accessibility.
acceptance_criteria: At desktop width the Rows per page label/select renders in the footer row immediately before the row-range text. It no longer renders in the top toolbar. Row-range and Previous/page/Next controls remain present and aligned. Existing page-size callback, controlled preference behavior, id/name, and localized text remain unchanged. Add focused render coverage for order and absence from toolbar.
close_reason:
Implemented in d1e55ef. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (59d765b): reactivity 52/52, layout 9/9, style 7/7, admin-workbench 8/8, server-column-tools 2/2, entity-table 15/15, each on a freshly published dist for its own target; native gate 14/14.

Rows per page now renders in the footer immediately before the row-range text, and no longer in the top toolbar; the toolbar holds toolbar_actions plus the column chooser. Row-range and Previous/page/Next remain present and aligned. The page-size id/name derivation, controlled-preference behaviour and localized text were moved verbatim rather than reimplemented, and the label still physically wraps the Select, so the label/select association and keyboard access survive by construction.

⚠️ THIS BEAD BROKE THREE BROWSER TESTS AND ITS OWN REPORT DID NOT KNOW. The implementation reported that the existing tests "continue to hold" because they target '[data-entity-table] label select'. That was true natively and FALSE in a browser: the native tests do not render the filter row, and the new browser coverage was compile-only, so nothing executed it. Moving the control made the status filter the first label-select in the table, and that query kept working while silently returning the WRONG ELEMENT - the failure surfaced as pageSizeSelectId == "entity-status-filter". A second query, '[data-entity-table] > div:last-child > span' for the row range, started returning null once the footer regrouped.

Fixed in 59d765b by giving both controls stable hooks (data-entity-page-size-control, data-entity-row-range) and repointing the five call sites, so identity no longer depends on document order. The general lesson is worth keeping: a positional DOM query does not fail when the layout changes, it starts describing something else.

title: Allow normal KpiCard labels to wrap to two lines without ellipsis
description: Office Coordinator renders the adopted eight-card KpiStrip at 1680px. Ordinary labels including No-Hire Conversions, Payments Collected, Customer Success Pts, Conversations Open, and Responses Pending are visibly ellipsized because KpiCard hardcodes single-line truncate on the label. The legacy stat cards wrap these ordinary labels across at most two lines, preserving meaning while keeping equal card geometry.
design: Replace the single-line truncation policy with a bounded two-line label treatment owned by KpiCard. Preserve the full accessible label, equal card heights, help-control alignment, responsive grid behavior, and compact-mode density. Extremely long caller copy may clamp after two lines, but normal Office KPI labels must remain fully visible.
acceptance_criteria: At an eight-card 1680px KpiStrip, each named Office-length label renders without an ellipsis and uses no more than two lines; cards remain equal height and values/descriptions retain their alignment; compact and mobile layouts remain usable; the accessible name contains the complete label; component and browser evidence cover representative short, two-line, and overlong labels.
close_reason:
Implemented in 6fc60b4 and completed in 0235660, and VERIFIED IN A BROWSER at the bead's own 1680px eight-card geometry.

WHAT SHIPPED: KpiCard's label is now line-clamp-2 with break-words instead of truncate, and carries min-h-8 UNCONDITIONALLY. The unconditional part is the load-bearing half: 32px is exactly two line boxes (--text-small is 11px with line-height calc(16/11), so a line box is 16px), so a one-line label and a two-line label leave identically sized boxes. Equal card height and value alignment are therefore a structural reservation rather than something that happens to hold for the current copy. Measured: every card's label box is exactly 32px and every card is 189px tall. No per-card "lines" prop was added - the caller passes text and the pattern owns the treatment. An over-long label still clamps visually, and kpi_card_accessible_name builds aria-label from the raw string, so assistive tech always gets the complete label (pinned by a unit test).

A SECOND, REAL DEFECT THE BROWSER PROOF EXPOSED, fixed in 0235660: values were NOT actually aligned. Measured valueTop was 567 on cards without a status and 570 on cards with one. The status accent strip was rendered only when status != Neutral, so its 3px pushed those bodies down while neutral cards started higher. In a strip that mixes status and neutral cards - which is the normal case, and exactly what the Office Coordinator renders - every value sat 3px off its neighbour. The strip is now always laid out and merely uncoloured when neutral, which is the same reasoning as min-h-8 one level up: equal geometry has to be structural, not a side effect of which cards happen to carry a status. This bead's acceptance explicitly requires values to retain their alignment, so it is in scope; it would not have been found without measuring, because a class-level check would have reported line-clamp-2 present and passed.

ONE ACCEPTANCE ITEM RESOLVED DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN BY ASSERTION: the fixture had been edited to hang a .help() control on "Customer Success Pts", one of the labels this bead names as ordinary. A help control is a flex sibling of the label and costs it 20px (measured 83px -> 63px), and a fit sweep showed that label holds two lines at every width from 70px up and needs three at 63px. So the clip had nothing to do with the wrapping policy under test. Rather than redesign the card to make the assertion pass, the help control moved to a short label and the width interaction is filed as ldui-yhvf with those measurements. All five labels this bead names now render unclipped.

EVIDENCE on the current tree: admin_workbench_smoke 7/7 PASS (including wide_viewport_kpi_labels_wrap_without_ellipsis_and_stay_aligned, which asserts no ellipsis via scrollHeight > clientHeight rather than by inspecting classes, equal card heights, and exact value alignment), style_audit_smoke 7/7, layout_audit_smoke 9/9 - the last two confirming the always-on accent strip did not move any ratcheted count. Native suite green, clippy clean.

title: Keep FilterSidebar toggle clickable when a right-side panel with header actions is collapsed
description: Office Coordinator renders FilterSidebar on the right with an AI model Select and setup action in header_actions. When collapsed to 44px, the opacity-hidden header-actions wrapper retains its full width and the header keeps px-3 padding. In the rendered Office consumer, the toggle center is at x=1472 while the aside begins at x=1612; overflow-hidden clips it and elementFromPoint resolves the underlying Rows-per-page Select. Chrome cannot activate Expand AI Assistant. Found during Office op-dlfua.7.23 exact sealed visual interaction pass.
acceptance_criteria: For SidebarSide::Right and SidebarSide::Left, with and without header_actions, a collapsed 44px FilterSidebar keeps the toggle's complete 28px hit target inside the aside; header actions remain mounted but occupy no collapsed layout width and receive no pointer events; elementFromPoint at the toggle center resolves the toggle; clicking it expands the panel; expanded header layout remains unchanged; component and browser coverage prove the regression.
close_reason:
Fixed in d8e1373 and 0235660, VERIFIED IN A BROWSER, and the coverage was BREAK-TESTED rather than merely observed to pass.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is ours: the header-actions slot added in ldui-bx6n used opacity-0 pointer-events-none on collapse. That hides paint but not layout - the wrapper kept its full intrinsic width via shrink-0. On a right-docked panel the collapsed header's flex-row-reverse line then demanded far more than the 44px rail, and with the title already shrunk to zero there was nothing left to absorb the overflow, so the toggle was pushed past the panel's own edge and clipped by its overflow-hidden. Collapsed state now zeroes the wrapper's real footprint (w-0, mx-0, its own overflow-hidden) so it contributes nothing to the header line.

ACCESSIBILITY: the slot stays MOUNTED deliberately - unmounting it would discard interaction state a consumer holds inside a header control, which is the whole reason the slot exists - but it now also goes inert in addition to aria-hidden, so a visually hidden, non-interactive control is not still reachable by keyboard or screen reader. pointer-events-none alone would have left it tabbable.

BREAK-TEST, because a passing assertion is not evidence it would catch the regression: restoring the pre-fix geometry in the live DOM (shrink-0 and intrinsic width back on the wrapper) produced actionsWidth 128px against an assertion requiring under 1, hitIsButton false, and the toggle escaping the aside - off the LEFT edge on a right-docked panel, which is exactly the shape reported (toggle centre 1472 against a panel starting at 1612). All three assertions fire on the defect. The scaffold was removed afterwards.

The test covers all four acceptance cells - Left and Right, each with and without header_actions - and asserts the real geometry: document.elementFromPoint at the toggle's own bounding-rect centre resolves the toggle, the complete 28px target sits inside the aside, collapsed actions report inert and aria-hidden and about zero width, a real click expands the panel again, and the header_actions Select's value survives the collapse/expand round trip, which is what proves "stays mounted" rather than assuming it.

ONE TEST DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED while verifying: the "expanded layout unchanged" assertion compared raw getBoundingClientRect values across the cycle. Clicking the toggle scrolls it into view, so y moved 405 -> 2503 while x, width and height matched exactly - the assertion was measuring scroll position. It now compares the toggle's offset from its own panel's origin, which is the invariant that actually matters and is scroll-independent.

EVIDENCE: reactivity_smoke filter_sidebar 2/2 PASS, including the pre-existing filter_sidebar_search_accessible_name_covers_every_variant which stayed green. Native suite green, clippy clean, xtask reactivity count pin updated.

title: The ld-text-* type ramp is emitted by components but defined by no stylesheet
description: SectionHeading, KpiStrip and other patterns render class strings ld-text-display / ld-text-title / ld-text-subtitle / ld-text-body / ld-text-small / ld-text-caption. NOTHING DEFINES THEM. Verified 2026-08-31: zero '.ld-text-' rules in styles/tokens.css (which defines only an @theme block), zero in demo/input.css, demo/custom-components.css and demo/output.css, and zero occurrences of 'ld-text-title' in the demo's own BUILT css (demo/dist/output-ffe34e129099e7b5.css). They are not Tailwind utilities, so @source scanning cannot generate them. The demo is therefore rendering the ramp undefined too, which is why this has gone unnoticed. Consumer impact: SectionHeading composes its class as '{level.text_class()} font-semibold tracking-tight text-base-content ...', so a heading gets WEIGHT and COLOUR but no SIZE STEP - with Tailwind preflight resetting heading sizes, an H2 SectionHeading renders at body size. In 4iiz-etl's portal we replaced hand-rolled 'text-lg font-bold' headings with SectionHeading and the headings visibly shrank.
design: Either define the six .ld-text-* classes in styles/tokens.css (an @utility or @layer components block mapping each step to its font-size/line-height, alongside the @theme tokens already there), or stop emitting them and compose the ramp from Tailwind utilities the way font-semibold/tracking-tight already are. The first keeps the ramp a single named contract, which is the point of having it.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the six ld-text-* steps resolves to a real font-size/line-height in a consumer build. The demo demonstrably renders SectionHeading H2/H3/H4 at distinct sizes. A test or CI check fails if a component emits an ld-* class that no stylesheet defines - that is the class of defect this is.
close_reason: Retracted by the reporter: not a defect. The .ld-text-* rules are generated at runtime by UiTokensPreamble (src/tokens/preamble.rs); I had grepped only built CSS, where a runtime-injected sheet correctly never appears.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Confirmed the impact, but the stated cause needs one correction before anyone fixes the wrong thing.

"NOTHING DEFINES THEM" is not quite right. src/tokens/preamble.rs:139 emits a real rule per step - .ld-text-{name} { font-size: var(--ld-text-{name}); line-height: var(--ld-line-{name}); } - and ui_tokens_css() is injected at RUNTIME by the UiTokensPreamble component. The demo mounts it (demo/src/main.rs:13 and demo/src/client_snapshot_test_host.rs:66), so in the demo the ramp does resolve.

Your evidence is nonetheless accurate and the consumer impact is real: the six classes are absent from styles/tokens.css, demo/input.css, demo/custom-components.css and the BUILT stylesheet, because they are injected at runtime rather than generated. So the actual defect is a silent, undocumented dependency: any consumer that uses SectionHeading/KpiStrip WITHOUT also mounting UiTokensPreamble gets weight and colour but no size step, and with preflight resetting heading sizes an H2 renders at body size - precisely the shrink you saw in the 4iiz-etl portal. Nothing warns them, and the demo cannot reveal it because the demo happens to mount the preamble.

That makes your first design option the right one, and for a stronger reason than "single named contract": the ramp should not be reachable only through a component the consumer might not render. styles/tokens.css is generated by cargo xtask gen-tokens from the ui-tokens crate (that is also how the --color-table-* values are kept from drifting, ldui-gp34), so the six steps belong in that generator's output next to the @theme block, from the same source values the preamble uses. Emitting them in both places is fine and keeps runtime-only consumers working, as long as both derive from ui-tokens rather than being written twice.

Worth keeping from your acceptance criteria: the check that fails when a component emits an ld-* class no stylesheet defines. That is the part that would have caught this at source, and it generalises beyond the type ramp to --ld-space-*, --ld-stroke-* and --ld-radius-*, which are emitted the same way.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
RETRACTED BY THE REPORTER — THIS BUG DOES NOT EXIST. My investigation was wrong and I am sorry for the noise.

The `.ld-text-*` classes ARE defined: `src/tokens/preamble.rs` generates one rule per step at RUNTIME —

    .ld-text-{step} { font-size: var(--ld-text-{step}); line-height: var(--ld-line-{step}); }

— emitted by `UiTokensPreamble`, which a consuming app mounts at its root. 4iiz-etl's portal mounts it (shell.rs) and the ramp resolves correctly in the browser.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG, since the method is the reusable part: I grepped for `.ld-text-` in CSS FILES ONLY — styles/tokens.css, demo/input.css, demo/output.css, and the demo's built bundle — found zero in all of them, and treated that as proof. For a runtime-injected stylesheet, zero in built CSS is the EXPECTED reading, not evidence of absence. I never grepped `src/tokens/`, which is where the definition lives. I then generalised from that to "the demo renders the ramp undefined too", which was the same error restated with more confidence.

What actually put me right was a DIFFERENT check: scanning every `ld-*` class ldui emits and finding nine more apparently-undefined ones (`ld-pressable`, `ld-focus-ring`, `ld-elevated`, ...). Nine at once was implausible, and chasing them led to `src/tokens/animations.rs` holding CSS as Rust strings — the same runtime-injection mechanism. A finding that would mean the library is broken for everyone deserves that second look BEFORE it is filed, not after.

The suggestion in the acceptance criteria — a check that fails when a component emits an `ld-*` class no stylesheet defines — would ALSO have to know about the runtime-injected sheets, or it would report exactly the false positives I hit. That may still be worth having, with that caveat, but it is a separate idea and not a bug; please close this as invalid rather than acting on it.

title: Expose semantic icon color on PageQuickActionContent
description: PageQuickActionContent owns the Icon child but exposes only an outer class, so a consumer cannot apply a semantic color to the glyph without page-specific descendant CSS that couples to the internal i element. Coordinator currently needs green Payments and Client Success glyphs while retaining normal button-label color.
acceptance_criteria: Add an optional reactive icon_color or equivalent typed semantic presentation prop that is passed directly to the owned Icon. Default rendering remains source- and render-compatible. Document the semantic-color usage and cover at least success, warning, and default behavior without requiring consumer descendant selectors.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed in 5e1f9d7. PageQuickActionContent now forwards a typed reactive icon_color to its owned Icon; focused tests passed 5/5 and the pre-push gate passed 14/14.

title: Legacy unlayered .fab rule in custom-components.css overrides daisyUI 5 positioning
description:
demo/custom-components.css ships a legacy pre-daisyUI-5 rule:

    .fab { position: relative; ... }

with a header comment claiming the FAB is "not included in daisyUI 5" - which is no longer true; daisyUI 5 ships its own .fab inside @layer utilities.

Because the demo's rule is UNLAYERED author CSS, the Cascade Layers spec gives it unconditional priority over ANY layered rule regardless of specificity or source order. It therefore silently overrides position:fixed for EVERY Fab rendered in the demo, not just one page.

This was found while fixing ldui-0qro: the Help FAB rendered in normal document flow (measured x=668,y=1725, below a workbench occupying y 344..1164) instead of anchored bottom-right. Verified directly with getComputedStyle/offsetParent - the FAB's computed position was `relative`, not `fixed`. It had stayed invisible because the existing FabDemo page never measured placement precisely.

ldui-0qro worked around it at the call site with an inline style:position="fixed" (inline beats any non-!important stylesheet rule), which is correct for that bead's scope but leaves the trap in place for every other Fab caller.

FIX: delete or correct the obsolete .fab rule in demo/custom-components.css so daisyUI 5's own layered .fab applies, then drop the inline workaround in demo/src/demos/admin_workbench.rs. Re-run admin_workbench_smoke (currently 6/6) and the fab demo page to confirm placement still holds. While there, audit custom-components.css for OTHER unlayered rules making the same obsolete "not in daisyUI 5" claim - the same cascade trap would apply to each, and each would be equally invisible until something measured it.
close_reason:
Done, and the residual audit this bead asked for is now complete. I own this repo's changes, so I have confirmed the fix rather than deferring to whoever made it.

PART 1 - the reported rule is gone. Commit 5e1f9d7 removed
    .fab { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; position: relative; }
from demo/custom-components.css and corrected the file header, which had claimed "custom components not included in daisyUI 5: FAB (Floating Action Button) with speed dial" - untrue since daisyUI 5 ships its own .fab. It also removed the inline style:position="fixed" workaround ldui-0qro had added to demo/src/demos/admin_workbench.rs, which is the right follow-through: with the shadowing rule gone, daisyUI's own .fab supplies position:fixed and the override stops being load-bearing.
VERIFIED IN THE TREE: no .fab position rule remains (only the speed-dial child selectors .fab > *:not(:first-child) and the .fab-flower placement), and the built stylesheet carries daisyUI's .fab with position:fixed inside @layer daisyui.l1.l2.l3. admin_workbench_smoke passed 6/6 live afterwards.

PART 2 - audit of the remaining file for the same trap. Every top-level selector in demo/custom-components.css is one of: .collapse-plus, .fab, .hover-3d, .hover-gallery, .indicator-item, .overflow-hidden, .text-rotate. Of those, .hover-3d, .hover-gallery and .text-rotate are genuinely custom (no daisyUI/Tailwind class of that name), and .fab is fixed. The three that DO collide with real daisyUI/Tailwind names are NOT bare redefinitions:
  .collapse-plus:focus:not(.collapse-close) > .collapse-title:after  (and siblings) - overrides only the pseudo-element content
  .indicator-item.indicator-top.indicator-center                      - three-class compound, positions one specific combination
  .overflow-hidden > .drawer > .drawer-side                           - uses the utility only as an ancestor; does not redefine it
Each is a targeted override carrying !important, which is a materially different pattern from the .fab bug: that one was a BARE class redefinition silently changing a fundamental property (position) with nothing to announce it, which is why it stayed invisible until something measured placement precisely. So no second instance of this trap exists in the file.

RESIDUAL MAINTENANCE NOTE, not reopened: those three overrides are unlayered AND !important, so they beat daisyUI unconditionally and will keep doing so even if daisyUI later fixes the quirks they compensate for. Worth revisiting on a daisyUI upgrade rather than now.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Office consumer review on 2026-08-30 confirms this is not demo-only: every satellite now needs the standard bottom-right Help launcher through the shared Fab component. Remove the obsolete unlayered rule so consumers can rely on the documented fixed-position contract without inline or page-specific workarounds.

comments.author: davidcforbes

title: Preserve EntityTable stable column order across reactive localized definitions
description: Office Coordinator reproduces a stable-ID preference corruption when EntityTable column definitions react to EN/ES. Starting from the declared order work_type, client, case_type, status, last_outcome, last_contact, actions, toggling EN to ES to EN causes the persisted column_order to become client, case_type, work_type, status, last_outcome, last_contact, actions. title: Give interactive EntityTable rows an opinionated light-blue hover state
description: EntityTable marks activateable rows with cursor and focus-ring classes but supplies no hover background. Coordinator's legacy interaction uses a light-blue row hover to communicate the mouse focus target. This is table interaction presentation and should be framework-owned instead of repeated in consumer CSS.
acceptance_criteria: Rows with on_row_activate or selection receive a light-blue semantic hover background across all visible cells in wide and compact layouts. Non-interactive rows do not. Selected and semantic-emphasis states remain legible, forced-colors remains usable, and browser coverage verifies hover presentation.
close_reason:
Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. Interactive EntityTable rows (those with on_row_activate or a selection binding) now get a framework-owned light-blue hover background across all visible cells in both the wide and compact layouts, reusing the existing --color-table-filter token rather than a hardcoded hex. Non-interactive rows get nothing.

Layering is handled by OMISSION rather than override: entity_row_hover_class(interactive, selected) emits the hover classes only when interactive AND NOT selected, so a selected row simply never carries them - a :hover rule would otherwise out-specify the selected background regardless of source order. EntityRowEmphasis still sets no background (the ldui-mqb invariant), so Summary/Muted/Attention compose freely, and table-zebra targets td/th rather than tr so it never competes with the row-level class. Commits 5cd25c4 and df293f5.

EVIDENCE: native tests plus interactive_rows_get_the_framework_hover_and_selection_suppresses_it run LIVE on 2026-08-31 = PASS; native suite 2663 green.

TWO FINDINGS FROM THE LIVE RUN, both of which compile-only coverage would have missed entirely:

1. The first live run failed and the cause was the TEST HARNESS, not this feature. chromiumoxide 0.7.0's Browser::new_page unconditionally sends Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled(true), ignoring Viewport::has_touch and independent of set_viewport's mobile:false. With touch emulation forced on, Chromium reports (hover: hover) = false, so EVERY @media (hover:hover)-gated Tailwind hover: utility silently failed to apply - even though the CDP mouse move genuinely did put the element into :hover. Worked around with a force_desktop_hover_media helper in tests/common/mod.rs. This would have defeated any future hover-gated browser assertion in this repo, not just this one.

2. Fixing the harness then exposed a REAL accessibility defect in this feature: the fixed light-blue background had no paired fixed foreground, so under the environment's default dark theme (near-white base-content) hovered text dropped to roughly 1:1 contrast. Axe caught it. Fixed by pairing hover:text-table-filter-content with hover:bg-table-filter.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Source verification 2026-08-30: opinionated hover landed on main in 5cd25c4. Interactive unselected EntityTable rows use the semantic table-filter light-blue token; selected/non-interactive controls and forced-colors coverage are present.
