title: Admin-workbench reference omits the Help floating action button
description:
Consumer report (4iiz-office, 2026-08-30): the opinionated admin-workbench composition reference is missing the blue Help floating action button anchored bottom-right that the Coordinator production UI carries. The reference currently composes AppShellTopBar, a borderless PageHeader with PageQuickActions, KpiStrip, EntityTable with aligned filters and a right-docked FilterSidebar (ldui-ynmd.3), but renders no Fab: grep of demo/src/demos/admin_workbench.rs finds no Fab usage at all, only a KPI card's help TEXT.

The point of that reference is that the consumer's regression came from composing valid primitives into the WRONG HIERARCHY, so an omitted element in the reference is exactly the kind of gap it exists to prevent - a consumer comparing against it will conclude the help affordance is not part of the approved composition.

LDUI already ships the primitive: src/components/fab/ (Fab, FabMainAction, FabClose). REUSE it - do not add a second floating-button component and do not introduce an Office-specific Help route, copy or handler; activation stays caller-owned via a callback, as with the reference's other actions.

ACCEPTANCE: the workbench reference renders a Help floating action button anchored bottom-right at both the wide desktop and compact mobile viewports, built from the existing Fab; it has an accessible name and visible focus treatment; it does not overlap or obscure the table's pagination/footer or the right assistant panel, and does not introduce horizontal overflow at compact width; collapsing/expanding the assistant does not strand or hide it; the browser proof asserts its presence, placement and accessible name at both viewports.
close_reason:
Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. The admin-workbench composition reference now renders the blue Help floating action button anchored bottom-right, built by REUSING the existing src/components/fab/ primitive (Fab + Button) with no change to the component and with activation caller-owned via a callback - no Office route, copy or handler was added. Commits 99697bf (feature) and c02cf04 (placement fix).

EVIDENCE: tests/admin_workbench_smoke.rs run LIVE on 2026-08-31 = 6/6 PASS, asserting presence, bottom-right placement and accessible name at BOTH the wide desktop and compact mobile viewports; style_audit_smoke 7/7 PASS on the same tree, so the new markup pushed no ratcheted ceiling; native suite 2650 green.

THE FIRST LIVE RUN CAUGHT A REAL BREAKAGE that compile-only coverage could never have shown: the FAB measured at x=668, y=1725 while the workbench occupied x 280..1416, y 344..1164 - it was rendering in normal document flow BELOW everything, so position:fixed was not in effect at all.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is repo-wide rather than local: demo/custom-components.css ships a LEGACY pre-daisyUI-5 rule, .fab { position: relative; ... }, whose own header comment claims the FAB is "not included in daisyUI 5" - no longer true. That rule is UNLAYERED author CSS, and per the Cascade Layers spec unlayered author styles beat any layered rule unconditionally, regardless of specificity or source order; daisyUI 5 ships its own .fab inside @layer utilities. So the legacy rule silently overrode position:fixed for EVERY Fab in the demo, and stayed invisible only because the existing FabDemo page never measured placement precisely. Verified directly with getComputedStyle and offsetParent rather than inferred. The containment approach was NOT at fault: the content column did correctly become the FAB's containing block.

Fixed at the call site with an inline style:position="fixed" (an inline style beats any non-!important stylesheet rule unconditionally), keeping the change inside this bead's file scope. The underlying legacy .fab rule is filed separately as a follow-up.

title: Give ServerDataTable opinionated column tools and slice-safe export projection
description: EntityTable exposes a compact gear column chooser, caller toolbar actions, stable preference ownership, and an atomic displayed projection for CSV. ServerDataTable exposes none of those extension points. Office Conversations is honestly cursor-paged and can now use the aligned server filter row, but it cannot provide the same approved table tools without reimplementing framework presentation or pretending the loaded slice is the complete result set.
design: Add source-compatible optional ServerDataTable presentation tools: the existing compact gear trigger and left/in-viewport chooser behavior, stable column visibility/order/width preferences, and a toolbar-actions slot adjacent to the chooser. Add a server-specific atomic display projection whose type and documentation explicitly identify it as the current accepted server slice; never label it AllFiltered and never fetch or synthesize unseen rows. Reuse the EntityTable preference and chooser machinery where types genuinely match, but keep server query ownership, filtering, sorting, cursor tokens, and export authorization caller-owned.
acceptance_criteria: A ServerDataTable caller can opt into an accessible compact gear chooser that remains inside the viewport, hide/reorder optional columns while required columns remain visible, persist presentation preferences under a stable caller namespace, place an Export action adjacent to the gear, and receive one atomic projection of only the accepted displayed server slice. Retained loading/failure keeps the old projection and labels. The projection cannot be mistaken for the complete server result set, no client-side query behavior is introduced, existing callers remain source-compatible, and focused wide/compact rendering demonstrates the menu and toolbar placement.
close_reason:
Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. ServerDataTable gained source-compatible optional presentation tools: the compact gear chooser with in-viewport placement, stable column visibility/order preferences under a caller namespace, and a toolbar-actions slot adjacent to the chooser - reusing EntityTable's chooser and preference machinery rather than reimplementing it (src/components/entity_table/** was not modified). Server query ownership, filtering, sorting, cursor tokens and export authorization remain caller-owned; no client-side query behaviour was introduced.
THE EXPORT SAFETY POINT, which was the real risk: a server table only ever holds one page, so a projection named or documented like EntityTable's complete-snapshot export would let a consumer ship a CSV that silently contains one page while presenting it as the whole filtered set.  is therefore a DISTINCT type with NO AllFiltered scope at all, documented as only ever holding the current accepted server page, and its sole constructor is a pure function of effective_columns/rows - so no code path can fetch or synthesize unseen rows. The mistake is unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.
Commits 9cca892 (feature), 80a07b0 (rustfmt the suite, which had been committed unformatted and would have failed the gate's fmt-check), c8bb775 (focus fix + style).
EVIDENCE: 13 native tests, and tests/server_table_column_tools_smoke.rs run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS, asserting the chooser opens inside the viewport, the required column is never offered as a toggle, hiding a column removes its header, reordering works, Escape closes AND returns focus to the trigger, and the projection matches the displayed slice. Its lane is wired into xtask full_steps() as test-server-table-column-tools.
NOTE the first live run failed on focus return, with a non-obvious root cause: moving a column to an end of the order reactively DISABLES that same move button, the browser blurs the focused element on disable with a null relatedTarget, and on:focusout then closed the chooser before Escape fired - leaving nowhere to return focus. Fixed by mirroring EntityTable's existing restore_column_move_focus. The style ceiling also went over by exactly one (typography 93>92) because the new fixture added two <code> spans without font-sans; fixed at source, ceiling untouched.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Close-reason addendum (the original lost two backticked identifiers to shell command substitution):

The export-safety type is named ServerTableDisplayedSlice. It is a DISTINCT type from EntityTableDisplayProjection, carries NO AllFiltered scope variant at all, and its sole constructor is a pure function of the effective columns and the loaded rows - so no code path can fetch or synthesize unseen rows. That is what makes the one-page-CSV mistake unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged: a server table only ever holds one page, and a projection that borrowed the complete-snapshot vocabulary would let a consumer export a single page while presenting it as the whole filtered set.

title: Add a focused opinionated admin-workbench composition reference
description: The individual LDUI parts are difficult to judge in isolation, and the Coordinator regression came from composing valid primitives into the wrong hierarchy. Add one deliberately small demo/reference state that proves the intended opinionated workbench composition without becoming a production page abstraction.
design: In the existing demo/story mechanism, compose AppShellTopBar with brand/search/presence/settings/language/account/sign-out slots; a borderless PageHeader with no back slot, greeting/subtitle, and seven PageQuickActions; KpiStrip with eight varied cards; EntityTable with typed text/select filters in its aligned filter row; and FilterSidebar docked right with assistant content and controlled collapse. Use synthetic data and callbacks only. Reuse existing components exactly; if the fixture exposes a separate framework defect, file a follow-up instead of growing this story into a page generator.
acceptance_criteria: The reference visibly matches the intended hierarchy at a wide desktop viewport and a compact mobile viewport: one standard topbar, one base-page header, icon quick actions, separate KPI cards, no external filter bar, table-aligned filters, and a right assistant whose collapse returns width to the table. The demo contains no Office branding dependency, network/API code, domain calculations, persistence, or production route. A focused browser review records expanded/collapsed assistant and compact wrapping with no horizontal escape, clipped menus, duplicate landmarks, or console errors.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. Added one deliberately small demo/reference state proving the intended opinionated workbench composition - AppShellTopBar with its slots, a borderless PageHeader with greeting/subtitle and seven PageQuickActions, KpiStrip with eight varied cards, EntityTable with typed text/select filters in its aligned filter row, and a right-docked FilterSidebar with controlled collapse - using synthetic data and callbacks only, reusing the existing components exactly. It is a reference state, not a page abstraction or generator, and it introduces no duplicate titlebar, table-filter or collapsible-panel component. This is the epic's whole point: the consumer's regression came from composing VALID primitives into the wrong hierarchy, which only a rendered composition can catch. Commit 551793f, with its browser lane WIRED into xtask full_steps() (admin_workbench_step + test-admin-workbench subcommand + a full-only unit test) so the evidence is actually obtainable. EVIDENCE: tests/admin_workbench_smoke.rs run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS at both a wide desktop and a compact mobile viewport, recording expanded/collapsed assistant and compact wrapping.

title: Make PageHeader quick actions an opinionated responsive icon-action row
description: PageHeader accepts arbitrary action children but wraps them in a fixed non-wrapping flex row. A base page with seven cross-surface actions can overflow, and every consumer must hand-compose icon, visible label, tooltip/accessibility, and button/link/form styling. Office Coordinator consequently rendered seven raw text-only submit buttons and lost both the approved glyphs and the standard page-action hierarchy. PageHeader also hardcodes a bottom divider even when the base-page composition is intentionally open.
design: Add a small exported PageQuickActions pattern and icon-plus-label action content helper, designed for use in PageHeader's actions slot with LDUI Button, LinkButton, or typed submit Button. The bar owns accessible navigation/toolbar naming, consistent outline sizing, gaps, responsive wrapping or measured overflow, and stable icon/text alignment; activation, routes, targets, methods, and domain authorization remain caller-owned. Make PageHeader's action host compatible with wrapping and add a typed source-compatible appearance/divider option so a base page can omit the bottom rule. Do not add Office routes or a Coordinator-specific action enum.
acceptance_criteria: Seven icon-and-visible-label actions fit or wrap predictably beside a title/subtitle at wide width and remain reachable without horizontal page overflow at compact width. Every action retains a clear accessible name and focus treatment; icon-only collapse, if used, preserves tooltips and accessible labels. Callback Buttons, LinkButtons, and native submit Buttons are composable without raw daisyUI button markup. PageHeader can explicitly render with or without its bottom divider, action children are no longer trapped in a non-wrapping row, existing callers render compatibly by default, and focused rendered examples cover base-page/no-back, long localized labels, and compact overflow.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. Added the exported PageQuickActions pattern plus an icon-plus-label action helper for PageHeader's actions slot, usable with Button, LinkButton or the typed submit Button (ButtonType::Submit). The bar owns accessible naming, consistent outline sizing, gaps, responsive wrapping and stable icon/text alignment, while activation, routes, targets, methods and authorization stay caller-owned. PageHeader's action host now WRAPS instead of being a fixed non-wrapping row - the original defect, which made seven cross-surface actions overflow and pushed the consumer onto raw text-only submit buttons - and its previously hardcoded bottom divider is now a typed, source-compatible option so a base page can omit the rule. Landed in commit 329f617 (bundled by a git race with the concurrent KpiStrip agent; all 13 files present). EVIDENCE: 11 native page_header/page_quick_actions tests, plus tests/page_quick_actions_smoke.rs run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS, covering seven icon-and-label actions wrapping without horizontal overflow, tooltip/accessible-label agreement and a reactive title.

title: Implement the specified opinionated KpiStrip as independent responsive cards
description: Future-Architecture.md names KpiStrip as the Layer-2 pattern for a responsive row of consistently sized stat cards, but src/patterns has no KpiStrip. Office Coordinator therefore composes eight Stat children inside the low-level daisyUI Stats container, whose joined border and shared background make the result read as one table row instead of eight cards. Production evidence shows the intended hierarchy: a Work Stats section and period control above eight separate rounded, shadowed cards with clear gaps.
design: Add an exported pattern-level KpiStrip plus an opinionated KpiCard (or equivalently small typed item model). KpiStrip owns the responsive grid, equal-card geometry, spacing, and compact behavior; each card owns consistent label, value, description, optional semantic status/trend/help, and unavailable presentation. Build from LDUI tokens/components internally, but do not expose a joined Stats appearance and do not encode Coordinator's eight metrics or business meanings. Keep section heading and period-selection policy caller-owned through ordinary composition.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can render one through at least eight reactive KPIs as visually independent cards. At the Coordinator reference width, eight cards form a coherent row when space permits; narrower widths wrap into a balanced grid without horizontal scrolling, joined borders, collapsed gaps, or unequal visual hierarchy. Labels, values, descriptions, optional status/trend/help, unavailable values, localization changes, and long copy remain legible. Card semantics and accessible names are coherent, existing Stats/Stat APIs remain unchanged, the pattern is exported and documented, and focused render/browser coverage proves wide and compact layouts.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. Added the pattern-level KpiStrip plus an opinionated KpiCard: KpiStrip owns the responsive grid, equal-card geometry, spacing and compact behaviour, while each card owns label, value, description, optional semantic status/trend/help and an unavailable presentation. Built from LDUI tokens/components WITHOUT exposing a joined Stats appearance - which was the actual defect, since the consumer's eight Stat children inside daisyUI's Stats container shared one border and background and read as a single table row instead of eight cards. No consumer metrics or business meanings are encoded; section heading and period selection stay caller-owned through ordinary composition, and the existing Stats/Stat APIs are untouched. Commit 329f617. EVIDENCE: 19 native tests, plus live browser coverage on 2026-08-30 through the admin-workbench composition reference (admin_workbench_smoke PASS), which renders eight varied cards at both a wide desktop and a compact mobile viewport and asserts they wrap into a balanced grid with no horizontal scrolling.

title: Complete the opinionated Coordinator workspace visual foundation
description: The Office Coordinator production comparison exposes two gaps in the opinionated layer: Future-Architecture.md specifies KpiStrip but no implementation exists, so consumers fall back to daisyUI's joined Stats strip; and PageHeader's generic actions slot does not provide the responsive icon-and-label quick-action treatment needed for a seven-action base-page header. Existing AppShellTopBar, EntityTable controlled column filters, and right-side FilterSidebar already cover the titlebar, integrated filters, and collapsible assistant and must be reused rather than duplicated.
design: Complete only the missing reusable presentation layer. Add KpiStrip/KpiCard and a minimal PageQuickActions composition that works inside PageHeader. Prove the intended combination in an LDUI demo/reference fixture using existing AppShellTopBar, PageHeader, EntityTable filter row, and right FilterSidebar. Keep routes, HTTP forms, identity, API data, business copy, persistence, and assistant logic caller-owned. Do not add an Office-specific page component or a page generator.
acceptance_criteria: The child work supplies the missing KpiStrip and page quick-action composition, the existing typed Button submit semantics are usable for POST launch forms, and a focused rendered reference demonstrates the full workbench composition at wide and compact widths. No duplicate titlebar, table-filter, or collapsible-panel component is introduced; current low-level components remain independently usable and existing callers remain source-compatible.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE - all three children implemented and verified live in a browser on 2026-08-30. ynmd.1 supplied the missing KpiStrip/KpiCard so KPIs render as visually independent cards rather than daisyUI's joined Stats strip (commit 329f617, admin_workbench_smoke PASS). ynmd.2 made PageHeader's action host wrap and added the PageQuickActions icon-action composition plus a typed optional divider (329f617, page_quick_actions_smoke PASS). ynmd.3 added the focused workbench composition reference proving the full hierarchy at wide and compact widths (551793f, admin_workbench_smoke PASS). The typed Button submit semantics the epic depends on were already shipped and are browser-verified (ldui-9vs). No duplicate titlebar, table-filter or collapsible-panel component was introduced - AppShellTopBar, EntityTable controlled column filters and the right FilterSidebar are reused as required - the low-level components remain independently usable, and existing callers stay source-compatible. Supporting suites on the same tree: native gate 14/14 and 11 of 13 browser lanes green, including entity_table_smoke 9/9 and both snapshot-table consumer-blocker proofs.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
The full Office satellite portfolio comparison is complete: 25 additional legacy/current pairs, 50 rendered pages at 1600x1000. It confirms the scope of this epic rather than adding another reusable framework defect.

`ldui-ynmd.1` KpiStrip affects Contribution, Finances, Conversations Report, Dashboard Detail, NPS Surveys, Office Assignments, Day Planner, Pending, No-Hire Detail, Conversation Detail, and Dashboard's top summary band, in addition to Coordinator. title: Demo /components/tab panics: Tab inside TabSet requires a stable tab_key
description: The tab showcase page crashes the wasm app at runtime: panicked at src/components/tab/component.rs:405 'Tab inside TabSet requires a stable tab_key', followed by 'Uncaught RuntimeError: unreachable'. The page renders the shell but no <main>, so /components/tab never mounts. Three browser checks fail because of it: tab_click_selects_via_oracle, tab_layout_is_clean, report_layout_backlog (the last navigates to tab). PRE-EXISTING - git log shows no commit in the 2026-08-29 open-beads wave (b420e4f..HEAD) touched src/components/tab/ or demo/src/demos/tab.rs; the last change was 9854e23 (ldui-875k Office UI foundation). Either the demo must pass tab_key for every Tab inside a TabSet, or the component must not panic on its absence. Found by running the browser lanes against a hand-verified server on 2026-08-30.
close_reason:
Fixed and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. Three separate defects, found in sequence because each one hid the next:
(1) The reported panic: plain (non-island) Leptos #[component]s never open an owner boundary, so TabSet's provide_context leaked to LATER SIBLINGS on the same page; an unrelated uncontrolled <Tab> (no tab_key) saw that ambient context and hit the assert, taking the whole wasm app down - /components/tab rendered a shell with no <main> at all. Both mismatched combinations now degrade gracefully (uncontrolled tab + logging::warn!) instead of panicking. Commit 19ed829. NOTE this is the SAME bug class as ldui-1jxa's FieldContext leak, fixed the same day.
(2) With the page finally mounting, roving focus was reachable for the first time and was wrong: TabSetContext::registrations was in registration-CALL order, but a <Show>-wrapped tab registers after later unconditional siblings (empirically [alpha,gamma,delta,epsilon,zeta,beta]), so next_enabled_tab's index-based neighbour lookup walked the wrong sequence. Fixed with dom_ordered_registrations() which reorders by actual DOM position.
(3) focus_tab deferred .focus() through request_animation_frame, racing any synchronous read of document.activeElement; made synchronous, matching the established pattern in data_table/body.rs. Commit 707b3e1.
EVIDENCE: /components/tab confirmed mounting in headless Chrome (main present, 24 tabs) after (1); reactivity_smoke went 49/51 -> 51/51 after (2) and (3), with tab_click_selects_via_oracle passing; layout_audit_smoke 9/9 (its two failures had been this same panic); native suite 2631 green.

title: Support generation-bound displayed snapshot deltas during replacement
description: SnapshotTableState only changes displayed rows through complete(), which consumes the single active request, increments the dataset/access generation, and clears action bindings. A real snapshot page must remove claimed rows and apply SSE deltas locally while preserving deterministic EntityTable focus, and it may need to refresh the still-displayed dataset while a different office replacement remains in flight. Using a fake same-dataset request either supersedes the real office request or changes focus scope and erases action feedback; keeping deltas only in local_rows leaves source_data with stale authoritative membership. Add a typed, stale-safe displayed-snapshot update boundary that preserves identity coherence without exposing consumer-set dataset identity.
acceptance_criteria: The state can mint or execute a generation/revision-bound update for the currently displayed dataset that atomically replaces rows/revision/count/metadata, rejects stale or mismatched updates, preserves the dataset/access focus generation for incremental row changes, and leaves an unrelated active replacement request intact. SnapshotTablePage authoritative source_data updates with the delta so focused filtered/sorted/paged row removal chooses the correct next target. Keyed action completion remains valid in the same generation. Native and browser negative controls cover own claim removal, another-user SSE removal, duplicate/stale delta, a delta during an office replacement, filtered/sorted final-row focus recovery, and completion of the still-pending replacement.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. SnapshotTableState gained a generation/revision-bound displayed-snapshot update for the currently displayed dataset: it atomically replaces rows/revision/count/metadata, rejects stale, duplicate and out-of-order deltas, PRESERVES the dataset/access focus generation for incremental row changes (so EntityTable focus scope and keyed action feedback survive), and leaves an unrelated in-flight replacement request intact and still completable. SnapshotTablePage's authoritative source_data updates with the delta. Commit ed275dd; browser lane wired in 6e41b04 (it was previously registered nowhere, so its evidence was unobtainable). EVIDENCE: 15 native reducer tests, plus tests/snapshot_table_delta_smoke.rs run live against a real server on 2026-08-30 = 4/4 PASS - own_claim_removal_delta_replaces_rows_without_bumping_generation, sequential_own_claim_and_sse_removal_deltas_both_apply, duplicate_stale_delta_replay_is_rejected, delta_during_replacement_leaves_it_intact_and_it_still_completes. Remaining gap for a follow-up: DOM focus recovery on filtered/sorted FINAL-row removal is not separately asserted in the browser (the generation preservation it depends on is proven both natively and in the browser).

title: Expose complete EntityTable controls through SnapshotTablePage
description: The canonical SnapshotTablePage owns its internal EntityTable but SnapshotEntityTableConfig cannot supply page_reset_key, viewport_fit, toolbar_actions/on_display_projection, or column_chooser_trigger. Office No-Hires already requires filter changes to reset paging, fill-parent row capacity, a gear chooser, and CSV export adjacent to table utilities. Migrating to the archetype currently regresses those accepted behaviors or forces a page-local duplicate table/chooser. Add typed behavior-only passthroughs while continuing to forbid rows, dataset identity, revision, count, generation, or persistence I/O.
acceptance_criteria: SnapshotEntityTableConfig exposes typed page-reset identity, viewport-fit policy, caller toolbar actions, display-projection callback/action-column policy, and chooser presentation; SnapshotTablePage forwards each to its internally owned EntityTable without allowing identity-critical bindings. The reference fixture and focused browser proof show local filter reset from a later page, adaptive height, icon chooser opening visibly, export receiving the authoritative rendered projection, and no storage I/O or dataset-identity drift. Existing callers retain defaults and public documentation names the consumer migration path.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. SnapshotEntityTableConfig now exposes typed behavior-only builders - page_reset_key, viewport_fit, toolbar_actions, on_display_projection, projection_action_columns, column_chooser_trigger - and SnapshotTablePage forwards each to the EntityTable it owns internally. Identity-critical bindings remain STRUCTURALLY impossible (rows, dataset identity, revision, count, generation and persistence I/O have no fields on the config). Existing callers retain defaults and compile unchanged; the consumer migration path is documented in doc/patterns/client-snapshot-list.md and doc/components/entity_table.md. Commits 59089ee (feature) and 4b8b455 (fixture fix); the browser lane was registered in 6e41b04 - before that it was wired nowhere, so this bead's evidence was structurally unobtainable. EVIDENCE: native forwarding/defaults tests, plus tests/snapshot_table_page_controls_smoke.rs run live against a real server on 2026-08-30 = 1/1 PASS covering local filter reset from a later page, adaptive height, the icon chooser opening, export receiving the authoritative rendered projection, and no generation/identity drift. NOTE: the first live run FAILED (viewport_fit reported enabled while effectivePageSize stayed 25) - root-caused to the FIXTURE, whose 160px budget left less than one measured row so auto_page_size_for_height's documented below-floor branch correctly retained the configured size; the library passthrough was confirmed working via DevTools remeasurement. Residual fragility: the fixture budget is tuned to a rendered ~35px row height rather than a token.

title: Scope FieldContext so sibling controls do not reuse the first field id
description: In the Office No-Hires standalone WASM page, the first LDUI Field provides ld-field-0 and later unrelated Input and Select components consume that same FieldContext. Eight controls rendered with id=ld-field-0, including a DatasetSelector and EntityTable column filters that are not children of the original Search Office Field. Chrome reports Duplicate form field id in the same form. The current Field component calls provide_context before invoking Children, but the context is observable by subsequent siblings instead of being confined to this Field control.
acceptance_criteria: Render multiple sibling Field/Input controls plus later standalone Select, DatasetSelector, and EntityTable filter controls in a CSR WASM fixture. Each Field label points to exactly its own unique control id; sibling or later controls do not consume an earlier FieldContext; caller-supplied ids continue to win; Chrome reports no duplicate form-field-id issue. Add a browser-level regression because the existing native unit test for next_field_id does not expose the owner/context leak.
close_reason: Fixed and committed (fc894ab). FieldContext is now scoped to the Field's own children, so later unrelated Input/Select/DatasetSelector/EntityTable-filter controls no longer consume an earlier Field's context. Previously the first Field provided ld-field-0 and eight later sibling controls all rendered with id=ld-field-0, which Chrome reported as 'Duplicate form field id in the same form'. Caller-supplied ids continue to win and existing callers compile unchanged. EVIDENCE: 2 new native regression tests that prove the exact owner/context leak mechanism (the pre-existing next_field_id unit test structurally could not see it, since the bug was context VISIBILITY, not id generation); full native suite 2585 passing. A browser regression fixture (/field-context-scope + tests/field_context_scoping.rs) was added and is compile-verified; it will execute in the scheduled full gate.

title: Expose current EntityTable presentation controls through SnapshotEntityTableConfig
description: SnapshotTablePage is the canonical client-snapshot composition, but SnapshotEntityTableConfig does not expose current EntityTable capabilities needed by production consumers: viewport_fit, page_reset_key, toolbar_actions, on_display_projection, projection_action_columns, and column_chooser_trigger. No-Hires must otherwise fall back to raw EntityTable or lose viewport-fit paging, filter-to-first-page behavior, table-local CSV export, and the glyph column chooser.
acceptance_criteria: SnapshotEntityTableConfig provides typed builders for viewport fit, page reset identity, table toolbar children, display projection callback and action-column policy, and reactive column-chooser trigger; SnapshotTablePage forwards each option without allowing caller-supplied dataset, rows, revision, or focus generation; the reference fixture covers omitted defaults and configured behavior; No-Hires can use the canonical page without a lower-level EntityTable escape hatch.
close_reason: Resolved by the same work as ldui-myhh (commits 59089ee + 4b8b455; lane wired in 6e41b04). This bead asked for SnapshotEntityTableConfig to provide typed builders for viewport fit, page-reset identity, toolbar actions, display projection and chooser presentation; all are delivered as behavior-only passthroughs forwarded to the internally owned EntityTable, with identity-critical bindings still impossible. EVIDENCE: native forwarding/default-preservation tests plus 1/1 live browser proof (see ldui-myhh); sibling host suites snapshot_table_delta_smoke 4/4 and snapshot_table_smoke 2/2 remain green.

title: Add same-generation authoritative row mutation to SnapshotTableState
description: The canonical SnapshotTablePage owns authoritative source rows inside SnapshotTableState, but the controller exposes no transition for a successful row mutation such as a No-Hire claim or an SSE row removal. Replacing the snapshot through start_request plus complete increments the dataset/access generation and clears action feedback, which prevents EntityTable same-scope focus recovery and loses the keyed outcome. Add a typed checked transition that updates one complete displayed snapshot within its current dataset/access generation, preserves valid unrelated action feedback, and rejects stale action/dataset bindings.
acceptance_criteria: A framework-issued mutation handle or equivalent checked API can atomically replace authoritative rows, revision, count, and metadata only for the still-current displayed dataset/access generation; successful row removal keeps focus_scope stable so EntityTable recovers against visible sorted paged order; the matching action can finish as success or partial success; stale, consumed, access-replaced, and dataset-replaced mutations fail closed; native and browser negative controls cover these cases.
close_reason: Resolved by the same work as ldui-vn81 (commit ed275dd; lane wired in 6e41b04). This bead asked for same-generation authoritative row mutation so a row change does not have to go through start_request+complete, which bumps the dataset/access generation, resets EntityTable focus scope and erases keyed action feedback. The delivered delta API is exactly that: a framework-minted, checked, generation/revision-bound handle that atomically updates rows WITHOUT the generation bump, rejecting stale/duplicate/out-of-order applications. EVIDENCE: 15 native reducer tests incl. keyed-action-completion-remains-valid-in-the-same-generation, plus 4/4 live browser checks (see ldui-vn81).

title: Make Tabs a controlled accessible tabset
description: Tabs is currently only a styled div, while Tab renders an anchor without href, role, tabindex, aria-selected, an activation callback, or sibling keyboard coordination. Office Account and Day Planner attach role, aria state, and click handlers ad hoc; Conversations Report bypasses LDUI with raw tab buttons. An anchor without href is not natively keyboard focusable, and none of these consumers receive a coherent roving-focus tab contract.
design: Add a source-compatible controlled tabset contract. LDUI should own tablist and tab roles, active and disabled presentation, stable tab/panel association, roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End navigation, and one typed selection proposal. Callers own the selected stable key, panel content, routing, and localization. Preserve the existing layout-only API as a compatibility path or provide a deliberate migration path.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can supply stable tab keys, a controlled selected key, localized labels, and one on_select callback without raw role, aria, tabindex, or event attributes. Exactly one enabled tab is in the page tab order; Arrow keys follow orientation, Home/End reach extremes, Enter/Space selection behavior is documented, and disabled tabs are skipped. Each tab exposes correct aria-selected and aria-controls relationships to its panel. External selected-key replacement, removal of the selected tab, dynamic label replacement, horizontal overflow, and focus restoration remain coherent. Existing visual variants remain available and focused native/browser fixtures cover pointer and keyboard operation.
close_reason: Implemented controlled accessible tabsets with source-compatible layout mode and focused coverage.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Added TabSet as the controlled accessibility owner around existing Tabs variants, keyed Tab items, and TabPanel siblings. It owns tablist/tab/tabpanel roles and relationships, manual activation, roving tabindex, orientation-aware Arrow/Home/End navigation, disabled skipping, collision-safe IDs, reactive localization, internal compact overflow, invalid-selection fallback, and focus restoration only when a removed tab held focus. Existing Tabs/Tab calls remain layout-compatible. Added canonical and mutation fixtures, expanded the existing selective tab browser journey without increasing the enforced 32-test count, and documented migration. Verified 25 focused native tests, showcase cargo check, browser-target compilation, scoped rustfmt, and git diff --check; real browser execution remains in the final selected run.

title: Support typed native form semantics in Button
description: LDUI Button hardcodes type="button" and exposes no typed way to render a submit or reset button. The Office satellite conversion therefore uses raw daisyUI buttons for native POST launch forms across page headers, cross-satellite actions, and row actions. Those controls bypass Button focus-ring, motion, ripple, loading, variant, disabled, and future accessibility behavior even though their only unusual requirement is native form submission.
design: Add a small semantic enum such as ButtonType with Button, Submit, and Reset variants, defaulting to Button for source and safety compatibility. Render the corresponding native type attribute while retaining the existing Button API and styling. Keep form action, method, target, and navigation policy on the caller-owned form; do not add Office-specific launch behavior. Document precedence if arbitrary attributes can also supply type.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can render LDUI Button as type button, submit, or reset; the default remains type button; submit activates the containing form exactly once by click and keyboard activation; reset follows native form behavior; disabled and loading submit buttons cannot submit; visual variants, node refs, ripple, focus ring, and arbitrary data or aria attributes still work; nested and form-associated edge behavior is documented; native and browser fixtures cover all three variants and verify the emitted type attribute.
notes: Promoted to P1 from the 2026-08-30 Office Coordinator production comparison. Seven satellite launch actions are POST forms; without typed submit semantics, the consumer must use raw daisyUI buttons and cannot satisfy the opinionated PageQuickActions composition. Required by ldui-ynmd.2 and ldui-ynmd.3 under ldui-ynmd. This changes only native Button semantics; route/method/target remain consumer-owned.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. Button gained typed ButtonType { Button (default), Submit, Reset } emitting the native type attribute, so consumers get native form submission without losing the framework focus-ring, variant, ripple, loading and accessibility contract. Form action/method/target stay caller-owned; precedence versus a spread attr:type is documented and tested (the spread wins, matching the existing Progress attr:max precedent). Loading natively disables ONLY submit buttons - narrowed from an earlier revision that disabled every type, which would have silently made downstream loading action buttons inert and unfocusable - pinned by a 2x2x3 truth table over the pure resolver. Commits 43cfcb1, 0a8cb9c, ccba650. EVIDENCE: 50 native button tests plus four browser checks run LIVE against a real server on 2026-08-30 = PASS: button_type_variants_emit_the_matching_type_attribute, submit_button_activates_form_once_per_click_and_per_key (no duplicate submission), disabled_and_loading_submit_buttons_cannot_submit, reset_button_restores_native_defaults. Note ldui-55lp was a duplicate of this bead and was closed against the same work.

title: Make ServerDataTable query controls match declared server capabilities
description: Cursor-mode ServerDataTable currently treats the controlled cursor query as proof that every query-shape control is supported. It therefore always renders a free-text search box and page-size selector, and sortable/filterable columns can emit corresponding proposals. Office Awaiting's keyset endpoint truthfully supports only a fixed 20-row slice plus opaque Previous/Next cursors. The consumer cannot hide unsupported search or page-size controls without abandoning the opinionated table or accepting UI that appears to work but is rejected/reverted.
design: Add an explicit typed server-query capability/control policy, independent from pagination strategy. The caller declares which of search, page-size selection, sorting, and column filtering the endpoint accepts. Cursor navigation remains required and controlled. Defaults should preserve existing ServerDataTable behavior; hiding a control must also make its proposal path inert. Prefer a cohesive capability value over several unrelated booleans, and reject contradictory configurations rather than silently widening server capability.
acceptance_criteria: A cursor-paged ServerDataTable can render only Previous/Next controls for a fixed server slice, with no search box or page-size selector and no way to emit unsupported search/page-size/sort/filter proposals; opaque cursor navigation and retained loading/failure behavior remain unchanged; callers can independently enable supported query capabilities; legacy and current cursor callers remain source-compatible under documented defaults; accessible labels and keyboard order remain coherent when controls are omitted; focused native and real-browser fixtures cover cursor-only, mixed-capability, and default-compatible configurations.

A page-level Reset may exist, but EntityColumnFilter currently carries only a column ID and renderer, so the framework cannot disclose or clear hidden active filters.

Add enough typed filter presentation metadata, such as localized label, active state, and clear intent, to render one responsive fallback in the table toolbar or a compact filter panel. Do not render duplicate focusable controls at the same breakpoint, and do not make column visibility own domain filter state.

title: Support cursor pagination in ServerDataTable without invented totals

Add a typed cursor or keyset paging strategy so server-owned tables can represent this API truthfully.
design: Model offset and cursor paging as explicit mutually exclusive strategies. Cursor tokens remain opaque caller-owned transport values; the table owns only presentation and emits typed navigation intent. Search, sort, and filter changes must restart from the first cursor generation.

title: Close invariant gaps in SnapshotTable foundation design before implementation
description:
## Context

This is the requested consumer review of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-snapshot-table-opinionated-foundation-design.md` at WDO commit `f39f541`, checked against `Future-Architecture.md` and the current `FilterSchema`, `EntityTable`, and `DataTable` APIs.

The overall direction is correct: keep transport and domain policy in consumers, make dataset replacement atomic, retain old content while a replacement loads, centralize page-state/action feedback, and keep the composition explicit Rust rather than a page generator. The following public-contract gaps should be resolved in the design before the foundation is implemented or frozen for consumers.

## Priority findings

1. **The proposed page slots do not enforce selector/table identity coherence.** The design says `SnapshotTablePage` accepts already-built `DatasetSelector`, `FilterBar`, and `EntityTable` slots, while also claiming the page derives selector presentation, table dataset identity, and rows from one `DatasetPresentation`. An opaque child can still bind unrelated signals and reproduce the original defect: new selector identity over old rows. Specify context-bound render closures or typed slot/config inputs that receive only a framework-derived read-only snapshot view. The canonical API must make a mismatched selector/table dataset identity impossible or explicitly detectable; documentation alone is not enforcement.

2. **The public orthogonal state shape permits contradictory combinations.** Independent public `dataset`, `content`, `access`, and `action` fields allow states such as `NeverLoaded + Ready`, a non-empty snapshot labeled `EmptyDataset`, or content derived from a previous revision paired with a newly displayed snapshot. Preserve legitimate orthogonality, but use private fields plus constructors/reducer transitions, and derive content from the displayed snapshot and current local-result count (or bind it to the displayed dataset identity/revision). Access replacement precedence must also be encoded rather than left to consumers assembling the struct.

3. **Caller-issued request tokens weaken the promised race guarantee.** A consumer can reuse or decrease the supposedly monotonic token; then a stale response can again match the active token and dataset identity. The pure transition model can deterministically mint its own opaque sequence token without using wall-clock time. At minimum, `start_request` must reject non-increasing/reused tokens and return the accepted opaque request handle used by completion/failure methods.

4. **A singular `ActionFeedbackState<K>` conflicts with keyed concurrent row actions.** “Idle or one keyed outcome” cannot represent two pending row mutations, or a pending mutation alongside a preference/action conflict, although the design says pending disables only the corresponding action. Either declare and enforce one in-flight page action, or model keyed concurrent action state (for example a keyed collection plus one latest live-region announcement). The chosen concurrency and dismissal/retry semantics need to be explicit.

5. **Reactive behavioral columns can leave the current sort cache stale.** `SortedIndexCache` currently keys reuse only by `Rc` row identity and `EntitySort`; it does not include column definitions. The design promises that reactive columns use the latest comparator/sort-key callbacks. If those callbacks change while rows and sort remain unchanged, the visible order incorrectly reuses old indices. Either keep behavioral column definitions stable and make only localized presentation text reactive, or add a stable column-definition revision/fingerprint to cache invalidation and reconcile removed/non-sortable sort IDs. Apply the same presentation/behavior split to compact rendering.

6. **`SnapshotViewDefaults<F>` does not exclude dataset identity “by construction” when `F` is arbitrary.** Current `FilterSchema<T>` stores `PhantomData<T>` and validates only declared string keys; it cannot prevent a consumer-defined serializable `F` from containing `office_id` or another dataset selector. Use a framework-owned schema-keyed filter payload, a sealed/validated projection that serializes only schema-declared fields, or narrow the claim and add runtime validation. Include a negative compile/runtime fixture whose consumer filter type attempts to carry dataset identity.

7. **The sortable-header accessibility contract is incomplete.** The design gives the nested sort control only the localized column header as its accessible name and keeps `aria-sort` on the parent `th`. The existing `ldui-w1e` acceptance requires the focused control to expose current sort state. Define localized current-state and next-action text (including multi-sort position where applicable) and expose it directly to the focusable control or via an explicitly associated description; do not rely on assistive technology inferring the parent header state.

8. **Focus recovery needs a dataset/generation boundary and eligibility rule.** “If the row disappears from the supplied dataset” also occurs during dataset replacement, access replacement, filtering, or wholesale refresh. The table must not move focus from a removed row into an unrelated row in a newly selected dataset. Reset/suppress row-action recovery across dataset identity generations and access replacement; for an in-dataset removal, target the same action only when it remains rendered, enabled, and focusable, otherwise use the named table-region fallback. State what happens when filtering/paging hides the focused row without deleting it.

These are design corrections, not a request to broaden the consumer MVP or introduce framework transport/persistence.
design:
## Recommended resolution

- Introduce a framework-derived `SnapshotTableView` (name illustrative) containing displayed/requested identity, displayed rows/revision/count, transition kind, and valid panel state. Pass this value into selector/table render closures or typed configs owned by `SnapshotTablePage`.
- Keep the state machine pure and deterministic: it owns the next request sequence and returns an opaque request handle; completion and failure consume/check that handle plus dataset identity.
- Keep orthogonal axes internally, but expose only validated constructors and reducer operations. Bind any derived content result to the displayed snapshot revision.
- Decide whether actions are serialized or concurrent and encode that choice in the type. If concurrent, separate keyed operational state from the single announcement chosen for the live region.
- Split reactive column presentation from stable sorting/cell behavior, or introduce an explicit semantic column revision that invalidates `SortedIndexCache` and normalizes preferences/sort clauses.
- Replace arbitrary persisted `F` with a schema-projected payload, or require an explicit projection callback whose output can contain only validated local-filter keys.
- Add localized sort-state/next-action strings to the shared table text contract and specify the focused control's computed accessible name/description.
- Include dataset identity/generation in the focus record, clear it on replacement/access transitions, and verify target focusability before moving focus.

title: data_table auto-rows measure timer fires after unmount — disposed-signal panic
description:
component.rs:802: schedule_measure() runs set_timeout_with_handle(measure_rows, Duration::ZERO) and DISCARDS the TimeoutHandle, so nothing can cancel it. The auto-page Effect (~component.rs:816, deps: auto_page_size/table_size/data/page_size) schedules it on mount and on every data change; the ResizeObserver callback schedules it too. measure_rows then calls auto_rows.get_untracked() and auto_rows.set(...) with NO disposed-guard.

If the host app navigates away inside that zero-delay macrotask window, the timer fires after the DataTable's reactive owner is disposed and the whole wasm app panics: reactive_graph traits.rs:361 'Tried to access a reactive value that has already been disposed.'

Repro: any router navigation immediately after a DataTable (auto_page_size or not — the measure Effect always runs) mounts or re-renders; caught deterministically by 4iiz-etl's PixelProof visual gate (bead bd_4iiz-etl-rnn.24) on its History→Errors transition. The gate currently paces navigations ~150ms apart to drain the pending macrotask — a workaround, not a fix.

Fix: (1) store the TimeoutHandle (the search debounce at component.rs:421/:445 already models exactly this — keep the two consistent) and clear it in on_cleanup; (2) belt-and-braces: measure_rows should use try-forms (auto_rows.try_with_untracked / try_set) so a late callback degrades to a no-op instead of a process-wide panic. ServerDataTable's debounce keeps its handle but is never cleared on cleanup either — same pass should cover it.
close_reason: All three timer-outlives-owner sites fixed and merged to main (4e22e34): measure timer handle stored/cancelled on reschedule and on_cleanup with try-form guards in measure_rows; client search debounce try-sets and cancels on unmount; ServerDataTable debounce entry-guarded and cancelled on unmount. Regression test data_table_timers_survive_unmount arms all three timers and navigates in the same task — it captured two disposed-signal panics before the fix, green after; full reactivity suite 25/25, clippy clean, 2273 lib tests green. 4iiz-etl (bd_4iiz-etl-rnn.24) can drop the 150ms navigation pacing workaround.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Second site, same class (found by the same 4iiz-etl gate run once navigations were paced past the ZERO-delay measure timer): server_component.rs:259/:319 — ServerDataTable's 300ms search debounce stores its TimeoutHandle in a signal but NEVER cancels it in on_cleanup. When it fires after the table's owner is disposed, the closure's emit_query(1) untracked-reads page_size/sort state on disposed signals -> the same reactive_graph traits.rs:361 panic. component.rs:421/:445 (plain DataTable's debounce) shares the shape. Fix family for all three timers: cancel the handle in on_cleanup AND make the callbacks use try_ forms so a late fire degrades to a no-op. The consuming gate currently paces navigations 500ms apart (> the longest timer) as a workaround.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Third site, same class, and the one no consumer-side pacing can dodge: the ResizeObserver attached at component.rs:840-868. When SPA navigation removes the table wrapper from the DOM, the observer can deliver a size-change callback IN THE SAME TASK as the unmount; the callback runs schedule_measure/measure_rows against the just-disposed owner -> the same reactive_graph disposal panic, and a wasm panic poisons the whole instance. on_cleanup's disconnect() runs during reactive teardown, which can be AFTER the delivery is already queued for that task. Fix: disconnect the observer BEFORE DOM removal (or first thing in cleanup) AND guard measure_rows with try_ reads/writes so any late delivery is a no-op. The 4iiz-etl visual gate now navigates between routes with FULL PAGE LOADS (fresh instance per route, teardown never runs) to keep this class out of its captures - SPA click coverage there is reduced to one deliberate DataTable-free transition until this bead lands.

title: Repo is unbuildable: sibling ai-chat-core added Usage::reasoning_tokens and three call sites here do not set it
description: cargo xtask verify is 10/14 as of 2026-08-10. clippy-lib, clippy-demo, check-demo and test-lib all FAIL with E0063 'missing field reasoning_tokens in initializer of Usage'. Three call sites: src/components/ai_chat/tests.rs:224, :237, and demo/src/demos/ai_chat.rs:32. NOT caused by any change in this repo. ai-chat-core is a PATH dependency at ../Rust-DeskApp/crates/ai-chat-core, and that repo landed aac92bf 'feat(engine): surface reasoning_tokens on Usage' minutes earlier, so the struct gained a field and every struct-literal construction here stopped compiling. This is the cross-repo path-dep hazard CLAUDE.md documents for ui-tokens, in the opposite direction: rather than this repo referencing something absent upstream, upstream changed under this repo with no commit here.
design: Set reasoning_tokens at the three call sites. Prefer 0 for the test fixtures unless a non-zero value is meaningful to what they assert. CONSIDER asking the sibling whether Usage should be #[non_exhaustive] with a Default or a builder - it is a wire/telemetry struct that will keep gaining fields, and every future field will break every struct-literal consumer the same way. That is the durable fix and it belongs upstream.
acceptance_criteria: cargo xtask verify returns to 14/14. The three call sites compile. If the upstream struct is made non_exhaustive, consumers construct it through Default or a builder instead of a literal.
notes: TIMING CAUTION: ../Rust-DeskApp/crates/ai-chat-core/src/event.rs still had UNCOMMITTED modifications when this was filed, so a concurrent session is actively working on that struct. Re-check the current upstream shape before fixing, or the fix may be stale on arrival. Filed rather than fixed for exactly that reason.
close_reason: Fixed in fbd2fd1. Gate back to 14/14, exit 0, all steps PASS. The error named reasoning_tokens but the struct actually grew THREE fields in aac92bf (reasoning_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens) - surfaced by a rust-analyzer diagnostic after the first edit, not by the compiler message. So the three call sites spread ..Default::default() rather than naming fields: Usage derives Default, and naming them would compile today and break again on the next telemetry counter. Zero for the new counters is semantically right, not just convenient - upstream documents reasoning_tokens as a SUBSET of output_tokens that must never be summed with it, and only reasoning models report it, so zero is what a non-reasoning uncached turn actually reports. Swept the repo: no fourth Usage literal. RE-CHECKED the upstream shape before editing per this bead's own timing caution - the sibling's uncommitted event.rs edits had landed by then.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: STILL WORTH DOING UPSTREAM, not fixed here: Usage is a telemetry struct that will keep gaining counters, and every addition breaks every struct-literal consumer across every repo that depends on ai-chat-core. Making it #[non_exhaustive] would force consumers onto Default/builder construction and turn a compile break into a non-event. That belongs in ../Rust-DeskApp/crates/ai-chat-core, so it is the sibling owner's call - this consumer-side spread only protects THIS repo.

title: A failed Tailwind build leaves trunk serving a STALE output.css, and both browser audit suites pass green against it
description: Found 2026-08-10 while landing ldui-vh6. A syntax error in demo/input.css (a comment quoting a glob ending in */ closed the comment early) made tailwindcss exit with CssSyntaxError. trunk carried on and kept serving the PREVIOUS output.css. Both browser suites then ran and PASSED against that stale stylesheet - cargo xtask test-style 7/7 and test-layout 9/9, with STYLE-EXIT=0. cargo xtask verify cannot see it either, because it runs cargo check and never invokes trunk. CONSEQUENCE: the entire computed-style audit system - every ceiling, every ratchet, the whole point of ldui-9rf - can report green while measuring a stylesheet that failed to build. The suites are not testing the CSS you just wrote; they are testing whatever CSS last succeeded. This is strictly worse than the known 'npm install missing -> stale dist' trap already in the demo-trunk-build-prereqs memory, because that one fails loudly on first run while this one only bites after a previously-good build exists.
design: The audit harness must refuse to run against a stylesheet it cannot prove is current. Options: (a) have the xtask browser-suite steps run the tailwind build themselves and FAIL on a non-zero exit rather than delegating to trunk's pre_build hook, whose failure trunk swallows; (b) assert a freshness marker - stamp a build id into output.css and have harness_at verify the served stylesheet carries the id of the current input.css hash; (c) at minimum, grep the trunk log for CssSyntaxError and fail the step. (b) is the only one that also catches a stale dist from any other cause.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberately broken demo/input.css makes cargo xtask test-style and test-layout FAIL, not pass. The failure message names the stylesheet build, not a mount timeout or a ceiling breach. A negative control proves it: break input.css, watch the suite go red, restore, watch it go green.
notes: The trap that produced it is now documented in demo/input.css's own comment, but that only covers this one trigger. The general hole - a green audit run against a stylesheet that failed to build - is what this bead is for. Related: the same class of silent staleness bit an agent earlier the same day when a concurrent session's trunk build rewrote demo/dist under a running suite, causing 9 layout tests to fail on untouched pages.
close_reason: Fixed in c51010c. Design covers all THREE failure modes, not just tailwind's exit code: the stylesheet build moved out of trunk's swallowed pre_build hook into demo/build-css.mjs invoked by xtask (fails loud), plus a run-unique marker republished into dist and asserted by harness_at - so a stale dist from ANY cause is caught, which an exit-code-only fix would miss. Marker is an unmatchable id RULE rather than a comment, because comments are absent from the CSSOM and stripped by the release minifier. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN BOTH DIRECTIONS: with the original trap re-created, test-style and test-layout both went RED at exit 1 naming the stylesheet build, and the running-server path panicked with STYLESHEET BUILD FAILED; restoring input.css returned 7/7 and 9/9 green. Marker proven inert byte-for-byte: report_layout_backlog identical across all 7 swept pages, 214 lines of violations, same scanned/total per page, backlog 52 both times. Failure mode 2 confirmed twice - deliberately, and then by accident when an sccache failure left trunk serving a stale dist and all 7 style tests correctly reported the stylesheet instead of a bogus ceiling breach.

title: test-style is RED: the demo's audit profile declares no deviations, so daisyUI's own defaults read as 123 depth + 99 typography violations
description: cargo xtask test-style FAILS on /components/data-table: typography 99 > ceiling 89, depth 123 > ceiling 109. Not a regression in this repo - the engine got stricter under us (pixelproof-style-audit is a PATH dep, so two commits landed live with no commit here): 9856c40 models shadow COLOUR HUE and INSET in ShadowSpec, and 9b5020a skips inert layers and measures font resolution. Stricter matching means daisyUI's own defaults now mismatch where they previously slipped through. THE VIOLATIONS ARE REAL, NOT FALSE POSITIVES: (a) DEPTH - every button.btn.btn-sm carries daisyUI's 'rgba(0,0,0,0.15) 0 6px 12px -2px, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0 3px 6px -2px', which is not in ui_tokens::elevation::LEVELS; (b) TYPOGRAPHY - table.table-lg cells are 18px, off the 6-step ramp [28,20,16,14,12,11]; and <code> elements resolve ui-monospace against a profile pinned to ui-sans-serif. This is EXACTLY the finding from the office-perf pilot (ldui-9rf.11 fix round): an undeclared-but-intentional value makes the whole family report noise, and because the sweep pushes ONE violation per element and breaks, a genuinely wrong shadow on those same buttons would be invisible. Those ceilings are currently protecting nothing.
design: Do NOT raise the ceilings to make it green - that cements the noise and permanently blinds both families on that page. Do what the office-perf pilot did: give the demo's profile explicit, documented DEVIATIONS for the daisyUI defaults the demo deliberately uses, then re-measure and set ceilings to the new (much lower) counts. Concretely: declare daisyUI's .btn shadow set in the profile's .shadows(), and either add 18.0 to .type_ramp() as a declared table-lg step or stop using table-lg in the demo. The <code>/ui-monospace mismatch is a separate question - a <code> element SHOULD be monospace, so the engine's per-element family rule arguably needs a monospace-element exemption; raise that against PixelProof rather than distorting the profile.
acceptance_criteria: cargo xtask test-style passes with ceilings LOWER than today's committed numbers, and every remaining violation is a real drift rather than a declared default. The profile's deviations carry a comment saying why each is deliberate.
notes: Found 2026-08-09 by re-running the consumer suite immediately after the engine changed. The main gate (cargo xtask verify, 12/12) does NOT include test-style - it is in verify-full - so this is red without the fast gate noticing.
close_reason: Fixed by declaring the demo's deviations, not by raising ceilings (b2fbd74). Total violations 334 -> 177 across 4 pages, zero slack, nothing raised: data-table depth 109->18, typography 89->83; button depth 36->0. test-style PASS, verify 12/12, test-layout 8/8 ratchet unmoved. Two corrections found: the .btn shadow was demo/input.css's own push effect, not a daisyUI default; and h1 text-3xl at 30px was a REAL defect, fixed to .ld-text-display. Engine gaps filed as PixelProof-0oc (no monospace exemption) and PixelProof-0il (parseShadows cannot read oklch).

title: [streaming] Add an authenticated fetch-based SSE hook with owned lifecycle
description: The framework use_event_source hook correctly owns native EventSource lifecycle, but EventSource cannot set Authorization headers. Applications that legitimately fall back from cookies to bearer sessions must either duplicate fetch/ReadableStream parsing and reconnection or lose live updates. 4iiz-Office issue op-rrp9 needs a universal client primitive; authentication policy and any short-lived ticket issuance remain application/server concerns.
acceptance_criteria: Add a direct Leptos hook for authenticated fetch-based server-sent-event streams that accepts caller-supplied safe headers without putting credentials in the URL; incrementally parses SSE framing across arbitrary chunk boundaries, including named events, data lines, ids, retry hints, comments, CRLF, and final partial buffers; owns AbortController, reader, callbacks, timers, and cleanup without leaks; exposes connected/reconnecting/stopped and parse/transport diagnostics; supports bounded backoff, Last-Event-ID, explicit stop, owner cleanup, and injectable sleep/fetch seams for deterministic native tests; provide typed JSON convenience matching use_event_source_json; document when to use native EventSource versus authenticated fetch streaming; include wasm/browser reconnect and unmount coverage; never log or expose authorization headers.
close_reason: use_event_source_fetch in utils: fetch+ReadableStream SSE with caller headers per (re)connect, pure SseParser (WHATWG grammar) + take_utf8_prefix, retry:/Last-Event-ID reconnection, abort-on-cleanup. Reuses EventSourceHandle. 14 unit tests.

title: [modal] Support specific accessible dialog names and descriptions
description: Modal hardcodes aria-label="Modal" on every native dialog and exposes no label, aria-labelledby, or aria-describedby contract. Consumer dialogs render visible translated headings inside ModalBox, but assistive technology hears only the same generic English word for every dialog. Raw dialogs also persist because callers cannot connect a title/description through the component API. Consumer finding: office-perf op-99t7/op-cy77.2.
acceptance_criteria: Add explicit mutually coherent accessible-name and description props supporting direct localized labels and labelledby/describedby IDs; remove the hardcoded generic name when a specific contract is supplied while retaining a safe backward-compatible fallback. Document title/description wiring, ensure open/close focus behavior and native dialog semantics remain intact, and add DOM/axe/browser tests for unique localized names, descriptions, missing/duplicate IDs, nested heading content and backward compatibility. Migrate office-perf dialogs once the path dependency includes the change.
close_reason: Modal gains label / labelled_by / described_by; labelled_by suppresses aria-label so the visible translated heading is what AT hears; generic fallback only when unnamed. Typo'd aria_modal attr removed. Commit b1b259c; browser test modal_is_named_by_its_visible_heading.

title: [field] Make labels, help text, and validation programmatically associated
description: Field documents itself as a form-field wrapper, but it renders the visible <label> and the children as siblings inside a div and supplies neither for/id nor aria-labelledby. Help, warning, success and error lines are also unrelated <label> elements without aria-describedby/aria-errormessage. A screen reader therefore cannot reliably associate any of this text with the Input/Select/Textarea child. Input itself has no first-class accessible-label/description props. Consumer finding: office-perf op-99t7/op-cy77.2.
acceptance_criteria: Define one direct accessible association contract across Field and the standard form controls. Prefer generated/stable IDs plus label for, aria-describedby and aria-invalid/aria-errormessage, or an equally semantic wrapper shape that works for every supported child; do not rely on placeholder text. Ensure multiple fields do not collide, optional caller IDs remain stable, error/help IDs update without dangling references, required state is announced, and existing visual markup/classes remain compatible. Add DOM/axe/browser tests covering Input, Select and Textarea in default/error/help/required states plus documentation and demo examples; provide a migration path for existing callers.
close_reason: Field mints ids + provides FieldContext; Input/Select/Textarea auto-consume it: label[for]->id, help via aria-describedby, error via aria-errormessage + aria-invalid (mirrored into describedby). Pure field_line shared by render and context. See git log (commit after b1b259c); browser test field_wires_label_help_and_error_to_the_input.

title: [day scheduler] Add accessible event activation and keyboard movement contracts
description: DayScheduler renders visual event divs only and exposes no event callback, custom event content, focus semantics, selection state, or keyboard move/resize contract. The office-perf Day Planner therefore reimplements scheduler blocks and HTML5 drag/drop in application code; its clickable/draggable divs have no keyboard-equivalent workflow. This is a universal interaction responsibility, not an app-local workaround. Consumer finding: office-perf op-03ix/op-99t7.
acceptance_criteria: Extend DayScheduler with stable event identity plus optional typed activation/selection and move callbacks, an accessible event label/description contract, focusable native or correctly-keyed event controls, Enter/Space activation, and documented keyboard movement with configurable snap/range bounds and disabled/read-only behavior. Provide a direct custom-content escape hatch only if needed for consumer parity without exposing layout internals. Keep pointer behavior and pure lane geometry intact, respect reduced motion/focus styling, and add unit, DOM, browser keyboard, demo and backwards-compatibility tests. Migrate office-perf Day Planner to the component without losing optimistic rollback or appointment read-only behavior.
close_reason: DayScheduler interaction contract: on_event_activate/selected_event/on_event_move/on_event_resize/event_content, focusable role=button blocks with accessible names, index-keyed nodes so focus survives moves. Commit eccb48e; reactivity test day_scheduler_keyboard_moves_event.

This surfaced in office-perf's production Task Queue after migrating from a hand-shaped Table.
