title: SlaChip: fmt_duration lost d2d-ui's overflow clamp in the port, so a multi-year breach wrapped out of the pill
description:
FIXED 2026-07-31 (raised from 4iiz-Office op-jmxb).

THE DEFECT: against real data every breached row in the Office Performance Consultant Task Queue rendered its SLA chip as two lines -- "+1981d 13h" then "over" -- with the word "over" sitting on or below the pill's red border. Twelve of twelve visible rows. The breach magnitudes were genuine (+1981d, +1785d, +1462d ... from 2021-2023 due dates); the number was right and the chip could not hold it.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE FORMAT, IT IS THE COMMENT. sla_chip_fmt_duration said "Ported verbatim from d2d-ui's fmt_duration". It was not verbatim. d2d-ui carries a clamp this port dropped:
    if days > MAX_DISPLAY_DAYS { format!(">{MAX_DISPLAY_DAYS}d") }   // 99
added by 4iiz-Office op-4tr for exactly this failure. The desktop had already solved it; the web port arrived without the guard; and the "verbatim" claim is what kept the gap invisible, because anyone comparing the two would trust the comment rather than the code.

WHY NOT SIMPLY RE-ADD THE CLAMP: ">99d" is bounded, and it is bounded by DISCARDING ORDER -- 100 days overdue and 5.4 years overdue both render ">99d", so in a queue sorted by urgency the rows that most need distinguishing become identical at the very top of the list.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD -- precision that degrades with magnitude:
    >= 365d -> "5.4y"     >= 10d -> "364d"     > 0d -> "9d 5h"
    >= 10h  -> "23h"      > 0h   -> "9h 30m"   else -> "45m"
The finer unit is dropped exactly when the coarser one reaches two digits, because that is where it stops informing and starts costing the width that broke the pill. This BOUNDS the breached label at 12 chars ("+9d 23h over") for ANY input -- the same width the design already fits. The old form had no bound at all, so it was permanently one unusually stale record away from breaking again.
Also added whitespace-nowrap to the chip: the formatter bounds what is normally produced, the class makes "should never wrap" into "cannot wrap".

TESTS: 4 new, including every_label_fits_the_one_line_pill, which sweeps ~1 minute to 100 years in both directions and asserts the 12-char bound -- a property test, not an example. Full suite 1957 + doctests green, clippy -D warnings clean.
VERIFIED in a real browser against the live dev mirror: all 12 rows now read "+5.4y over" / "+4.9y over" / ... on one line inside the border. Screenshot in 4iiz-Office docs/ui-audit/op-jmxb-sla-chip-fixed.png.

FOLLOW-UP FILED in Rust-DeskApp: d2d-ui should adopt the same scheme so the two surfaces stop disagreeing about the same number.
close_reason: Shipped in this working tree: src/components/sla_chip/style.rs (degrading-precision fmt_duration + a corrected doc header that records the dropped clamp) and component.rs (whitespace-nowrap). 4 new tests including the 12-char property sweep; 1957 + doctests green; clippy -D warnings clean; verified in a browser against live data.

title: Layout-audit sweep does not return through the Rust CDP binding
description:
Blocks ldui-dg2 from being wired into verify-full.

The sweep LOGIC is verified. Run verbatim through Chrome DevTools against the
live demo it completes in ~1.5s per page and produces correct results across all
six audited pages (button/alert/card/tab/data-table/kanban): 0 overlaps, and the
grid/internal counts that are now the committed ceilings in
tests/layout_audit_smoke.rs.

What does not work is shipping that same JS into the page from the Rust test:

  tests/common/mod.rs::layout_report -> h.page().evaluate*(SWEEP_JS)

Symptoms tried, in order:
  1. evaluate() with '(() => {...})()'  -> HANGS with no error, no panic, past
     the 60s wait_for_selector budgets, i.e. it is not the mount wait.
  2. evaluate() with 'JSON.stringify(function(){...}())' -> still hangs.
  3. evaluate_function() with 'function () {...}'   -> fast, clean error:
     -32000 'Given expression does not evaluate to a function'
  4. evaluate_function() with '(function () {...})' -> same -32000.

NOT an environment problem: the pre-existing reactivity_smoke suite passes 6/6
in 17.5s against the same server, same harness, same Chrome. It only ever
evaluates SHORT expressions (~50 bytes) via the same page().evaluate.

Leading hypothesis, untested: expression SIZE. SWEEP_JS is ~7KB; every call that
works elsewhere is tiny. Worth testing with a long-but-trivial expression (e.g. a
6KB '1+1+1+...') to separate size from shape before touching the sweep again.
Second hypothesis: chromiumoxide's Evaluation heuristic picking callFunctionOn
for a string starting with '(' and containing '=>'.

Until this is fixed:
- layout_step() exists and 'cargo xtask test-layout' is wired, but it is
  deliberately NOT added to verify-full -- a hanging step would hang the gate.
- The tests keep their #[ignore], so a bare 'cargo test' is unaffected.

Do not 'fix' this by loosening the assertions. The assertions are right; the
transport is not.
close_reason: block_on-inside-async deadlock in pixelproof-web's Harness::drop, fixed in PixelProof 126acfe. Drop went from infinite hang to 363us; layout suite passes 8/8. All three hypotheses on the ticket were wrong -- the sweep transported fine all along, the hang was in teardown.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
FIXED. Root cause was not in this repo, and not any of the three hypotheses
on this ticket.

The bug is a classic block_on-inside-async deadlock in the sibling PixelProof
crate:

  pixelproof-web/src/harness.rs  impl Drop for Harness
    let _ = futures::executor::block_on(self.browser.close());

browser.close() posts a message to the CDP handler task and awaits a oneshot
reply, so it can only resolve while that handler is being polled. Drop runs
inside the async test body, so block_on parks the very runtime thread the
handler needs. close() never completes; the drop deadlocks with Chrome pinned
at 100% CPU.

What made it hard: the failure is in TEARDOWN. Every assertion had already
passed; cargo just never got to print 'ok' because the test function could not
return. It is indistinguishable from a hung request unless you bracket the
phases. A probe that printed around each step settled it in one run:

  harness_at       1.71s   ok
  evaluate tiny    0.85ms  ok
  evaluate sweep   2.83ms  ok   <- the sweep was ALWAYS fine
  drop harness     hangs        <- the actual bug

All three hypotheses recorded here were wrong, and worth recording as wrong:
- Expression SIZE: disproved. A 6834-byte expression returned in 1.56ms.
- chromiumoxide's function-detection heuristic: not implicated.
- evaluate vs evaluate_function: a red herring I introduced myself while
  chasing the hang. evaluate() works; switching to evaluate_function() was
  what produced the -32000 'Given expression does not evaluate to a function',
  because CDP callFunctionOn rejects a parenthesised function expression.
  Reverted to evaluate().

Fix (PixelProof 126acfe): Drop no longer blocks — it aborts the handler task
and lets Browser's own Drop terminate the child, which is safe because
chromiumoxide spawns it with kill_on_drop. Added Harness::close() for callers
wanting the clean CDP handshake. Drop went from an infinite hang to 363us.

Likely also the cause of the stale ldui-pp-profile-* directories these suites
leave behind (93 of them at one point) -- the browser was never closing
cleanly.

Result: tests/layout_audit_smoke.rs now passes 8/8 in 26.6s, both directly and
through 'cargo xtask test-layout' with its own spawned server. layout_step()
is now wired into verify-full.

title: Migrate off daisyUI 4 form classes (form-control / label-text) — they are no-ops in daisyUI 5
description:
Found while working ldui-6qb. Blocks its form-control requirement.

daisyUI 5 REMOVED .form-control, .label-text and .label-text-alt. Verified:
  grep -c 'form-control' demo/node_modules/daisyui/daisyui.css  ->  0

The repo still uses them 206 times:
  src/       81 occurrences across 14 files
  demo/src/  125 occurrences

These classes now do NOTHING. The consequence is not cosmetic: .form-control
supplied 'display: flex; flex-direction: column' to the wrapper. Without it a
<label class="form-control w-full"> falls back to display:inline, so w-full is
inert and the label text and its input flow inline instead of stacking. Example:
src/components/login_screen/component.rs:330.

Why this blocks ldui-6qb: that ticket requires 'label-to-input gap (4-8) must be
clearly smaller than the gap to the next field group (24+)' -- the article's
opening example. Right now there IS no controlled label-to-input gap to check,
because the class that would establish the stacking context is dead. The rule
cannot be satisfied or asserted until the wrapper actually lays out.

Replacement in daisyUI 5 is .fieldset + .label. Note .fieldset ships
gap: calc(0.25rem * 1.5) = 6px, which is OFF our canonical scale -- decide
whether to accept daisyUI's internal value or override it to 4 or 8px as part
of this work.

Scope: replace the dead classes, verify the rendered stacking, then re-check the
ldui-6qb form-control rule against something that actually lays out.

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md

title: Decide whether 2px is a sanctioned decorative sub-unit
description:
Blocks ldui-dg2. Surfaced by the ldui-lua audit (finding F3).

9 of the 14 off-4-grid occurrences in the web source are 2px, and every one is
a decorative accent rather than layout spacing:

  login_screen/component.rs:282      space-y-0.5
  metric_row/component.rs:38         gap-0.5
  result_list/component.rs:56,189,221  gap-0.5
  toolbar/component.rs:62,291        h-0.5, -bottom-0.5  (underline bar)
  vertical_steps/component.rs:56,59,119,133  w-0.5, mt-0.5  (connector rail)

The desktop scale already carries an off-grid 2px (ui_tokens BADGE_PADDING_V),
so sanctioning 2px would be an honest codification of existing practice on both
faces rather than a concession.

If we sanction it, the canonical scale becomes 2,4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,96 with
2 flagged decorative-only (never a container padding, gap between siblings, or
stack rhythm value). If we do not, these 9 rules need migrating to 4px, which
will visibly thicken indicator dots and connector rails.

Decide BEFORE ldui-dg2 builds the detector, or the checker flags 9 legitimate
rules as violations on day one.

Remaining genuine violations either way: 6px (data_table w-1.5 x3,
segmented_bar h-1.5 x2, tree gap-1.5 x2) and 14px (vertical_steps w-3.5/h-3.5
x2).

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md
close_reason: Decided: 2px is NOT sanctioned as spacing. Scale stays 4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,96; sub-4 values are strokes with their own token family and are excluded from the spacing checker. The 7 genuine spacing violations were migrated to the 4px floor; off-grid is now 3/443 (0.7%), all stroke-role. Unblocks ldui-dg2.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
DECISION: do NOT sanction 2px as a spacing unit. The canonical spacing scale
stays 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96.

Rationale. My audit initially recommended sanctioning it, but inspecting the 14
LIVE off-grid uses (the earlier list included doc-comment @source lines) shows
they split cleanly into two groups rather than forming one decorative class:

STROKES / TRACKS / HIT-TARGETS -- not spacing, keep the values, give them the
stroke family from ldui-1mx and exclude from the spacing checker:
  toolbar/component.rs:291        h-0.5, -bottom-0.5  2px active underline
  vertical_steps/component.rs:119 w-0.5               2px connector rail
  segmented_bar/component.rs:77   h-1.5               6px bar track
  data_table/header.rs:130        w-1.5               6px invisible resize hit target

GENUINE SPACING -- only 5 live uses, migrate to the 4px floor:
  login_screen/component.rs:282   space-y-0.5 -> space-y-1
  metric_row/style.rs:64          gap-0.5     -> gap-1
  result_list/component.rs:189    gap-0.5     -> gap-1
  result_list/component.rs:221    gap-0.5     -> gap-1
  vertical_steps/component.rs:133 mt-0.5      -> mt-1
  tree/component.rs:280           gap-1.5     -> gap-2   (6px, same class of fix)

SIZE, genuinely off-grid:
  vertical_steps/component.rs:114 w-3.5 h-3.5 (14px) -> w-4 h-4 (16px)

This is strictly better than sanctioning 2px: the checker gets one unambiguous
rule (spacing must be on the scale; strokes are a separate family with separate
tokens) instead of a scale with a special-case member that needs a
'decorative-only' caveat the checker cannot verify. It also matches ldui-1mx's
existing instruction -- 'do not chase sub-4 values: 1px and 2px borders are
legitimate strokes, not bad spacing' -- without letting that leak into gaps.

Cost is 7 one-line edits. Unblocks ldui-dg2.

title: Reconcile named layout dimensions between the desktop and web faces
description:
Surfaced by the ldui-lua audit (finding F6). Distinct from migrating utilities onto a scale.

The two faces AGREE on the spacing scale but DISAGREE on the named dimensions
ui_tokens already defines. This is the part that actually makes desktop and web
look like one product.

  Role                  ui_tokens   web              status
  NAV_ACCENT_WIDTH      3           w-1 = 4          diverge
  RIGHT_PANEL_WIDTH     280         w-48/w-64 = 192/256   diverge
  TABLE_ROW_HEIGHT      40          not expressed    absent
  TABLE_HEADER_HEIGHT   36          not expressed    absent
  CARD_ROW_HEIGHT       120         not expressed    absent
  CARD_PADDING/GAP      16          daisyUI default  absent
  STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT     28          content-sized    absent
  BADGE_PADDING_H/V     8 / 2       daisyUI default  absent

The values 28, 36, 120 and 280 appear nowhere in the web source.

Agreeing already: TITLE_BAR/HEADER_HEIGHT 48, NAV_RAIL_WIDTH 64,
NAV_ITEM_SIZE 48, NAV_ICON_SIZE 24.

Decide per row whether the desktop value, the web value, or a third number is
right, then pin it in ui_tokens and reference it from both faces. Note that
card and badge inherit daisyUI internal padding that is not on our scale and
not under our control -- decide whether to override or accept.

Also: the calc(100vh - 260px) / calc(100vh - 200px) viewport offsets in
data_table and gantt hardcode an assumed chrome height, which is exactly the
HEADER_HEIGHT + STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT sum the tokens already name.

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md
close_reason: Took the two the web can own (RIGHT_PANEL_WIDTH -> 280px, NAV_ACCENT_WIDTH -> 3px via the stroke token), both verified in the browser. The table/card/badge/status-bar dimensions are daisyUI-owned on the web and are explicitly out of scope. BADGE_PADDING_V fed back as Rust-DeskApp beads-b2nw.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
ANALYSIS DONE, decisions NOT taken -- they are yours, and they change pixels
in two shipped products.

The rule I applied everywhere else (adopt where it is a no-op, flag where it
is a visual change) leaves these needing a call:

ALREADY AGREE, nothing to do:
  TITLE_BAR_HEIGHT / HEADER_HEIGHT  48  = web 48
  NAV_RAIL_WIDTH                    64  = web w-16
  NAV_ITEM_SIZE                     48  = web h-12/w-12
  NAV_ICON_SIZE                     24  = web h-6

PARTLY RESOLVED by the ldui-1mx work:
  NAV_ACCENT_WIDTH  was 3.0 and off the 4px grid among the named dimensions,
  with nothing testing it. It now derives from stroke::ACCENT -- same value,
  correctly classified, and a new test grid-checks every other named
  dimension. The web still draws this accent as w-1 (4px). Making them agree
  means moving the web to 3px, a 1px visual change on the nav rail.

NEED A DECISION:
  RIGHT_PANEL_WIDTH   280 vs web w-48 (192) / w-64 (256). Note the web does
                      not really pin this -- AppShellSidePanel takes a width
                      prop and 192/256 are the documented examples. Cheapest
                      convergence is to default it to w-70 (280px, which
                      Tailwind's numeric scale generates) and leave the prop.
  TABLE_ROW_HEIGHT    40  -- not expressed on the web at all; daisyUI's
                      .table sizes rows from cell padding. Adopting means
                      overriding daisyUI.
  TABLE_HEADER_HEIGHT 36  -- same, and 36 is off our own canonical scale.
  CARD_ROW_HEIGHT     120 -- not expressed on the web.
  STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT   28  -- AppShellStatusBar is content-sized (px-4 gap-2,
                      no height). 28 is also off the canonical scale.
  BADGE_PADDING_V     2   -- genuine off-grid padding in the shared crate. I
                      left it and marked it a known exemption in the new
                      grid test rather than change how every desktop badge
                      renders as a side effect.

The values 28, 36, 120 and 280 appear NOWHERE in the web source, so none of
this is drift that crept in -- the two faces simply answered different
questions. Three of the desktop values (28, 36, and the 3px accent) are
themselves off the canonical scale, so 'make the web match the desktop' is not
automatically the right answer.

Also relevant: data_table and gantt hardcode calc(100vh - 260px) and
calc(100vh - 200px), which are hand-computed chrome heights. Whatever
HEADER_HEIGHT + STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT settle at, those should be derived from

Recommendation: take RIGHT_PANEL_WIDTH and NAV_ACCENT_WIDTH (cheap, low risk),
and explicitly declare the table/card/status-bar dimensions OUT of scope for
the web on the grounds that daisyUI owns them -- rather than leaving them
looking like unfinished convergence.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
DONE for everything the web side can decide; the rest is explicitly out of scope.

TAKEN, both verified rendering in the browser:
  RIGHT_PANEL_WIDTH   280  -- AppShellSidePanel now documented as w-70 (280px,

title: Add automated spacing + overlap checks to the PixelProof web suite
description:
Workstream D, web half. Turn the article's manual '10-minute spacing audit' into a permanent test, reusing the reactivity-test seam that already exists (?pp-freeze=1 + window.__APP_DEBUG__ -- see the web-pixelproof-parity memory).

Three assertions over the rendered DOM, via getBoundingClientRect:
1. Overlap: no two visible sibling elements' boxes may intersect. This is the regression test for the entire class of bug where a component grows and its neighbour does not move.
2. Grid: every gap between vertically adjacent siblings, and every inset from a container to its first child, must be a member of the canonical scale. Report violations with selector and value.
3. Internal <= external: for every container, padding must be <= the gap to its siblings. This is the check that catches two cards visually merging.

The desktop half builds the same three checks over its SemanticNode tree via /api/dom; the rect data is equivalent, so the assertion logic should read the same on both faces. Land the detector BEFORE the token migration so the backlog is enumerated rather than guessed.
close_reason: Suite passes 8/8 via cargo xtask test-layout and is wired into verify-full. Zero overlaps and zero off-grid gaps we own; remaining counts are daisyUI's 6px internal gaps, held as committed ceilings.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
From the ldui-lua audit -- the extractor spec already exists.

The audit's Tailwind-utility extractor is documented step-by-step in the Method
section of doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md. It was a throwaway Python
script and is deliberately NOT committed: per doc/ci-cd.md's two-layer rule,
detector logic belongs in the Rust xtask crate. Port it there rather than
inheriting a script.

Two traps the audit hit, both of which will bite the port:
1. A raw px/rem regex that allows whitespace reads 'bg-base-200 px-4' as the
   raw value '200 px'. Require no space and no trailing '-'.
2. /// doc comments quote class strings both as usage examples and as
   '@source inline(...)' Tailwind safelist hints. Counting them inflates
   results by 21% (839 -> 443 measurable). Tag and exclude them.

Also note w-px/h-px/gap-px are 1px hairline dividers, not spacing -- classify
separately or they read as off-grid violations.

BLOCKED on ldui-mai.2 (the 2px decorative sub-unit decision). Without it the
detector flags 9 legitimate accent rules as violations on day one.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
SUBSTANTIALLY DONE, one transport bug open (ldui-mai.5).

BUILT: tests/common/layout_audit.rs (sweep + pure logic + unit tests) and
tests/layout_audit_smoke.rs (6 page assertions + a negative control + a
backlog reporter). 'cargo xtask test-layout' orchestrates the server, sharing
run_browser_suite() with test-reactivity.

The three checks are implemented, plus a fourth the ticket implied but did not
name -- see below.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE DEMO (driven through Chrome DevTools, since the Rust
binding is blocked -- ldui-mai.5). Final measured state, all six pages:

  page          scanned  overlap  grid  internal
  button            71      0       0      0
  alert             39      0       0      0
  card              76      0       0      0
  tab               52      0       0      1
  data-table      1771      0       2      0
  kanban           136      0      34      2

ZERO overlaps and ZERO off-grid gaps that we own. Those are the committed
ceilings.

THREE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES FOUND AND FIXED -- each would have made the
detector useless in a different way:
1. daisyUI 'join' collapses shared borders, so joined buttons overlap by
   exactly 1px. That was 100% of the 24 'overlaps' initially reported
   (23 on data-table, 1 on kanban). Now exempt.
2. 'gap 0' internal>external hits: siblings deliberately flush (card-body
   above card-actions) are sections of one surface, not competing groups.
   Now require a real gap before the rule applies.
3. THE IMPORTANT ONE -- measuring gaps inside a wrapping flex container is
   meaningless: the distance from a short item to the next row is the row-gap
   PLUS the height difference to its tallest neighbour. This produced 19
   phantom '28px gaps' (12px gap + 16px height delta). Before my Section
   change it read 0 only because 8+16=24 happened to land on the scale --
   i.e. it was silently wrong from the start and luck was hiding it. Flex and
   grid containers are now checked by reading their DECLARED row/column-gap.

ADDED CHECK 3a. The ticket's check 3 is 'container padding vs gap to its
siblings'. The desktop Kanban finding it cites is actually the other
direction: a CHILD's padding vs the gap BETWEEN children. Both are now
checked. 3a is what confirms the ldui-6qb Kanban fix landed -- kanban's card
violations are gone.

WHAT THE REMAINING NUMBERS ARE: the 'grid' counts are daisyUI's own declared
6px gaps (calc(0.25rem * 1.5)) inside .btn/.label/.fieldset. 6px is off our
canonical scale and is not ours to change without overriding daisyUI
internals. kanban's 2 internal are daisyUI's .mockup-window (20px padding,
also off-scale) against a 16px section gap.

A NOTE THE DESKTOP HALF NEEDS: the desktop suite warns a clean sweep is only a
ratchet because a semantic rect is a DECLARATION. getBoundingClientRect is a
real post-layout measurement, so that caveat does not transfer -- an overlap
reported here really renders. The web half is the stronger of the two.

NOT wired into verify-full until ldui-mai.5 is fixed; a hanging step would
hang the gate. 'cargo xtask test-layout' runs it explicitly.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
DONE and now enforced. ldui-mai.5 is fixed, so the suite runs end to end:

  cargo xtask test-layout   ->  8 passed in 26.6s (own spawned server)

layout_step() is wired into verify-full. Final measured state, which the Rust

scanned counts: 71 / 39 / 76 / 52 / 1771 / 136):

  page          scanned  overlap  grid  internal
  button            71      0       0      0
  alert             39      0       0      0
  card              76      0       0      0
  tab               52      0       0      0
  data-table      1771      0       2      0
  kanban           136      0      34      2

ZERO overlaps and zero off-grid gaps that we own. Every remaining grid hit is
daisyUI's declared 6px gap (calc(0.25rem * 1.5)) inside .btn and .label --
reported with selector and value, exactly as the ticket asked, and not ours to
change without overriding daisyUI internals. kanban's 2 internal are daisyUI's
.mockup-window. Those are the committed ceilings and may only be lowered.

One repair worth recording: the flex/grid declared-gap fix had been lost when
the concurrent session reverted this tree, so the suite briefly reported 0
off-grid everywhere -- a FALSE clean, because without it the checker measures
gaps inside wrapping flex containers (meaningless: row-gap plus the height

title: Drive web line-height from the shared typography::LINE_* ramp
description:
Workstream A, web half. Rust-DeskApp gained a grid-aligned line-height ramp in ui-tokens (typography::LINE_DISPLAY/TITLE/SUBTITLE/BODY/CAPTION/SMALL = 36/28/24/20/16/16, plus line_for_size()), and the desktop renderer now pins DirectWrite to UNIFORM line spacing so line boxes stop being fractional font metrics.

The web side inherits the same tokens through the path dep. Do the equivalent:
- Emit the LINE_* ramp as CSS custom properties (--line-body etc.) alongside the existing spacing scale.
- Set an explicit line-height on every type-ramp class instead of inheriting the browser/Tailwind default, so a stack of N lines lands on the grid on both faces.
- Verify a paragraph of body text occupies exactly N * 20px, not N * (font metric).

Why it is first: on the desktop side three different line heights (a hardcoded 19.0, a hardcoded 20.0, and a runtime measurement) were the direct cause of the reported inconsistent line spacing. Pin the rhythm before migrating any other token, or the visual baselines get burned twice.
close_reason: Spacing + stroke + radius + grid-aligned type ramp emitted as CSS custom properties and as a generated Tailwind @theme; every ramp step pins an explicit line height. Verified behaviour-preserving by diffing the compiled stylesheet.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION from the ldui-lua audit (finding F2).

This ticket says to emit the LINE_* ramp 'alongside the existing spacing scale'.
There is no existing spacing scale on the web side.

src/tokens/preamble.rs IS genuinely wired to ui_tokens -- an upstream change
flows through without hand-copy -- but it emits only:
  --ld-duration-{fast,normal,slow}
  --ld-ease-{linear,standard,decelerate,accelerate}
  --ld-elevation-{2,4,8,16,64}

No spacing, no line-height, no typography.

So this ticket has to add the FIRST --ld-space-* block as well as --ld-line-*.
If it does not, ldui-1mx has nothing to map the Tailwind theme onto and will be
blocked. Sizing the work accordingly.

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
DONE. Implemented in src/tokens/preamble.rs + styles/tokens.css.

Two emission paths, because they serve different consumers:

1. src/tokens/preamble.rs (runtime, <style> on :root) now emits, alongside the
   pre-existing motion/elevation vars:
     --ld-space-xxs .. --ld-space-huge        (the FIRST spacing custom
                                               properties on the web side)
     --ld-stroke-hairline .. -emphasis
     --ld-radius-control/card/badge/pill
     --ld-text-<step> + --ld-line-<step>      for all 6 ramp steps
   plus a .ld-text-<step> class per step pinning BOTH font-size and
   line-height, so no ramp step inherits the browser or Tailwind default.

2. styles/tokens.css (build time, Tailwind @theme) generated by the new
   'cargo xtask gen-tokens', imported by demo/input.css. This is what actually
   drives the utilities the 424 component files already use.

UNITS -- the part that nearly went wrong. My first pass emitted the tokens' raw
DIPs as px. That is a WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text) regression: it pins every font
size and gap against the user's browser font-size preference. Tailwind ships
rem sizes and UNITLESS line-height ratios precisely to avoid this. The
generator now converts DIP -> rem (lossless; every scale step divides 16
exactly) and emits line height as calc(20 / 14) style ratios. Only border
widths stay px -- a hairline must not grow with the type.

VERIFIED behaviour-preserving, not assumed: compiling demo/input.css with and
without the token import yields ZERO semantically different theme values
(script compared every --* declaration, evaluating calc() ratios). Tailwind's
own text-xs/sm/base/xl now resolve through our LINE_* ramp and land on exactly
the values Tailwind already shipped -- they stop being a coincidence.

Acceptance criterion from the ticket ('a paragraph of body text occupies
exactly N * 20px') is locked by
tokens::tests::a_stack_of_n_body_lines_is_exactly_n_times_20px.

12 new tests in src/tokens/tests.rs (39 total in the module, all passing) plus
9 in xtask. Gate green apart from the browser suites.

NOTE: this ticket's premise was wrong and the audit corrected it -- there was no
'existing spacing scale' on the web to sit alongside. This added it.

title: Adopt the shared spacing & vertical-rhythm system in the web UI framework
description:
Port the spacing/sizing rules audited in Rust-DeskApp (docs/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-system-audit.md) to the Leptos/daisyUI face of the framework, so desktop and web share one system rather than two dialects.

SOURCE
- Article: Mohit Phogat, "The Spacing System That Makes Every UI Look More Intentional" (Medium, 2026-06-22).
- Desktop audit + plan: C:\dev\Rust-DeskApp\docs\plans\2026-07-26-spacing-system-audit.md

THE RULES WE ARE ADOPTING
1. One base unit. Every spacing value is a multiple of 8, with 4 as the sanctioned sub-unit. Canonical scale 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96.
2. Internal <= external. A container's padding must be <= the gap between it and its neighbours, or the containers visually merge.
3. Tokens, never raw values. No arbitrary px/rem in a margin, padding or gap.
4. Deterministic line height. One grid-aligned line-height per type-ramp step; no per-component guesses.
5. The audit is automated, not manual (see child issue on the DOM overlap/grid checks).

WHY THIS LANDS ON THE WEB SIDE TOO
leptos-daisyui-rs consumes ui-tokens from Rust-DeskApp via a path dep, so the token work done there (extended spacing scale, new line-height ramp, stroke family) arrives here for free -- but only if components actually reference the tokens instead of hardcoding Tailwind spacing utilities. The desktop audit found the tokens existed and were used in 5 of ~105 component files; the same question has to be asked here before assuming we are clean.

SCOPE
- Audit the 96 components for off-scale spacing and for Tailwind utilities used in place of tokens.
- Map ui_tokens::spacing + the new typography::LINE_* ramp onto CSS custom properties / a Tailwind theme extension, so one scale drives both faces.
- Enforce the internal-to-external rule where components nest (Card, Modal, Drawer, Table, Form control + label + helper text).
- Add the automated spacing/overlap checks to the existing PixelProof web suite (see web-pixelproof-parity memory: the ?pp-freeze=1 seam + window.__APP_DEBUG__ oracle already exist).

NOT IN SCOPE
- Adopting upstream's workspace restructure (Option B still holds: stay flat, cherry-pick).
- Changing the daisyUI theme palette. This is spacing and sizing only.

SEQUENCING
Mirror the desktop order: line-height determinism first, then the automated detector, then the token migration. Migrating tokens before the rhythm is pinned changes pixels without fixing anything and burns the visual baselines twice.
close_reason: All five rules satisfied and enforced; verify-full 12/12 including the layout audit and the real wasm build. Zero overlaps, zero off-grid gaps and zero internal>external violations that we own across the six audited pages. Three pre-existing bugs found and fixed along the way (daisyUI 4 form classes, the pixelproof-web drop deadlock, the CRLF drift check).

title: DataTable: sort comparator compares cells as strings, so money/number columns sort wrong ($1,000 < $900)
description:
Requested by 4iiz-inventory (bead bd_4iiz-inventory-3f5.5). Paired with the same defect in the d2d-ui sibling (Rust-DeskApp beads-gaf0) -- please keep the two designs aligned.

## The bug

DataTable's sort comparator compares cell values as STRINGS:

    // components/data_table/component.rs, sorted_indices memo
    let a_val = data_vec.get(a).and_then(|row| row.get(col_id)).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
    let b_val = data_vec.get(b).and_then(|row| row.get(col_id)).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
    match sort_order.get() {
        SortOrder::Asc  => a_val.cmp(b_val),
        SortOrder::Desc => b_val.cmp(a_val),
    }

So any column holding a formatted number sorts LEXICOGRAPHICALLY:

    "$1,000"  <  "$900"     because '1' < '9'
    "525"     <  "9"        days-in-stage
    "10%"     <  "9%"

Since Column::new() is SORTABLE BY DEFAULT (only Column::new_non_sortable opts out), any
consumer who puts money or durations in a table gets a wrong sort with no warning. That is
worse than no sort: the user believes they are looking at the largest balances and they are
not.

## What this component already gets RIGHT (please preserve it)

It sorts an INDEX PERMUTATION (`sorted_indices`) and never mutates `data`, so row identity
survives sorting by construction. The d2d-ui sibling mutates rows in place and corrupts its
own selection state as a result (Rust-DeskApp beads-e476). This design is the correct one --
the only thing wrong here is the comparator.

## Suggested fix

Give the column a sort TYPE, or the cell a typed key. Options:

  (a) add `sort_as: SortAs::{Text, Number, Date}` (default Text) to Column, and parse/compare
      accordingly -- Number strips currency symbols, thousands separators, %, and compares as
      f64 with a total order (handle NaN/absent deterministically);
  (b) allow a per-column comparator callback;
  (c) let a row supply a typed sort key per column alongside the display string.

(a) is the smallest change for consumers and matches how our columns are actually declared.

## Acceptance

- ["$900", "$1,000", "$85"] with sort_as: Number sorts ascending to ["$85", "$900", "$1,000"].
- ["9", "525", "10"] sorts ascending to ["9", "10", "525"].
- Text columns are unchanged and remain the default.
- Empty / absent cells sort consistently and are NOT conflated with zero -- an em dash means
  "not measured", which is a different thing from 0 and must not sort as 0.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Fixed. Design (option (a) from the report), so the d2d-ui sibling (beads-gaf0) can mirror it:

- New `SortAs { Text (default), Number, Date }` in `src/components/data_table/sort.rs`; `Column.sort_as` + builder `Column::with_sort_as(SortAs::Number)`. Text is the default, so every existing table is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `parse_number` strips currency symbols, thousands separators, %, and reads accounting parens as negative: "$1,000.50" -> 1000.5, "(1,234)" -> -1234, "9%" -> 9. `parse_date` takes ISO-8601 (date or datetime) and US M/D/YYYY, packing to a comparable YYYYMMDDhhmmss key.
- MISSING != ZERO: a blank / em-dash / unparseable cell is missing and sorts LAST in BOTH directions (spreadsheet behaviour), so a desc sort still opens on the largest real value instead of a wall of dashes. Comparison uses f64::total_cmp, so the comparator stays a valid total order.
- The index-permutation sort (the thing this component already got right) is untouched: only the comparator changed, so row identity / selected_rows still survive a sort by construction.

Acceptance verified in the browser (demo /components/data-table, new 'Typed Sorting' section), not just in unit tests:
- Balance asc: ($1,250.50) | $85 | $900 | $1,000  -- and desc reverses it.
- Days asc: 9, 10, 525, then the em dash; desc: 525, 10, 9, and the em dash STILL last.
- Opened (Date) sorts chronologically both ways.
23 unit tests in sort.rs cover the parsers, the missing-value rule and the acceptance cases.

title: .beads/issues.jsonl export is stale — closures live only in the local Dolt DB
description: The git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl does not reflect the Dolt DB. It contains 23 issues, all status=closed, and does NOT contain ldui-b08 (closed 2026-07-10) or ldui-e8o (created 2026-07-10). So the JSONL export -- the git-backed recovery path -- has stopped keeping up with bd writes. Risk: if the local Dolt DB in .beads/dolt/ldui is lost, recent issue state is unrecoverable from git. 'bd dolt push' to the fork now works (see ldui-e8o), which mitigates but does not fix this: the JSONL is what a fresh clone reads. Investigate auto-flush (config: no-auto-flush, flush-debounce) and whether the pre-commit hook that used to run 'bd sync --flush-only' was disabled by the bd v1.0 upgrade that removed the 'bd sync' subcommand (see kv.memory.bd-v1-pre-commit-hook-fix -- that memory notes this repo's .git/hooks/pre-commit still has the bug and was never patched).
acceptance_criteria: A fresh 'bd export' (or the commit hook) writes ldui-b08 and ldui-e8o into .beads/issues.jsonl, and the file is committed. Subsequent bd close operations update the JSONL without manual intervention.
notes: DIAGNOSED, not fixed. 'bd export' itself works: a probe export to a temp file yields 77 issues (2 open, 75 closed) and DOES contain ldui-b08, ldui-e8o and ldui-izn. The tracked .beads/issues.jsonl has only 23 (all closed). So the export code path is healthy; what is broken is the auto-flush that should refresh the tracked file after mutations. Ruled out: the stale 'bd sync --flush-only' pre-commit hook theory -- core.hooksPath=.githooks, and no hook under .githooks/, .git/hooks/ or .beads/hooks/ references 'bd sync'. Deliberately NOT auto-fixed: overwriting issues.jsonl (23 -> 77 entries) at session end could disturb beads' import path, and off-machine durability is already restored now that 'bd dolt push' to the fork works (ldui-e8o). Next step: work out why auto-flush is not firing (config keys no-auto-flush / flush-debounce, and note .beads/beads.left.jsonl + export-state.json exist, suggesting a compaction/split scheme that may explain the 23-issue subset). Then run 'bd export --output .beads/issues.jsonl' and commit.
close_reason: Root cause was NOT a broken auto-flush. The .githooks/pre-commit hook intentionally early-exits for the Dolt backend (grep '"backend":"dolt"' -> exit 0), because the Dolt backend syncs via 'bd dolt push/pull', not JSONL. The repo migrated to Dolt on 2026-05-28 (last issues.jsonl commit f2caf01), so the tracked JSONL froze at a 23-issue snapshot by design while the DB grew to 77. The 'closures live only in local DB' risk was real only until the Dolt remote was repointed to the fork (ldui-e8o) -- 'bd dolt push' now backs everything up off-machine. Resolution: refreshed .beads/issues.jsonl to the current 77-issue state via 'bd export' and committed it (665acd4) as a human-readable/PR-visible snapshot. Going forward it's a manual convenience mirror ('bd export --output .beads/issues.jsonl' when git should reflect current state); the authoritative backup is 'bd dolt push'. Verified DB intact after export (open beads unchanged).

title: markdown ThemeContext signals disposed while global observer holds them (AiChat WASM panic)
description: Browser smoke (ldui-0wf) found: sending any message in the AiChat demo panics the whole WASM app: 'At src/markdown/theme.rs:46:34 you tried to access a reactive value defined at theme.rs:100:18 but it has already been disposed', followed by RuntimeError: unreachable and a follow-on 'RefCell already borrowed' panic. Root cause: use_theme() creates RwSignals owned by the first calling component's reactive owner (theme.rs:100-101) and registers them with install_theme_observer (global, once per document). AiChat rebuilds MessageBubble/MarkdownView on every poll tick, so the first bubble's owner is disposed while the global observer + subsequent palette() calls (theme.rs:46) still reference the dead signals. Fix: give ThemeContext signals document lifetime (create under a detached/leaked root owner or thread_local singleton), independent of any component scope.
close_reason: Both fixed in 05260cd and verified live in the browser smoke session. ldui-i4t: ThemeContext is now a thread_local document-lifetime singleton whose signals are created under a deliberately parentless leaked Owner (document_root_owner via Owner unset/new/set), so the global MutationObserver can't outlive them — AiChat send no longer panics; reviewer verified the ownership trick against reactive_graph 0.2.14 source; regression test added in 44d7c52. ldui-4i0: performance.memory now read as a property via js_sys::Reflect::get (Performance web-sys feature added) — no more per-tick TypeError. Live re-verify: console fully clean on all pages, 1725 lib tests.

title: EntityTable: focus region is tabindex=-1, so a scrolling table with non-interactive rows has no keyboard-focusable element (axe scrollable-region-focusable)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by 4iiz-etl's visual gate at 390x844 (axe-core scrollable-region-focusable, blocking) on Jobs field-detail, job-report-rendered and report-rendered.

THE REGION (component.rs ~2030): <div role="region" tabindex="-1" data-entity-focus-region="true" class="... overflow-auto ...">. Rows get tabindex=0 only when interactive (~3134, tabindex=interactive.then_some(0)), i.e. when on_row_activate/selection is wired.

So a table that (a) scrolls - viewport_fit max_height with more rows than fit, or the compact presentation on a narrow viewport - and (b) has non-interactive rows, has NO keyboard-reachable element inside its scroll container. axe: 'Element should have focusable content / Element should be focusable'. A keyboard user cannot scroll it.

SUGGESTED FIX: make the region tabindex=0 whenever rows are not interactive (roving focus on rows covers the interactive case), or always tabindex=0 with the existing focusin bookkeeping tolerating focus on the region itself. The consumer-side pattern this replaced (a role=region tabindex=0 wrapper, 4iiz-etl's .etl-table-region) passed the same rule.

Research-only from the consumer side; the change is this repo's to make.
close_reason: Scroll region tabindex now derived from row interactivity (entity_region_tabindex): 0 when rows are non-interactive (region is the tab stop), -1 when rows are interactive (roving row stop stays the only one). Browser proof scrolling_region_with_non_interactive_rows_is_keyboard_reachable passed on first execution inside verify-full's test-client-snapshot lane (22/22): tabindex=0, region.focus() takes focus, axe scrollable-region-focusable clean on the scrolling viewport-fit fixture; interactive list keeps -1.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Fix: the scroll region's tabindex is now derived from row interactivity (entity_region_tabindex, pure + unit-tested): rows interactive (on_row_activate or selection) keep the region at -1 so the roving row stop remains the only one; non-interactive rows make the region tabindex=0 so a scrolling table is keyboard-reachable. The existing focusin bookkeeping already tolerates focus on the region itself (focus_record_from_event returns None when the target is not a row action). Browser proof appended to entity_table_smoke: viewport-fit fixture (non-interactive, 17 rows in a 180px budget => scrolls) asserts tabindex=0, region.focus() takes focus, zero rows are tab stops, role/aria-label present, and axe rule scrollable-region-focusable scoped to the fixture reports nothing; the interactive client-snapshot list asserts tabindex=-1 with >=1 row stop.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Design: Collapse gains typed id/name/aria_label props (MaybeProp<String>, mirroring Checkbox). Identity is structural (read once): explicit id wins, else a minted ld-collapse-N; name defaults to the id; the title id is <id>-title and reaches CollapseTitle through a CollapseContext so the input's aria-labelledby resolves to the visible title without consumer wiring.
