title: EntityTable: give generated selection checkboxes deterministic id and name
description: Office Checklists desktop proof uses EntityTableMultiSelection. The generated select-all and row selection checkboxes expose localized aria-labels but neither id nor name, so Chrome reports form controls without an id or name. Consumers cannot repair framework-owned inputs without reaching into the DOM.
acceptance_criteria: EntityTable single- and multi-selection checkboxes receive collision-safe deterministic ids and stable names derived from the table identity and stable row key. The select-all control is included. Existing aria labels, controlled selection semantics, keyboard behavior, and stable row keys remain intact, with component/browser coverage for multiple tables on one page.
close_reason:
Implemented in bcfb9d3. VERIFIED on the final tree (4c91330): native gate 14/14 (3175 tests); entity-table 20/20, reactivity 68/69 (the one failure is ldui-q73d's own), admin-workbench 17/17, server-column-tools 3/3, layout 15/15, style 13/13.

The generated select-all and row checkboxes now carry deterministic id AND name — name separately from id because name is what makes it a real form control, which is what Chrome's report was actually about.

ldui-j6sh's scheme is RESTATED rather than imported (data_table::identity is private and was out of scope; the module doc says so): a once-per-instance minted or caller-supplied prefix, an injective escape of the row key so 'a b', 'a-b' and 'a_b' cannot collide, and {prefix}-select-all / {prefix}-select-row-{encoded key}. Row identity is minted inside the per-key cell, so no index is in scope to alias against — the failure mode where an id re-points at a different row after paging is unrepresentable rather than avoided.

title: Layout and style audits sweep 7 of 40+ demo pages, so every opinionated pattern is unmeasured
description:
Found on 2026-09-01 while verifying the ldui-17rz / ldui-ztgo / ldui-kx7y wave. Three implementers independently predicted that their demo changes would move layout/style page ratchets. NONE moved - because the pages they changed are not swept at all.

THE AUDITED SET IS SMALL AND HAS NOT GROWN WITH THE LIBRARY:

  layout_audit_smoke: /components/{alert,button,card,charts,data-table,kanban,tab}   (7)
  style_audit_smoke:  /components/{button,card,charts,data-table,kanban}             (5)

NOT SWEPT, despite being the newest and most consumer-facing surface:
  /components/section-heading      (gained 3 Sections today, ldui-17rz)
  /components/kpi_strip            (gained two 12-card Sections today, ldui-ztgo)
  /components/record_header        (whole pattern added today, ldui-9d0q)
  /components/selectable-summary   (whole pattern added today, ldui-l5cw)
  /components/search_picker_dialog (gained a Section today, ldui-iq0o)
  /components/day_scheduler, /components/entity-table-grouping, and the rest

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE MISSING NUMBERS. The spacing/typography/shape/depth rules exist because those defects are invisible in review and only show up under measurement - that is the premise of doc/visual-quality/. The OPINIONATED PATTERNS are exactly where this repo has been putting its consumer-facing effort, and they are the part with no computed-style coverage. Today alone the swept pages caught a stale mono-font ratchet and an SVG-text grid drift, while the unswept pages absorbed six new demo Sections with no measurement whatsoever.

It also makes a whole class of implementer report unfalsifiable: "ratchets may move, please re-measure" cannot be confirmed or denied for a page that is never measured, and reads as covered when it is not.

SCOPE: add the opinionated pattern pages to both suites' page sets, measuring each page's real counts and committing them as ceilings rather than guessing (the suites' own docs require the actual measured count with no slack). Expect a first pass to surface genuine debt - that is the point, and it should be recorded per page with the reason, exactly as /components/charts and /components/data-table already do. Budget for the runtime: each added page costs a browser sweep in two lanes.

Worth deciding at the same time whether every demo page should be swept by default with an explicit opt-OUT list, rather than an opt-IN list that silently omits everything added after it was written. The current shape means a new pattern is unaudited unless someone remembers, and nobody did for six of them.
close_reason:
Fixed in 4c91330. Layout 9 -> 15 tests, style 5 -> 13; the six opinionated pattern pages (kpi_strip, record_header, selectable_summary, section_heading, search_picker_dialog, day-scheduler) are now measured.

⚠️ THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS FIX SILENTLY DID NOTHING, which is worth recording because it is the same defect one level up. Coverage in these suites comes from per-page `audit_test!(name, index)` macro invocations, not from entries in the PAGES const. Adding six entries left both suites GREEN and unchanged at nine tests, while appearing to cover six more pages. A check that passes because it measures nothing is precisely what this bead was filed against. The evidence that the fix works is the TEST COUNT changing, not the suite passing.

WHAT THE FIRST SWEEP IMMEDIATELY FOUND: SelectableSummaryCard carried Tailwind's stock shadow-sm — exactly what ldui-k4fn had replaced with the declared .ld-card-depth elevation for KpiCard hours earlier the same day. Two card families in one library disagreeing about elevation, invisible in review and invisible to the audits because that page was not swept. Adopting the declared elevation took its DEPTH findings from 43 to 0. That single finding justifies the bead.

CEILINGS ARE MEASURED AND CLASSIFIED, not estimated: day-scheduler typography 4 (daisyUI's own kbd-xs step); search_picker_dialog depth 4 (daisyUI's oklch()/oklab() alert shadow, which the engine's parser cannot read, so a declared spec would encode a mis-parse); record_header grid 44 (a declared 6px gap on the glyph-action row — off the canonical scale, but the same 6.00 value already sits in data-table's ratcheted findings, so it comes from a shared source rather than this pattern). The other three pages are clean at 0 across every family.

NOT DONE, and deliberately: the bead also asked whether the page set should be opt-OUT rather than opt-IN, so a new pattern is swept by default instead of only when someone remembers. That is a larger change to how the suites enumerate pages and is worth its own bead — the six pages here were the urgent part, since they were shipping unmeasured.

title: SearchPickerDialog vetoes Escape but lets a backdrop click close it behind the owner
description:
Flagged by ldui-e0fw's implementation; left alone there because src/patterns/ was outside that bead's file scope.

SearchPickerDialog hand-rolls its own dialog-close handling (src/patterns/search_picker_dialog.rs:370, `on:cancel=handle_dialog_cancel`) rather than using the controlled contract ldui-e0fw just added to Modal. That means it carries exactly the defect e0fw fixed:

`cancel` fires for ESCAPE ONLY. A backdrop click does not fire `cancel` at all - ModalBackdrop is a `method="dialog"` form, so it closes the dialog through a SUBMIT, which is why e0fw had to hook `submit` as well. So this pattern vetoes Escape and lets the backdrop close the dialog silently behind its owner, leaving the caller's state true while the dialog is shut. That is the same class of bug the Office NPS consumer reported against Modal.

The same reasoning applies to daisyUI's own in-content close button, which is also a `method="dialog"` submit.

SCOPE: migrate SearchPickerDialog onto `Modal`'s `on_close_request` / `ModalCloseProposal` instead of its own `on:cancel`, so backdrop and Escape both reach the owner with a typed cause, and delete the hand-rolled veto. Then extend the existing search-picker browser suite (it already has a registered lane, `cargo xtask test-search-picker-dialog`) with a BACKDROP close case - the gap is precisely that no test exercises the backdrop, which is why this survived.

Worth a wider grep while there: any other component or pattern hand-rolling `on:cancel` on a dialog has the same hole.
close_reason:
Implemented in 18fb6aa. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (c948eab): search_picker_dialog 7/7 including the new backdrop case, within 12 lanes / 140 checks / zero failures. Native gate 14/14.

⚠️ MY FILED PREMISE WAS WRONG, and the implementation corrected it. I wrote that this pattern "lets a backdrop click close it behind the owner". It did not: Modal was never given backdrop=true, so ModalBackdrop was never rendered and NO click-outside affordance existed at all. The on:cancel handler was genuinely Escape-only, but nothing was leaking past it.

WHAT SHIPPED, therefore, is two things rather than one. The hand-rolled on:cancel veto is replaced by Modal's controlled contract (on_close_request / ModalCloseProposal from ldui-e0fw), so Escape, Backdrop and DialogForm all route through the same request_close path with a typed cause. AND backdrop=true is now set, so the dismissal affordance actually exists.

⚠️ THAT SECOND PART IS A CALLER-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: pickers now dismiss on an outside click where that was previously inert. It is conventional for a search picker and it is what this bead's intent implied, but it is an ADDITION rather than a repair and should not be discovered by surprise. on_close's signature is unchanged and Escape/Cancel behave identically, so existing callers remain source- and behaviour-compatible in every other respect.

The Button-in-dialog-form trap found in ldui-e0fw's fixture was checked here rather than assumed: this pattern's Cancel control is a plain on:click Button outside any method="dialog" form, so there was nothing to fix.

The backdrop coverage that was missing is now in the registered lane (tests/search_picker_dialog_smoke.rs, backdrop_click_closes_and_restores_focus), located by stable data-modal-backdrop / data-search-picker-dialog selectors. Its absence is precisely why this survived, so the bead would have been half-done without it.

title: NavRailItem has the same unmarked bare button as the app-shell rail, so NavRail consumers still see the drift
close_reason:
Implemented in d269b53, with a contrast fix in c948eab. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (c948eab): 12 lanes, 140 checks, zero failures. Native gate 14/14.

THE SWEEP, not just the one component. NavRailItem, DockItem, Tree's expander, JsonTreeViewer's two disclosure toggles, TagInput's remove control, the markdown editor's three mode toggles and graphic_editor's eight overlay buttons are all genuinely deliberate unstyled actions and now carry data-pressable. Every other <button> in src/ was checked individually and already carries .btn or sits inside an exempt ancestor. The marker was applied per component with a stated reason rather than sprayed - a marker meaning "deliberate" is worthless if everything carries it. Pressable itself was confirmed to already emit it, so components routing through it needed nothing.

A NATIVE GUARD NOW EXISTS: tests/no_bare_library_buttons.rs fails on any new unmarked bare button, with a documented allowlist for the cases a source scan cannot judge. That converts a recurring consumer complaint - 160 of one audit's 841 findings tracing to our rail - into something that cannot regress silently.

⚠️ AND IT CAUGHT AN ERROR IN MY OWN INSTRUCTION. I asked for text-base-content/60 to be measured against base-100: it is 4.64:1 there and passes AA, so the agent correctly left it under the gate I set. But it also measured the rail's ACTUAL background, bg-base-300, where the same colour is 4.42:1 and FAILS the 4.5:1 threshold - and flagged the discrepancy instead of silently choosing one. The ratio that matters is against the surface the text actually sits on. Raised to /75 in c948eab, which is also this crate's documented muted-copy idiom, with the two tests that pinned /60 updated to pin /75 and say why.

title: Add typed secondary value axis to categorical LineChart
description: The Office Conversations Reporting page combines three count series with average first-response duration. The opinionated categorical LineChart supports multiple series but gives every series one shared numeric value axis. Office must not restore a private dual-axis SVG. Add an opt-in typed primary or secondary axis assignment per series, including independent domains, right-side tick labels, units, tooltip and hidden-table fidelity, and no behavior change for existing single-axis callers.
acceptance_criteria: A categorical LineSeries can opt into a secondary value axis through a typed public API; LineChart independently computes finite domains and renders readable left and right ticks and localized axis labels; legend, markers, patterns, point cards, keyboard activation, and accessible hidden-table values remain correct; missing values and all-zero domains remain safe; existing callers render byte-for-byte-equivalent single-axis structure when the feature is unused; tests and visual coverage include mixed count and duration series.

title: AppShellIconNavItem emits a bare <button>, so the rail self-reports as button-without-btn drift in every consumer
description:
AppShellIconNavItem renders a bare <button>, so the library's own nav rail self-reports as component drift in every consumer that runs the style audit — while this same library ships the primitive that fixes it.

EVIDENCE, from 4iiz-etl's portal audit on 2026-08-31 (841 findings across ten screens at two viewports):

  160 of them are `button-without-btn`, and essentially all trace to the rail:
      div.flex.flex-1 > nav.flex.flex-col > div.flex.flex-col > button.relative.flex
        button-without-btn: raw <button> lacks .btn

  That consumer's ENTIRE crate contains six `<button` occurrences in source,
  several of which are comments documenting deliberate ones. The findings are
  not its markup — they are AppShellIconNavItem's, at
  src/components/app_shell/component.rs:514, multiplied by ten rail items on
  every page at both viewports.

WHY THIS IS AWKWARD RATHER THAN COSMETIC: `button-without-btn` is a drift signal consumers are expected to drive toward zero, and ~19% of one app's total findings are produced by the library itself. A consumer cannot fix them — the markup is not theirs — so the only options are to absorb them into a raised ceiling (which hides real drift in the same family) or to budget them as a named intentional gap. Both make the library's own component look like the consumer's problem.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS HERE. `Pressable` emits data-pressable="true", and the drift rule recognises it — audit/src/drift.rs's own test says so in as many words:

    /// The library's `Pressable` primitive emits `data-pressable="true"` as
    /// its auditable marker; the button rule must recognize it so a designed
    /// unstyled action never counts as drift (and the counts drop honestly,
    /// not via exemption comments). Genuinely raw buttons keep flagging.

An unstyled nav item is exactly "a designed unstyled action". Having AppShellIconNavItem emit the marker (or build on Pressable) would take those findings to zero honestly, by the library's own stated standard.

SUGGESTED: have AppShellIconNavItem render through Pressable, or emit data-pressable="true" on its <button>. Either satisfies the rule the library already wrote for this case.

NOT A BUG REPORT ABOUT WORK IN PROGRESS: filed against COMMITTED code (component.rs:514 is in HEAD). The entity_table refactor uncommitted in the working tree on 2026-09-01 does not currently compile (`selection_header` defined at component.rs:920 but out of scope at 1586) — that is in-progress work, is NOT what this bead is about, and needs no action from anyone.

Filed from 4iiz-etl at the owner's request. No source changes made in this repo; the working tree was left untouched.
acceptance_criteria: A page rendering AppShell's icon rail produces zero button-without-btn findings from the rail itself, achieved via Pressable / the data-pressable marker rather than by exempting the rule.
close_reason:
Implemented in 00b2f7d. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (c948eab): 12 lanes, 140 checks, zero failures. Native gate 14/14.

Chose NOT to add .btn. The drift rule (audit/src/drift.js) exempts any button carrying data-pressable, so the rail item is now marked as the deliberate unstyled action it already was: one attribute, no class or behaviour change, so appearance cannot shift and no shadow/DEPTH count moves. Adding .btn would have brought padding, min-height, background and a shadow to a compact icon rail - fixing an audit finding by changing the design it was reporting on.

Verified it targets the right component rather than assuming: AppShellIconNavItem's class begins "relative flex flex-col", matching the button.relative.flex selector in the consumer's own findings.

⚠️ THIS FIX ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH, which its own report flagged. NavRailItem has the identical unmarked shape, so a consumer using NavRail rather than AppShell's rail saw no improvement at all. Followed up as ldui-2e7a, which swept every library-emitted bare button and added a native guard so the next one cannot ship unmarked.

title: Icon: add run-control glyphs (pause, play, save) - PageQuickActions is unadoptable for control-plane toolbars without them
description:
The Icon alias table has no start/stop/save glyphs, which blocks PageQuickActions for any control-plane toolbar.

CONCRETE BLOCKER, from 4iiz-etl (bd_4iiz-etl-9cb.11). Its operator portal has a six-button quick-action toolbar on Home: Pause all, Resume all, Restart all, Snapshot, Reap orphans, Freshness check. That is exactly what PageQuickActions is for - its own doc calls it "an opinionated, wrapping icon-action row for a PageHeader's actions slot", and PageHeader has the slot. Adoption is blocked because PageQuickActionContent requires an icon per action and three of the six do not resolve:

    Restart all      refresh    resolves
    Reap orphans     trash      resolves
    Freshness check  activity   resolves
    Pause all        --         MISSING
    Resume all       --         MISSING
    Snapshot         --         MISSING

An unresolved name returns `blank`, the sprite's neutral glyph (icon/component.rs:190), so adopting today would render a placeholder beside three of six buttons. That consumer had just finished REMOVING placeholder glyphs (raw emoji in button labels rendered as tofu boxes in the WSL/Chrome font set), so adopting the pattern would reintroduce the defect class it had just fixed. Half-adopting for only the three that resolve is worse - a toolbar with three icons and three bare labels.

Confirmed absent from the alias table: pause, play, circle-play, square-pause, save, floppy-disk, camera.

REQUESTED, smallest set that unblocks it:
  - pause  (or square-pause)
  - play   (or circle-play)
  - save   (or floppy-disk / camera) for a snapshot action

WHY THIS IS LIKELY GENERAL RATHER THAN ONE APP'S QUIRK: start / stop / save is the basic verb set of any control-plane or admin surface - schedulers, job runners, media, anything with a run loop. The table already carries the CRUD and navigation verbs (plus, pencil, trash, refresh, search, filter, upload, external-link) but not the run-control ones, so PageQuickActions is currently adoptable for record pages and not for operational ones.

Filed from 4iiz-etl at the owner's request. No source changes made in this repo - the working tree there had unrelated entity_table work in progress and was left untouched.
acceptance_criteria: pause, play and a save/snapshot glyph resolve in the Icon alias table; a PageQuickActions row of Pause/Resume/Restart/Snapshot/Reap/Freshness renders six real icons and no 'blank'.
close_reason:
Implemented in 832bddf. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER on the final tree (59d765b): reactivity 52/52, layout 9/9, style 7/7, admin-workbench 8/8, server-column-tools 2/2, entity-table 15/15; native gate 14/14.

pause, play and save now resolve in the Icon alias table, with the consumer's own vocabulary aliased directly: pause and square-pause to pause; play, circle-play and resume to play; save, floppy-disk and snapshot to save. The bead's six-button row (Pause all, Resume all, Restart all, Snapshot, Reap orphans, Freshness check) renders six real glyphs and no blank.

THE GUARD WAS BREAK-TESTED, not merely written. An unresolved name does not error - it returns blank, the sprite's neutral glyph - so a test asserting resolution is worth nothing unless it is shown to fail. The implementer commented out the "pause" arm, confirmed exactly two tests failed, reverted, and verified the file's diff was empty afterwards.

⚠️ LIMIT OF WHAT THIS REPO CAN GUARANTEE, worth passing to the consumer. The sprite is NOT vendored here: it is a host-document asset per Icon's own doc contract, so this repo owns only the alias table. These aliases resolve to symbol NAMES; whether a given consumer's sprite actually contains pause, play and floppy-disk is a property of THEIR document that no test here can assert. The bead's acceptance ("renders six real icons and no blank") is therefore only half-guaranteed by this change - the consumer must confirm their sprite carries those three symbols, or they will get the placeholder they were trying to avoid.

title: KpiStrip picks its column count from the viewport, so a strip in a narrow container renders unreadable cards
description:
Measured on the admin-workbench eight-card strip (data-testid admin-workbench-kpis), sweeping the viewport and reading each card's rendered width plus its label's scrollHeight (the height its full text needs) against clientHeight (what line-clamp-2 allows):

  viewport  cardW  label needs, no help  label needs, with help
  1280       67    80px  (5 lines)       144px (9 lines)
  1680      117    32px  (2 lines) OK     32px (2 lines) OK
  2200      182    32px  OK               32px OK
  2560      227    32px  OK               32px OK

At 1280 every label in the strip is heavily ellipsized. The strip is unusable there, and 1280 is an ordinary laptop width.

CAUSE: KpiStrip's column count is driven by VIEWPORT breakpoints - grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3 md:grid-cols-4 xl:grid-cols-8. Tailwind's xl is 1280px, so the moment the WINDOW reaches 1280 the strip switches to eight columns, whether or not the strip itself has room for eight. In the workbench demo the strip sits in a content column that is roughly 648px wide at a 1280px viewport, so eight columns give 67px cards - narrower than a single word of an uppercase 11px label.

This is not specific to the demo. Any consumer that places a KpiStrip inside a nav rail plus content column, a split pane, a drawer, or any constrained region hits it: the breakpoint asks how wide the WINDOW is, and the answer has almost nothing to do with how wide the STRIP is. It is also invisible in the common case, because a full-width strip at 1680 looks fine - which is exactly how it survived until a label-wrapping bead forced someone to measure.

FIX: make the strip's responsive behaviour depend on its own width rather than the window, with Tailwind 4 container queries - @container on the strip and @min-* column variants in place of sm:/md:/xl:. That is what container queries exist for, and it makes the component correct in any container without the consumer having to know.

SCOPE NOTE, and why this is filed rather than done: this changes responsive behaviour for every existing consumer of KpiStrip. A strip that currently goes to eight columns at a 1280px window would instead go to eight columns when the STRIP is wide enough, which is the intended behaviour but is still a visible change to existing screens. It also needs the layout/style ratchets re-measured, since column counts move element geometry on any page carrying a strip. Worth confirming the intended breakpoints with the consumer before landing.

Related: ldui-yhvf (a help control costs its label 20px) is the same family - both only bite once cards are narrow, and container queries would remove most of the pressure.
close_reason:
Fixed in 0848607 and VERIFIED IN A BROWSER across six viewports.

THE FIX: KpiStrip's column steps were VIEWPORT breakpoints (sm/md/xl), so the strip went to eight columns the moment the WINDOW reached 1280px regardless of how wide the strip itself was. They are now container queries, so the strip asks how wide IT is. An element cannot answer its own container query, so the strip gained a structural container wrapper that carries no spacing of its own; the `class` prop and `node_ref` stay on the grid div where their documentation says they are, and the grid keeps `data-kpi-strip` so existing selectors are unaffected.

THRESHOLDS ARE DERIVED FROM MEASUREMENT, not taste. A card needs about 117px to hold a two-line label (ldui-tbaw's fit sweep: a 20-character label holds two lines at 70px of label width and up, and label width is roughly card width minus 34px of padding):

  @sm  384px  -> 3 cols = 117px
  @lg  512px  -> 4 cols = 116px
  @5xl 1024px -> 8 cols = 114px and up

@5xl RATHER THAN @6xl, and this is the part worth recording: I first shipped @6xl (1152px), then measured and found the consumer's strip is 1046px - so @6xl would have quietly dropped them from eight columns to four. That is a visible layout change I would have delivered while believing I was only fixing a bug. @5xl keeps eight columns at their width.

MEASURED AFTER, on the workbench demo:

  window  strip   cols  cardW
  768     390     3     119
  1024    390     3     119
  1280    646     4     150     <- the reported case; was 67px, labels needing 5-9 lines
  1680   1046     8     117     <- unchanged from before: eight in a row
  2200   1566     8     182

Tailwind generates the rules correctly from the Rust source (verified `@container (width >= 24rem)`, `>= 32rem`, `>= 64rem` and `container-type` in the published stylesheet) - worth checking, because a class the extractor misses would silently leave the strip at two columns.

ONE CASE NOT FIXED, and it is not this bead: at 390px the demo page starves the strip to 12px via a 60px parent. I suspected my own container-type at first, since containment removes an element's content contribution to its parent's sizing - so I tested it, setting containerType='normal' in the live DOM and re-measuring: identical geometry, so the ancestors decide it and the pre-change strip was equally starved. Filed as ldui-kwup.

EVIDENCE: admin_workbench_smoke 7/7, layout_audit_smoke 9/9, style_audit_smoke 7/7 on a freshly published dist; native suite and clippy clean. No ratcheted count moved.

title: pixelproof-web Harness forces touch emulation, so every hover-gated CSS assertion silently fails
description:
Found while verifying ldui-jdzr on 2026-08-31.

chromiumoxide 0.7.0's Browser::new_page unconditionally sends Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled(true). It is hardcoded: it ignores Viewport::has_touch, and it is independent of whatever set_viewport passes for mobile. Every page a pixelproof-web Harness creates therefore comes up with touch emulation ON.

CONSEQUENCE: with touch emulation forced on, Chromium reports (hover: hover) = false. Tailwind gates its hover: utilities behind @media (hover: hover), so EVERY hover: utility silently fails to apply in the harness - even though a CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent mouseMoved genuinely does put the element into the CSS :hover state. The element really is hovered; the media query just says this device cannot hover, so the rule never matches.

This is a silent, general trap: any browser assertion about a hover-gated style will fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the code under test, and the failure looks exactly like "the component does not paint on hover". It cost a full investigation cycle here: the component was correct the whole time, and CSS-not-generated, specificity, unlayered legacy CSS and zebra striping were all ruled out first.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE (local, this repo): tests/common/mod.rs gained a force_desktop_hover_media helper that sends Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled(false) after page creation; the hover assertion passes with it. That fixes leptos-daisyui-rs only, and every other consumer of pixelproof-web has the same latent problem.

REQUEST: handle this in pixelproof-web itself, so callers get correct hover-media semantics by default rather than each discovering it. Options, roughly in order of preference: (1) have Harness disable touch emulation after new_page unless the caller asked for touch; (2) honour Viewport::has_touch when creating the page; (3) if chromiumoxide must be taken as-is, expose a documented desktop_hover()/has_touch(false) on the harness so the fix is discoverable instead of folklore. Whichever is chosen, the behaviour is worth one line in the harness docs, because the symptom points anywhere except the real cause.
notes: BLOCKED ON SIBLING REPO (PixelProof), recorded 2026-08-31. The defect is in pixelproof-web's Harness (C:/dev/PixelProof/crates/pixelproof-web/src/harness.rs), which this repo consumes; that file currently has uncommitted work for an unrelated chrome-executable feature. THIS REPO IS NOT BLOCKED: tests/common/mod.rs already carries a working force_desktop_hover_media helper (Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled(false)) and the hover assertion passes live (commit df293f5). What remains is the upstream fix so other consumers do not each rediscover it: chromiumoxide 0.7.0's Browser::new_page hardcodes setTouchEmulationEnabled(true), ignoring Viewport::has_touch, which makes Chromium report (hover: hover)=false and silently defeats every @media(hover:hover)-gated Tailwind hover: utility. Preferred fix order: (1) Harness disables touch emulation after new_page unless touch was requested; (2) honour Viewport::has_touch; (3) failing those, expose a documented desktop_hover()/has_touch(false) so the workaround is discoverable rather than folklore.
close_reason:
Fixed UPSTREAM in PixelProof de72536, which this repo consumes as a path dependency. This bead is no longer blocked.

WHAT SHIPPED: pixelproof-web's Harness now turns touch emulation back off after new_page, unless the caller sets the new HarnessConfig::touch (default false). chromiumoxide's Browser::new_page hardcodes Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled(true) and ignores the viewport's own has_touch, so every harness page came up claiming to be a touch device; Chromium then reports (hover: hover) as false and every @media(hover:hover)-gated rule - which is every Tailwind hover: utility - silently stops matching. Option (1) from this bead's preferred order, plus a documented with_touch() builder so the touch case stays reachable.

VERIFIED, and deliberately not by asserting the CDP call: the regression test asserts the MEDIA QUERY (matchMedia('(hover: hover)').matches), so it still fails if a future chromiumoxide reintroduces the behaviour by another route. It also asserts the touch:true case reports FALSE - without that half, an unwired option would let the test pass trivially, which is the failure mode this whole bead is about. Both halves pass live.

The first run of that test failed on its second launch with "Browser process exited with status 21 before websocket URL could be resolved" - two harnesses cannot share one Chrome profile concurrently. Scoped so the first is dropped before the second launches; that is a property of the harness worth knowing when writing multi-launch tests.

pixelproof-web is green on the current tree: unit tests plus all four ignored browser lanes (4/3/2/1 passed), workspace clippy -D warnings clean.

THIS REPO: tests/common/mod.rs's force_desktop_hover_media helper is now redundant, since the harness does this by default. It is deliberately left in place for now - it is harmless (setting touch emulation false twice is a no-op), and removing it is a separate change that should be made when this repo next picks up the sibling's commit, with the hover assertions re-run to prove the default alone carries them. Worth a follow-up if it is still there in a month.

title: DataTable: semantic column kinds (numeric, identifier) so callers stop hand-writing tabular-nums and font-mono
description:
FILED FROM 4iiz-etl (bd_4iiz-etl-q7p), measured 2026-08-30 across a 10-screen operator portal.

Column offers only with_class(&'static str) - a raw CSS escape hatch - so every consumer re-invents the same handful of column KINDS in Tailwind. Measured in one consumer:

  98  with_class calls on columns in total
  43  contain tabular-nums          (numeric columns)
  30  are exactly "text-right tabular-nums ..."  (numeric alignment)
  20  contain font-mono             (identifier columns)

So roughly two thirds of all column styling in this consumer expresses just TWO intents: "this is a number" and "this is an identifier".

THE CLINCHING MEASUREMENT: of 24 columns declaring with_sort_as(SortAs::Number), 22 ALSO hand-write tabular-nums, and 2 do not. The component already knows the column is numeric - the caller states it for sorting - and then 92 percent of callers repeat that fact in CSS while 8 percent forget and get silently inconsistent rendering. Presentation is not being derived from information the component already holds.

REQUEST: semantic column kinds that own their presentation, e.g.

  Column::new("captured", "Captured").numeric()      // right-align + tabular figures + the ramp's numeric step
  Column::new("job", "Job").identifier()             // the theme's declared mono face

Ideally .numeric() also implies SortAs::Number so the two cannot disagree, and identifier() applies a face the StyleProfile accepts (see ldui-kq9w - today every hand-applied font-mono is reported as a font-family deviation, 223 findings in this consumer, because the audit has no way to know the mono was deliberate and the component was not the one applying it).

WHY NOT JUST KEEP with_class: it works, which is why it has survived, but it pushes design-system decisions to hundreds of call sites. The owner's ruling for this consumer is to use the opinionated components and stop overriding them; a column cannot honour that while the only way to right-align a number is to type Tailwind.
acceptance_criteria: Column exposes numeric() and identifier() (or equivalent) that own alignment, figure style and font face from the theme; numeric() implies SortAs::Number; a consumer can express every column in 4iiz-etl's portal without with_class for these two intents; the identifier face is one the StyleProfile accepts
close_reason:
Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. DataTable's Column now has .numeric() and .identifier() semantic kinds, so callers stop hand-writing tabular-nums and font-mono. Commits 1fb074f (feature) and cc05f9b (ceiling, see below); mirrored onto EntityColumn in a5a7950 under ldui-no94.

.numeric() IMPLIES SortAs::Number, which is the point of the bead: the clinching measurement was that of 24 columns declaring SortAs::Number, 22 also hand-wrote tabular-nums and 2 did not, so the component already knew the column was numeric while 92 percent of callers restated it in CSS and 8 percent silently disagreed. Stating alignment, figure style and comparator as ONE fact removes the drift; a caller needing a different comparator can still call .with_sort_as(...) afterwards (builder order wins, tested). .identifier() leaves sorting untouched.

PRECEDENCE, documented and tested: an explicit with_class REPLACES the kind's default class wholesale rather than merging. The reason is not stylistic - Tailwind's cascade order is decided by generated stylesheet position, not by order within a class attribute, so a merge could not guarantee the caller's override actually wins.

EVIDENCE: 13 new native tests; native suite 2670 green; style_audit_smoke run LIVE on 2026-08-31 = 7/7 PASS.

CEILING DECISION, recorded because it is the one place on this page where raising beats fixing at source. Applying .identifier() to the demo's id column took /components/data-table's typography count from 92 to 105. I attributed the delta before acting rather than assuming: of 20 ui-monospace findings, roughly 14 sit on the table itself (10 on table.table.table-md, 4 on tr) - the identifier column across its rendered rows - with the remaining 6 on prose div.space-y-4 that predate this change. So the breach is entirely the deliberate identifier face. That is the OPPOSITE of the <code> debt this page already carried: a <code> span inheriting the UA monospace default inside sans prose is unintentional, which is why those 24 spans were genuinely fixed at source with font-sans across 2fb75d3 and c8bb775 rather than ratcheted. An identifier column is SUPPOSED to be monospace, so "fixing" it would mean deleting the feature. The finding exists only because StyleProfile carries a single family name (ldui-kq9w, blocked upstream in PixelProof). The ceiling is therefore raised to 105 with an in-code note that it MUST come back down when that bead lands; it is not new page debt.

title: ldui_audit: StyleProfile cannot express a deliberate monospace face, so every font-mono element is a finding
description:
FILED FROM 4iiz-etl (bd_4iiz-etl-cnu), measured 2026-08-30 across a 10-screen portal at two viewports.

StyleProfile takes ONE family name and the sweep compares each element's first computed family against it, so any element using a different face is reported. A consumer that deliberately uses font-mono for identifiers (job ids, table names, SQL, build stamps) therefore gets one finding per such element, forever.

MEASUREMENT: 389 TYPOGRAPHY findings across the portal, of which 223 (57 percent) are the identical string 'font-family "ui-monospace", expected ...'. Every one is intentional. The remaining 150 are genuine off-ramp font-size findings and are useful. So more than half the typography signal is noise a consumer cannot switch off, and it scales with how many identifiers a page shows, which is why typography now breaches the ceiling on ALL TEN screens at both viewports.

This is the same failure shape profile.rs's own comment already documents: feeding the whole family stack once made "every text element on every page a bogus finding", and the fix was to compare only the first family. The mono case is the surviving half of that bug.

SMALLEST USEFUL CHANGE: let StyleProfile carry additional accepted families (e.g. .mono_family("ui-monospace") or an accepted_families set), and treat an element whose first computed family matches ANY accepted family as conforming. Keep it explicit so an accidental third face still reports.

DO NOT solve this by telling consumers to raise their ceilings: the count grows with content, so a ceiling tuned today is breached by the next page that shows more ids, and the real signal (off-ramp font sizes) stays buried under it.
acceptance_criteria: A StyleProfile can declare additional accepted font families; elements matching one produce no font-family finding; an unaccepted third family still does; 4iiz-etl's portal typography findings drop by roughly the measured 223
notes:
BLOCKED ON SIBLING REPO (PixelProof), recorded 2026-08-31 by leptos-daisyui-rs-7e. StyleProfile lives in C:/dev/PixelProof/crates/pixelproof-style-audit/src/lib.rs; this repo only consumes it. That working tree currently has UNCOMMITTED work in the exact files this change touches (sweep.rs and style_sweep_test.rs) for an unrelated chrome-executable-discovery feature, so editing it would mix my change into someone else's in-flight commit. Requested change is unambiguous: let StyleProfile carry additional accepted families (e.g. accepted_families or .mono_family(...)) and treat an element whose first computed family matches ANY accepted family as conforming, keeping it explicit so an accidental third face still reports. Evidence from this repo that the gap is real and costly: deliberate monospace has twice forced source edits purely to hold a ceiling (24 code spans given font-sans across commits 2fb75d3 and c8bb775), and ldui-lrig/ldui-no94 have now shipped .identifier() columns that render the theme's mono face by design, which the audit reports one finding per element. Unblocks when PixelProof lands the accepted-families change. UNBLOCKED 2026-08-31: PixelProof landed 8a74b06 'sound shadow parsing and a monospace typography exemption' and that tree is now clean. THEY CHOSE A BETTER DESIGN THAN I ASKED FOR, and I agree with it. I requested an accepted_families set on StyleProfile; they instead exempt the FAMILY check on the mono TAGS (CODE, PRE, KBD, SAMP, TT). Their reasoning, from the code comment, is sound: a tag cannot be abused, whereas a computed-family test would ALSO silently accept a

that fell into monospace by accident - which would have traded a false positive for a false negative. The font-SIZE check still runs on those tags, so a code span at 13px is still off-ramp. They note that asserting WHICH mono family resolves is a later additive profile field, and writing it as a skip leaves room for it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS REPO, which is not what I assumed when I raised the ceiling: the exemption is tag-based, and Column::identifier() (ldui-lrig / ldui-no94) renders the theme mono face on a , NOT on a . So of the 20 ui-monospace findings on /components/data-table, the 6 prose spans should now be exempt while roughly 14 identifier cells will NOT be. The ceiling I raised to 105 in cc05f9b can therefore come DOWN, but not all the way to 92. NEXT: re-measure the page after the in-flight ldui-h7tw work lands, lower the ceiling to whatever the exemption actually leaves, and decide deliberately whether identifier cells should render their content in a element - which would be semantically defensible for a job id or reference AND would bring them under the exemption honestly, rather than by widening a ratchet.
close_reason:
Resolved upstream in PixelProof 8a74b06, and the benefit is now realised on this side. THEIR DESIGN IS BETTER THAN WHAT I REQUESTED. I asked for an accepted_families set on StyleProfile. They instead exempt the FAMILY check on the mono TAGS (code, pre, kbd, samp, tt). Their reasoning, quoted from the code: a tag cannot be abused, whereas a computed-family test "would also silently accept a

that fell into monospace by accident" - i.e. my version would have traded a false positive for a false negative. The font-SIZE check still runs on those tags, so a at 13px remains as off-ramp as anything else, and they left room for a later additive profile field asserting WHICH mono family resolves. MEASURED EFFECT HERE, and it is much larger than I predicted: /components/data-table's typography count fell from 105 to 31. I had estimated only about 6 would clear, on the assumption that Column::identifier()'s mono cells would stay reported because the exemption is tag-based. The real drop was 74. I measured rather than assumed by zeroing every typography ceiling and reading the failure output, which also confirmed button (1), card (1), kanban (7) and charts (78) were already at their true counts and needed no change - so the win is specific to the page that was carrying inline . The ceiling raised in cc05f9b has therefore come back down to 31 in e040f98, exactly as that commit's note promised. That matters beyond tidiness: this suite's own doc says the sweep pushes at most one violation per element, so a ceiling with slack is precisely where a real regression hides. 61 of the 92 that predated the identifier work turn out to have been unfixable-by-construction mono debt masking that much headroom. Style lane 7/7 PASS on the current tree.

title: Tighten KpiStrip supporting-description typography
description: The bottom supporting copy in Coordinator stat cards reads too close in size to the metric label/value. KpiStrip owns this typography through its description renderer, so consumers should not need descendant CSS to restore the compact legacy hierarchy.
acceptance_criteria: KpiCard description and trend copy use the smaller supporting-copy type step while labels and values remain unchanged. The result is readable in eight-card strips at desktop width and wraps without clipping; visual/demo coverage documents compact and default variants.
close_reason:
Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. KpiCard's description and trend copy now use the ramp's smaller supporting-copy step while the label and value are unchanged, restoring the compact hierarchy without consumers needing descendant CSS. Commit 5cd25c4.

ROOT CAUSE was an inversion, not merely "too large": the description was on ld-text-caption (12px) while the card's own label sits on ld-text-small (11px) - the supporting copy was literally LARGER than the label it supports, which is why it read as competing with the metric. Both description and trend now use ld-text-small.

EVIDENCE: native tests, plus admin_workbench_smoke run LIVE on 2026-08-31 = 6/6 PASS, which renders a KpiStrip of eight varied cards at both a wide desktop and a compact mobile viewport and asserts they wrap without clipping or horizontal overflow - the eight-card desktop legibility case this bead names. style_audit_smoke also passed on that tree, so the new type step sits on the declared ramp rather than pushing the page's typography ceiling.

title: Support native submit and reset semantics in Button
description: LDUI Button always renders type=button. Explicit same-origin launch and ordinary form workflows therefore must use a raw button or lose native form submission, which conflicts with the component-drift rule and omits the framework focus/variant contract. Add a typed button-type prop covering Button, Submit, and Reset while preserving Button as the safe default.
acceptance_criteria: Button exposes a typed native type prop whose default remains button; submit participates in its owning form and reset restores native controls without requiring a click callback or JavaScript transport. Rendered type, disabled behavior, Enter/form submission, reset behavior, focus styling, and absence of duplicate submission have focused native/browser coverage. Documentation includes the explicit POST launch-form use case and existing callers remain source compatible.
close_reason: Duplicate of ldui-9vs, already implemented in this repo (commits 43cfcb1, 0a8cb9c, ccba650). Button exposes typed ButtonType { Button (default), Submit, Reset } emitting the native type attribute (src/components/button/style.rs:141-165); submit participates in its owning form and reset restores native controls with no click callback or JS transport. Browser coverage exists for all four demanded behaviors: button_type_variants_emit_the_matching_type_attribute, submit_button_activates_form_once_per_click_and_per_key (no duplicate submission), disabled_and_loading_submit_buttons_cannot_submit, reset_button_restores_native_defaults (tests/reactivity_smoke.rs:4148-4261), plus a 2x2x3 native truth-table for the disabled/loading resolver. The POST launch-form use case is documented in doc/components/button.md and the component docs. Existing callers are source-compatible (default remains type=button).

title: DataTable auto_page_size: first-row height measurement overflows with variable-height rows, producing scrollbar + pagination together
notes:
Filed from 4iiz-etl 2026-08-29 (owner review of the height-resize behavior: pagination count should absorb the height change 'so it does not trigger an internal scrollbar - inconsistent with pagination, usually one or the other but not both').

MECHANISM (component.rs ~853): auto_page_size derives rows-per-page from measure('tbody tr', FALLBACK_ROW_HEIGHT) - the FIRST body row only. The consumer's tables have variable-height rows (module-name cells wrapping under whitespace-normal break-all, a two-line pause-controls action cell), so when the first row is short the derived count overflows the definite height and the wrapper scrolls - the exact both-at-once inconsistency the design's own docs promise to avoid. The min_rows floor scroll (very short windows) is fine and documented; this is the NORMAL-window case.

SUGGESTED FIX, in preference order:
  1. Measure the MAX offset_height across the currently rendered tbody rows (cheap: one pass over children in the existing ResizeObserver callback), so the fit is conservative and never overflows. Average is not enough - one tall row still overflows.
  2. Belt-and-braces: after applying a derived count, if wrapper.scroll_height > wrapper.offset_height by more than a row's tolerance, decrement the count once on the next frame (bounded, no loop) - catches heights that change AFTER measurement (images, fonts).
  3. Keep FALLBACK_ROW_HEIGHT for the nothing-rendered-yet first paint as today.

TEST SHAPE: rows_per_page_for_height already unit-tested; add a case where row heights vary (feed the max) plus a wasm/DOM test with one tall row asserting no scroll overflow at the derived count.

CONSUMER: 4iiz-etl portal - History/Queue/Jobs/Running all use auto_page_size with wrapping cells; no ETL-side change needed once this lands.
close_reason: Fixed and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. auto_page_size no longer derives rows-per-page from the FIRST body row: it measures the MAX offset_height across the rendered rows, so a short first row can no longer produce a count that overflows the definite height and yields a scrollbar and pagination together. Because the measured row set is itself a function of the derived page size, a naive max would oscillate; the fix adds an era-scoped high-water mark (era = dataset revision + container width) so the effective row height only ratchets up within an era and the derived count reaches a fixpoint - pinned by a test that replays the exact oscillation trace, plus a contrast test proving the same trace never settles without the ratchet. The belt-and-braces overflow decrement is floored at min_rows per auto_page's documented contract, and is unmount-safe. Commits 454d091, c5c9209, 2fb75d3. EVIDENCE: 30 native auto_page tests, plus auto_page_size_does_not_overflow_with_a_tall_variable_height_row and auto_page_size_keeps_a_usable_page_and_scrolls_short_viewports run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS. The live run caught a real regression the native tests could not: the overflow decrement was shaving a row off the retained below-floor fallback.

title: DataTable: substring TEXT filter variant for high-cardinality columns (filterable_text)
notes:
Filed from 4iiz-etl 2026-08-29 (owner request on the Queue/Schedule page): 'can the Job column filter be a text box instead of a dropdown picklist. The user should be able to enter a few characters of the name and the table filters to only show matching rows.'

CURRENT STATE: src/components/data_table/filter.rs renders one <select> per filterable column over distinct_values() with exact-match semantics (FILTER_ALL sentinel = empty string). For a high-cardinality column (67 job ids, RFC3339 timestamps) the dropdown is unusable - you scroll a list as long as the table.

REQUESTED SHAPE:
  - Column::filterable_text() (alongside the existing filterable()) marking the column for a text <input> in the same filter row, styled to the filter-row tokens (bg-table-filter etc.).
  - Matching: case-insensitive SUBSTRING against the cell's raw value ('mat' matches zoho-matters and Matter_Timeline). Debounce ~150ms so a keystroke storm does not re-filter per char on 200-row pages.
  - ColumnFilters representation: same map, but the consumer must be able to distinguish exact (select) from contains (text) - either a FilterValue enum {Exact(String), Contains(String)} or a parallel kind lookup from the column def. ServerDataTable forwards it through TableQuery so server-paged consumers (4iiz-etl History) can implement contains server-side; DataTable applies it client-side.
  - Empty input = no filter (same as FILTER_ALL).
  - a11y: aria-label 'Filter {column} by text'.

CONSUMER PLAN (4iiz-etl, once this lands): Queue Job column first (the requesting page), then Jobs job/dst, History module, Running job - every high-cardinality column currently stuck with an exact dropdown. ETL will do that sweep; ping back on this bead when released.
close_reason: Added Column::filterable_text with ColumnFilterKind::Contains, a 150ms-debounced aligned text input, case-insensitive client substring matching, controlled server proposal restoration, text-only vocabulary exemption, reactive accessible naming, docs, and existing browser-journey coverage. 249 focused DataTable tests pass; showcase WASM and reactivity target compile.

title: Give EntityTable page-size controls stable unique browser identities by default
description: Office satellite browser smokes found Chrome form-control metadata issues on every EntityTable whose caller omitted page_size_control_id. EntityTable passes the optional value straight to Select, so the framework-owned rows-per-page control has an accessible label but no id or name. Setup mounts three tables, so consumers also cannot safely repair this with one shared hard-coded value.
design: When no caller override is supplied, EntityTable should generate a deterministic per-instance id and name for its page-size Select. Preserve the caller-owned page_size_control_id override and ensure multiple EntityTables on one page never emit duplicate identities. The framework should own this because it owns and renders the control.
acceptance_criteria: An EntityTable without page_size_control_id renders a page-size select with non-empty id and name; two or more tables mounted together receive unique values; caller-supplied identity remains stable and honored; labels remain correctly associated; focused browser coverage reports no missing-id-or-name issue for the framework control.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. EntityTable now mints a deterministic per-instance id AND name for its framework-owned page-size Select when the caller supplies no page_size_control_id, reusing the crate's established AtomicU64 id-minting idiom (mirrors Field's next_field_id). A caller-supplied identity still wins and stays stable, label association is unchanged, and two or more EntityTables mounted together never collide. Commit 543dec6; the browser test was ORPHANED (it lived in tests/entity_table_page_size_identity.rs, which no lane ran, so this bead's evidence was unobtainable) and was folded into tests/entity_table_smoke.rs in commit 1bedc9e. EVIDENCE: native uniqueness/override tests, plus page_size_select_gets_unique_identity_without_an_override_and_honors_one run LIVE against a real server on 2026-08-30 = PASS, asserting non-empty id+name, mutual uniqueness across three mounted tables, the override honored verbatim, label association, and axe zero-blocking with no console errors.

title: Allow per-action message detail in ActionFeedback
description: ActionFeedbackEntry stores only an outcome enum, and ActionFeedbackTexts provides one generic sentence per outcome for the entire component. Real Office mutations must show attempt-specific information such as the affected record, a server conflict reason, a partial-success count, or a retryable transport detail. Pages therefore render raw alert blocks beside the opinionated feedback layer or omit the useful response detail.
design: Extend the keyed action outcome with optional caller-supplied plain-text primary or detail content while keeping ActionFeedbackState authoritative for semantic color, pending behavior, retry, dismiss, and live-region policy. Dynamic domain and server copy stays caller-owned and text-only; framework default text remains the fallback. Tie content to the same keyed transition sequence so an older completion cannot replace a newer message.
acceptance_criteria: Each keyed pending or completed outcome can carry optional attempt-specific text without HTML injection. Missing content uses the localized framework default. Multiple concurrent keys retain independent content, while the one latest transition produces one coherent live announcement. Retry, dismissal, replacement by a newer attempt, stale or duplicate completion, dataset/access generation reset, and locale replacement cannot display detail from another key or attempt. Existing state-only callers remain source-compatible. Native and browser fixtures cover conflict reason, partial-success counts, retryable failure detail, concurrent actions, stale completion, and screen-reader announcement text.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. ActionFeedback's keyed outcomes now carry optional caller-supplied plain-text primary/detail content (text nodes only - no inner_html anywhere, so no HTML injection), while ActionFeedbackState stays authoritative for semantic color, pending behavior, retry, dismiss and live-region policy; missing content falls back to the localized framework default. Content rides the PRE-EXISTING attempt/sequence gate rather than a parallel mechanism, so a stale or duplicate completion cannot attach its text to a newer attempt, and concurrent keys keep independent content while only the latest transition announces. Locale and content are orthogonal by construction: text is composed at render time from live texts, with nothing cached. Commit cb349b9. EVIDENCE: 13 new native pattern tests (adversarial - they assert the FORBIDDEN text is absent), plus action_feedback_attaches_attempt_specific_content_and_rejects_stale_completions in tests/snapshot_table_smoke.rs run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS.

title: Give FilterSidebar search a reactive accessible name
description: FilterSidebar renders its optional search input with only a placeholder. It has no associated label and no aria-label, so the accessible name depends on placeholder fallback and disappears as durable context once a user types. This is the same component-owned accessibility defect previously fixed for DataTable search, and consumers cannot repair the internal input from the call site.
design: Add complete reactive search copy to FilterSidebar, including a dedicated accessible label. Preserve the current optional search behavior and existing source compatibility with a safe documented fallback for callers that have not supplied the new label. Keep search value and filtering caller-owned. The rendered input must have one stable accessible name without adding visible layout or coupling the name to current input value.
acceptance_criteria: When search is present, its input has a nonempty accessible name independent of placeholder and current value. The label reacts to locale changes without replacing the search signal, caret, focus, or typed text. Search omission emits no hidden label. Multiple FilterSidebars on one page remain independently named. Existing callers remain source-compatible under a documented fallback. Native render tests, axe, and a real-browser fixture cover empty, typed, localized, collapsed, expanded, and right-side variants; the input-outside-field audit no longer reports this internal control.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. FilterSidebar's optional search input now has a dedicated reactive accessible name (an sr-only label bound by id plus aria-label), independent of the placeholder and of the current value, mirroring the DataTable search fix (ldui-86h). The id is minted once per instance outside any reactive closure, so a locale change updates only the label text node and the aria-label attribute - the input element is never re-created, and the typed value, caret and focus survive. No hidden label is emitted when search is absent; multiple sidebars stay independently named; callers without the new label get a documented English fallback. Commits bc76c04, 5f5d76c, 96b4f5c. EVIDENCE: 4 native TDD tests plus filter_sidebar_search_accessible_name_covers_every_variant run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS (empty, typed, localized, collapsed, expanded and right-side variants, with axe clean). The live run initially failed only because the test drove the locale toggle with a real CDP click, which legitimately moves focus to the toggle - measuring the click, not the locale change.

title: Support stable value and display label pairs in table filters
description: ServerDataTable filter_options accepts only Vec<String>, so each option uses the same string for transport value and visible label. The Conversations API intentionally returns typed vocabulary entries with kind, stable value, and localized display label. A server column filter therefore cannot submit an authoritative provider or domain value while showing safe user-facing copy, and locale changes would require replacing the query value itself.
design: Introduce a typed column-filter option such as DataTableFilterOption with separate stable value and reactive display label, usable by ServerDataTable and the shared filter-row renderer. Controlled query state continues to carry only the stable value. Preserve the existing Vec<String> path as a source-compatible shorthand where value equals label. Keep vocabulary ownership and transport fetching with the caller; LDUI owns select rendering, accessible naming, controlled value restoration, and localization-safe option replacement.
acceptance_criteria: A filterable column can receive authoritative options whose submitted value differs from visible text. User selection proposes the stable value, while the select and accessible option expose the supplied label. Replacing labels for a locale change leaves the active query value unchanged. Active values remain visible during page and vocabulary refresh; duplicate values, empty reserved values, and a supplied value missing from the new vocabulary have documented fail-closed behavior. Current string options remain source-compatible, local exact-value filtering remains correct, and native plus browser fixtures prove value-label separation, controlled rejection, localization replacement, and an active value absent from the current server slice.
close_reason: Added DataTableFilterOption/DataTableFilterOptions with separate stable values and labels, a source-compatible string adapter, reactive label replacement, controlled rejection restoration, active-value retention, and fail-closed duplicate/empty validation. 245 DataTable tests, showcase WASM check, and existing 32-check reactivity target compile pass.

title: Add controlled single-row selection to ServerDataTable
description: Office Conversations keeps the selected Desk ticket in a page signal, receives only a page-local index from ServerDataTable, and resolves that index against a separate reactive row vector. ServerDataTable cannot render the selected row or expose aria-selected because it deliberately has no selection state machine. During retained loading or cursor replacement, an index can identify a different entity. ldui-or7 supplies stable row identity; the remaining gap is a controlled, identity-based selection seam for server-owned rows.
design: Add an optional controlled single-row selection model to ServerDataTable after stable row keys exist. The caller supplies the selected stable key and receives one proposed replacement key per plain click or keyboard activation. LDUI owns selected-row styling, aria-selected, and focus semantics; the caller continues to own domain selection policy, data fetching, detail launch, and whether a key remains selected when it is outside the displayed slice. Keep row activation and inspection as distinct explicit intents, with documented precedence.
acceptance_criteria: A controlled caller can supply zero or one selected stable row key and receive one key-based proposal from click, Enter, or Space. The matching displayed row renders selected styling and aria-selected; an absent key never selects a same-index replacement. Retained loading, retained failure, cursor next or previous replacement, server sorting, and reactive row replacement cannot transfer selection to a different entity. Rejected or delayed proposals restore the supplied DOM state without feedback loops. Activation and inspection remain separately available, modified-click behavior is documented, existing index-only callers remain source-compatible, and focused native plus browser fixtures cover cursor replacement and keyboard selection.
close_reason: Added controlled stable-key ServerDataTable single selection with fail-closed row_key configuration, selected styling and aria semantics, proposal-first coexistence with activation, native reducer coverage, and expanded existing cursor browser fixture. 241 focused native tests pass; showcase WASM and reactivity target compile.

title: Require truthful filter vocabularies for ServerDataTable
description: When ServerDataTable filtering is enabled and filter_options is omitted, the component derives dropdown choices from distinct values in only the currently displayed server page. The source comments correctly note that this understates a paged population, but the UI still presents those values as the available server filter vocabulary. A user therefore cannot select values that exist outside the current slice, and a selected value can disappear after paging.
design: Introduce an explicit server-filter vocabulary policy. A server-owned table with filterable columns should receive authoritative controlled option sets, or the caller must explicitly declare current-slice filtering semantics. It must not silently infer population-wide choices from one page. Keep local DataTable distinct-value filtering unchanged. Preserve active controlled values during option refresh and make unsupported or contradictory configurations fail visibly in development.
acceptance_criteria: With offset or cursor server paging, every enabled filter column uses an explicit authoritative vocabulary or an explicitly labelled current-slice policy; omitting both cannot render an incomplete dropdown as population truth. Values absent from the current page remain selectable when supplied by the server, and an active value remains visible and removable while rows or vocabularies refresh. Capability disablement removes both controls and proposal paths. Dataset/query reset, localization, empty vocabularies, stale option replacement, and controlled query rejection remain coherent. Existing local DataTable filtering is unchanged, and native/browser fixtures use at least two disjoint server pages to prove the missing-current-page-value case.
close_reason: ServerDataTable now requires authoritative filter_options or an explicit localized current-slice vocabulary, preserves accepted values through refresh, exposes runtime truth markers, and fails ambiguous or conflicting configurations visibly. 243 focused DataTable tests, showcase WASM check, and existing reactivity target compile pass.

title: Carry stable identity and typed payloads through ResultList
description: ResultList accepts only display-only ResultRow values and returns that display copy from on_select. Its render key is page index plus a content hash. Office account search must activate a stable case number and may show duplicate client or summary copy, so No-Hires and Account bypass ResultList with page-local result buttons to retain the transport identity. Encoding an identifier into title or subtitle would couple domain transport to visible copy and still would not provide a typed payload.
design: Add a source-compatible keyed or generic result-list path that separates stable identity and caller payload from title, subtitle, and snippet presentation. LDUI should continue to own listbox semantics, keyboard selection, scrolling, hover, and display. Callers own result payloads and activation effects. Preserve the existing ResultRow API as a convenience adapter.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can provide a stable key, localized display projection, and typed payload for each result; selection and activation return the exact current keyed payload without reconstructing it from display text or index. Replacing results with reordered, duplicate-looking, relabeled, inserted, or removed entries cannot activate a stale payload or transfer selection to another identity. Arrow/Home/End/Enter and pointer behavior, aria-activedescendant IDs, scrolling, empty state, and external result replacement remain coherent. Existing ResultRow callers remain source-compatible, and focused native/browser fixtures reproduce duplicate labels and asynchronous result replacement.
close_reason: Implemented and verified. Public KeyedResultList carries a stable key + localized display projection + typed payload per result; activation returns the exact current keyed payload resolved from live items at activation time (never a captured index or display text), so reordered, duplicate-looking, relabeled, inserted or removed results cannot activate a stale payload. Legacy ResultList/ResultRow callers remain source-compatible via the ResetFirst adapter. EVIDENCE: 32 focused native tests, plus the dedicated browser lane keyed_result_list_smoke run against a real server on 2026-08-30 = 7/7 PASS, covering duplicate labels activating distinct payloads, reorder/insert/relabel/removal identity, keyboard + aria-activedescendant coherence, and the empty state. Commits 4677c7b, 2431a56.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Pause checkpoint 2026-08-29: Tasks 1 and 2 are complete in d90ca43 and 7ac1640. The stable typed item model, validation/reconciliation helpers, and private generic listbox core are implemented; legacy ResultList remains source-compatible through ResetFirst. Focused command cargo test --lib components::result_list --no-default-features passes 28 tests with no warnings. Resume at Task 3: public KeyedResultList, showcase/browser fixture, consumer guide, then final verification and closure. Issue intentionally remains in_progress.

title: Allow FilterBar composition without a global search control
description: FilterBar requires a search Children slot even when a page intentionally has no global search. The approved Office No-Hires page moved search into aligned EntityTable column filters, but it must still supply a fabricated Column filters explainer to satisfy the required slot. That leaves unnecessary utility content above the table and prevents the framework-owned chips, result count, Reset, Save as Default, and actions from standing alone.
design: Make the search slot optional while preserving the current search-first default for existing callers. When absent, omit the search wrapper entirely and let utility controls, active-filter summary, result count, caller actions, Reset, Save as Default, and feedback use the available row width. Keep filter state and persistence caller-controlled.
acceptance_criteria: A FilterBar can render with or without a search control. Search-backed callers render compatibly. A no-search configuration emits no empty or placeholder search region, keeps a coherent region name and keyboard order, and lays out children, active chips, result count, actions, Reset, Save as Default, and feedback without wasted width at wide or compact breakpoints. Search omission does not change filter schema, dataset identity, reset, persistence, or localization behavior. Focused render and browser fixtures cover actions-only, column-filters-only summary, and ordinary search configurations.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. FilterBar's search slot is now optional (Option<Children>), gated with the same .map() idiom the component already uses for its active_binding and result slots, so an absent search emits NO node at all - not an empty or placeholder region - and the remaining framework-owned pieces (chips, result count, Reset, Save as Default, actions, feedback) take the full row width. The search-first layout is preserved for existing callers, which compile unchanged. Filter schema, dataset identity, reset, persistence and localization are untouched: the diff is layout/composition only. Because an omitted node cannot enter the tab order, keyboard order stays coherent by construction. Commit 2c46e71. EVIDENCE: 7 native tests, plus three browser fixtures run LIVE against a real server on 2026-08-30 = PASS: filter_bar_actions_only_omits_the_search_wrapper, filter_bar_columns_only_summary_omits_the_search_wrapper, and filter_bar_ordinary_search_configuration_still_renders_the_search_wrapper_first.

title: Add controlled single-row selection to EntityTable
description: EntityTable exposes stable row keys and on_row_activate but cannot represent which row is currently selected. Office Coordinator, Pending, Office Assignments, and Office Notes all drive a master-detail or target panel from row activation, yet the table cannot highlight or announce that controlled selection. Each page therefore owns selected identity while the opinionated table renders no matching aria-selected or selected-row state.
design: Add an optional controlled single-selection binding, separate from row activation and row actions. A small EntityTableSelection value should carry the selected stable row key and emit replacement proposals. EntityTable owns selected-row styling and accessibility; callers retain domain state, detail loading, and whether activation also changes selection. Keep the default non-selectable rendering source-compatible.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can bind an optional selected stable row key and receive one selection proposal for pointer or documented keyboard selection. The matching wide and compact row has coherent selected styling and aria-selected semantics without changing the canonical row key. Row-action controls do not accidentally select or activate the row. External selection replacement, filtering, sorting, paging, row removal, dataset replacement, disabled/noninteractive rows, and a selected key absent from the visible page have documented fail-safe behavior. Define duplicate and empty-key behavior explicitly and fail visibly in development rather than silently aliasing rows.
acceptance_criteria: A server table caller can provide a stable key for each row; DOM/render identity follows that key across retained loading, cursor replacement, offset navigation, sorting proposals, and reactive row updates; focus and any detail state do not transfer to a different entity occupying the same numeric slot; keyed activation/inspection returns the displayed entity identity without a second index lookup race; duplicate or empty keys have documented fail-closed behavior; existing index-only callers remain source-compatible; focused native and browser fixtures cover reordered rows, cursor next/previous replacement, retained failure, insertion/removal, and a duplicate-key rejection.

title: DataTable: per-row full-width detail subrow for long explanatory text
notes:
NO LONGER BLOCKING ANYTHING (2026-08-28). The 4iiz-etl case that prompted this
bead has been solved WITHOUT a detail subrow, because investigating the data
changed the answer.

The "why" text on that mirror table is not per-row: it comes from
`Verdict::why()`, a `&'static str` with seven possible values, one per verdict.
As a column it printed the same sentence on every healthy row. A detail subrow
would therefore have repeated identical text under every row using twice the
height — worse than the column, not better. It became a LEGEND instead: one line
per verdict present, and the table converted to DataTable normally.

KEEPING THIS OPEN, at lower urgency. A per-row full-width detail row is still
the right primitive for genuinely per-row long text, and the requirements in the
original note stand as written. What changed is only that no consumer is waiting
on it today, so it can be designed alongside ldui-gbs (geometry stability across
sorting) rather than ahead of it — which was the interaction the original note
flagged as the risky part anyway.

⚠️ WORTH KEEPING FROM THIS EPISODE, for whoever implements it: before adding a
subrow to hold a long column, check whether the text VARIES per row. If it is
derived from a small enum, a legend is smaller, always visible, and needs no
library change at all.

description: Found while building 4iiz-etl's operator-console History page (bead bd_4iiz-etl-rnn.16, report .superpowers/sdd/c45-report.md in that repo): DataTableServerComponent/ServerDataTable does not forward on_row_activate or on_row_inspect (the ldui-tmr double-click callback) to DataTableBody at all, unlike the client-paged DataTable where ldui-tmr landed fully.
