Fix: forward both callbacks in the server variant identically to the client one, matching the deferred-single-click/dblclick-cancel timing.
close_reason: ServerDataTable forwards on_row_activate/on_row_inspect to the shared body with the same click/dblclick/keyboard contract as DataTable (page-local indices, documented); demo wiring + a browser test prove rows are keyboard-operable and a plain click activates; reactivity suite green. 4iiz-etl History can drop the per-cell-link workaround.

title: SegmentedBar/PhaseProgress: partial fill of the current segment
description: Needed by 4iiz-etl portal redesign: the run capsule instrument showing capture -> reconcile -> apply as three equal segments where completed segments are solid, the current segment is partially filled to a percent, and future segments are muted; optional failed tone for the current segment. SegmentedBar today renders discrete token cells only. Either extend SegmentedBar with a per-segment fill fraction or add a small PhaseProgress component following the CapacityBar prop style (phases: &[&str], current: usize, pct: u8, failed: bool, aria-label from phase+pct). Used on every Running Now row and on the run-detail template.
close_reason: PhaseProgress component landed: equal-width phase segments with partial current fill, failed tone, progressbar semantics (valuetext = phase+pct per the bead), data-phase-state contract, 16 unit tests, demo page. Chose a new component over extending SegmentedBar since segment identity (phase) and fill semantics differ from proportional distribution.

title: DataTable: double-click row activation callback
description: Needed by 4iiz-etl portal redesign. DataTable has on_row_activate (single click / Enter) but no secondary activation. Add on_row_inspect: Callback<usize> fired on dblclick (and a keyboard equivalent, e.g. Shift+Enter) so list pages can use click = drilldown navigation and double-click = raw record inspector (Modal with field=value list). Must not interfere with click-to-select or fire on_row_activate twice; standard dblclick discrimination is acceptable since single-click navigation is non-destructive.
close_reason: on_row_inspect landed: dblclick + Shift+Enter secondary activation with detail>1 click swallowing so on_row_activate fires exactly once per double-click; pure discriminators unit-tested; demo coverage with testids. Full-suite verification deferred to end-of-session gate run per owner instruction.

title: Gauge: arc gauge component with budget bands
description: Needed by 4iiz-etl portal redesign (Home instrument cluster). A ~240-degree arc gauge: value/max with unit label and sub-caption, tabular-nums readout, and warn/error budget bands painted on the track (thresholds as fractions). radial_progress is a full-ring daisyUI progress and does not cover banded thresholds or the open-arc dial form. Should follow the CapacityBar/SlaChip pattern: pure props, no fetching, @source inline doc header for Tailwind safelist. Consumers: server CPU/memory/disk/network gauges on the portal home page.
close_reason: Gauge landed: 240-degree arc dial, warn/error bands as threshold fractions on the track, zone-escalating value arc, tabular-nums readout with unit and sub-caption, role=meter, paint routed per svg_paint_routing, unit tests and demo page. Full-suite verification deferred to end-of-session gate run per owner instruction.

title: The gate never lints xtask — the crate that IS the gate. A clippy error has sat there since 2026-07-26
description: cargo xtask verify runs clippy-lib, clippy-demo and clippy-audit. There is no clippy-xtask step, so the xtask crate is never lint-gated. Consequence: cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings currently FAILS (real exit 101) on clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args at xtask/src/main.rs:1717, introduced by b68c94a on 2026-07-26 and undetected for two weeks. verify reports 13/13 PASS throughout. This is the same family as the test-mode feature being invisible to the gate (fixed 2026-08-09, 052a125): a step list that enumerates crates will silently omit whatever is added later, and here it omits the tool that enforces the whole gate. Note test-xtask DOES run xtask's tests, so the crate is not entirely unguarded - it is specifically the lint that is missing.
design: Add a clippy-xtask step alongside clippy-lib/clippy-demo/clippy-audit and update the exact-list assertion at xtask/src/main.rs:1301 (vec!["clippy-lib", "clippy-demo", "clippy-audit"]) plus the doc/ci-cd.md gate table. Fix the existing lint in the same change or the new step lands red. Clippy must stay PER-CRATE here - --workspace fails on leptos csr feature unification.
acceptance_criteria: cargo xtask verify includes a clippy-xtask step and is 14/14 green. Deliberately reintroducing a lint in xtask/src/main.rs turns the gate red.
notes: Found 2026-08-10 while verifying the ldui-hun fix: a rust-analyzer dead_code diagnostic prompted an independent clippy run, which failed. The implementing agent's 'clippy -D warnings clean' claim was accurate for the crates the gate covers - xtask simply is not one of them. Also worth noting the pipe trap bit me here in real time: 'cargo clippy ... | tail -8' reported exit 0 because that is tail's status; the real code was 101.
close_reason: Fixed in d0b86d9. Added a clippy-xtask gate step (verify is now 14 steps), widened and renamed the exact-list assertion to clippy_subcommand_runs_every_crate_step so a future crate cannot be added without failing it, documented the row in doc/ci-cd.md with the REASON rather than just the command, and fixed the two-week-old needless_borrows_for_generic_args it exposed. Verified independently by me, not delegated: cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings went 101 -> 0, cargo test -p xtask 37 passed, and clippy-xtask PASSES in the gate run. NOTE the same gate run is 10/14 for reasons unrelated to this change - see ldui-2rz.

title: FilterSidebar: a side prop for right-oriented panels
description:
REQUESTED BY: 4iiz-Office (owner live-review feedback 2026-08-09): the Client Coordinator workspace needs its RIGHT-hand Assistant panel collapsible, mirroring the left FilterSidebar.

THE GAP: FilterSidebar has no side/orientation prop — it is left-oriented only (collapsed rail on the left, toggle chevron pointing right, rotated title reading downward). A right-hand panel needs the mirror: rail on the right, chevron pointing left when expanded, and the collapsed rail's rotated title reading the natural direction for a right edge.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a `side: SidebarSide` prop (Left default, Right) that flips the chevron direction, the border side, and the rotated-title orientation. Everything else (collapsed/on_toggle/active_count/title/toggle_label/children) is orientation-independent and stays as is.

CONSUMER NOTE: 4iiz-Office is using a minimal inline collapse on the right panel meanwhile (per its placeholder convention) and will swap to this when it ships.
close_reason: Landed fe3eaab. side: SidebarSide (Left default, Right, #[non_exhaustive]) in a new style.rs per the Module Structure convention. Found TWO left-hardcoded sites the bead did not name: the 52px header row order (justify-between + DOM order put the toggle at the inner edge only by accident of being second; on a right panel that pins it against the window frame and inverts the affordance - fixed with flex-row-reverse, measured in-browser), and the prose contract in three doc sites saying 'A left-hand collapsible filter panel'. Audited clean: no shadow-*, no side-specific rounded-*, no origin- needed (rail centres at x=22 of 44 both sides), padding symmetric. The filter-search magnifier stays left - that is reading direction, not orientation - and is pinned by a test. Left output proven byte-identical TWICE: source-level rebuild diffed against git show HEAD (5/5, differences=0) and DOM-level read from the running browser, including no trailing space on the header. verify 13/13, 2171 lib tests, style 7/7, layout 9/9, no ceiling raised.

title: Gantt dependency-preview line uses dead daisyUI 4 vars in a stroke= attribute — likely invisible today
description: src/components/gantt/timeline/dependency_preview.rs:50,52 hardcode 'var(--fallback-su,oklch(var(--su)/1))' and the --wa equivalent, emitted at :62 as stroke=move || stroke_color.get(). TWO defects in one line. (1) --su/--wa/--fallback-su are daisyUI 4 variable names and DO NOT EXIST in daisyUI 5 - verified by grep against demo/node_modules/daisyui/daisyui.css, zero matches. With no valid resolution the whole oklch() is invalid, the presentation attribute is dropped, and stroke falls back to its initial value NONE - so the dependency-drag preview line is almost certainly not rendering at all today. (2) Independently, this is a var() inside a stroke= PRESENTATION ATTRIBUTE, the exact hazard src/charts/paint.rs exists to eliminate: SVG2 parses presentation attributes with the property's isolated value grammar, so custom-property substitution is not specified to run there, and the SVG WG has an open request (Nov 2025) to specify or forbid it. src/components/gantt/timeline/timeline_markers.rs:460,474 have the same shape with a CALLER-SUPPLIED colour, so a consumer passing var(--color-primary) lands it straight in stroke=/fill=.
design: Replace the dead daisyUI 4 vars with daisyUI 5 tokens (var(--color-success) / var(--color-warning)). Then route through crate::charts::paint - but note attrs_for (src/charts/paint.rs:45) returns the WHOLE style value and dependency_preview.rs:67 already carries a static style='opacity: 0.7; pointer-events: none;', so this needs a style-MERGING variant of attrs_for, not a second call site. That merging variant is the real work here.
acceptance_criteria: The dependency preview line renders visibly during a drag under daisyUI 5, in both the valid-target and invalid-target states. No var() appears in any stroke= or fill= presentation attribute anywhere under src/components/gantt/. The charts routing guard (tests/charts_paint_routing.rs) is extended to scan beyond src/charts, or a sibling guard covers gantt.
notes: Found 2026-08-09 by the ldui-1g5 review, which correctly flagged that the new guard's blast radius stops at src/charts: tests/charts_paint_routing.rs:1555 scans only that directory, so the gate reads 13/13 green while this ships. I verified both halves independently - the var()-in-stroke at the source, and the absence of --su in daisyUI 5.
close_reason: Landed 6d65df0 + fix round 6c7147a. The preview line WAS invisible - computed stroke 'none' before, real oklch after; only the currentColor arrowheads rendered. Fixed the dead daisyUI 4 tokens, routed all SVG paint through a new n-ary merge_style, and widened the guard in place (charts_paint_routing.rs -> svg_paint_routing.rs, scanning all of src/). The guard immediately found a THIRD site (today_navigation.rs: today line invisible, today column falling back to fill rgb(0,0,0) - the solid-black failure paint.rs predicts, observed live). Review then found a FOURTH (dependency_link.rs:192) and a FIFTH with a far wider blast radius (tokens/animations.rs .ld-focus-ring, dead --p on all EIGHT focusable control types - ring silently resolved to currentColor, near-white against a primary fill). Also caught that tokens/tests.rs:379 was ASSERTING the dead token, pinning the bug in place. All three reviewer-demonstrated guard bypasses closed with named negative controls asserting offenders==1 (comment-zeroed scan, attr: prefix skipped, name laundering), plus logical_lines added unprompted so a rustfmt wrap cannot poison a routed binding. Exhaustive re-sweep of every daisyUI 4 variable family across src/, demo/src/, styles/, audit/, xtask/ returns nothing. Verified independently by me.

title: RosterGrid: roving tabindex + arrow navigation (a 2-D grid is currently rows x cols tab stops)
description: RosterGrid puts tabindex=0 on every tile, so a 30-worker x 7-day roster is 210 sequential Tab presses to traverse and reach the next control. DataTable is one stop per ROW and DayScheduler one per EVENT; a roster is inherently two-dimensional, so the count is the PRODUCT rather than a sum. Keyboard-operable but not keyboard-usable.
design: The ARIA grid pattern: roving tabindex (one tab stop for the whole grid) with Arrow/Home/End moving focus between cells. cell_key_activates (src/components/roster_grid/types.rs:122) is deliberately Enter/Space-only, so the arrow keys are free. This repo already implements roving focus in MenuItem - follow that.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered roster of any size presents exactly ONE tab stop. Arrow keys move focus between cells, Home/End to row extremes. Enter/Space still activate. A display-only roster still has no tab stop at all.
notes: Raised by the ldui-m9s review 2026-08-09, explicitly as a follow-up rather than a blocker. Retrofitting this LATER changes the focus contract consumers will have built against, so it is worth doing before office-perf-web adopts the component.
close_reason: Landed b70c0ef + 55387bf, fix round e9d2866. Reviewed and re-reviewed clean. Roving focus verified in the live DOM (84 tiles, exactly 1 tabindex=0, invariant maintained across key presses; ArrowLeft at col 0 does not wrap). clamp_focus_cell is pure, Option-returning, short-circuits on n==0 before n-1, with two exhaustive sweeps. Fix round closed a regression THIS feature introduced - Alt/Cmd+Arrow (browser Back/Forward) were being swallowed by an unconditional prevent_default - plus Ctrl+Home/End dead on macOS, and named the interactive demo grids. Also adopted all 3 optional items: aria-selected on the gridcell replacing aria-pressed (which was asserting a toggle the component does not control), focused promoted to a Memo, and a no-op-movement early return that preserves the restorable raw coordinate.

title: visual-quality: fallback-font rulebook entry now understates coverage — engine catches missing @font-face as of PixelProof-zbr
description: doc/visual-quality/fallback-font.md is headed 'partially automated ... does NOT catch a missing @font-face' and its coverage table tells consumers the missing-declaration row needs a project-local STATIC check (e.g. office-perf-web font_pipeline.rs). PixelProof-zbr landed 2026-08-09 (PixelProof commit 9b5020a): the sweep now MEASURES whether the declared family actually paints (canvas metrics vs two generics) instead of asking document.fonts.check, and reports 'does not resolve — no @font-face rule and no system font by that name' as a distinct TYPOGRAPHY violation from the existing 'has an @font-face rule but never loaded'. Both rows are now automated, proven by browser negative controls. Update the status line and coverage table, and re-verify against the real suite by deleting the @font-face block (the empirical test that originally exposed the gap) before relaxing any static check — do NOT drop office-perf-web's font_pipeline.rs on the strength of this description alone. TRAP carried over: Trunk emits integrity= on the stylesheet, so hand-editing built CSS makes the browser discard the file and render unstyled, which looks like a spectacular detection and is an artifact; edit source and rebuild.
close_reason: Rulebook updated (68cedb8): both failure modes now automated per PixelProof-zbr, with the caveat the bead did not have - a CSS generic family is exempt from the resolution probe (PixelProof-1mf), and Tailwind's default stack starts with ui-sans-serif, so an app pinning from body_font_family() gets NO coverage. Static font_pipeline.rs check explicitly retained, not relaxed.

title: DataTable — a per-row action-column slot
description: REQUESTED BY: 4iiz-Office, crates/office-perf-web/src/screens/workspace/coordinator/open_work.rs and .../manager/exceptions.rs. THE GAP: widgets::DataTable has no slot for a per-row ACTION column, so any table needing row-level buttons (Open / Complete / Delete / Call / SMS) cannot use it. CONSEQUENCE TODAY: both consumers fall back to composing raw Table/TableRow/TableCell plus Button by hand, which loses DataTable's sorting, density and column-sizing behaviour and duplicates layout logic across screens. WHAT IS NEEDED: an action-column slot on DataTable that receives the row and returns a view, rendered in a right-aligned cell that does not participate in sorting. NOTE FOR THE DESIGN: office-perf's rows carry up to seven action controls, several DISABLED with an explanatory tooltip (e.g. 'no call/SMS route resolves for every work type this row can carry'), so the slot must tolerate a variable number of controls and disabled states rather than assuming one button. ★ FILED 2026-08-09 — referenced in office-perf source but absent from this board until now.
close_reason: Landed 3a46607 + fix round 226053d. Reviewed: requirement satisfied, index arithmetic verified structurally safe (data indices minted by enumerating data collections; bulk-select and action cells are siblings outside those loops), row identity traced through sort+paging+bulk_select. Reactivity contract documented correctly, sr-only Actions header, test-layout ratchet unchanged at (2,0).

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
MERGED FROM ldui-b1n (duplicate, superseded). Additional consumer detail: the affected tables are Open Work, Awaiting Assignment, Per-worker Load and Office Exceptions (4iiz-Office workspace plan 2026-08-09, Tasks B2/C1/C5). Wanted actions are icon buttons: complete / delete / open / call / sms.
VERIFIED 2026-08-09 against this repo before implementing: the target is src/widgets/data_table.rs (rows: Vec<Vec<String>>, no render hook) - NOT src/components/data_table/, which ALREADY has Column::action() plus cell_renderers: Vec<Callback<(usize, TableRow), AnyView>> via Column.renderer_index. The two DataTables are distinct components. Worth deciding explicitly whether the widget grows a render hook or whether these consumers should move to components::DataTable, rather than assuming.

title: RosterGrid / ScheduleGrid — a worker x weekday shift matrix
description: REQUESTED BY: 4iiz-Office, crates/office-perf-web/src/screens/workspace/setup/schedule.rs (the Office Setup page's schedule section). THE GAP: there is no roster/shift-matrix control in leptos-daisyui-rs. WeekView and DayScheduler are TIME-CALENDARS (hours down one axis), which is a different shape from what a staffing roster needs: a grid of WORKER x WEEKDAY where each cell carries a shift (or an absence), not an hour range. WHAT IS THERE NOW: a MINIMAL Table-cell placeholder, built to the owner's direction rather than hand-rolling a substitute, with this bead named on screen so the gap is visible instead of silently missing. WHAT IS NEEDED: a RosterGrid/ScheduleGrid taking rows = workers, columns = weekdays, cells = a shift value plus a state (working / off / holiday), ideally with a compact and a comfortable density. CONSUMER NOTE: office-perf will swap the placeholder for the real component when this ships; the placeholder is deliberately minimal so that swap is clean. ★ FILED 2026-08-09 — the office-perf source has referenced this id since the Setup page was built and it did NOT exist on this board until now; the code comment claimed it was filed. Eight such ids were referenced and none existed.
close_reason: Landed d32266b + fix round 561514a. Reviewed: all 5 non-negotiables met; normalize_cells total in both directions with no indexing/unwrap/panic in the module. Blocking finding fixed - a read-only selected_cell no longer fakes interactivity (display-only roster: 20 tiles, 0 tabindex/role/aria-pressed, ring still live), now pinned by grid_is_interactive + a regression test. Follow-ups ldui-m9s.1 (roving tabindex) and .2 (polish).

title: BarChart: no per-bar colour prop
description: charts::BarChart takes one color: String applied to every bar - no per-bar colour override. A consumer with a mixed above/below-baseline series (e.g. state_for-derived on-track vs behind weeks) cannot colour individual bars, only the whole chart. Found building the 4iiz-Office Office Leader closed-work-by-week chart (op-wa07 Task C4): worked around it by colouring the whole chart via a wrapping div's Tailwind text colour + color="currentColor", keyed off the series' overall majority state, and restoring the per-bar judgement as a row of Badge chips underneath (one per bar). Wanted: an optional Vec<String> colors (same length as data) that overrides the single color per-bar.
close_reason: Landed 398d525/627444f/45cb392 + fix round c153c58. Reviewed, fix round re-reviewed clean. Progress value/max (indeterminate preserved, verified in Chrome), BarChart bar_colors (total fallback, no panic on length mismatch), Heatmap HeatScale::Judgement with theme-token defaults meeting all 3 consumer constraints. Vacuous symmetry test fixed and proven by see-it-fail.

title: Heatmap: no favourable/unfavourable dual-hue axis
description: charts::Heatmap takes one rgb tint whose alpha scales with intensity (0..1) - single hue only. A consumer judging cells against a target (state_for-style OnTrack/Behind) has no way to express the judgement as colour, only magnitude. Found building the 4iiz-Office Office Leader KPI-by-office heatmap (op-wa07/op-bkh7 Task C3): had to fall back to intensity=|deviation| with a single accent hue, and restore the judgement as the cell's text label instead of colour. Wanted: an optional second rgb (e.g. favorable_rgb/unfavorable_rgb) or a signed intensity (-1..1) where sign picks the hue and magnitude picks the alpha.
close_reason: Landed 398d525/627444f/45cb392 + fix round c153c58. Reviewed, fix round re-reviewed clean. Progress value/max (indeterminate preserved, verified in Chrome), BarChart bar_colors (total fallback, no panic on length mismatch), Heatmap HeatScale::Judgement with theme-token defaults meeting all 3 consumer constraints. Vacuous symmetry test fixed and proven by see-it-fail.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
MERGED FROM ldui-g2c (duplicate, superseded). Two constraints from the consumer that this bead did not carry and that bind the design:
(1) NO NEW COLOUR - the palette must come from existing daisyUI theme tokens (success/warning/error), not new hues. So the dual-hue axis should take theme tokens, not raw rgb triples, or at minimum accept both.
(2) COLOUR MUST CARRY THE JUDGEMENT ONLY, NEVER THE CATEGORY - office-perf's KPI legend states this explicitly. So the API must not tempt a consumer into colouring by series/category.
(3) SENSE IS PER-MEASURE, NOT GLOBAL: for some measures higher is better, for others lower is (handle time, overdue count). A single global 'higher is good' flag is insufficient - sense must be settable per cell or per column.
Consumer site: crates/office-perf-web/src/screens/workspace/manager/kpi_by_office.rs

title: Pilot proof: break-and-revert
description: Plan Task 12 in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-08-visual-quality-checks.md. In office-perf-web input.css temporarily: (1) comment out the Manrope font-face -> typography family must fire on all text (the statically-uncatchable regression); (2) corrupt --shadow-card to 0 9px 9px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5) -> depth family fires. Restore both, re-run green. Paste both failing describe() outputs as a comment on this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Both injected regressions caught and cleared; evidence recorded in bead comment
close_reason: Both controls seen failing and recovering. Also disproved the brief's typography premise: a missing @font-face leaves the suite green (vacuous document.fonts.check). Rulebook corrected 61ace74; engine bead PixelProof-zbr filed.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Task 12 break-and-revert executed against office-perf-web, 2026-08-09, at 1440x900
against one fixed bundle (build 03:19). Baseline and final runs both: 4 passed, exit 0,
zero slack notes. All artifacts restored byte-identical (md5 + the font's sha384 back to
`.bundle-ready`'s manifest value).

METHOD. Not `input.css`. That repo has a live concurrent session committing every few
minutes, so the break window was moved off any tracked file: the controls edit the BUILT
stylesheet in `crates/office-perf-web/dist/` (gitignored) and the suite is driven by the
already-compiled `style_audit` test binary. The direct driver was first proven equivalent
to `cargo make test-style` by reproducing the green baseline exactly.

Two traps found while getting this right, both of which silently fake a "detection":
- **Subresource Integrity.** Trunk emits `<link ... integrity="sha384-...">`, so ANY edit
  to `output-*.css` makes the browser DISCARD THE WHOLE STYLESHEET. The first attempt
  rendered the app unstyled, `--font-sans` was undefined, `body_font_family` read back
  "Times New Roman", and the suite "failed" with typography 41-57 on every route. That is
  not the audit detecting a font regression; it is the audit comparing against garbage.
  The sha384 must be recomputed and index.html rewritten with every edit.
- **`.shadow-card` cannot be the depth target.** Confirmed PixelProof-gbg from the DOM:
  a card computes as five layers, four inert
  (`rgba(0,0,0,0) 0px 0px 0px 0px` x4, then `rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0px 1px 15px 0px`), so it
  already reports 1 violation whatever `--shadow-card` holds. One violation per element,
  then break -> corrupting `--shadow-card` moves NO count. The depth control therefore
  targets `.btn:not(.btn-ghost):not(.btn-link)`, which `office_profile` declares and which
  is clean at baseline.

=============================================================================
CONTROL 1 (typography) - THE BRIEF'S LITERAL STEP 1 DOES NOT FAIL. NEW FINDING.
=============================================================================

Commenting out the Manrope `@font-face` block leaves the suite GREEN:

    test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; ... finished in 10.70s   REALEXIT=0

Mechanism, probed in-page with the block removed:

    document.fonts.check('16px "Manrope"') -> true
    document.fonts.size                    -> 0        (FontFaceSet EMPTY)
    getComputedStyle(body).fontFamily      -> "Manrope, -apple-system, ... sans-serif"
    getComputedStyle(body).fontWeight      -> "500"

Both font rules in the engine sweep are blind to this. Rule 1
(`!document.fonts.check(...)`) is vacuously TRUE because no face matches, so nothing is
"unloaded". Rule 2 (per-element first-family string) never fires because `--font-sans`
still NAMES Manrope, so every computed value still reads "Manrope" while the text
actually paints in the fallback. Nothing in the rendered computed style distinguishes
this from a healthy page.

So this regression is caught only STATICALLY, by `font_pipeline.rs`'s
`INPUT_CSS.contains(r#"font-family: "Manrope""#)` - the opposite of the brief's premise.

CONTROL 1b (typography, the regression that IS caught): keep the `@font-face` and make
the woff2 404 (the realistic "font pipeline broke" case - a face declared but unloadable).

    document.fonts.check('16px "Manrope"') -> false
    document.fonts.size                    -> 1, faces: [{family:"Manrope", status:"error"}]
    getComputedStyle(body).fontFamily      -> "Manrope, -apple-system, ..."   (IDENTICAL)

Note the computed family is byte-identical in both scenarios; rule 1 is the ONLY thing
separating them. Suite result - all four routes fail, +1 typography each, nothing else
moved:

    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 4 failed; ... finished in 10.27s   REALEXIT=101

    thread 'queue_style_is_within_ceiling' panicked at
      crates\office-perf-web\tests\style_audit.rs:383:85:
    /queue: over ceiling - typography: 5 > ceiling 4
    style audit for /queue: 210 scanned, 48 total across 7 families
      TYPOGRAPHY      0.00  @font-face  declared family "Manrope" is not loaded - text is
                                        silently falling back
      TYPOGRAPHY     10.00  nav.flex.flex-col > div.flex-1.min-h-0 > div.w-full.pt-1 ...
      TYPOGRAPHY     10.00  nav.flex.flex-col > div.flex-1.min-h-0 > div.w-full.pt-1 ...
      TYPOGRAPHY     10.00  nav.flex.flex-col > div.flex-1.min-h-0 > div.w-full.pt-1 ...
      TYPOGRAPHY     24.00  div.flex.items-start > div > div.flex.items-center > h2...

    /account:   typography: 6 > ceiling 5   (123 scanned, 39 total)
    /settings:  typography: 5 > ceiling 4   (116 scanned, 35 total)

  ul.menu             display:flex  flex-direction:column  flex-wrap:wrap

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
FIXED. Cause was not the flex-wrap I first suspected.

The '.menu-title's parent turned out to be a <span role=menuitem>, not the
<li> daisyUI documents. That span is rendered by MenuItem's NON-INTERACTIVE
is_submenu branch (component.rs, the final 'else'), which wraps children so
the container keeps an id/role/tabindex for roving focus.

daisyUI styles a menu item's content box as
  display: grid; grid-auto-flow: column; align-items: center
so an icon, label and badge share one line. Its selector excludes a direct
'ul' and '.menu-title' -- but NOT our wrapper. So the structural container
collected the item grid and laid the MenuTitle out beside its SubMenu,
vertically centred, instead of above it.

That also explains why my first two hypotheses were wrong:
- 'wraps into columns': forcing flex-wrap:nowrap changed nothing, because the
  wrap was never involved.
- 'something is ~55px too wide': the scrollWidth 263 vs clientWidth 208
  overflow is real but INCIDENTAL -- it is still 263 after the fix. It is a
  long label in a w-64 rail, not this bug. Not worth a ticket on its own; the
  rail scrolls.

FIX: the wrapper carries 'contents' (display: contents), so it generates no
box and its children rejoin the <li>'s flow -- the structure daisyUI
documents -- while keeping the attributes the focus machinery needs. Removing
the wrapper outright was the alternative but would have taken the id, role and
tabindex with it.

MEASURED in the live page:
  before  title (36,252)  nested list (125,138)  titleAboveSub false
  after   title (24,132)  nested list ( 40,169)  titleAboveSub true
          all group titles share x=24 (Action 132, Data Display 433,
          Navigation 1634) -- a column again, not a row

Three tests pin it, including that 'contents' stays in the documented
@source inline list, since a consumer copying that list into their own
input.css would otherwise reproduce the bug with no way to see why.

Gate 9/9. Confirmed against the rendered PNG: the sidebar now matches the
2026-07-06 baseline's structure.

BASELINES: still stale and still NOT recaptured. alert is 0.7194 (was 0.6907
before this fix). The residue is legitimate -- my Section gap change plus two
nav entries ('SWR Cache', 'Toolbar') added since the baseline -- but the other
8 pages have not been eyeballed yet, and recapturing blesses whatever is on
screen. That review is the remaining work.

title: Browser suites leak a Chrome profile dir per harness launch (~1.5GB/session)
description:
Found while tidying up after the ldui-mai epic.

tests/common/mod.rs::config() mints a unique throwaway Chrome profile dir per
harness launch:

    let unique = format!("ldui-pp-profile-{}-{}", pid, nanos);
    cfg = cfg.with_launch_arg(format!("--user-data-dir={}", profile_dir));

The unique-per-launch part is deliberate and correct -- it was added because a
shared profile leaked localStorage (the persisted theme) between tests and
runs. What is missing is the other half: nothing ever removes the directory.

Measured: 81 dirs / ~1.5 GB accumulated in %TEMP% across one working session,
on top of 93 cleared earlier the same day. Every visual, reactivity and
layout-audit test launch adds one.

Note this is INDEPENDENT of the Harness::drop deadlock fixed in PixelProof
126acfe. That bug meant the browser never closed cleanly; this one persists
even now that it does, because the directory is created by the test config
rather than owned by the Harness.

Options, roughly in order of preference:
  a) Give pixelproof-web's Harness ownership of the profile dir -- it can
     create it, and remove it in Drop after the handler is aborted (the child
     is dead by then, so the files are unlocked). Fixes it for every consumer
     of the crate, not just this repo.
  b) Have config() reap any ldui-pp-profile-* dir older than, say, an hour on
     startup. Self-healing and cheap, but leaves the current run's dir behind.
  c) Wrap the path in a Drop guard on the test side.

(a) is the real fix; (b) is a good belt-and-braces addition regardless, since
a killed test process can never clean up after itself.

Not urgent -- it is disk, not correctness -- but it is silent and unbounded,
which is how you end up with tens of gigabytes in %TEMP% and no idea why.
close_reason: Harness now owns the profile dir (PixelProof f03cdcc): removed on close(), removed in Drop after explicitly dropping the Browser first, and strays reaped on the next launch for processes that were killed. 14 harness launches now leave zero directories behind; verify-full 12/12.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
FIXED via option (a), the real fix, plus (b) as a genuine necessity rather
than belt-and-braces.

PixelProof f03cdcc adds HarnessConfig::with_isolated_profile(). The harness now
mints and OWNS the directory instead of the caller passing --user-data-dir and
nobody deleting it. Opt-in, off by default: turning it on unilaterally would
change where Chrome stores state for every existing consumer.

Cleanup is layered, because no single layer suffices:
  close()   removes it after the CDP close handshake, when the child is
            already reaped. The reliable path.
  Drop      now drops the Browser FIRST. This was the subtle part: Drop runs
            its body BEFORE the struct's fields drop, so without the explicit
            drop the child was still alive and still holding the directory
            open on Windows when we tried to remove it. 'browser' became an
            Option purely to make that ordering expressible. Then it retries
            briefly, because kill_on_drop terminates the child asynchronously.
  reaper    collects strays on the next launch. NOT optional: a test process
            killed by a timeout, taskkill, or a cancelled CI job never runs
            teardown at all, so without this those leftovers are permanent.

The reaper is deliberately conservative -- exact prefix match, only dirs
untouched for an hour -- because it runs against the shared OS temp dir, where
being wrong means deleting somebody else's data. Two of its four tests exist
only to pin that: one asserts an unrelated directory survives the most
aggressive possible threshold, the other that a near-miss prefix
('pixelproof-profil') survives too.

Its threshold is a parameter rather than a constant so the tests can drive
staleness directly. Back-dating a DIRECTORY's mtime on Windows needs
FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS -- my first attempt failed with Access Denied --
and the parameter is the better seam anyway.

MEASURED, not assumed:
  before   1 directory (~18 MB) per harness launch, forever
  after    14 harness launches across the reactivity and layout suites
           leave ZERO directories behind
  gate     cargo xtask verify-full 12/12
  crate    pixelproof-web 42/42 lib tests

Consumer side: tests/common/mod.rs drops ~15 lines of hand-rolled path code
for one builder call.

after the ldui-1mx migration, and nearly all are in the size family (w-/h-).
The single biggest contributor:

  icon and icon_tile span 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 64 px

20px and 40px are off the canonical scale (4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,96). But this
is not a mechanical substitution -- it is a design decision about how many icon
sizes the library should offer and what they mean. Snapping 20 -> 24 and
40 -> 48 changes rendered icon sizes wherever those steps are used.

Related, same shape: base_theme_selector, gantt and kanban each use BOTH 20px
and 24px for what looks like the same small-control role (see the audit's
same-role table). Whatever ramp is chosen should settle that too.

Suggested approach: define the ramp as a named enum with as_str() like the
other style enums, decide its steps deliberately, then migrate call sites to it.

Not urgent -- these are on the 4px grid, just not on the 9-step scale, so
nothing here is a rendering bug.

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md (F4, F5)
close_reason: Premise corrected: both are already named enums, and 20/40 are legitimate size steps, not off-scale spacing -- sizes are a separate family. Fixed the real issue: 5 call sites that bypassed the enums now use IconSize::Small. Four tests pin the ramp, including an explicit assertion that it is allowed off the spacing scale.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
DONE, but the ticket's premise was wrong and the resolution is different from
what it proposed.

PREMISE CORRECTION: icon/icon_tile were never 'seven raw utilities'. Both are
already named enums with as_str():
  IconSize      16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48   (XSmall..XLarge)
  IconTileSize  24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 64   (Xs..Xl)

once, not at one component improvising.

DECISION: do NOT snap 20 and 40 onto the canonical spacing scale. Sizes are a
separate family from spacing. Spacing answers 'how far apart?' and must land on
the scale; a size ramp answers 'how big?' and follows its own roughly
geometric progression. Snapping IconSize::Small 20 -> 24 collides with Medium,
and 20 -> 16 collides with XSmall; IconTileSize::Md 40 (the DEFAULT) collides
with Lg at 48 and Sm at 32 either way. Both ramps would collapse from 5 steps
to 4 for no benefit. The shared token crate already takes this position --
TABLE_ROW_HEIGHT is 40 and nobody flagged it.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and is now fixed: five call sites bypassed the enums
and hardcoded the utilities, which is the real 'raw utilities' problem the
ticket was pointing at:
  base_theme_selector/component.rs:102  h-5 w-5 text-primary
  base_theme_selector/component.rs:115  w-5 h-5
  kanban/column.rs:101,213              w-5 h-5
  gantt/timeline/today_navigation.rs:150 h-5 w-5

    scale (asserts !is_on_scale(20)) so the exemption is stated, not implied
  - the ramp is strictly ascending
  - IconSize::Medium == ui_tokens NAV_ICON_SIZE, so where the desktop names an
    icon dimension the two faces agree
  - as_str() and as_px() can never disagree (w-N must equal as_px()/4)

The audit's related observation -- base_theme_selector/gantt/kanban using both
20px and 24px for 'the same small-control role' -- resolves as legitimate

Documented in CLAUDE.md as the third family alongside spacing and strokes.

NOT DONE, and deliberately: widgets/avatar_badge.rs carries a third size ramp
(AvatarBadgeSize). It is a different component with its own concerns; folding

title: Enforce internal <= external in nested components
description:
Workstream C, the rule that produces the most visible win per edit.

Gestalt proximity: a container whose internal padding exceeds the gap to its neighbours visually merges with them. The desktop audit found a concrete violation in Kanban (CARD_PADDING 12 inside vs CARD_GAP and COLUMN_PADDING 8 outside) -- cards merging with the column edge and with each other.

Check and fix the web equivalents wherever components nest:
- Card in a grid or stack
- Modal / Drawer body padding vs. the backdrop inset
- Table cell padding vs. row separation
- Form control: label-to-input gap (4-8) must be clearly smaller than the gap to the next field group (24+). The article's opening example is a label sitting equidistant between two inputs, leaving the user to work out which one it belongs to -- confirm we never produce that.
- List item padding vs. item separation

Once ldui-dg2 lands its internal-vs-external assertion, this becomes a fix-the-reported-list task instead of a manual hunt.
close_reason: Kanban, result_list, the demo Section wrapper and the form-control case all fixed and verified in the browser. Modal/Drawer/Table padding is daisyUI-owned and out of scope; the 2 remaining kanban hits are daisyUI's mockup-window, held as a committed ceiling. Now enforced by ldui-dg2's check 3 in both directions.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:

  kanban/card.rs:34    'kanban-card ... p-3'          internal padding 12px
  kanban/column.rs:129 'kanban-cards p-4 space-y-2'   card gap 8px, column pad 16px

  drawer/component.rs:136  passes through daisyUI's 'drawer-side'
Table cell padding is likewise daisyUI's '.table'. We contribute no padding at

title: Map the shared spacing scale onto the Tailwind theme and migrate components off raw utilities
description:
Workstream C, web half. Depends on the audit and on line-height being pinned.

- Extend ui_tokens::spacing consumption here once SPACE_XXXL (64) and SPACE_HUGE (96) land upstream -- the desktop audit found the scale truncating at 48 was what pushed everything above it into improvisation (56, 68, 72, 88, 90, 96, 110, 150...).
- Generate the Tailwind theme spacing keys from the token values so there is one source of truth, rather than Tailwind's defaults happening to agree with ours.
- Consume the new stroke family (HAIRLINE/THIN/ACCENT/EMPHASIS) for borders and dividers so hairlines stop being counted as off-grid spacing.
- Migrate components family by family, worst divergence first: container padding, then gaps, then radii.

Do not chase sub-4 values: 1px and 2px borders are legitimate strokes, not bad spacing. Give them the stroke tokens and leave the values alone.
close_reason: Tailwind theme generated from ui_tokens (cargo xtask gen-tokens -> styles/tokens.css, drift-gated by the tokens-fresh step). Upstream SPACE_XXXL/SPACE_HUGE/stroke family added in Rust-DeskApp 532f6ea to unblock it. Off-grid down 14 -> 3 of 443 live occurrences, survivors all stroke-role. Remaining size-family work split out as ldui-mai.4.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION from the ldui-lua audit (findings F3/F4).

This ticket is smaller than assumed but aimed at the wrong target.

Already effectively clean -- little to migrate:
  padding  109 uses  100% canonical
  margin    66 uses   97%
  space     27 uses   96%
  gap      106 uses   92%

The actual problem:
  size (w/h/min/max)  295 uses  75% canonical

75 of the 90 off-canonical uses are in the size family. Re-aim the migration
there. In particular icon/icon_tile span 16/20/24/32/40/48/64 -- that is a size
ramp wanting one name, not seven raw utilities. The other real disagreement is
20px vs 24px for the same small-control role (base_theme_selector, gantt, icon,
kanban each use both).

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
MOSTLY DONE. Scope was corrected by the audit (see earlier comment) and the
upstream prerequisite had to be built first.

UPSTREAM PREREQUISITE -- this ticket said 'once SPACE_XXXL (64) and SPACE_HUGE
(96) land upstream' and 'consume the new stroke family'. None of that existed,
and Rust-DeskApp had ZERO open issues, so nothing was going to deliver it.
Added it there directly (Rust-DeskApp 532f6ea):
  spacing.rs  SPACE_XXXL=64, SPACE_HUGE=96, SCALE now [f32;9], is_on_scale()
  stroke.rs   HAIRLINE/THIN/ACCENT/EMPHASIS + is_stroke()  (new module)
  NAV_ACCENT_WIDTH now derives from stroke::ACCENT -- same value 3.0, correctly
              classified, so the new grid check over the named layout
              dimensions does not need to special-case it.
Desktop workspace still compiles (cargo check --workspace clean, 38 ui-tokens
tests pass).

DONE -- 'generate the Tailwind theme spacing keys from the token values so
there is one source of truth': 'cargo xtask gen-tokens' writes styles/tokens.css
from ui_tokens; demo/input.css imports it; the gate's new 'tokens-fresh' step
fails if the committed file drifts.

TRAP FOUND, worth knowing before anyone extends the generator: adding named
--spacing-* keys silently redefined max-w-xs from 20rem to 0.5rem -- a 40x
shrink across upload_file, data_table (x2) and component_customizer. Tailwind
resolves max-w-*/w-* against --spacing-* BEFORE --container-*. Caught by
diffing the compiled stylesheet, not by any test. The generator now emits only
--spacing (the base unit, so the numeric scale is token-derived) and a unit
test guards against named keys returning.

accent/emphasis (Tailwind) and --ld-stroke-* (runtime). Deliberately did NOT
mass-rename ~100 'border'/'border-2' call sites to 'border-hairline'/
'border-thin': Tailwind's numeric border widths already equal the stroke
values, so it is pure churn with no visual change and worse readability. The
goal the ticket states -- 'so hairlines stop being counted as off-grid
spacing' -- is achieved by the family EXISTING as a distinct concept that the
checker excludes, not by the class names.

14 -> 3 of 443 live occurrences (3.2% -> 0.7%), and all 3 survivors are
stroke-role (toolbar underline, vertical-steps connector rail). Padding stays
100% canonical.

(10.4%) are still off the canonical scale, nearly all in w-/h-. The biggest
single item is icon/icon_tile spanning 16/20/24/32/40/48/64 -- that wants one
named size ramp rather than seven raw utilities, and it is a design decision
about how many icon sizes the library should offer, not a mechanical

title: DataTable: keyboard operability for interactive rows (a11y)
description: DataTable rows responded to click but were not keyboard-focusable, so selection and activation were pointer-only (identified while writing doc/components/data_table.md). Fix: when a table is interactive (selected_rows OR on_row_activate supplied), rows get tabindex=0 + aria-selected (valid on a <tr>'s implicit role=row), and Enter/Space mirror a click with Ctrl/Shift parity; Space preventDefaults its page-scroll. Plain display tables gain no tab stops (gated by row_is_interactive()). The internal on_row_click callback was refactored from (idx, MouseEvent) to (idx, ctrl, shift) bools so mouse and keyboard share one path. 4 unit tests on row_is_interactive; browser-verified.
close_reason: Shipped in 4e777c1 on main. Interactive rows (selected_rows or on_row_activate supplied) are focusable (tabindex=0) with aria-selected; Enter/Space mirror a click with Ctrl/Shift parity; Space preventDefaults page-scroll; plain display tables gain no tab stops. Internal on_row_click refactored (idx, MouseEvent) -> (idx, ctrl, shift) so mouse+keyboard share one path; public API unchanged. 4 unit tests on row_is_interactive() + browser-verified: selection table (Enter/Space select, Ctrl+Enter toggle 3,5, Shift+Enter extend 5,6,7, aria-selected=true on focus); activation table (Enter/Space activate count 2 no-select, Ctrl/Shift+Enter select no-activate, ArrowDown no-op); Space preventDefaulted; plain rows unfocusable; 2/22 demo tables expose tabindex, 0/18 plain tables leak one. Gate 7/7, 1903 lib tests. Remaining (documented, separate/larger): full role=grid semantics with arrow-key roaming.

title: DataTable: opt-in row activation (on_row_activate)
description: Opt-in on_row_activate callback + row_click_kind()/RowClickKind in selection.rs: a plain click activates (receiving the row's ABSOLUTE index, same space as selected_rows), a Ctrl/Shift click still feeds the selection state machine, and with no callback registered every click selects exactly as before. Landed uncommitted+unbeaded in the working tree ~06:06-06:08 on 2026-07-17 by a session that stopped before adding a demo; committed in 4ba5884 and demoed afterwards. Filed retroactively so the work has a record.
close_reason: Demoed and browser-verified; shipped in 5519631 on main. Added a 'Row Activation (on_row_activate)' demo section with live readouts (last activated index, activation count, Ctrl/Shift-only selection set) so the two interactions are visibly independent. All four documented claims verified by driving real clicks: (1) plain click activates and does NOT select — count 1, selected (none); (2) Ctrl/Shift click selects and does NOT activate — count frozen at 2, set 5,6,7; (3) the index is ABSOLUTE not page-relative — page 2's first row 'User 9' reports 8, and after a descending sort 'User 12' reports 11; (4) a table WITHOUT the callback still selects on a plain click (index 2, activation count 0), confirming the 'zero behavior change by default' guarantee. Gate 7/7. NOTE: an early reading suggesting (4) was broken was my own test bug — Section renders a <div>, not <section>, so closest('section') returned null and grabbed the wrong table.

title: Reusable stale-while-revalidate keyed resource cache (generalize inventory WallCache)
description: inventory-web hand-rolled an app-wide WallCache (RwSignal<Option<(key,DTO)>> in a context that survives route re-mounts): on return to a screen it renders the cached payload INSTANTLY while a background refetch revalidates (bd_4iiz-inventory-gu3; back-nav 2270ms->142ms, no spinner). This stale-while-revalidate KEYED RESOURCE CACHE is a reusable web-framework primitive — promote it so every data screen gets instant back-navigation without hand-rolling a per-screen cache. Proposed API: a use_swr_resource(key_fn, async fetcher) hook (returns cached-or-loading view state + a 'revalidating' flag) and/or a CacheProvider context keyed by a string. Keep the fetch layer pluggable (gloo-net/fetch agnostic). First consumers: inventory Lifecycle + the drilldowns (epic bd_4iiz-inventory-22t). SCOPE: web/client only — the server-side result cache (bd_4iiz-inventory-zbi) is app/server side, NOT this.
notes:
Implemented as src/utils/swr.rs (promoted alongside utils::debounce, which was extracted from the same host app for the same reason):

- SwrState<T,E> { Loading | Ready{data, revalidating} | Error } — exhaustive, so a match can't forget the cached-but-stale case an ad-hoc Option<Result<..>> match does.
- SwrCache: type-erased (Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>) so ONE app-wide context serves every screen/DTO; a key stored as one type and read as another misses rather than misrenders. get/get_untracked/set/invalidate/clear/len/is_empty.
- provide_swr_cache() / use_swr_cache() — docs stress it must go ABOVE the router (a cache inside a route dies with the route = the exact re-mount it exists to survive).
- use_swr_resource(key_fn, async fetcher) -> SwrResource { state, revalidating, key, refetch(), invalidate_and_refetch() }.
- swr_state_from(fetch, cached) — the whole decision table as a pure fn, unit-tested (10 tests) without a DOM/resource/async runtime.
- Fetch layer stays pluggable: the module never performs a request; any async Fn(String) -> Future<Output=Result<T,E>> works (gloo-net/reqwest/hand-rolled).
- Demo: new /components/swr page with a mount toggle standing in for a route re-mount, plus provide_swr_cache() above <Router> in demo main.rs.
REAL BUG caught only by driving the hook in a browser (all 8 unit tests were green through it):

On a key change, the hook rendered the PREVIOUS key's payload as if it were the new key's FRESH data, for the full fetch duration. Observed: switching to an uncached 'quarter' displayed 'payload for month (fetch #4)' labelled fresh for 1.2s, then swapped to quarter. It should have shown Loading.

Cause: a Leptos resource keeps serving its previous value while it re-runs, so after the key changes resource.get() still returns the OLD key's data. The hook trusted resource.get() as 'the fetch for the current key' — violating its own documented contract ('a value cached under the old key never renders for the new one').

Fix: the resource now resolves to (key_it_was_fetched_with, result). The state reader discards a value whose tag != the current key (treating it as 'not fetched yet' -> cache lookup -> Loading), and the cache-write Effect stores under the resource's own tag rather than key.get_untracked(), which may already have moved on. Two regression tests pin the resulting states.

Note this bug was invisible to unit tests by construction: swr_state_from's decision table was always correct — the defect was in what the hook FED it. That's the same lesson as ldui-29l: the pure math was never wrong, the DOM/reactive wiring was.

Also worth knowing: an early browser reading ('fetch #2 resolving in 16ms' despite a 1200ms simulated latency) was itself an artifact of this bug — stale values masquerading as fresh ones. After the fix, timings are a clean 1209/1214ms.
close_reason: Implemented src/utils/swr.rs: SwrState/SwrCache/provide_swr_cache/use_swr_cache/use_swr_resource/swr_state_from (see notes for the API). 10 unit tests on the pure decision table + a /components/swr demo page. Browser-verified end-to-end: cache miss -> Loading at 4ms then fresh at 1209ms (real latency); cache hit (re-mount, standing in for back-nav) -> cached value rendered at 4ms marked 'revalidating', NEVER a spinner, revalidated to fresh at 1214ms. ONE REAL BUG found only by driving it -- see notes.

title: DataTable: responsive / auto-growing page size (rows-per-page from window height)
description: Consumer request from 4iiz-inventory (epic bd_4iiz-inventory-22t): pagination should GROW as the window is resized (a taller window shows more rows). Today page_size is a fixed Signal<usize> (default 10, component.rs) with no resize logic; max_height gives scroll-in-fixed-area but not a growing page size. Add opt-in responsive paging: a ResizeObserver (or window resize listener) on the table container that derives rows-per-page from available height / measured row height and feeds page_size. Lighter interim already possible (callers pass a resize-driven Signal to the existing page_size prop) — but no call site does this and the 'grows on resize' contract lives nowhere; make it a first-class opt-in prop (e.g. auto_page_size: bool). First consumer: inventory Explorer + StageDetail.
notes:
PORT SOURCE: rust-deskapp already implements this on the desktop DataTable — crates/d2d-ui/src/controls/data_table.rs: rows_per_page_for_height(h) (:675) = ((h - header_offset - PAGINATION_HEIGHT) / ROW_HEIGHT).floor().max(1); set_rows_per_page_to_fit() (:680) called on resize. Web port = a ResizeObserver on the table container feeding the SAME arithmetic into the existing page_size Signal. Not a from-scratch build — mirror the desktop logic.
Browser verification caught two defects the unit tests could not:

1. max_height is a CEILING, not a height. The container shrink-wrapped its rows, so the measured viewport was a function of the row count being derived from it -> settled at 1 row in a 382px box and could never grow. Fix: when auto_page_size is on, promote max_height to a definite 'height' (and fall back to height:100% when no max_height). The prop docs originally stated the wrong precondition ('pass max_height') and were corrected to 'needs a definite height'.

2. Infinite 2-cycle oscillation (5 rows@37px <-> 1 row@52px, forever, re-arming a timeout each pass). Root cause found from the numbers: 37+87 = 52+72 = 124 = container height. The 15px delta is a HORIZONTAL SCROLLBAR -- the wrapper is overflow-y:auto, so when the widest rendered cell makes the table wider than the wrapper, an h-scrollbar appears and is subtracted from clientHeight. That made viewport = f(row count) with no fixed point. Fix: measure with offset_height() (flex-allocated border-box height, which no scrollbar or cell content can move) instead of client_height(). A cycle-detection guard was tried first and REJECTED -- it made the ladder worse (7/9 vs 8/9) because the ResizeObserver fires multiple times per resize and the episode resets interleaved unpredictably. Removing the coupling beat patching the symptom.

Also: measurement is deferred to a 0ms macrotask (a ResizeObserver callback can run mid-layout; latching a transient left the table a row short), plus a re-measure pass keyed on page_size.

Final: resize ladder 9/9 exact vs floor((offsetH-headerH)/rowH) across grow/shrink/revisit/degenerate; degenerate 150px settles monotonically 8@52 -> 1@52 and stays (no oscillation, no churn); recovers to 5.
close_reason: Implemented: auto_page_size prop + auto_page.rs (rows_per_page_for_height, ported from d2d-ui rows_per_page_for_height). ResizeObserver on the table's scroll wrapper (mirrors toolbar's pattern) feeds the measured viewport/header/row heights into the pure fn. Web measures rendered heights rather than d2d-ui's fixed HEADER_HEIGHT/ROW_HEIGHT consts (daisyUI row height varies by table size); consts kept as fallbacks. 19 unit tests + demo section with a user-resizable box. TWO REAL BUGS found only by driving a browser (unit tests were green throughout) -- see notes.

title: DataTable: per-column filter-dropdown row (Column::filterable)
description: Consumer request from 4iiz-inventory (epic bd_4iiz-inventory-22t): drilldown tables want a filter ROW with dropdown filters for the top 4-5 columns. Today src/components/data_table/ has ONLY a single global free-text 'searchable' input (component.rs:153,273-291) — no per-column filter selects. Add an opt-in filter row: a Column flag (e.g. filterable: bool) + a filter row rendered under the header (new filter.rs or in header.rs) with a Select of that column's distinct values; combine active per-column filters (AND) with the existing global search. Keep it opt-in so existing callers are unaffected. Verify with the inventory Explorer/StageDetail grids as first consumer.
close_reason: Implemented: Column::filterable() opt-in + filter.rs (distinct_values / row_matches_filters / prune_stale_filters / has_filterable_columns + DataTableFilterRow). Filter <tr> renders inside the header's <thead> via a new optional children prop, so ServerDataTable is untouched. Per-column filters AND with each other and with the existing global search; stale selections are pruned when data changes; page resets to 0 on filter change. New DataTableTexts.filter_all ('All'). 23 unit tests + demo section. Browser-verified: exactly 1 filter row across 21 demo tables (opt-in holds); Role=Admin 60->12; +Status=Active -> 4 rows = exactly i%15==0 (Users 1/16/31/46, ground truth); +search 'User 31' -> 1; reset ladder 4->12->60.

title: AppShellIconNav: support a rail background image/pattern (brand texture behind the nav rail)
description:
GAP found while porting the 4iiz Office Performance desktop app to the web (4iiz-Office op-7hx). The desktop's branded nav rail renders a dark-navy base + a subtle vertical gradient + a cyan DOT-WAVE brand texture PNG behind the nav items. The Leptos AppShell has NO way to do this: AppShellIconNav supports only solid daisyUI background classes; there is no background-image / pattern / overlay prop.

For reference, the desktop framework d2d-ui does not have it either — it exposes only AppShell::with_rail_bg(color), a FLAT colour — so the office DESKTOP app hand-draws the dot-wave PNG itself over the rail. Both frameworks are missing the same capability; this bead is the Leptos half.

ASK: let a consumer supply a background IMAGE (or CSS background layer) for the icon rail — e.g. a bg_image prop on AppShellIconNav (a URL or a class) — composited UNDER the nav items and header, and NOT tiling over item hover/active states or the count badges. It should coexist with the existing solid-colour background (base colour + optional gradient + optional image overlay).

CONSUMER: 4iiz-Office crates/office-perf-web/src/shell.rs. Brand asset: crates/office-perf-gui/assets/brand/sidebar-bg.png (and .webp). Today the web rail is a flat navy with no texture, so it does not match the desktop.

INTERIM: until this lands, the office web app applies the texture via a CSS background on the rail. Please replace that with the real API when it exists.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Implemented on AppShellIconNav: bg_color / bg_gradient / bg_image (+ bg_size, bg_repeat).

The rail's background now stacks three layers, back to front: bg_color -> bg_gradient -> bg_image texture. All three go on the <nav>'s OWN background, and an element's background always paints beneath its content -- so nav-item hover/active backgrounds and the count badges paint on top, unobscured, with no overlay div and no z-index games. That is the 'composited UNDER the nav items, NOT tiling over hover/active states or badges' requirement, satisfied structurally.

One non-obvious finding for the consumer (4iiz-Office office-perf-web) and for the d2d-ui half of this gap:
  A bg-[#0b1e3a] CLASS does NOT reliably set the rail's base colour. The rail hard-codes bg-base-300, both are plain utilities in the same cascade layer, and the generated sheet's order decides -- measured in the browser, bg-base-300 wins and the rail stays grey. Hence bg_color is an INLINE style (inline beats any class). Use bg_color="#0b1e3a", not a bg-[...] class.

Safety: bg_image is a URL and is escaped into a quoted CSS url("...") (quotes/backslashes escaped, control chars dropped), so it cannot break out and inject declarations. bg_color is validated as colour-shaped (hex / rgb() / oklch() / var() / named / color-mix) and dropped entirely if it isn't -- 'red; background-image: url(evil)' emits nothing. bg_gradient is raw CSS by necessity (it IS a linear-gradient(...) expression) and is documented as trusted input, same trust level as the class prop.

A repeating texture wants bg_repeat="repeat" WITH bg_size="auto" (the default 'cover' scales one copy to fill the rail and defeats the tile).

Unbranded rails are untouched: with no bg_* props the component emits no style attribute at all (verified in the DOM -- 3 of the 4 rails on the demo page have no style attr).

Verified in the browser on the new demo section (/components/app-shell -> 'Branded Rail'): computed background-color = rgb(11,30,58), background-image = texture + linear-gradient, background-repeat = repeat; item labels and the '7' badge render legibly over the dot-wave. 17 app_shell unit tests incl. the injection cases.

@4iiz-Office: the interim CSS-background workaround in crates/office-perf-web/src/shell.rs can now be replaced with these props.

title: AiChat auto-scroll reads stale scroll_height, leaves latest message below fold
description: Browser smoke (ldui-0wf) confirmed the Task 19 deferred auto-scroll concern is a real bug. Repro: AiChat demo, stick engaged (scrolled to bottom), send a message. The reply arrives (bubbles 2->4, scrollHeight 352->733) but scrollTop lands at 267 while the true bottom is scrollHeight-clientHeight = 496 — ~230px of the newest content stays below the fold, and it never corrects. Also on the very first message: scrollHeight 352 vs clientHeight 237 (115px overflow) but scrollTop stays 0. Root cause: the auto-stick Effect at src/components/ai_chat/component.rs:183-191 calls el.set_scroll_top(el.scroll_height()) synchronously when  changes, but Leptos Effects run after the reactive update and BEFORE the browser lays out the newly-appended MessageBubble DOM, so scroll_height() is stale (too small). The stale programmatic scroll can also trip the on:scroll handler (component.rs:209-216) into recomputing should_stick_to_bottom with a large distance, flipping stick=false and disengaging future auto-scroll (explains scrollTop stuck at 0 on first send). Fix: defer the scroll to after paint — request_animation_frame (web_sys) before reading scroll_height and setting scroll_top, or set_timeout(0). The pure should_stick_to_bottom logic is correct and well-tested; the bug is purely the measurement timing in the Effect. NOTE: P1 theme panic (ldui-i4t) and P3 memory error (ldui-4i0) were both verified FIXED live in this same session — console is clean, no more disposal panic.
close_reason: Fixed in 3b600d4: deferred the auto-stick scroll write into a request_animation_frame callback (leptos::prelude::request_animation_frame, one-shot per Effect run, None-guarded) so it reads scroll_height AFTER the browser paints the new bubbles. Re-verified live on rebuilt WASM (a86fe2309...): after 1st message distance-from-bottom=0 (was 115px overflow at scrollTop 0); after 2nd message scrollTop 497 of 733, distance -1≈0 (was 267/dist 229 below fold). Console clean. Also added a direct regression test 44d7c52 pinning that theme singleton signals survive caller-owner disposal (theme review Important). 1725 lib tests.

title: Integrate ui-tokens shared crate into leptos-daisyui-rs
description:
Bring in the shared `ui-tokens` crate from the Rust-DeskApp workspace so leptos-daisyui-rs consumes the same design tokens (durations, easings, shadow elevation tiers, colour palette anchors) as d2d-ui. This is the prerequisite for the motion-port epic (ldui-e1o) — without a single source of truth for motion durations and shadow tiers, every component-level port would have to redefine the same constants and the libraries would drift.

## Why now

The d2d-ui motion epic (Rust-DeskApp/beads-14f) shipped 2026-05 with a complete `ui_tokens::motion` (Easing enum, DURATION_FAST_MS/DURATION_NORMAL_MS, cubic-Bezier control points) and `ui_tokens::elevation` (LEVEL_2..LEVEL_64 Shadow structs). The motion-port epic (ldui-e1o) is parked until this anchor is in place.

## Decision: path-dep vs git-dep vs vendored

The original parity epic (beads-76r) flagged this as needing a "path-dep decision". Three options:

1. **Path-dep** (`ui-tokens = { path = "../Rust-DeskApp/crates/ui-tokens" }`) — cleanest while both repos are local. Breaks for downstream crates.io consumers and for CI without sibling-repo checkout.
2. **Git-dep** (`ui-tokens = { git = "https://github.com/davidcforbes/rust-deskapp", branch = "master" }`) — works for crates.io publication and CI. Slower (git fetch on each build). Pinning to a commit hash recommended.
3. **Vendored copy** — manual sync. Drift-prone but simple.

Recommended: git-dep with a pinned commit hash. Migrate to path-dep only for local development if needed.

## Surface to consume

From the d2d-ui ui-tokens crate (C:\dev\Rust-DeskApp\crates\ui-tokens\src\):

- `motion.rs` — `Easing { Linear, Standard, Decelerate, Accelerate }`, `DURATION_FAST_MS`, `DURATION_NORMAL_MS`, cubic-Bezier control points
- `elevation.rs` — `Shadow { offset_x, offset_y, blur, opacity }`, named tiers `LEVEL_2`/`LEVEL_4`/`LEVEL_8`/`LEVEL_16`/`LEVEL_64`
- `colour.rs` / `theme.rs` (if applicable to web) — accent + neutral palette anchors

## How web consumes these (translation strategy)

- Emit motion constants as `--ld-duration-fast: 83ms; --ld-duration-normal: 200ms;` CSS variables in a token preamble (build-time, via a small leptos-side helper).
- Easing cubic-Bezier control points emit as `cubic-bezier(...)` CSS easing functions.
- Elevation shadows emit as `box-shadow: <offset_x>px <offset_y>px <blur>px rgba(0,0,0,<opacity>);` per tier.
- Colour palette consumed via existing daisyUI theme infrastructure.

## Verification

- New crate dependency builds clean (`cargo build`, `cargo test` from leptos-daisyui-rs root).
- Token preamble CSS emitted from a small `ui_tokens_css!()` macro or build.rs.
- At least one component (Button is the obvious candidate) uses one motion token (e.g., `--ld-duration-fast` for hover transition) to prove the chain.

## Unblocks

- ldui-e1o (motion + shadow system port) — explicitly blocked-by-convention on this bead.
close_reason: Implemented in 305c551: ui-tokens path dep + tokens module + UiTokensPreamble + demo inspection page. 1154 tests pass, wasm32 build clean.

description:
Epic to port the motion + drop-shadow system shipped in the d2d-ui Rust-DeskApp workspace (beads-14f, merged 2026-05) across to leptos-daisyui-rs. Cross-stack flow:

  d2d-ui (Direct2D, native) -> leptos-daisyui-rs (Leptos/WASM, CSS) -> table-rs (sibling effort, separate epic)

## Why

d2d-ui's beads-14f epic shipped a complete motion system: eased hover/press/focus, ripple reveals, elevation lift on hover, GPU drop shadows via CLSID_D2D1Shadow, dialog scale-up + backdrop fade, toast slide-in, menu/dropdown/drawer entrances. ~70 controls migrated. The patterns are now battle-tested in native code. Bringing them to the web library accelerates app development by sharing the same visual language across renderers.

## Scope

Port these motion patterns to their CSS / Web Animations API equivalents:

- Eased state transitions (cubic-Bezier hover/press/focus opacity + scale + colour)
- Ripple click reveal (radial expanding overlay)
- Elevation lift (shadow + slight translate on hover for Card / Fab)
- Drop shadows (CSS filter: drop-shadow or box-shadow per elevation tier)
- Dialog entrance: scale 0.92 -> 1.0 + backdrop fade-in
- Toast entrance: slide-in from corner
- Menu / dropdown / drawer slide-down or edge-slide
- Focus ring animated fade-in + outset

## Source of truth (d2d-ui side)

- `crates/d2d-ui/src/motion/` -- clock, easing, transition, spring, ripple, StateAnim
- `crates/d2d-ui/src/shadow.rs` -- CLSID_D2D1Shadow wrapper + ui_tokens::elevation::Shadow
- `crates/ui-tokens/src/motion.rs` -- Easing enum + DURATION_FAST_MS / DURATION_NORMAL_MS
- `crates/ui-tokens/src/elevation.rs` -- LEVEL_2 / LEVEL_4 / LEVEL_8 / LEVEL_16 / LEVEL_64 shadow tiers
- `docs/components/motion.md` -- reference doc

## Anchor on ui-tokens (depends on ldui-wab)

This epic depends on the ui-tokens integration tracked under ldui-wab. Once leptos-daisyui-rs consumes the shared ui-tokens crate, motion durations + shadow tiers automatically stay in sync with d2d-ui via a single source of truth. Without that anchor, this port would drift.

## Suggested fan-out (children to file when work starts)

1. ui-tokens integration (already tracked: ldui-wab)
2. Eased button hover/press/focus -- the universal interaction pattern
3. Eased checkbox / toggle / radio interaction
4. Card elevation lift (LEVEL_4 -> LEVEL_8 on hover)
5. Ripple effect on click (radial overlay)
6. Dialog scale-up + backdrop fade-in
7. Toast slide-in entrance from corner
8. Menu / dropdown slide-down entrance
9. Drawer edge-slide entrance
10. Focus ring animated fade-in

## Out of scope (this epic)

- Porting to table-rs -- separate sibling epic when ready
- Wholesale rewrite of existing leptos-daisyui-rs components -- this is additive
- Reactive signal redesign -- continue using existing Leptos signal patterns

## Related

- d2d-ui motion epic: Rust-DeskApp/beads-14f (closed 2026-05)
- d2d-ui WinUI 3 reference: Rust-DeskApp/beads-v3f, beads-n5a (closed 2026-05)
- Leptos parity epic: ldui parity epic (open)

title: Add multi-select to DataTable for parity with d2d-ui (Rust-DeskApp)
description:
Rust-DeskApp commit c5bdfa9 added multi-select to d2d_ui::controls::DataTable so desktop apps can support Ctrl/Shift-click row selection. The Leptos DataTable currently has no selection state.

Gap: To keep desktop ↔ web feature parity (per Rust-DeskApp/docs/leptos-parity.md), add equivalent multi-select to leptos-daisyui-rs's DataTable.

Proposed API (Leptos signal-based):
  - new optional prop: selected_rows: RwSignal<BTreeSet<usize>>
  - new optional prop: selection_anchor: RwSignal<Option<usize>>
  - new optional prop: on_row_click: Callback<(usize, MouseEvent)>
  - DataTableBody renders selected rows with class 'bg-base-200' (or similar)
  - Pure logic helper: pub fn handle_row_click(row_idx, ctrl, shift, &mut selected, &mut anchor, total) — mirrors d2d-ui's same-named method. Consumers can wire up MouseEvent.ctrl_key() / shift_key() to call it.

Reference: d2d-ui implementation at crates/d2d-ui/src/controls/data_table.rs handle_row_click — same semantics:
  - plain click: clear, select clicked, set anchor
  - Ctrl+click: toggle, set anchor
  - Shift+click: range from anchor (clears unless Ctrl held)

Clearing selection on page change / data refresh / sort change is also expected.

When complete, update Rust-DeskApp/docs/leptos-parity.md to mark this row from ❌ to ✅.
close_reason: Implemented in 0390652: pure handle_row_click helper with 15 tests + RwSignal multi-select wiring on DataTable + demo section. 1169 lib tests pass, wasm32 build clean.
