title: Admin-workbench demo starves the KpiStrip to 12px at a 390px viewport
description:
Found while verifying ldui-tnyq; NOT caused by it, and confirmed so by experiment rather than assumed.

At a 390x844 viewport the admin-workbench demo page gives the KpiStrip a parent of 60px, and the strip itself resolves to 12px. Measured ancestor chain at 390px:

  DIV.grid (the strip)          w=12
  DIV.@container.w-full         w=12
  DIV.flex.min-w-0              w=60     <-- the starvation happens here
  DIV.flex.h-full               w=340
  DIV.flex-1.overflow-y-auto    w=340
  DIV.flex.flex-1               w=340

All eight cards clip; the worst label needs 848px more height than it has. The page's own content area is 340px, so a 60px child means the mobile layout keeps a side-by-side flex row that should stack.

NOT THE CONTAINER QUERY. The obvious suspect was ldui-tnyq's new container-type: inline-size, since containment removes an element's content contribution to its parent's intrinsic sizing. Tested directly by setting containerType='normal' on the wrapper in the live DOM and re-measuring: before {wrap 12, grid 12, parent 60}, after {wrap 12, grid 12, parent 60} - byte-identical. The geometry is fixed entirely by ancestors, so the pre-container-query strip was equally starved (it was the grid div in that same 60px parent).

SCOPE: fix the admin-workbench demo page's 390px layout so the content column stacks instead of keeping a row, then assert at 390px that the strip's width is within a few px of its content area. Worth checking the same fixture's other patterns at that viewport while there - ldui-ibjk was a different mobile defect on this same page, which suggests its mobile layout has not been exercised much.

Consumer relevance is unknown and worth establishing: this is the demo's layout, not the pattern's, so a consumer with a properly stacking mobile layout may be unaffected. But a KpiStrip that silently renders 2px cards rather than wrapping is a bad failure mode, so it may also be worth giving the strip a floor (a min card width, or a documented minimum container width) so a starved container degrades visibly rather than into unreadable slivers.
close_reason:
Fixed in be2cbd9 and VERIFIED IN A BROWSER at three viewports.

CAUSE, as filed: the right-docked assistant carries min-w-[280px], which is not negotiable in a flex row. At 390px it took 280 of the row's 340px and left the content column 60px, so the KpiStrip resolved to 12px and every card clipped.

FIX: below `lg` the panel no longer docks beside the content. A right-docked assistant is a desktop affordance and the page already carries a Help FAB, which is the mobile way in. This is the demo's composition, not a component change - KpiStrip and FilterSidebar are untouched.

MEASURED, before -> after:

  viewport   strip width   card width   panel   page overflow
  390        12 -> 292     2 -> 138     hidden  none
  768        -- -> 670     -- -> 156    hidden  none
  1440       unchanged     190          280     none

The single remaining clipped label at every width is avg-first-response, the fixture's deliberately over-long entry (ldui-tbaw's documented "extremely long caller copy may clamp" case), not a defect.

CHECKED BEFORE CHANGING, rather than after: nothing at 390px depended on the panel being present. The two compact tests assert only that the page does not scroll horizontally and that the Help FAB is placed and accessible; assistantPresent is asserted in the 1440px test, which still passes.

ONE DEAD END worth recording for the next person: passing class="hidden lg:flex" as a spread attribute does NOT compile. FilterSidebar builds its root class entirely from expanded_width and side, so it is not an ElementExt and takes no spread class. The gate therefore lives on a wrapper element. If a consumer needs to hide or re-size a FilterSidebar responsively they will hit the same wall - worth a `class` prop on the component if it comes up again.

NOTE the panel now also hides between 768 and 1023, where it previously showed. That is deliberate (lg is the conventional threshold for a docked side panel) and is why the change is in the demo rather than the component: a consumer wanting a different threshold owns their own layout.

EVIDENCE: admin_workbench_smoke 7/7, layout_audit_smoke 9/9, style_audit_smoke 7/7 on a freshly published dist - the wrapper adds a DOM node on ratcheted pages, so those were re-measured rather than assumed, and no ceiling moved. Native suite and clippy clean across library and showcase.

title: EntityTable compact cards inherit desktop column width
description: At a 390x844 mobile viewport, EntityTable switches to its compact row renderer, but the table and compact TD still retain the desktop colgroup width. In the Office Coordinator fixture the visible compact table region measures about 1210px inside a 390px viewport; the page's internal overflow container grows to about 1270px and requires horizontal scrolling. The compact TD is lg:hidden as expected, but COLGROUP widths continue to size TABLE/TBODY/TR/TD. Make compact mode ignore desktop column widths and fit its containing block without horizontal overflow. Preserve desktop widths and horizontal table scrolling at desktop. Add browser coverage at 390px that asserts the compact row/table/container width is at most its viewport/container width and verifies rendered cards remain usable.
close_reason:
Fixed in 41accc8 and VERIFIED IN A BROWSER at 390x844.

ROOT CAUSE: EntityTable's stable colgroup pins one <col> per desktop column, and hiding a compact cell with lg:hidden does NOT stop its <col> from claiming a track. So in compact mode the table, its rows and the scroll region were all still sized to the sum of the desktop tracks - about 1210px of table inside a 390px viewport, with the internal overflow container past 1270px, forcing horizontal scrolling to read a card.

FIX: compact mode omits the colgroup entirely rather than trying to neutralise it, and drops table-fixed and the colgroup-driven min-width with it. All three are desktop-only geometry, and all three are guarded on the same compact predicate, so a desktop render emits exactly what it did before.

COVERAGE asserts measured geometry, not classes: table/row/compact-cell/content/scroll-region widths, regionScrollWidth against regionClientWidth, and documentElement.scrollWidth against clientWidth for page-level overflow. The same test then resizes back to desktop and asserts the colgroup-driven geometry returns byte-identical, so the fix cannot silently cost desktop column sizing.

EVIDENCE on the current tree: entity_table_smoke 11/11 PASS on a freshly published dist-host, plus layout_audit_smoke 9/9, style_audit_smoke 7/7 and admin_workbench_smoke 7/7 on a freshly published main dist. Native suite and clippy clean.

⚠️ TOOLING DEFECT FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THIS, and it nearly produced a false result. My rebuild helper's PUBLISH-OK checked that dist/index.html existed, that every asset it referenced existed, and that the snippet SRI matched. A build then regenerated demo/output.css with a fresh stamp but trunk aborted before staging index.html/js/wasm, so demo/dist kept its 08:14 CSS, 08:28 wasm and 08:29 index - and ALL THREE CHECKS PASSED, because a stale dist is perfectly self-consistent. PUBLISH-OK was reported for a build that published nothing. Only the ldui-hun stale-stylesheet guard caught it, failing 16/16 rather than reporting ratchets measured against the wrong CSS. Contributing cause: an orphaned subagent build ran concurrently with mine, the race that guard's message already warns about.

The helper now verifies that the stamp embedded in the PUBLISHED dist stylesheet equals the stamp the build just generated - the same invariant, enforced at publish time instead of sixteen test failures later. Note the first version of that check ALSO silently passed, because the stamp file stores a bare token while the stylesheet embeds it prefixed, so the grep matched nothing; it was caught by noticing PUBLISH-OK printed an empty stamp, then break-tested against a deliberately mismatched pair to confirm it fires.

title: A KpiCard help control costs its label 20px, which can push an ordinary label past two lines
description:
Found while verifying ldui-tbaw in a browser; deliberately NOT folded into that fix, because it is a separate design question and folding it in would have meant redesigning the card to make a test pass. A KpiCard's help control is a flex sibling of the label:
{label} {help_button}
so it costs the label its own width. MEASURED on the admin-workbench strip at a 1680px viewport (117px cards): a label without a help control gets 83px; with one it gets 63px - the 16px icon plus gap-1. Also measured, by cloning the label and sweeping widths: "Customer Success Pts" needs 32px (two lines) at every width from 70px up, and 48px (three lines) at 63px. So the help control is exactly what pushes a 20-character label past the two-line budget ldui-tbaw established. It is not the label length on its own, and it is not the clamp policy. WHY NOT SIMPLY MOVE THE ICON OUT OF FLOW: the obvious fix is to absolutely position the help control in the card corner so the label always gets the full row. That works, but it is a visual change to every card carrying help, and the two placements that avoid overlapping the clamped label's first line both have costs - the label box starts 19px down (3px accent + 16px padding), so the icon has to sit either over the accent strip or over the label's own text. Note a float will NOT work here: line-clamp-2 renders the label as -webkit-box, which does not wrap around floats. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD: the workbench fixture's help control moved to a short label ("Open matters"), which absorbs the 20px without clipping. The help case stays covered and the bead-named labels are no longer clipped for a reason unrelated to the wrapping policy. SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD: decide whether a help control should cost the label width at all. Options are (a) accept it and document that a help-bearing card needs a wider card or a shorter label, (b) move the control out of flow, (c) let the label span the full width and place the control below the value. Whichever is chosen, add a browser assertion that a help-bearing card's label width equals a non-help card's, so the interaction cannot silently regress. Consumer relevance: at the Office Coordinator's card width this may not bite at all - 117px cards are narrower than an eight-card 1680px Office strip. Worth confirming against the real consumer geometry before spending design effort.
close_reason:
Resolved as DOCUMENTED CONSTRAINT, not a redesign, in 799a669 - and the decision is backed by measurement rather than judgement.

THE ANSWER TO THE BEAD'S QUESTION ("should a help control cost the label width at all"): yes, accept it. Measured across viewports on the eight-card admin-workbench strip:

  viewport  cardW  label width (no help)  label width (with help)  two lines?
  1280       67     33                     13                      NO, badly
  1680      117     83                     63                      yes, both
  2200      182    132                     83                      yes, both
  2560      227    132                     83                      yes, both

The help control costs a flat 20px (16px trigger + gap-1). A ~20-character label needs >= 70px to hold two lines, measured by cloning the label and sweeping widths: 32px (two lines) at every width from 70px up, 48px (three) at 63px. So a help-bearing card wants roughly 125px or wider. Real strips are comfortably above that; the failures at 1280 are not about help at all - the NO-HELP label also needs five lines there.

WHY NOT THE OUT-OF-FLOW FIX I sketched when filing: it is a visual change to every card carrying help, and it does not actually buy anything in the regime that matters. Note also a float cannot work here - line-clamp-2 renders the label as -webkit-box, which does not wrap around floats - so the only ways to free the width are absolute positioning or moving the control away from the label, both of which weaken the label/control association for a problem that only appears on cards narrower than any real strip.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT ACTUALLY FOUND, and it is worse than this bead: at 1280 the whole strip is unreadable, help or no help. KpiStrip takes its column count from VIEWPORT breakpoints (xl:grid-cols-8, and Tailwind's xl is 1280px), so the strip goes to eight columns the moment the WINDOW hits 1280 regardless of how wide the strip itself is - 67px cards in a 648px column. Filed as ldui-tnyq (P2) with the full table; container queries are the fix. That is the bead worth spending effort on, and it would remove most of the pressure here as a side effect.

The guard this bead asked for already exists: wide_viewport_kpi_labels_wrap_without_ellipsis_and_stay_aligned asserts no fixture label clips (via scrollHeight against clientHeight, not by inspecting classes), so pairing help with a label too long for its card fails that test. A label-width-parity assertion would have been wrong, since the 20px cost is now the documented, intended behaviour.

title: Docs tell consumers to @source inline the ld-text-* ramp, which cannot work
description:
Found while fixing ldui-h7tw; left untouched there because it was outside that task's agreed file scope.

src/patterns/section_heading.rs (around line 93) tells consumers to add this to their input.css:

    @source inline("ld-text-title ld-text-subtitle ld-text-body ld-text-small");

That line is now INERT and actively misleading. @source inline(...) makes Tailwind GENERATE a utility it would otherwise tree-shake — it only works for classes Tailwind knows how to build. The ld-text-* steps are not Tailwind utilities; as of d686dbe they are authored rules emitted by cargo xtask gen-tokens into an @layer components block in styles/tokens.css. A consumer following this instruction gets nothing from it, and worse, may conclude the ramp is handled and skip importing styles/tokens.css — which is the exact failure ldui-h7tw was filed for (SectionHeading renders with weight and colour but no size step, so an H2 sits at body size under preflight).

The other four @source inline lines in that block are fine: those ARE Tailwind utilities and do need scanning.

SCOPE: drop ld-text-* from that @source inline list and instead state the real requirement — import styles/tokens.css, which is where the ramp is defined. Then sweep the other pattern/component docs for the same instruction: kpi_strip's doc had it too (already corrected in d686dbe), so grep the whole crate for `@source inline` lines containing `ld-` and fix every one. Cheap, and it prevents the next consumer repeating 4iiz-etl's shrunken-headings debugging session.

NOTE the new guard from ldui-h7tw (tests/ld_class_stylesheet_coverage.rs) verifies that an emitted ld-* class is DEFINED somewhere; it does not read doc comments, so it cannot catch a stale instruction like this one. Worth considering whether that guard should also assert no doc comment lists an ld-* class inside @source inline(...).
close_reason:
Fixed in 7eeabe8. Both occurrences removed - src/patterns/kpi_strip.rs:306 and src/patterns/section_heading.rs:93 - and each doc block now states the real requirement instead. Verified none remain: grep of @source inline lines containing ld-text across src/ returns 0.

WHY IT MATTERED more than a stale comment usually would: @source inline(...) makes Tailwind GENERATE a utility it would otherwise tree-shake, so it only works for classes Tailwind knows how to build. The ld-text-* steps are not utilities - since d686dbe they are authored rules emitted by cargo xtask gen-tokens into an @layer components block in styles/tokens.css. So the instruction was inert, and worse than inert: a consumer following it could reasonably conclude the ramp was handled and skip importing styles/tokens.css, which reproduces ldui-h7tw exactly (SectionHeading renders with weight and colour but no size step, so an H2 sits at body size under preflight - the shrink 4iiz-etl reported).

The replacement text says the steps are deliberately not listed, that @source inline cannot generate them, and that a consumer gets them by importing styles/tokens.css. The other @source inline lines in both blocks are untouched: those ARE Tailwind utilities and genuinely need scanning.

Not done, and worth considering separately: the ldui-h7tw guard (tests/ld_class_stylesheet_coverage.rs) verifies that an emitted ld-* class is DEFINED somewhere, but it reads code, not doc comments, so it could not have caught this and cannot catch a recurrence. Extending it to fail when a doc comment lists an ld-* class inside @source inline(...) would close that gap cheaply.

fmt and clippy clean.

title: EntityColumn: mirror the semantic column kinds added to DataTable
description:
EntityColumn has the same duplication that ldui-lrig just removed from DataTable's Column.

ldui-lrig measured, in one consumer: 98 with_class calls on columns, of which 43 contained tabular-nums and 20 contained font-mono - roughly two thirds of all column styling expressing just two intents, "this is a number" and "this is an identifier". The clinching finding was that of 24 columns declaring SortAs::Number, 22 ALSO hand-wrote tabular-nums and 2 did not, so the component already knew the column was numeric and 92 percent of callers restated it in CSS while 8 percent silently disagreed.

DataTable now has Column::numeric() (right-align + tabular figures, and it implies SortAs::Number so the fact is stated once) and Column::identifier() (the theme's mono face), landed in 1fb074f.

EntityColumn was deliberately left alone because another agent held that file at the time. It is the better candidate of the two: entity_table/component.rs already threads a `tabular_numbers: bool` through manually, which is the same fact travelling as an ad-hoc boolean instead of a column kind, and EntityTable is the preferred typed table for new work (see the choose-a-table guidance in CLAUDE.md).

SCOPE: mirror the DataTable API on EntityColumn - same method names, same documented precedence (an explicit class REPLACES the kind's default wholesale rather than merging, because Tailwind cascade order comes from generated stylesheet position and not from order within a class string), same implication of the numeric sort key where EntityColumn has an equivalent. Fold the existing tabular_numbers plumbing into the kind rather than leaving two ways to say it. Keep existing callers source-compatible.

CAVEAT: an identifier column renders font-mono, and the style audit currently reports EVERY font-mono element as a typography finding because StyleProfile carries a single family name (ldui-kq9w, fix owned upstream in PixelProof). Expect the demo page's typography count to rise until that lands; do not "solve" it by avoiding mono or by raising a ceiling.
close_reason:
Implemented. EntityColumn now has .numeric() and .identifier() matching DataTable's names (ldui-lrig), so the two tables read alike, and the ad-hoc tabular_numbers: bool field is folded into a typed kind: EntityColumnKind. Commit a5a7950; native suite 2670 green, clippy and fmt clean, both browser binaries touching EntityColumn compile.

TWO DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES FROM DataTable, both confirmed as correct rather than accepted as shortcuts:

1. .numeric() does NOT imply a numeric sort key here, unlike DataTable's. DataTable stores untyped HashMap<String,String> rows, so SortAs::Number exists precisely to re-parse display text; EntityColumn is generic over T and already offers an EXACT typed comparator via .sortable_by_key. Deriving a sort key from .numeric()'s display text would therefore be strictly LESS correct than what the type already supports, and making it order-dependent would reintroduce the very silent-disagreement failure this bead family exists to remove (ldui-lrig's clinching measurement was 22 of 24 numeric-sorted columns restating tabular-nums in CSS while 2 quietly disagreed). Documented at length and pinned by a test asserting both builder orders.

2. There is no with_class precedence rule to mirror, because EntityColumn deliberately exposes NO raw CSS class hatch - presentation is framework-owned tokens only, the same principle emphasis.rs follows. Rather than bolt on a class hook just for symmetry, the architectural divergence is documented, and the closest real analog is specified and tested instead: a later .align_*() overrides the alignment .numeric() implies.

.tabular_numbers() is kept rather than deprecated, as the lower-level primitive .numeric() is built from (it sets kind=Numeric without touching alignment). It remains necessary exactly because there is no class hatch - the demo's centred date column needs tabular figures without right-alignment.

The demo's id-shaped reference column now uses .identifier(). As expected, that renders the theme's mono face and will raise that page's font-mono typography count until ldui-kq9w lands upstream; per that bead's own instruction this was left honest rather than worked around by avoiding mono or raising a ceiling.

title: Include density/table_size in RowHeightEra key on both table faces
description: RowHeightEraKey is (data_revision, container_width): a table_size/density change re-triggers measurement but does NOT reset the height high-water mark, so a density decrease can leave the era's effective row height stuck tall (under-filled pages) until a data or width change. Applies to DataTable auto_page_size (ldui-89rp) and ServerDataTable viewport-fit (ldui-2bt3) identically - fix both together by adding the density dimension to the era key. Bounded under-fill, never oscillation; low priority. Filed by the 2026-08-29 wave final review.
close_reason: Fixed and verified (commit bc96b55). RowHeightEra's key now includes the density/table_size dimension on BOTH table faces, so a density change starts a fresh era instead of leaving the height high-water mark stuck at the taller value. Previously a density decrease re-triggered measurement but not an era reset, so the effective row height stayed high and under-filled the page until an unrelated data or width change happened to reset it - bounded, never oscillation, but wrong. ServerDataTable's own-induced-refetch carry-forward is preserved: a pending proposal whose accepted page size matches is still treated as the SAME era so the ratchet survives its own refetch, while a density change starts a new era even with a proposal pending. EVIDENCE: 4 new native tests (density resets the high-water mark on both faces; own-induced carry-forward still works for a same-density refetch), the pre-existing oscillation-trace and never-settles contrast tests still passing, full native suite 2618 green, and the viewport-fit browser negative controls PASS in the final run.

title: Gate DataTable body.rs aria-selected on selection, not interactivity
description: Follow-up from ldui-sh3's review ruling: EntityTable now gates aria-selected on the selection binding being configured, but DataTable's body.rs:322-330 still paints aria-selected on any interactive row (on_row_activate-only tables claim selectability to AT with no selection concept). Mirror EntityTable's entity_row_aria_selected gating: emit the attribute only when selection state is actually configured; pin both behaviors with native tests. Filed by the 2026-08-29 open-beads wave final review.
close_reason: Fixed and verified (commit bc96b55). DataTable's body now emits aria-selected ONLY when a selection binding is actually configured, mirroring EntityTable's entity_row_aria_selected helper (ldui-sh3). Previously it painted the attribute on any row it considered interactive, so a table using only on_row_activate - with no selection concept at all - told assistive technology that every row was selectable, a false claim. Activate-only DataTables now keep their prior DOM exactly. The selected-styling gate needed no change: selected_rows is already empty on both faces when no selection is configured, so styling was already consistent with the new attribute gate. EVIDENCE: native tests pinning BOTH shapes (activate-only -> attribute absent; selection-configured -> present as true/false), full native suite 2618 passing, and the data-table browser lanes green in the final run (reactivity data_table checks, layout 9/9, style all ceilings holding).

title: Re-export snapshot_table pure core from shared snapshot-core crate
description: Rust-DeskApp now has crates/snapshot-core: a faithful pure port of src/patterns/snapshot_table.rs @ 654c168 (PROVENANCE.md pins hashes; all 14 pure-model tests ported; pub(crate) SnapshotRenderDecision constructors and unmintable handles preserved; zero deps, no serde). Desktop SnapshotTablePage already consumes it; tui-daisy plans to as a third consumer (constraint: render-free, no serde by default). Unification: replace the local pure core with a re-export from path dep ../Rust-DeskApp/crates/snapshot-core so all three faces share one implementation. Our snapshot_table.rs is unchanged since 654c168 (verified 2026-08-29), so no rebase needed. Coordinate with rust-deskapp session before switching if our copy changes first. Relayed from rust-deskapp-42 cross-session message 2026-08-29.
notes:
BLOCKED ON SIBLING REPO (Rust-DeskApp), recorded 2026-08-31. DECISION: do not perform the swap yet - doing it today would REGRESS a consumer. crates/snapshot-core was ported from our snapshot_table.rs at hash 654c168, but commit ed275dd has since added the generation/revision-bound displayed-snapshot delta API here (beads ldui-vn81 + ldui-cb29, a 4iiz-office consumer blocker): a framework-minted checked handle that atomically replaces rows/revision/count/metadata WITHOUT bumping the dataset/access generation, so EntityTable focus scope and keyed action feedback survive, plus rejection of stale/duplicate/out-of-order deltas and coexistence with an unrelated in-flight replacement. Re-exporting from the sibling now would silently drop all of that. Required order: (1) Rust-DeskApp ports the delta API into snapshot-core from ed275dd, render-free and serde-free per the tui-daisy constraint; (2) they re-pin PROVENANCE.md at our new hash; (3) only then do we replace the local core with the re-export and re-run the 15 native reducer tests plus the snapshot_table_delta_smoke browser lane (4/4 green here) to prove nothing was lost. Their repo is read-only from this side.
UNBLOCKED 2026-08-31: Rust-DeskApp landed the port as 53db6e7 and re-pinned PROVENANCE.md from 654c168 to ed275dd. Independently verified from this side: cargo test -p snapshot-core = 33 passed (was 14); SnapshotDeltaHandle, SnapshotDeltaDisposition and SnapshotDeltaStartError are exported from the crate root; [dependencies] is empty, so the render-free/serde-free constraint holds by construction rather than by feature flag. They also ported ActionFeedbackContent and the start_action_with_content/finish_action_with_content surface beyond the delta list, which was the correct call and not scope creep: snapshot_table.rs at ed275dd delegates start_action to start_action_with_content, so a delta-only port would have made the new pin a false claim and the swap would have silently dropped the content API - exactly the failure mode this bead was being held open to avoid. Proceeding with the swap.
close_reason:
Done. The local pure core is gone; src/patterns now re-exports it from the shared snapshot-core crate (path dep ../Rust-DeskApp/crates/snapshot-core), so the desktop face, this web face and tui-daisy share ONE implementation instead of three copies. Commit ddc2fbe.

PRECONDITION MET: Rust-DeskApp landed 53db6e7, re-pinning PROVENANCE.md from 654c168 to ed275dd (our commit adding the delta API). Verified independently from this side before swapping rather than taking the report on trust: cargo test -p snapshot-core = 33 passed, the delta symbols are exported from the crate root, and [dependencies] is empty so the render-free/serde-free constraint holds by construction rather than by feature flag.

THEIR CALL TO PORT MORE THAN THE DELTA WAS CORRECT, not scope creep: snapshot_table.rs at ed275dd delegates start_action to start_action_with_content, so a delta-only port would have made the new pin a false claim and this swap would have silently dropped the ActionFeedbackContent API - the exact failure this bead was held open to prevent. Render helpers (content_text, keyed_entry_text, state_class) correctly stayed here with the renderer.

TEST COUNT 2670 -> 2637, a drop of exactly 33, fully attributed: 31 deleted from src/patterns/snapshot_table/tests.rs (whole file) and 2 from action_feedback.rs, every one a pure-model duplicate of a test snapshot-core now owns in its own 33-test suite. No renderer or integration test was removed. Keeping them would have been keeping a second copy of the thing this bead exists to de-duplicate.

PUBLIC API UNCHANGED for callers: patterns/mod.rs's re-export lists were untouched, and cargo check -p leptos-daisyui-showcase - a real consumer of start_delta/apply_delta/start_action_with_content - compiles unmodified. src/patterns/action_feedback.rs was also edited beyond the stated file list, which was structurally required and is noted here rather than buried: SnapshotTableState binds snapshot-core's own ActionFeedbackModel<K>, so a second local definition would have made .actions() return an incompatible type.

SEPARATE BREAKAGE FOUND AND FIXED WHILE HERE (commit a041d2d): tests/visual_smoke.rs no longer compiled, which also took out cargo clippy --all-targets and any unrestricted cargo test. Cause was a different PixelProof breaking change, 60dcd8b "distinguish a capture from a comparison", which removed Outcome::passed. The replacement is not a rename: Outcome::check() returns Ok in CAPTURE mode - a baseline was written, not verified - which is exactly the claim the removed field made silently. Since these tests are named *_matches_baseline, the new assert_matches_baseline helper also refuses a non-comparison outcome unless VISUAL_TEST_MODE=capture was explicitly set, so a misconfigured run that quietly captured cannot report green having verified nothing. clippy --all-targets is clean again.

title: Add a composable typed search-picker dialog pattern
description: Office No-Hires titlebar search and Account search independently compose query input, loading and error states, empty results, keyboard-selectable result rows, cancel, and activation. Modal and ResultList provide most primitives, but there is no opinionated composition that keeps dialog naming, focus return, search state, asynchronous result replacement, and stable typed result identity coherent. The current page-local versions already diverge in presentation and keyboard behavior.
design: After ResultList supports stable typed payloads, add a SearchPickerDialog pattern built from Modal, Field or Input, PageStatePanel-compatible states, and ResultList. Use typed composition and callbacks rather than a page or transport generator. The caller owns query execution, debounce policy, result payloads, authorization, and activation. LDUI owns dialog semantics, focus trap and return, labelled search markup, loading/error/empty presentation, keyboard result navigation, and responsive layout.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can open a controlled labelled search dialog, supply a controlled query and asynchronous result state, and receive the exact stable typed payload on activation. Opening focuses search; Escape or Cancel closes and restores focus; Arrow, Home, End, and Enter operate the result list; result replacement, duplicate-looking rows, loading, empty, retained error, and stale responses cannot activate an old payload. Compact and wide layouts remain visible without horizontal escape, localized copy is fully reactive, and existing Modal and ResultList APIs stay usable independently. Native and real-browser fixtures cover focus return, typed identity, asynchronous replacement, empty/error/retry, and two dialog instances.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. SearchPickerDialog composes Modal, Field/Input, PageStatePanel-compatible states and the keyed ResultList (ldui-r1z) into a controlled labelled search dialog; it INHERITS the typed-payload staleness guarantees from KeyedResultList rather than duplicating them (no parallel index/payload map), so result replacement, duplicate-looking rows, loading, empty, retained error and stale responses cannot activate an old payload. LDUI owns dialog semantics, focus trap and return, labelled search markup, state presentation and keyboard result navigation; the caller owns query execution, debounce, payloads, authorization and activation. Escape close routes through the dialog's native cancel event (an earlier revision claimed keydown preventDefault suppressed it, which is not how <dialog> works). Commits 0281d21, 1586473, 96b4f5c; lane wired via search_picker_dialog_step. EVIDENCE: 13 native tests plus tests/search_picker_dialog_smoke.rs run LIVE against a real server on 2026-08-30 = 6/6 PASS, covering focus return on Escape AND on the Cancel button, typed identity, async replacement, empty/error/retry and two dialog instances.

title: Add viewport-fit query sizing to ServerDataTable
description: EntityTable can derive visible row capacity from a definite browser-height region, but ServerDataTable still accepts only a fixed server page size. Office Awaiting and Conversations therefore either waste vertical space on tall windows, create nested scrolling on shorter windows, or implement another page-local ResizeObserver that must also reset cursor state and coordinate an asynchronous replacement fetch.
design: Add an opt-in server viewport-fit policy that reuses the proven EntityTable/DataTable measurement rules but emits a controlled page-size query proposal instead of slicing rows locally. Measurement is presentation state, not a persisted preference. Offset mode resets to page one; cursor mode requests the first slice because existing opaque tokens were minted for a different page size. Fixed-slice or page-size-disabled capabilities reject the policy visibly. Retain the displayed server slice while the caller accepts and fetches the replacement.
acceptance_criteria: A controlled offset or cursor ServerDataTable can opt into a definite-height viewport-fit policy and receive a page-size proposal matching measured row capacity. Browser resize, density, header or filter-row height, localized wrapping, and column changes recompute without oscillation. Cursor proposals reset to First and never reuse a token minted for another size; offset proposals reset to page one. Rejected or failed proposals retain the accepted rows and size, stale measurements cannot overwrite newer state, and page-size-disabled configurations fail closed. Fixed page-size behavior remains source-compatible. Native reducer tests and real-browser negative controls cover short and tall windows, horizontal scrollbars, retained failure, and rapid resize.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. ServerDataTable gained an opt-in viewport-fit policy that REUSES the proven auto_page measurement machinery (rows_per_page_for_height, max_row_height, auto_page_size_for_height, RowHeightEra) and emits a controlled page-size QUERY PROPOSAL instead of slicing rows locally. Offset proposals reset to page one; cursor proposals reset to First and never reuse a token minted for another page size (ServerCursorRequest::First carries no token by construction); fixed-slice / page-size-disabled capabilities fail closed with a visible role=alert config error; the accepted slice is retained while the caller fetches; a ViewportFitEpoch rejects stale measurements. Commits ddc6814, c6bb240, 2fb75d3. EVIDENCE: 13 native reducer tests including a replay of an oscillation trace that terminates plus a contrast test proving the same trace never settles without the own-induced-refetch era carry-forward, and browser negative controls run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS (growth-and-below-floor-retain, declined proposal retains accepted rows and size, cursor resets to First, rapid narrow resize settles, fixed-slice endpoint rejected visibly, differing-row-height refetch settles). CRITICAL NOTE: the first live run exposed that ViewportFitEpoch was never persisted, so NO proposal had ever fired for ANY viewport-fit table - the feature was entirely dead in the browser while its native reducer tests passed. Fixed in 2fb75d3; this is exactly the defect class compile-only fixtures hide.

title: Add a reusable opaque cursor history reducer
description: Many keyset APIs return only a next cursor. Office Awaiting and Conversations now each maintain a page stack, derive a previous token, reject stale Next or Previous proposals, reset history when query shape changes, and commit the stack only after a successful fetch. ServerCursorPagination correctly keeps transport caller-owned, but this identical opaque-history state machine is currently rebuilt in every consumer and is easy to update before the replacement slice succeeds.
design: Add a small transport-neutral ServerCursorHistory state or reducer that composes with ServerCursorPagination. It should derive accepted current query and ServerCursorPage metadata, translate a typed navigation proposal into an opaque request handle, and commit or fail that handle after the caller-owned fetch. It must not fetch data, parse cursors, own rows, invent totals, or impose an API schema. Query-shape replacement starts a new history generation; opaque tokens remain caller values.
acceptance_criteria: An API that returns only a next cursor can obtain truthful Previous and Next navigation without page-local Vec stacks. First, Next, and Previous proposals produce opaque caller-consumable request handles; only the latest matching success commits the new cursor and history. Failure retains the accepted slice and history, stale or duplicate completions cannot move navigation, and search, sort, filter, page-size, dataset, or access reset starts a coherent first-slice generation. The helper derives ServerCursorQuery and ServerCursorPage values accepted by the existing component, permits APIs that already return both cursors to continue without it, and focused reducer tests cover forward, backward, reset, retained failure, and out-of-order completion.
close_reason: Implemented. ServerCursorHistory is a transport-neutral reducer composing with ServerCursorPagination: it derives the accepted ServerCursorQuery/ServerCursorPage, turns typed First/Next/Previous proposals into opaque caller-consumable handles, and commits or fails them after the caller-owned fetch. It never fetches, parses cursors, owns rows, invents totals or imposes a schema; APIs returning both cursors can ignore it (server_component.rs untouched). Truthful Previous comes from an internal bounded forward-token history replayed by index, so next-cursor-only APIs no longer need page-local Vec stacks. Only the latest matching (generation, sequence) handle commits: stale completions are IgnoredStale, duplicates IgnoredConsumed, and a query-shape change starts a new generation that supersedes anything in flight. EVIDENCE (the bead names focused reducer tests as the evidence; it has no browser criteria): 10 reducer tests covering forward, backward, redo, reset, retained failure, out-of-order and duplicate completion, plus a compile-checked composition doctest against the real ServerDataTable API. Commits 2e82f6f, 7ad48da.

title: Add an opinionated reusable section heading composition
description: Office Staff and Setup contain identical local SectionHeading components, and other converted satellites repeat the same eyebrow, heading, description, and optional status layout inline. This is presentation structure rather than domain behavior, but LDUI has no reusable section-level heading between PageHeader and raw typography.
design: Add a small SectionHeader or SectionHeading pattern with reactive eyebrow, title, and optional description plus status or action composition. LDUI owns semantic spacing, typography, wrapping, and responsive alignment. Callers own copy, status meaning, action behavior, and the section content. Provide an explicit heading-level or semantic association so consumers do not hardcode an incorrect hierarchy.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can render reactive localized eyebrow, title, optional description, and optional status/action content without page-local layout classes. The component produces a valid heading hierarchy with a stable optional id for aria-labelledby, wraps status/actions without squeezing text, and remains readable at compact widths and in forced colors. Empty optional regions leave no spacing. Existing PageHeader semantics are not duplicated or weakened. A showcase and focused render/browser fixtures cover plain, status, action, long-copy, and localized variants.
close_reason: Implemented and verified. SectionHeading pattern with reactive localized eyebrow/title/optional description plus optional status and action slots; LDUI owns spacing, typography (.ld-text-* ramp, muted at text-base-content/75), wrapping and responsive alignment. Explicit HeadingLevel (H2 default, never emits h1, so it nests correctly under PageHeader's h1) with a stable optional id for aria-labelledby. Empty optional regions emit no node and therefore no gap. EVIDENCE: 6 native tests + doctests, and the dedicated browser lane section_heading_smoke run against a real server on 2026-08-30 = 5/5 PASS (plain, status, action, long-copy, localized). Commits 52a78c8, 697ad0e.

title: Add primary-secondary text presentation to EntityColumn
description: Office pages repeatedly use render_with to stack two ordinary strings in one cell: client plus matter, type plus stage, role plus scope, and a primary label plus supporting copy. Each page rebuilds the same flex column, font hierarchy, wrapping, and fallback punctuation. These cells are not rich domain widgets; they are a recurring table presentation pattern.
design: Add an opinionated primary-secondary text presentation for EntityColumn. The caller supplies canonical text plus primary and optional secondary callbacks; EntityTable owns typography, spacing, wrapping, compact rendering, overflow integration, and accessible composition. Do not introduce Office-specific labels or formatting.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can declare primary and optional secondary text without render_with; the component has intentional wide and compact layouts; empty secondary text does not leave spacing or punctuation; long and unbroken values obey the column overflow policy; the accessible/export value is complete and not spoken twice; sorting remains explicitly tied to the canonical or typed sort key; reactive column replacement updates both lines; existing custom renderers remain compatible; browser fixtures cover resizing, hiding, compact width, and forced colors.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. EntityColumn gained an opinionated primary/secondary text presentation: the caller supplies canonical text plus primary and optional secondary callbacks, and EntityTable owns typography (.ld-text-* ramp, muted secondary at text-base-content/75), spacing, wrapping, compact rendering and overflow integration. The accessible/export value stays complete and is not spoken twice (both visible lines sit in an aria-hidden wrapper beside a single sr-only node carrying the canonical text); sorting stays tied to the canonical or typed sort key; an empty secondary emits no node and therefore no spacing or punctuation; existing render_with renderers still win. Commits 706b60a, 1db73a6, 1d9e268. EVIDENCE: native tests including a columns-Signal replacement proving both lines re-render under true column replacement (the first review caught that this clause had been demonstrated with row-data mutation instead), plus entity_column_primary_secondary_composes_two_accessible_lines run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS. The live run initially failed on FIXTURE defects (a JS-escaping bug in the compact selector, a missing viewport settle, and a null-assertion incompatible with the driver's Option collapse), not on the component.

title: Add typed summary-row emphasis to EntityTable
description: The Office Finances snapshot has a Total row that must be visually distinct across every cell, while Contribution and other reporting snapshots have summary or aggregate rows with the same need. EntityTable has column renderers but no typed row-presentation seam, so consumers must repeat the same predicate and classes in every cell and still cannot apply one coherent row border, background, or compact treatment.
design: Prefer a narrow framework-owned semantic enum returned by a row callback, such as Standard, Summary, Muted, or Attention, rather than an unrestricted class-string hook. EntityTable owns tokens and responsive styling; consumers own only the typed classification predicate. This must remain presentation-only and must not change row identity, ordering, activation, selection, or mutation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can classify a row with a documented semantic presentation without duplicating per-cell renderers. Summary styling is coherent across wide and compact layouts, survives sorting, filtering, paging, hiding, resizing, zebra mode, hover, and focus, and remains legible in forced colors. Classification never changes row keys, accessible names, action eligibility, sort values, or source data. The default renders identically to current EntityTable. Focused native and browser fixtures cover a total row moving under sort and a compact summary row.
close_reason: Implemented and VERIFIED LIVE IN A BROWSER. EntityTable gained typed summary-row emphasis via a narrow framework-owned semantic enum (Standard/Summary/Muted/Attention) returned by a row callback - not a class-string hook - with EntityTable owning the tokens. It is presentation-only: no variant sets a background-color, so it composes with selection's bg-base-200 and with zebra striping rather than fighting them, and classification never changes row keys, accessible names, action eligibility, sort values or source data. The default renders identically to before. Emphasis is resolved once per data change and shared across the class, data-attribute and cell-content sites, so it is not recomputed per row and is decoupled from selection-click invalidation. Commits 1ec8cc1, 5bd7d19. EVIDENCE: native tests incl. a monotone/zebra-composition guard, plus entity_table_row_emphasis_survives_sort_and_composes_with_selection run LIVE on 2026-08-30 = PASS (a total row keeps its emphasis while moving under sort, and while selected on a zebra table).

title: DataTable search input and filter selects have no accessible name
notes:
Found 2026-08-28 while converting a table in 4iiz-etl. Its style audit reports,
on EVERY page carrying a DataTable:

  COMPONENT-DRIFT  input-outside-field: input has no fieldset ancestor
    div.etl-table-region > div.w-full > div.mb-3.flex > input.input.input-bordered
  COMPONENT-DRIFT  input-outside-field: select has no fieldset ancestor
    thead > tr.data-table-filter-row > th.p-1 > select.select.select-bordered

Both elements are ldui's own: the DataTable's `searchable` input and its
per-column filter `select`. Neither sits in a `fieldset`/`Field`, and neither
carries a visible or associated label.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A LINT: a bare `input` with only a placeholder is not
labelled for a screen reader — placeholder text is not an accessible name, and
it disappears the moment someone types. The same goes for the per-column filter
selects, where "which column does this filter?" is conveyed only by physical
position in the header row.

WHAT THE CONSUMER SEES TODAY: every page that turns on `searchable` or
`filterable` costs exactly +2 drift findings, so consumers ratchet their audit
ceilings to absorb library markup they cannot fix. 4iiz-etl has now done this
twice (`schemas`, then `home`), each time recording that the added findings are
ldui's chrome rather than the page's own. That is a workaround, not a fix, and
it quietly raises the ceiling that would otherwise catch real drift.

SUGGESTED: give the search input an accessible name (visually-hidden label or
`aria-label`, ideally derived from the table's own aria-label), and give each
filter select an `aria-label` naming its column. A `fieldset`/`Field` wrapper
would satisfy the rule structurally, but the accessible name is the substance —
the rule is a proxy for it.

Not urgent for 4iiz-etl: the ceilings absorb it. Filed because the accessibility
gap is real and every consumer inherits it.
close_reason: Completed in 09e150d and 6369f6c: client/server DataTable search inputs and column filters have real associated labels plus localized aria-labels; axe/browser checks pass and stateful relocalization is covered by the 32nd reactivity check.

title: PieChart slice separators are hardcoded stroke=white, which seams against dark themes
description: src/charts/pie_chart.rs:125 emits stroke="white" for the slice separators. It is a genuine literal, so the value-keyed paint routing correctly leaves it on the presentation attribute and the new guard passes it deliberately - this is not a routing bug. The problem is the colour: under dark/dracula/forest the separators read as bright white seams against --color-base-100 instead of disappearing into the card. The new /components/charts demo page now renders two pie charts with it, on a page whose entire purpose is visual review, and the guard test will accept it permanently.
design: Use var(--color-base-100) so the separator matches whatever surface the chart sits on. That makes it token-bearing, so it must then route through paint_attrs like every other non-literal colour.
acceptance_criteria: Pie slice separators are invisible against the card surface under light AND dark themes. The value routes through paint_attrs since it now contains var().
notes: Raised by the ldui-1g5 review 2026-08-09 as a follow-up, correctly out of scope for that bead.
close_reason: Landed e3d1cb2. Pie separators now var(--color-base-100), routed through paint_attrs like every other token-bearing colour. Verified under data-theme=dark on the real demo: rgb(255,255,255) -> oklch(0.2533 0.016 252.42), identical to that theme's --color-base-100, on all 8 separators, with 0 stroke attributes left on the DOM. This is also what forced merge_style to be n-ary rather than a (base, decl) pair - PieChart passes a routed fill AND a routed stroke.

title: RosterGrid polish: table accessible name, TABLE_SCROLL_WRAPPER_CLASS reuse, trim always-on title
description: Minor cluster from the ldui-m9s review, none blocking: (1) spread attributes land on the root <div> (component.rs:161), so a consumer cannot attach aria-label/aria-labelledby to the <table> itself - two rosters on one page are indistinguishable to a screen reader. Modal already has the label/labelled_by/described_by idiom to copy. (2) the hardcoded scroll wrapper 'w-full overflow-x-auto' (component.rs:163) duplicates TABLE_SCROLL_WRAPPER_CLASS (src/components/data_table/mod.rs:60), which is pub(super) and therefore reachable, and is pinned by a test asserting both DataTable variants use it - reusing it keeps the horizontal-overflow contract in one place. (3) title on every tile (component.rs:254) duplicates visible content as a hover tooltip on the display-only path and duplicates aria-label on the interactive one; DayScheduler's title carries only the event title, not the full accessible name.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can name the table itself; the scroll wrapper comes from the shared constant; title no longer duplicates the accessible name.
close_reason: Landed b70c0ef + 55387bf, fix round e9d2866. Reviewed and re-reviewed clean. Roving focus verified in the live DOM (84 tiles, exactly 1 tabindex=0, invariant maintained across key presses; ArrowLeft at col 0 does not wrap). clamp_focus_cell is pure, Option-returning, short-circuits on n==0 before n-1, with two exhaustive sweeps. Fix round closed a regression THIS feature introduced - Alt/Cmd+Arrow (browser Back/Forward) were being swallowed by an unconditional prevent_default - plus Ctrl+Home/End dead on macOS, and named the interactive demo grids. Also adopted all 3 optional items: aria-selected on the gridcell replacing aria-pressed (which was asserting a toggle the component does not control), focused promoted to a Memo, and a no-op-movement early return that preserves the restorable raw coordinate.

title: Charts other than BarChart/Heatmap still emit raw fill= and would hit the var()-in-presentation-attribute hazard
description: src/charts/paint.rs was introduced on 2026-08-09 (commit c153c58) to route a colour through style="fill: ..." when it contains var(), because SVG2 parses presentation attributes with the property's isolated value grammar and custom-property substitution is NOT specified to run there. Chromium already declines it for length attributes, and the SVG WG has an open request (Nov 2025) to specify or forbid it. If it is forbidden, the value stops parsing and the shape paints SOLID BLACK. Only BarChart (bar_chart.rs:129,196) and Heatmap (heatmap.rs:319) route through paint_attrs. LineChart, PieChart, StackedBarChart, StackedAreaChart and AreaChart still emit raw fill=color, so a consumer passing a daisyUI theme token (e.g. var(--color-primary)) through their color / per-segment colour props hits the same hazard with no protection.
design: Route every chart's fill through crate::charts::paint::paint_attrs, which is already value-keyed (color.contains("var(")) rather than chart-keyed, so it needs no per-chart logic. Literal colours must keep the fill attribute so existing DOM stays byte-identical - paint.rs already does this and has tests pinning it (literal_colors_keep_the_fill_attribute).
acceptance_criteria: No chart component emits a fill= attribute whose value contains var(. A test asserts this per chart. Literal-colour callers still render fill= unchanged.
notes: Raised by the fix-round re-review 2026-08-09 as an out-of-scope observation - the original finding was scoped to BarChart, so this was correctly not fixed there. Same defect class, no consumer is known to be hitting it yet.
close_reason: Landed ad52cf1. Reviewed: satisfied. Routed all 5 named charts PLUS sparkline (swept rather than working from the list), and extended paint_attrs to cover STROKE - the sharper argument being that stroke's initial value is none, so a value that stops parsing DELETES the line rather than blackening it, and LineChart/AreaChart/Sparkline draw their primary mark with stroke alone. Browser: 0 var() in any fill=/stroke= attribute vs 51 before; 71 token paints on style; 0 computing to black or none. Reviewer independently re-grepped src/charts and confirmed no defs/gradient/marker/pattern site was missed. Follow-ups filed: ldui-xxc (same defect live in gantt, outside the guard's scan), ldui-cy5 (PieChart stroke=white).

title: Two DataTables with overlapping features: converge widgets::DataTable and components::DataTable, or document the split
description: This library ships TWO DataTable components and nothing tells a consumer which to use. components::DataTable (src/components/data_table/) is the rich one: 28 props incl. cell_renderers, typed_cells, row_class_fn, Column::action(), selection with row_key identity, column chooser, per-column filters, extra_filter, toolbar slot, auto_page_size, server-side variant. widgets::DataTable (src/widgets/data_table.rs) is a simpler Vec<Vec<String>> table but owns three things the component does NOT have: badge_column_keys, link_column_keys, and bulk_select keyed by the first cell's String id. CONSEQUENCE: consumers pick by accident. 4iiz-Office picked the widget and then filed ldui-3qc asking for a per-row action column - which the COMPONENT already has via Column::action() + cell_renderers. That bead is being satisfied additively on the widget to unblock them, which deepens the duplication rather than resolving it.
design: Three options, needs the owner's call rather than an agent's: (a) port badge/link/bulk-select onto components::DataTable and deprecate the widget with a migration note; (b) keep both and document the split explicitly in CLAUDE.md and both doc comments - widget = read-mostly string tables, component = interactive typed tables; (c) reduce the widget to a thin preset over the component. (a) is the least duplication and the most migration cost for existing consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Either the two are converged, or both doc comments and CLAUDE.md state plainly which to reach for and why, so the next consumer does not pick by accident.
notes: Raised 2026-08-09 while implementing ldui-3qc. Not blocking that bead.
close_reason: Documented the split (989dfe6) per the bead's own acceptance criterion - both doc comments plus CLAUDE.md now state which DataTable to reach for and why. Convergence/deprecation deliberately NOT done: that is an owner-level architectural call, not an agent's.

title: Chart — a real per-bar colour prop
description: REQUESTED BY: 4iiz-Office, crates/office-perf-web/src/screens/workspace/manager/by_week.rs (the Office Leader page's 'Closed work by week'). THE GAP: the chart control cannot colour INDIVIDUAL bars from data — colour is per-series, not per-point. WHAT THE CONSUMER NEEDS: each week's bar coloured by ITS OWN above/below-target flag, so a viewer sees at a glance which weeks met the goal. WHAT THEY DO INSTEAD TODAY: the per-week state is restored as a row of Badge chips underneath the chart, one per week, each coloured by its own flag — a workaround that duplicates the data and takes vertical space. WHAT IS NEEDED: a per-bar (per-datapoint) colour prop, or a callback receiving the datapoint and returning a theme token. ★ FILED 2026-08-09 — referenced in office-perf source but absent from this board until now.

title: Heatmap — a favourable/unfavourable colour axis
description: REQUESTED BY: 4iiz-Office, crates/office-perf-web/src/screens/workspace/manager/kpi_by_office.rs (the Office Leader page's KPI-by-office grid). THE GAP: Heatmap renders a single crimson intensity ramp. A KPI grid needs the colour to carry DIRECTION — on-track vs behind — not just magnitude, and for some measures higher is better while for others lower is (handle time, overdue count). WHAT IS NEEDED: a favourable/unfavourable colour axis, i.e. a per-cell or per-column 'sense' so the component knows which end of the range is good, and a diverging palette rather than a single ramp. ⚠️ CONSTRAINT FROM THE CONSUMER: office-perf operates a 'no new colour' rule — the palette must come from existing daisyUI theme tokens (success/warning/error) rather than introducing new hues, and ★ COLOUR MUST CARRY THE JUDGEMENT ONLY, NEVER THE CATEGORY (their KPI legend states this explicitly), so the component must remain readable when colour is unavailable. ★ FILED 2026-08-09 — referenced in office-perf source but absent from this board until now.

title: DayScheduler's hour gutter is hardcoded 12-hour AM/PM, so it stays English on a Spanish page
description:
FROM office-perf (C:/dev/4iiz-Office), found 2026-07-28 in its first Spanish UI pass.

`DayScheduler` renders the hour gutter with a hardcoded 12-hour AM/PM clock. On
a Spanish page the whole screen is Spanish and the gutter still reads:

    8 AM  9 AM  10 AM  11 AM  12 PM  1 PM  2 PM ...

Spanish-speaking locales write the 24-hour clock in this context (08:00, 13:00).
The 12-hour form exists but carries "p. m." with spaces and periods, which is
fussier than it is worth for a calendar gutter.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: office-perf's client population is ~87%
Spanish-leading, and the consumer has now made every OTHER clock on the page
language-aware — the status-bar pill, the planner's block times, My Day's
appointment times. The gutter is the only English clock left, so a single screen
shows two conventions side by side, which reads as a bug rather than as a
mixture.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, in preference order:
  1. A `hour_format: Signal<HourFormat>` (or `use_24h: Signal<bool>`) prop on
     DayScheduler, defaulting to the current 12-hour behaviour so no existing
     consumer changes.
  2. Failing that, accept a formatter closure `Fn(u32) -> String` for the
     gutter label, which keeps the locale decision entirely with the consumer.

(1) is nicer for the common case; (2) is more flexible and cannot go stale as
locales are added.

CONSUMER-SIDE WORKAROUND TODAY: none that is worth doing. office-perf renders
its own blocks INTO DayScheduler's rects but the gutter is drawn by the
component, so the only alternative is to stop using it for the backdrop — which
would give up the gridlines, now-line, overlap-lane packing and hit-testing the
component exists to provide.

NOT URGENT: the labels are readable and unambiguous, just not localised.
notes:
CORRECTION FROM office-perf, 2026-07-28 — the premise of this bead was partly WRONG, and you built on it in good faith.

I filed it saying DayScheduler "hardcodes 12-hour AM/PM". It does not, and never
did. `hour_format: Signal<HourFormat>` has been a prop since the original port
(7b34b1ff), and OFFICE-PERF was passing `HourFormat::Twelve` unconditionally.
The last English clock on our Spanish page was our own choice, and the fix was
one line on our side:

    hour_format=Signal::derive(move || match lang.get() {
        Lang::Es => HourFormat::TwentyFour,
        Lang::En => HourFormat::Twelve,
    })

Verified in the browser: Spanish now reads 08:00/09:00/10:00, English still
reads 8 AM/9 AM/10 AM.

WHAT YOU ADDED IS STILL WORTH HAVING. `hour_label` (Callback<u32, String>) is
the escape hatch for a locale that wants NEITHER convention — hour names from an
i18n catalogue, or a format neither enum arm covers. office-perf does not need
it today; a future consumer plausibly will. I would not revert it.

ONE THING WORTH FLAGGING FOR OTHER CONSUMERS: HourFormat::TwentyFour is
`#[default]`. Anyone who adopts DayScheduler WITHOUT passing `hour_format` gets
24-hour, which for an English-only app is a silent behaviour change rather than
a new capability. Might be worth a line in the component docs, or in the
changelog entry, so it is not discovered in a screenshot.

Sorry for the wasted cycle. The rule I should have followed, and now have
written down: read the component's own props before filing across a repo
boundary.
close_reason:
Shipped as an optional `hour_label: Callback<u32, String>` on both DayScheduler and WeekView (commit d1d1a5d) — the bead's option (2). Overrides `hour_format` when supplied, so a consumer can render any label it likes ("8 h", a catalogue lookup, a locale-specific 12h form).

Correction to the report's premise, which matters for the consumer: the gutter was NOT hardcoded. Option (1) has been there since the port — `hour_format: Signal<HourFormat>` defaults to `HourFormat::TwentyFour`. office-perf sees AM/PM because its day planner explicitly asks for it at office-perf-web/src/screens/day_planner.rs:1007 (`hour_format=Signal::derive(|| HourFormat::Twelve)`). So there IS a consumer-side fix available today and it is one line: make that signal read the active locale and return TwentyFour for Spanish. Nothing needs to wait on this crate.

The new closure is for the case that one-liner can't cover — a locale wanting neither 24h nor English AM/PM.

HourFormat itself is unchanged, so the port stays in step with d2d-ui's own two-variant HourFormat (crates/d2d-ui/src/controls/day_scheduler.rs:25) — the desktop face has no locale hook either.

Verified: cargo xtask verify 9/9, test-reactivity 6/6, test-layout 8/8. Demo sections added on /components/day-scheduler and /components/week-view.

title: TextRotate: rotating words render above the baseline and are clipped (mostly invisible)
description: User-reported (2026-07-08), confirmed LIVE on /components/text_rotate. The rotating words are almost entirely invisible/clipped: e.g. 'Hello, I'm [blank]', 'Our product is [blank] and loved by developers worldwide' — the animated word area shows nothing or a sliver. Measured live: the .text-rotate > span > span items render with their tops ~80-164px ABOVE the .text-rotate box top (all items overflowsTop:true), and the box computes overflow:hidden with height == line-height (e.g. 40px for text-4xl), so the items are positioned outside the visible band and clipped away. Even the resting first-child (opacity 1, translateY 0) is not visible. Root cause is the component's positioning model in demo/custom-components.css lines 139-161: .text-rotate (relative, inline-block), middle .text-rotate>span (relative, inline-block, no height), items .text-rotate>span>span (absolute, top:0 left:0). The absolute items are not aligned to the text baseline and the container does not establish a correct visible band, so with the translateY(0 -> -20px) keyframes the text renders above the line. NOTE: source .text-rotate rule sets NO overflow, yet it computes overflow:hidden — track down where that comes from (possibly a Tailwind utility or inherited rule) as part of the fix. FIX (needs iterative CSS rework, not a one-liner): rebuild the container as a fixed-height overflow-hidden band with items vertically stacked and animating within it, aligned to baseline; verify each of the 6 demo examples shows the rotating word fully. Component: src/components/text_rotate/component.rs (markup) + demo/custom-components.css (.text-rotate rules + text-rotate-N-items keyframes). P3 visual.
close_reason: Fixed in 67f768e. Rewrote .text-rotate CSS (demo/custom-components.css) from a broken absolute/relative model to an inline-grid stack: display:contents on the middle span flattens it so items become grid children of .text-rotate, all sharing grid cell 1/1 (overlap in place), box sizes to widest word, visible word sits on the text baseline. Root cause was the old middle container computing to ~3 line-heights (120px), pushing items ~80px above the visible band where overflow clipped them. Verified live on the rebuilt artifact across all 6 demo examples: every visible word visInBand:true + box alignedToLine:true; animation cycles one word at a time correctly.

title: Hover3d: flicker on hover + cards overlap section headers
description:
User-reported (2026-07-08), two bugs on the Hover 3D demo page, both rooted in demo/custom-components.css .hover-3d (lines 256-284) + src/components/hover_3d/component.rs.

ISSUE 1 — FLICKER while hovering (even mouse ~stationary). Diagnosed LIVE with event counters: with a truly stationary cursor, ZERO mouse events fire over 2s and transform stays flat, and during movement each mousemove produces exactly one clean transform write (no cascade). So it is NOT a JS mousemove/mouseleave feedback loop. Root cause is GPU 3D compositing / z-fighting: .hover-3d sets transform-style:preserve-3d + perspective:1000px (lines 258-259) and hosts 8 empty hover-zone divs at z-index:10, pointer-events:all (lines 269-275) that are COPLANAR in that same 3D context with the tilted content child; the content also has transition:transform 0.1s (line 265). Once any tilt is applied (any hover), the coplanar zone overlay and the perspective-projected card surface z-fight and the compositor repaints every frame = visible flicker. Real-mouse micro-jitter + the 0.1s transition adds a jello wobble on top.
FIX options (pick minimal): (a) take the hover content out of coplanar conflict / promote it to its own layer — e.g. give the content will-change:transform or translateZ(0), or wrap the tilt target in an inner element isolated from the zones; (b) set pointer-events:none on the tilting content so only the (non-moving) zones+host do hit-testing; (c) drop transform-style:preserve-3d on the content children (they have no 3D children) and/or remove the 0.1s transition so tilt is instant. Verify live that flicker stops.

ISSUE 2 — cards OVERLAP the section header above them. Measured LIVE (static, NOT tilt-related — max up-tilt moves card only ~1px): the .hover-3d host box is SHORTER than its card content and centers the overflow, so the card bleeds ~10-22px ABOVE the host top into the preceding h2. E.g. Credit Card host height 224px vs card content 269px -> card top 22px above host; card top 382 vs 'Credit Card Style' h2 bottom 388 = 6px overlap; Product Showcase cards 11px over their h2. Host computes display:grid with a track shorter than content (source not in the .hover-3d rule as read — implementer should pin where display:grid/height comes from: a Tailwind class, the Card, or an inherited rule). FIX: make .hover-3d size to its content (height:auto / min-content, or align/justify so the card doesn't overflow the track), OR add adequate top spacing so the 3D card cannot collide with the header. Verify the card no longer touches the h2 above at rest.

Both fixes land in demo/custom-components.css and possibly src/components/hover_3d/component.rs. Low priority visual polish, but user-visible. NOTE during repro the MCP browser tab kept auto-drifting between hover_3d/hover_gallery/icon_tile — that was tooling confusion with multiple tabs, not a product routing bug (hover_3d loads fine on direct nav).
close_reason: Fixed in 5716a32 (demo/custom-components.css). OVERLAP: verified FIXED (measured + visual on rebuilt artifact). The perspective-projected card rendered ~10-27px outside its host box and collided with the section header above; added margin-block:1.5rem so the tilt has breathing room — card-top-to-header gaps went from -6..-11px (overlapping) to +13..+18px (clear); confirmed visually (Basic/Credit Card/Product Showcase all have clear space below their headers). FLICKER: changed the tilted content from transform-style:preserve-3d to flat — it removes the content from a shared 3D context coplanar with the z-index:10 hover-zone overlay (the diagnosed GPU z-fighting/repaint cause) while the tilt still works (verified: rotateX/Y still renders as matrix3d via the host's inherited perspective). CAVEAT: the flicker is a compositing repaint that only manifests with real-mouse hover (0 JS events fire on a stationary CDP cursor), so I could not reproduce it headlessly to confirm the fix eliminates it — needs user confirmation with a real mouse; reopen if it persists.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: RESOLVED 2026-07-08. ISSUE 2 (overlap): FIXED + measurement-verified (5716a32) — .hover-3d margin-block:1.5rem + display:block/height:auto; card-to-header gaps went from -6..-11px (overlapping) to +13..+19px (clear). ISSUE 1 (flicker): the tilt content was transform-style:preserve-3d (coplanar z-fight with the z-index:10 hover zones in the host's perspective context). Fixed to transform-style:flat (5716a32, tilt still renders as matrix3d) and HARDENED (4e8582b) with the strongest standard remedies for this GPU-compositing repaint class: will-change:transform + backface-visibility:hidden (content composites on its own layer, not repainting the shared 3D context per frame) + pointer-events:none (only the stationary zones hit-test; component is documented non-interactive-content-only). NOTE: the flicker is a REAL-CURSOR compositing artifact — synthetic/JS mouse events cannot reproduce it (0 events fire on a stationary cursor), so a human real-mouse hover is the only decisive confirmation; that's inherent to the bug, not a gap in the fix. Code-side resolution is complete + as robust as CSS allows. Closing; reopen if a real-mouse hover still shows flicker.

title: demo status bar calls performance.memory as a function — console error every tick on every page
description: Browser smoke (ldui-0wf): every demo page logs 'Uncaught TypeError: performance.memory is not a function' 30-150+ times (repeats on an interval). Source: demo status bar Memory widget (demo/src/core/layout.rs area) invoking performance.memory() — it is a (non-standard, Chrome-only) property, not a function, and js_sys bindings expose it differently. Fix: read it as a property with a guard (Reflect::get on performance, bail silently when absent), or drop the widget.

title: Motion: generic Transition<T>/Lerp + Keyframe/Track signal interpolation
description: d2d-ui motion/transition.rs provides a Lerp trait (f32, color, shadow, [f32;4]) + Transition<T> (fixed-duration eased interpolation with mid-flight retarget) + Keyframe<T>/Track<T> multi-stage choreography. leptos-daisyui-rs has no way to programmatically interpolate a Rust-owned signal over time (count-ups, animated numeric/color values, dynamic keyframes with variable endpoints) — CSS transitions cannot animate arbitrary signal state. Implement a Lerp trait + rAF-driven Transition signal, easings from ui-tokens (--ld-ease-* equivalents evaluated in Rust via the existing cubic-bezier solver pattern in d2d easing.rs). Include Track/Keyframe multi-stage support. Source: d2d-ui/src/motion/transition.rs (10.1K), easing.rs (6.0K).
close_reason: Implemented in 957fb96: motion Lerp/Transition/Keyframe/Track (verbatim d2d port, bezier solver byte-identical, retarget continuity tested) + use_animated reusing corrected raf driver. Review approved clean; 1618 tests green.

title: Motion: Spring physics primitive (rAF-driven signal)
description: d2d-ui motion/spring.rs has a damped-harmonic Spring (stiffness/damping, semi-implicit Euler, sub-stepped <=8ms, velocity-preserving retarget, is_settled). No CSS or leptos-daisyui-rs equivalent — CSS cannot express springs (pre-linear()). Port options: (a) requestAnimationFrame loop driving a Leptos signal (needs an is-animating gate; browser owns the frame clock), or (b) build-time linear() easing approximation for fixed spring params. Anchor params/durations on ui-tokens. Declarative motion is already at parity (ldui-e1o); this is the imperative gap. Source: d2d-ui/src/motion/spring.rs (5.1K).
close_reason: Implemented in e9da2c5 + fix b0580f0: src/motion (Spring verbatim port + 7 d2d tests, use_spring rAF hook with is-animating gate + on_cleanup, shared start_raf_loop driver; restart-after-settle Critical bug fixed via continue_or_mark_stopped). 1598 tests green.

title: Add ergonomic <ModalInfoRow>/<ModalSearchRow>/<ModalStatusRow> for find-and-restore recipe
description:
Rust-DeskApp commit 3b15491 added row-stack helpers to d2d_ui::Dialog: with_info_row(), with_search_row(), with_status_row(). These formalise the title→info→search→status→body→actions pattern used by find-and-restore style dialogs (see backup-monitor's Find & Restore as the reference consumer).

Leptos Modal currently has Modal/ModalBox/ModalAction/ModalBackdrop. Consumers can compose info/search/status rows by hand inside ModalBox, but there's no formalised pattern.

Proposal: add <ModalInfoRow>, <ModalSearchRow>, <ModalStatusRow> wrapper components that apply consistent flex/spacing/border-bottom styling so the recipe is one-line ergonomic. Each renders its children in a row with the daisy-themed dividers between rows.

Reference: Rust-DeskApp/docs/leptos-parity.md — Modal section. Lower priority than multi-select (ldui-odq) since this is ergonomic sugar, not a missing feature.

title: Document EntityTable selection, row_emphasis, and primary_secondary in doc/components/entity_table.md
description: doc/components/entity_table.md predates the 2026-08-29 wave and does not cover the controlled single-row selection (ldui-sh3), typed summary-row emphasis (ldui-mqb), or EntityColumn primary/secondary presentation (ldui-97v). Rustdoc is complete; the guide needs a section per feature incl. the selection-gated aria-selected contract and the emphasis composition rules (text/border only, composes with selection bg + zebra). Filed by the 2026-08-29 wave final review.
close_reason: Done (faea3a7). doc/components/entity_table.md now documents the three features shipped in the 2026-08-29/30 wave, written against the current code rather than the bead text: (1) controlled single-row selection - the proposal-first API, exact stable-key matching with no positional fallback (so filtering/sorting/paging/removal select nothing rather than the wrong row), and that aria-selected is emitted ONLY when a selection binding is configured so activate-only tables keep their prior DOM; (2) typed summary-row emphasis - the narrow Standard/Summary/Muted/Attention enum, presentation-only, with no variant setting a background-color, which is precisely why it composes with selection's background and with zebra striping instead of fighting them; (3) EntityColumn primary/secondary text - canonical text plus primary and optional secondary callbacks, an accessible/export value that stays complete and is not announced twice (visible lines in an aria-hidden wrapper beside a single sr-only node), sorting still tied to the canonical or typed sort key, and an empty secondary emitting nothing.

title: FilterBar always-rendered empty children wrapper can add a phantom wrap row
description: patterns/filter_bar.rs renders an unconditional children wrapper div (flex min-w-0 flex-[3_1_28rem]); with no children content at very narrow widths flex-wrap can place the invisible div on its own wrapped line, contributing a gap-3 row-gap of empty space. Pre-existing (noted during ldui-3br review; flex algebra verified harmless at tested widths). Make the wrapper conditional like the search/active_binding/result slots. Filed by the 2026-08-29 wave final review.
close_reason: Fixed and committed (faea3a7). FilterBar's children wrapper is no longer unconditional: it is now Option-gated with the same .map() idiom the component already uses for its search, active_binding and result slots, so an absent or empty children slot emits NO node. Previously the always-rendered <div class='flex min-w-0 flex-[3_1_28rem] ...'> could be pushed onto its own wrapped line at very narrow widths and contribute a gap-3 row-gap of empty space. The ordinary case (children present) keeps the flex-[3_1_28rem] growth other row items rely on, and existing callers compile unchanged. EVIDENCE: a native test pinning both shapes via the new filter_bar_children_wrapper helper (is_some when children are supplied, is_none when not) - a DOM-string assertion was not possible because .to_html() panics without the ssr feature; full native suite 2614 passing.

title: Calendar: evaluate native calendar grid widget (currently third-party wrapper only)
description: Calendar is a bare styling div hosting Cally/Pikaday/React Day Picker; DatePicker wraps native <input type=date>. d2d ships a full custom grid (month/year state + nav, select_day, is_today/is_selected, month/year quick-jump popups, typed date entry with validation). The wrapper approach is a deliberate design choice with real benefits (free locale/a11y/keyboard) — decide whether a pure-Rust CalendarGrid is wanted for no-JS-dep consumers (EUC/Rust-DeskApp parity), and if yes file the port. DayScheduler/WeekView (ldui-jcs.9/.13) do NOT depend on this. Source: d2d-ui/src/controls/calendar.rs (24.7K), date_picker.rs (24.2K).
close_reason: DECISION: build later, don't build now. Analysis in .superpowers/sdd/task-24-report.md. Zero present demand: EUC never uses Calendar/DatePicker (all 14 date-entry sites are native input type=date); Rust-DeskApp is the parity source, not a consumer, and its parity doc already scores Calendar done. Only calendar-shaped future need is EUC FR-25-024 blackout-period calendar, documented deferred with no spec. Cost ~700-900 LOC MVP with genuinely-new ARIA-grid/keyboard/locale work (day_scheduler/week_view hour-grid math not reusable). TRIGGER to flip to build-now: EUC concretely needs per-day decoration, programmatic month/year state, or range selection beyond native input type=date.
